defects.name: Adapted Cantrip
defects.detail: The whole feat is inert. The record's choice carries `inert: "Recorded only: the cantrip is not added to your prepared options or your repertoire — add it yourself…"`, and the harness confirms it: verdict inert-declared, two different answers moved nothing (`moved:false`, `movedPaths:[]`), silentDefault true, sheetDiff empty. So none of the three delivery clauses land — no addition to the prepared-cantrip options (the dailyChoice lane, which per Q23 belongs in Daily preparations and is not offered there either), no repertoire replacement, and the chosen cantrip is castable nowhere in the class entry. This is not a lane gap: `grantedRepertoire`/grantedRepertoireAdds (build.ts:3796, 3980) already adds spells into a caster's entry, and FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS already grants a chosen cantrip from a filtered list. Builder half fails twice more. (a) Q9 — the picker offers all 115 cantrips with no tradition filter; the record's own note admits it ("the picker can't filter that, because your tradition depends on your class"), yet `OpenChoiceFrom.traditions` exists and the resolver already runs against a concrete character, so a caster is shown their OWN tradition's cantrips, which the feat forbids. (b) the repertoire branch's mandatory question — which cantrip known is given up — is never asked: choiceCount is 1 and no picker over the character's own repertoire is rendered, so a repertoire caster is left in a state the feat does not describe. Noted in passing: the feat prints "spellcasting class feature" as a prerequisite and eligibleHosts still returns fighter/human.

defects.name: Additional Lore
defects.detail: Only the first sentence is built. FEAT_GRANTS['additional-lore'] is {loreChoices:1} (src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:22) — a free-text Lore subject, granted trained. THREE things the text promises are absent. (1) "At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory": the record carries no rankUpgrade, and the Lore grant loop (src/rules/build.ts:3435-3441) hardcodes maxRank(cur,'trained') and never applies the `at()` level-upgrade helper the other grants use — so no extra increase is offered at 3/7/15 and the rank never rises. Observed: a level-20 fighter with the feat and subject "Warfare" reads Warfare Lore rank "trained", +22, timeline a single "Trained" at level 1. (2) The repeatable clause is broken at the storage key: maxTakable is null so the feat stays offerable, but the builder binds every instance's input to `${featId}:${index}` (Builder.tsx:1894 loreKey2, read back at build.ts:3436), so two takes share the key `additional-lore:0`. Observed: two takes with subjects Warfare and Sailing produced exactly one lore skill, lore:warfare — the second instance grants nothing and the two instances cannot hold different subcategories, which is the one filtering the text DOES require ("you must select a new subcategory"). (3) The answer is not legible on the feat: the FeatChoice carries no `choice`, so the feat entry reads "Additional Lore" with no subject (twice, if taken twice), and the skill breakdown names the source "a trained skill" rather than the feat. The Lore-already-trained non-filter is fine — free text cannot over-filter.

defects.name: Adopted Ancestry
defects.detail: The feat's whole payload is unbuilt, and the record says so itself: its choice carries inert = "Recorded only: the chosen ancestry's feats aren't yet offered in your ancestry feat slots — add them through Setup -> Overrides". Confirmed by grep: nothing in src/ reads the `adoptedAncestry` flag, and eligibleFeatsForSlot (src/rules/featSlots.ts:88-99) gates an ancestry slot on f.traits.includes(build.ancestryId), the versatile heritage's own id, heritage-level extraAncestryFeatTraits (the half-elf/half-orc route) or the universal-ancestry trait — there is no hook for a feat-chosen ancestry, so "You can select ancestry feats from the ancestry you chose, in addition to your character's own ancestry" never widens any slot, now or at any later level. The picker itself is also wrong at both edges. Too narrow: its options are a hardcoded 8 (Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Human, Leshy, Orc) with the note "Only ancestries marked common in the app's data are listed" — the app marks 20 ancestries uncommon and 22 rare, including catfolk, hobgoblin, kholo, kobold, lizardfolk, ratfolk, tengu and tripkee, so "another ancestry to which you have access" is hard-blocked rather than reachable with its rarity shown (Ruling H). Too wide: the character's OWN ancestry is offered live — the fighter/human host is shown "Human", the one pick that buys nothing across the whole career (Q21), and it is neither excluded nor greyed with a reason (Q27). The answer IS echoed onto the feat's label, so the "name the adopted ancestry" requirement is met; the sheet half of the grant cannot be judged because the route into it does not exist.

defects.name: Advanced Weaponry
defects.detail: Two of the feat's three requirements are undelivered, and the record says so itself. BUILDER: the text's first question — "Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks" — is never asked. `declared` is `record.choice` only, choiceCount 1, and that one picker is the TRAIT picker. Its 8 options are exactly right (disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, versatile bludgeoning/piercing/slashing — versatile correctly split three ways), so the second question is fine; the first has no picker at all. This is not a lane gap: the sibling evolution feats pushing-attack and weighty-impact both carry `choice {flag:'pushingAttack', prompt:'Eidolon attack', kind:'array', options:[primary, secondary]}` in effect-backfill.json, which is the same question in the same words. SHEET: the picked trait is never written onto the chosen attack. The record's own `inert` string is the admission — "Recorded only — the app doesn't track traits added to an eidolon's unarmed attacks. Note in your eidolon's notes WHICH attack (primary or secondary) you chose; Grasping Limbs later needs the attack that gained grapple" — and grep confirms `advanced-weaponry`/`advancedWeaponry` appear nowhere under src/. The companion harness limit explains the empty diff but establishes nothing, and the surface plainly exists: deriveEidolon in src/rules/companions.ts builds attacks[0]/attacks[1] each with a `traits: string[]` line, and COMPANION_MODS already lets an owner feat reach them (Ranged Combatant's grantedStrikes, Dual Energy Heart's evoNote, and Pushing Attack's note that NAMES the chosen attack from the player's own answer). Same shape, same file, one entry short. A versatile pick additionally has to make that damage type selectable on the attack, which is the whole mechanical content of three of the eight options. This is the Ranged Combatant ruling again — a companion feat whose entire content is a picker whose answer the eidolon never receives.

defects.name: Aeonbound
defects.detail: Only the resource is built; both mechanical clauses are absent. The record carries exactly one authored field — `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` — and that is the sole entry for `aeonbound` in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (verified by scanning the file; there is no second row). The per-day pip is correctly owed and correctly delivered. MISSING 1 — the degree shift. "When someone rolls a failure or a critical failure on a check to Treat your Wounds, you can... increase the degree of success by one step" is a textbook `degreeShifts` entry (`shift: 'oneBetter'`, `when: 'on a check to Treat your Wounds'`, `skills:['medicine']`, `actions:['treat-wounds']`), which per Q2 would produce both surfaces — a Medicine star and a Treat Wounds marker — from one authored entry. The record has no `degreeShifts` field at all, so neither surface exists, and Q15 does not exempt it (that governs crit-SUCCESS triggers; this fires on a failure). Note it must cover BOTH entry degrees, failure and critical failure — the Dragon's Presence omission from Round 10. MISSING 2 — the toolkit waiver. "You and your allies can Treat your Wounds without a healer's toolkit" gets no `note`, no `situational`, and the record appears in no registry (`registries: []`), so the sheet says nothing. Ruling D governs its placement (a clause with no stat row of its own marks the thing it modifies — the Magic Hands/Treat Wounds shape), and Principle A means the ally-facing half still owes an indication on the record it modifies rather than nothing. Wording must keep the narrow scope: it waives the kit only for treating THIS character's wounds. The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and the app asks nothing. The `forced-placement` limit affects only whether this host is offered the feat, not any of the above.

defects.name: Aerial Boomerang
defects.detail: The impulse does reach the actions list (sheetDiff inserts "Aerial Boomerang" at actions[0], with its 2-action cost and its air/impulse/kineticist/primal traits), but the three numbers the player reads off that entry are gone from the app's own text, and I confirmed this is real damage rather than a truncated evidence pack: public/core-descriptions.json stores "races away from you in a . Each creature in the area takes damage with a save against your class DC." The pristine archive record (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-4206.json) reads "in a 60-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 2d4 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC." So the AREA (60-foot line), the DAMAGE (2d4 slashing) and the SAVE (basic Reflex) were all stripped at import — the signature of the @Template/@Damage/@Check cleaner deleting the value along with the markup. The entry therefore prints an impulse with no area, no dice and no save name, and the heightening line "Level (+2) The damage increases by 1d4" has no base to build on, so a level-20 kineticist who should read 11d4 reads nothing. Two further gaps, both smaller: the record carries no scaling field, so even with the base restored the entry would print the 1st-level line and leave the +1d4-per-2-levels arithmetic to the player; and the 1-action concentrate RETURN action gets no entry of its own (only one action row was added), with its requirements — line of effect to the boomerang, within 60 feet of it — living only in the prose. The record has no entry in effect-backfill.json at all. Nothing else is owed: the damage to creatures in the area and the whirling square land on enemies and the battlefield, the until-end-of-next-turn duration is a Q1 non-implementation, and the class DC already has its own row so no specialStatistic is due. The builder correctly asks nothing.

defects.name: Ageless Spirit
defects.detail: The record delivers NOTHING on either half. core.json feats/ageless-spirit carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `choice`, no daily choice, no skill grant — and the evidence agrees (`declared: []`, `presentsChoices: []`, `sheetDiff: []`, `silentOnBothHalves: true`, no harnessLimits). Builder/daily half: "During your daily preparations… gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice" is never asked, in the builder OR at Daily preparations. Sheet half: "This proficiency lasts until you prepare again" — no skill row ever moves and nothing is sourced to the feat. The lane is built and the template already exists: its twin `ancient-memories` (ghoran, identical text) carries `choice {flag:'ancientMemoriesSkill', prompt:'Skill remembered from a past life', kind:'skills', daily:true, note:'Trained in this skill until your next daily preparations…'}`. ⚠ Two caveats for whoever authors it: (a) `askedAtDailyPrep` (src/rules/derive.ts:975) deliberately excludes `kind:'skills'` from the Rest sheet, so copying that shape asks the question in the BUILDER, not at daily prep as Q23 requires — the code comment admits "Ancient Memories is the one record in that state today"; (b) `dailyChoiceGrants` (derive.ts:1365) only reads `options[].grant`, so a `kind:'skills'` daily answer grants no rank at all — the twin's answer is prose-only, so copying it would leave the sheet half still dead. The third clause ("you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option") has no lane — the twin carries it as note text only.

defects.name: Ancestral Linguistics
defects.detail: The record delivers nothing at all, on either half. core.json carries only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `choice`, no `dailyChoices`, no `languageChoices`, no `passiveEffects.grantsLanguages`. registries is empty, no src file mentions the id, sheetDiff is empty and the builder renders zero pickers (crossChecks.silentOnBothHalves = true, and no harnessLimit excuses it: the harness did NOT flag `daily-choice`, because there is no daily choice on the record to flag). BUILDER half: 58 feats carry `choice.daily`; this is not one, so the language pick is asked NOWHERE — not in the builder (which is correct per Q23) and not at Daily preparations (dailyChoicesFor walks ownedDailyChoiceRecords looking for `choice.daily`, finds nothing here). The two-tier legal list the text specifies (every common language, plus any other language you have access to) therefore does not exist either. SHEET half: no language ever reaches the languages list, so the 'you know this language until you prepare again' temporary marking and the clear-and-re-pick at the next preparation have nothing to attach to; and the 'can't be used as a prerequisite for a permanent character option' exclusion is moot because no grant is ever made. A 1st-level elf ancestry feat that is completely inert.

defects.name: Ancestral Longevity
defects.detail: Completely inert, same shape as Ancestral Linguistics. core.json carries no `choice`, no `dailyChoices`, no `trainedSkillChoice`; FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS (src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts) has no 'ancestral-longevity' key — its near-twin 'ancient-memories' at line 29 does; registries is empty; sheetDiff is empty; the builder renders zero pickers; crossChecks.silentOnBothHalves = true with no harnessLimit. BUILDER half: the daily skill pick is asked nowhere. It cannot be asked at Daily preparations (dailyChoicesFor only reaches records with `choice.daily`), and it is not asked in the builder either, so the 'one skill of your choice' pick, the skippable 'you CAN', and the re-ask every day are all absent. SHEET half: no skill row ever moves, so the trained rank, its recomputed modifier, the 'lasts until you prepare again' marking, and the two prerequisite exclusions (not a base for a skill increase, not a prerequisite for a permanent option) are all undelivered. ⚠ Worth the owner's attention as a family: the follow-up Expert Longevity DOES carry a `choice`, so the record it is defined against grants nothing for it to upgrade.

defects.name: Animal Senses
defects.detail: What works: the effectChoice picker ("Choose a sense from your inherent animal") offers exactly the three printed options and the answer is READ — picking scent moves defenses.senses[1].name/.range/.acuity to scent / 30 / imprecise, so the sense shape prints completely. Four defects around it. (1) BUILDER, spurious duplicate: the record also carries a top-level `choice` (flag `animalSenses`, prompt stored literally as "Prompt") which the builder renders as a SECOND dropdown for the same question (Builder.tsx:1817 renderChoice, key `1:ancestry:0`), and its answer is read by nothing — no occurrence of `animalSenses` anywhere in src/, and featChoices[<slot>] has no reader for this flag. Verdict echo-only with silentDefault: the player answers the sense question twice, one answer is inert. Exemplar Dedication's precedent applies — delete it, or make it the per-taking store (see 3). (2) BUILDER, missing gate: "You must have low-light vision before you can gain darkvision with this feat" is enforced nowhere. EffectChoice options (types.ts:1332) have no gate/disabled/reason field, and the picker (Builder.tsx:1974) renders every option live, so the harness's human fighter — normal vision — was offered Darkvision as a live pick. This is the Q9 half (Manifold Modifications shape), not the Q27 display half. (3) BOTH HALVES, repeat clause broken: maxTakable:null → maxTakes()=Infinity, so the feat CAN be taken again, but the working answer is stored at `animal-senses:sense` — one key per RECORD (build.ts:3505 `build.effectChoices[`${recordId}:${ch.id}`]`) — so the second taking cannot record a different sense and the sheet can never accumulate two. Note the inert picker in (1) is the one keyed per slot. (4) SHEET, Q13 not delivered: senses are a Map keyed by sense name (derive.ts:2029 addSense) with no supersede rule, and both DetailsTab and VitalsRail print every entry, so a low-light ancestry plus this feat's darkvision lists Low-light vision AND Darkvision side by side. NOT a defect: the "inherent animal typically has that sense" restriction is unfilterable by design — the beastkin heritage stores `inherentAnimal` as free text and its own note says the feats let you pick the sense — and the picker prompt does name the inherent animal. harnessLimits: forced-placement (host lacked the beastkin heritage), which explains eligibleHosts=[] only.

defects.name: Aquatic Elf Warrior
defects.detail: Two defects, both on the sheet half. (1) The proficiency remap is authored as a FLAT rank instead of mirroring the simple category: featGrantsAuto.ts:34 has weaponFamiliarity {weapons:[crossbow, heavy-crossbow, dagger, longspear, spear, trident], rank:'trained'}. The text says to treat the martial ones AS SIMPLE WEAPONS, i.e. use the character's own simple-weapon rank, and 11 classes have simple > martial at high level (cleric/druid/witch/sorcerer/oracle/animist/psychic/summoner/kineticist expert; alchemist/monk master). Measured by building the characters: a level-20 elf CLERIC (simple expert, martial untrained) wielding a trident prints +22/+17/+12 at rank trained where the feat entitles them to expert, +24; an elf MONK (simple master) also prints +22 where master gives +26. maxRank keeps it from ever lowering a rank, so Q10 is satisfied — it just under-delivers by 2 to 4 on the attack row. The app already has the exact right shape and uses it elsewhere: mirrorCategory:'simple' (jotunborn-weapon-familiarity, advanced-monastic-weaponry, explosive-savant). (2) "You don't take a -2 circumstance penalty to melee slashing or bludgeoning attacks while underwater" has no surface at all: the feat id appears in no entry of situationalBonuses.ts (registries list only featGrantsAuto), so no melee Strike row carries a `*` for it. The lane exists and is live — situationalBonuses supports {kind:'strikeAttack'} and MainTab.tsx:460 renders the star per strike instance — it is simply unauthored. (Underwater Marauder carries nothing for the same clause either, so this is a small family, not a one-off.) Builder half correct: the feat asks nothing and no picker was rendered.

defects.name: Aqueous Dragonblood
defects.detail: Only the base swim Speed arrives; three of the four clauses are unbuilt and the one picker is dead. (1) The branch "if you already have a base swim Speed, it increases by 5 feet" never fires — measured: a character holding Wavetouched Paragon (swim 15) who then takes Aqueous Dragonblood still shows swim 15, where the text gives 20. The record carries only speeds:{swim:15} and speeds are combined by max, not by the printed +5. (2) The builder's picker is the same defect from the other side: `choice` {flag:'choice', prompt:'Choose an option', options Yes / No} storing existing-swim-speed / no-swim-speed, answered both ways with nothing moving (verdict echo-only, silentDefault true) — those two values appear nowhere in src/. It is also a phantom question in the Round-5 / Exemplar Dedication sense: the app can read whether the character already has a base swim Speed, so this should be computed rather than asked, and the prompt "Choose an option" tells the player nothing. (3) "you take only a -1 circumstance melee penalty to slashing or bludgeoning attacks that pass through water (instead of -2)" has no situational entry — the feat id is in no registry at all — so no melee Strike row carries the `*`, though the {kind:'strikeAttack'} star lane is live (MainTab.tsx:460). (4) "hold your breath underwater for 10 minutes" has no `note`, so it is readable only in the raw description. The draconic-exemplar narrowing is inert for a different reason and I am not counting it as this feat's defect: the choiceOptionLimits lane exists (derive.ts:1246 effectiveChoiceLimits / narrowChoiceOptions) but NO record in the app offers a draconic-exemplar pick and the 44 draconicExemplar records are name-only stubs with no swim data — there is nothing to filter yet.

defects.name: Arcane Fists
defects.detail: Three of the four sheet clauses reach nothing; `sheetDiff` is `[]` with no harnessLimits, and the record carries only critSpec/critSpecLevel/critSpecWeapons. Built a magus and read deriveStrikes with and without the feat — the Fist row is identical in both: damage "1d4+1 B", traits [agile,finesse,nonlethal,unarmed]. (1) "The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6" — not applied. derive.ts:3810 hardcodes the d4→d6 upgrade to powerful-fist / warrior-automaton / warrior-jotunborn only; the general lane is `unarmedTraits` with `setDie` (24 feats use unarmedTraits today, e.g. syu-tak-nwas-deadly-hair with match+stepDie), and this record carries none. (2) "Your unarmed attacks gain the arcane trait, making them magical" — no trait added and no magical flag; `unarmedTraits:[{add:['arcane']}]` is exactly the shape and is unused. (3) "You don't take the normal −2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack" — no `note`, no `situational`; `registries` is empty and grep finds no arcane-fists in src/, so the clause exists nowhere the player can read it on the strike row (Ruling D / the textNumbers pack even extracts "−2 circumstance" from the text). Delivered: the crit-spec clause — critSpecSources gains `{level:5, weapons:{groups:['brawling']}}` from the feat and matches both brawling unarmed attacks and brawling weapons via group. "This critical specialization effect uses your spell DC instead of your class DC" has nothing to bind to, since CRIT_SPEC prose prints no DC at all ("must succeed at a Fortitude save"), which is a display gap rather than a wrong number.

defects.name: Armor in Earth
defects.detail: Only the grantsAction half arrives — the sheetDiff shows the impulse entering the action list (actions[0] 'Armor in Earth') and nothing else. Everything the stone armour does is absent: there is NO mode for this feat anywhere (no entry in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, no hit for 'armor-in-earth' in src/, scripts/data/ or effect-backfill.json; the record itself carries zero mechanical fields). So there is no toggle, no Dismiss, no self-exclusion, no 10-minute duration text, no AC Bonus +4, no Dex Cap +1, no Check Penalty −2, no Speed Penalty −10 ft, no Str 3 / Bulk 1 / group plate, no armour specialization, no suppression-and-replication of the worn armour's runes, no 'uses your highest armour proficiency', and no 3rd-level rewrite to heavy / +5 / bulwark. The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and renders no picker, and the level-3 upgrade is not rendered as a second pick. This is a skipped record rather than a missing capability: the two sibling impulses of identical shape ARE authored as display-only modes carrying the full statistics in their note — `metal-carapace` and `hardwood-armor` in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, both with duration "10 minutes (Dismissible; using the impulse again ends the old one)" and both ending "The app cannot swap armor statistics automatically — unequip your worn armor while this is active." Judged against that precedent, the mode + full-text note is squarely in lane and owed; only the automatic armour-statistic SWAP (and with it the Dex-cap/armour-spec/rune-replication numbers) is the part the app has already conceded it has no route for, so that sub-half is closer to no_lane than to a build task.

defects.name: As in Life, So in Death
defects.detail: Both halves miss a different requirement, and the grant itself is the only thing delivered (Adopted Ancestry is owned, level 1, grantedBy = as-in-life-so-in-death, no slot charged). BUILDER: the feat's whole point is "You can choose any ancestry", overriding Adopted Ancestry's common-ancestry restriction. The rendered picker offers exactly the 8 common ancestries — Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Human, Leshy, Orc (optionCount 8, optionsTruncated 0) — so a skeleton who was a kobold, hobgoblin or tengu in life cannot record it. Nothing in the app can widen a granted feat's list (FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE only pins a fixed answer). The answer is also echo-only in a way that matters: featSlots.ts:87-99 gates ancestry-feat slots on build.ancestryId, a versatile heritage's id, `extraAncestryFeatTraits` and `universal-ancestry`, and never reads the adopted-ancestry pick — so Adopted Ancestry's own effect (select that ancestry's feats when you gain an ancestry feat) is not live, which Principle G requires of a grant. SHEET: the auto-success clause — "you do not have to attempt Deception checks against a creature's Perception DC to successfully Impersonate yourself as a member of that ancestry" — plus its two carve-outs (no protection against divination; no benefit against a creature actively attempting Perception) reach nothing. registries lists only featFeatGrants, the record carries no `situational` and no `note`, and the diff shows no situational entry. This is not a capability gap: eight sibling feats carry precisely this shape (childlike-plant +4 "to Impersonate a human version of yourself", round-ears, sinister-appearance, feathered-cloak…), and `on:'action'` markers already exist for hide/sneak/avoid-notice, so the Impersonate marker Q8 asks for is one row of data.

defects.name: Athamaru Lore
defects.detail: Two of the four clauses are undelivered. (1) REDUNDANT FALLBACK, builder half — `featGrantsAuto.ts:60` carries `{ skills: { athletics: 'trained', nature: 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true`, unlike its twin automaton-lore on the next line. Measured on a druid/athamaru already trained in Athletics and Nature: `character.skillFallbacks` is null, `pickersFor` renders nothing, and the trained-skill set with the feat is byte-identical to the set without it. The player is never asked for a replacement and simply loses both grants — the text's "you instead become trained in a skill of your choice" is silently swallowed, and it should be able to fire twice. (2) THE LORE ITSELF, sheet half — `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS` grants `additional-lore` (it does appear on the sheet as a bonus feat with `grantedBy: athamaru-lore`), but no ATHAMARU LORE skill ever appears. Additional Lore's subject lives in `FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['additional-lore'] = { loreChoices: 1 }`, and Builder.tsx:1896 renders that Lore text box only for the feat PICKED IN A SLOT — never for a granted bonus feat — so `featLoreChoices['additional-lore:0']` is never written and build.ts:3435 trains nothing. The fix the sibling records already use is a `'lore:athamaru': 'trained'` entry on this feat (compare `anadi-lore`, `android-lore`, `nagaji-lore`), which would also satisfy the builder requirement that the subject arrive pre-filled rather than asked. Correct today: Athletics and Nature both read trained. Secondary and systemic rather than specific to this feat — the skill breakdown's timeline names a background or class source but never a feat, so neither grant says where it came from.

defects.name: Athamaru Weapon Familiarity
defects.detail: The first and primary clause — the martial-to-simple proficiency remap — has no field on the record at all and no registry entry (`registries: []`; every other ancestry familiarity feat carries `weaponFamiliarity`, e.g. `azarketi-weapon-familiarity`, `centaur-weapon-familiarity`, `conrasu-weapon-familiarity` in featGrantsAuto.ts). Measured directly: a wizard/athamaru (trained simple, untrained martial) holding a Trident rolls +2/-3/-8 at rank `untrained` both WITH and WITHOUT the feat, at level 1 and at level 5. Nothing remaps, so nothing can name the feat in the breakdown either. The named set that should be remapped is athamaru-trait weapons plus crossbow, heavy crossbow, longspear, spear, trident, restricted to the martial members and applied only where it improves the rank (Q10). The empty `sheetDiff` in the pack is not the evidence for this — the reference host owns no weapon — the direct build is. The SECOND clause is correct and needs no change: `critSpec: true`, `critSpecLevel: 5`, `critSpecWeapons: { traits: ['athamaru'], bases: ['crossbow','heavy-crossbow','longspear','spear','trident'] }`, and `critSpecSources` filters `s.level <= c.level`. Measured: the Trident shows no crit spec at level 1 and shows it at level 5, and the set is not narrowed to martial, matching the sentence.

defects.name: Automaton Lore
defects.detail: Two clauses land and two do not. CORRECT: Arcana and Crafting read trained; and the redundancy fallback is genuinely built (`featGrantsAuto.ts:61` carries `redundantFallback: true`) — measured on a wizard/automaton trained in both from class, it renders TWO pickers ("Already trained in arcana — replacement skill", "Already trained in crafting — replacement skill"), each answer trains its skill (answering medicine + survival produced exactly two extra trained skills), and Builder.tsx:1878 already greys options the character is trained in with a reason, per Q27. MISSING (sheet): no AUTOMATON LORE skill ever appears. Additional Lore is granted as a bonus feat with `grantedBy: automaton-lore`, but its subject lives in `FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['additional-lore'] = { loreChoices: 1 }` and Builder.tsx:1896 renders that Lore box only for a slot-PICKED feat, never a granted one, so `featLoreChoices` is never written and no Lore is trained — same shape as Athamaru Lore; the sibling records solve it with a `'lore:automaton': 'trained'` entry, which also keeps the subject unaskable as the text requires. MISSING (builder + sheet): the whole **Enhancement** clause. No picker anywhere asks "Arcana or Crafting" — the only pickers this feat renders are the two fallbacks — and no rank moves: measured at level 9 with Lesser Augmentation pointed at automaton-lore, Arcana and Crafting both stay trained. The clause needs a two-option picker with BOTH options always live (Q21: an option the character is already expert in is the one that becomes master) and a set/upgrade that reads the rank held at the time, never a flat set to expert.

defects.name: Bamboo and Silt Repose
defects.detail: Both printed clauses are undelivered — the feat is entirely inert. The record in core.json carries only id/name/level/category/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId: no `note`, no `situational`, and `registries: []` (it appears in none of the eight id-keyed registries). Nothing is marked on the Speed row and nothing on Stride, so a player who takes it sees the feat's name and nothing else. `silentOnBothHalves` here is genuine: no harness limit applies, the host is a native yaksha, and the builder correctly asks nothing (the feat names its own terrain types). The app has the lane and uses it for the identical sentence elsewhere — situationalBonuses.ts:3444 `'unimpeded-journey': [{ on: 'action', id: 'stride', note: 'Unimpeded Journey: you ignore the effects of difficult terrain, and treat greater difficult terrain as difficult terrain.' }]`, with the same shape at 3437 rite-of-passage, 3439 stonestep-shisk, 3447 wildwood-halfling and 3408 water-dancer. So this is one missing authored entry, and it must carry BOTH halves plus both qualifiers — non-magical only, and only light undergrowth / shallow bogs, mud and water — since carrying just the "ignore" half is the documented Dragon's Presence failure mode.

defects.name: Beast Trainer
defects.detail: The builder half is right — the picker offers EXACTLY Pet and Train Animal, both live, no repeats. The answer reaches nothing: `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS['beast-trainer'] = ['train-animal']` (src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:73) is a flat unconditional map, and `grantedFeatByChoice` is honoured for BACKGROUNDS only (`bg?.grantedFeatByChoice`, src/rules/build.ts:430). Measured by rebuilding an orc fighter three ways: choice=pet → granted ['train-animal'], no companion; choice=train-animal → ['train-animal']; unanswered → ['train-animal']. So a player who picks Pet is silently given Train Animal instead — a missing grant AND a spurious one in the same act, and the Pet branch's whole point (a Tiny minion on the Companions tab) never appears even though the target is ready to receive it: `companionGrants.ts:81` already carries `'pet': {kind:'familiar', abilityBudget:2}`. This is Round 5's worked shape (Ranged Combatant) exactly — an answer that changes only the label. The Nature grant is correct (untrained→trained, attributed) and, correctly per the printed text, no redundancy fallback is invented for it.

defects.name: Beastbrood
defects.detail: Every sheet lane works when the feat is forced onto a character — Society untrained→trained, Courtly Graces owned (`grantedBy: beastbrood`, no slot) with both of its situational bonuses reaching Deception and Diplomacy, and the redundancy fallback firing only when another source already trains Society (measured with the Pathfinder Hopeful and Trade Consortium Underling backgrounds; answering it trains the chosen skill). But NO CHARACTER CAN TAKE IT. I brute-forced every ancestry × every legal heritage at level 20 over the ancestry/general/skill slots: Beastbrood is offered by no host, while Battleblooded, Beast Trainer, Bargain Hunter and Battle Medicine all resolve to one. Cause: the versatile-heritage gate at src/rules/featSlots.ts:91 tests `f.traits.includes(her.id)`, and the Tiefling heritage's id is `aon-tiefling` while its trait is `tiefling`. Nephilim passes only because its id and trait are the same string. ⚠ This is not one feat: six versatile heritages have an id that is not among their traits — aon-tiefling (16 feats), aon-aasimar (20), aon-aphorite, aon-ganzi, aon-ifrit and hungerseed (trait `oni`) — and each adds ZERO ancestry feats (measured: human bare 49 eligible, +nephilim 100, +aon-tiefling 49, +aon-aasimar 49). Legacy edition is not the explanation: legacy-era content is hidden only when the per-character "Hide legacy data" toggle is on. The fix is to match the heritage's TRAITS as well as its id.

defects.name: Blessing of the Five
defects.detail: Delivered: the ability reaches the actions list at 3 actions (sheetDiff actions[0]), its stored description carries the Frequency line, the full effect text, the five-excluded-creatures sentence and the whole alternative revival use (with ref-links to Heal, The Godclaw and Doomed 1), and `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` produces the single daily pip (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]) — one use covering both halves of the ability, correctly. Missing: the Heal itself. The record carries NO `innateSpells`, so the spell is never castable or reachable from the ability and the rank the whole ability turns on — (ceil(level/2))−1, i.e. rank 4 at 10th, rank 9 at 19th — is printed NOWHERE on the sheet; the player must compute it by hand every level. With no grant there is also nothing for the "up to five creatures remain unaffected" clause to attach to, so the `spellNotes` requirement (principle N2 — write the feat's text into the granted spell's description under the feat's name) fails with it. This is a data omission, not a lane gap, and its own family proves it: three sibling Hellknight-order records carry exactly the fields needed — `devil-allies` has innateSpells with `heightenAt` steps plus a spellNote, `righteous-resistance` has innateSpells + spellNote, `locate-lawbreakers` has innateSpells with usesPerDay. `heightenAt {level, rank}[]` (types.ts:1521, applied at build.ts:4673) can express the −1 formula as explicit steps (3→1, 5→2, … 19→9). Note when authoring: the 3-action version and the base rank 0 at levels 1–2 both need saying, and the daily use should not be double-counted between `usesPerDay` and the existing `limitedUses`.

defects.name: Bone Magic
defects.detail: Two builder defects and one sheet defect. BUILDER (1) — the Special clause "Choose when you gain this feat whether your innate spells are primal or occult" is NEVER ASKED. `builder.declared` is only `registry.FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS`; the record carries no `choice` and no `effectChoices`, so there is no second picker at all (not a dead picker — an absent one). BUILDER (2) — the cantrip list is NARROWER than the feat's own restriction. featCantripGrants.ts:24 hardcodes 33 options, but the union of the occult and primal cantrip lists in core.json is 49 common, current-edition cantrips. Never offered: musical-accompaniment, deep-breath, slashing-gust, glass-shield, tremor-signs, eat-fire, illuminate, detect-metal, needle-darts, draw-moisture, rousing-splash, root-reading, take-root, timber, live-wire, glamorize — and the app itself lists every one of those under `awakened-magic` (primal) or `awakened-jewel` (occult), so this is a stale list rather than a ruling. Q9/Q21 cannot justify the omission: none of the 16 is illegal or wasted. SHEET — because the tradition is never asked, the innate entry's tradition falls back to the SPELL's first tradition (build.ts:4705, `g.tradition ?? spells[id].traditions[0]`), so picking Electric Arc (traditions [arcane, primal]) labels the character's innate casting ARCANE, a tradition this feat never allows (Q12 — the sheet must not say something false about the spell); and the downstream lizardfolk feat `bone-investiture`, whose prerequisite is Bone Magic, hardcodes `tradition:'primal'` on its Dinosaur Form grant instead of following the answer, which is exactly the clause "this choice applies to all innate spells you gain from lizardfolk ancestry feats that have Bone Magic as a prerequisite". Delivered correctly: the cantrip picker's answer IS read (verdict read, reaches spellcasting[innate-casting].cantrips), it is at-will with no use pips, and cantrips auto-heighten to ceil(level/2) (SpellsTab.tsx:1267). The empty sheetDiff is the unanswered-picker shape, not a dead grant.

defects.name: Breath of the Dragon
defects.detail: Nothing but the raw sentence is delivered. The action row exists only because the record has `actionCost {actions:2}` (sheetDiff actions[0]); storedFields carry no grantsActions, no specialStatistic, no damage scaling, no traits beyond dragonblood/magical, and registries is empty. Four requirements unmet on the SHEET half: (1) shape, damage type and save are printed as the generic 'match those of your draconic exemplar (see above)' — the app's own draconicExemplar collection is 44 name-only stubs (id/name/aonId, no descriptions, no shape/damage/save columns), so the lookup table the '(see above)' points at does not exist here; (2) the DC is never printed as a number, although the lane that fits it exactly is built — `specialStatistic` with `basis: {higherOfClassDcOrSpellDc}`, the same shape as the chronoskimmer and deviation DCs (docs/mechanic-lanes.md §K, 11 records); (3) no level scaling — the popup says 1d4 to a 19th-level character who should read 10d4; (4) no resolved damage-type trait, so the player cannot tell whether a target's resistance bites. BUILDER half: the answer this feat is supposed to consume is recorded nowhere — grep finds no draconic-exemplar pick on any record (the dragonblood heritage grants only the trait and a fear degreeShift; the lineage feats ask only their skill fallbacks). The app's own precedent for this is `draconic-resistance`, which asks its consumer-side question outright ('Choose the damage type associated with your draconic exemplar', effectChoices with a per-option resistance grant) — Breath of the Dragon asks nothing and reads nothing. CORRECT as-is: no use pip for the 1d4-round recharge (O2). MINOR display: the description still carries the AoN chrome trailer 'Breath of the Dragon leads to… Debilitating Breath, Energize Bite, …' (the leading 'Source … pg. 45' header is handled by AstRenderer's meta block).

defects.name: Breath of the Dragon (Dragonblood)
defects.detail: Same unbuilt record as its general-feat sibling, and worse in one respect. THE TEXT ITSELF HAS LOST BOTH AREA VALUES: public/core-descriptions.json feats/breath-of-the-dragon-dragonblood reads 'you can exhale a torrent of energy in a or a , dealing 1d4 damage' — the sibling record prints 'a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line'. Since the record carries no area field either, the ancestry version — the one a dragonblood character actually takes — shows an area of nothing at all, and the values have to be recovered from the source (an import defect in the description, not a rendering one). Everything else matches the sibling: storedFields hold only rarity/level/category/actionCost/aonId, registries empty, so the shape, damage type and save stay the generic 'match those of your draconic exemplar' sentence; the 'higher of your class DC or spell DC' is never printed as a number although the `specialStatistic` lane with `basis:{higherOfClassDcOrSpellDc}` exists for exactly that shape; the damage never scales past the printed 1d4; and the action's trait list carries no resolved damage-type trait. BUILDER half: the pick it is supposed to read does not exist anywhere in the app (no draconic-exemplar choice on the dragonblood heritage or any lineage feat; core.json's 44 draconicExemplar records are name-only stubs), so the feat correctly presents no picker of its own and correspondingly has no answer to resolve. The 1d4-round recharge needs only its sentence (O2) and has it. Harness note: `forced-placement` — no rendered slot offered this dragonblood ancestry feat to the fighter/human host, so eligibility is unevidenced either way; the sheet half was still measured and the defects above are read off the record and its own description.

defects.name: Aquatic Eyes
defects.detail: The feat grants DARKVISION to every character on the FIRST taking, and lists it beside low-light vision. Observed by building the characters: a level-20 human (ancestry vision 'normal') with Aquatic Eyes shows senses "normal, low-light-vision, darkvision"; an elf shows "low-light-vision, darkvision". The cause is a double authoring — effect-backfill.json carries TWO rows for this id, one writing conditionalSenses [{ifPresent:'low-light-vision', base:low-light-vision, upgraded:darkvision}] (line 9523) and a second writing a flat senses:[{name:'low-light-vision'}] (line 68227) — and derive.ts:2129-2138 evaluates "already have" against the senses gathered SO FAR plus the ancestry's vision. The flat grant lands first, so the feat satisfies its own "if your ancestry already has low-light vision" test and upgrades itself. Two things are wrong at once: darkvision is granted where the text conditions it on the ancestry, and both senses are shown where Q13 rules that only darkvision is displayed when it supersedes low-light. Fix is one deletion (drop the flat `senses` backfill row); the conditionalSenses lane alone is already correct and tested (test/fix-campaign.test.ts 'conditional sense upgrades'). Builder half also fails, differently: maxTakable:2 lets the feat be taken a second time UNCONDITIONALLY, where the Special gates the repeat on "your ancestry has neither low-light vision nor darkvision" (Q9 — an illegal second taking should not be offered), and "You can't retrain out of this feat" is modelled nowhere. Note the second taking is moot today anyway, since the first already hands out darkvision.

defects.name: Arcane Dragonblood
defects.detail: The "instead" in "If you would automatically become trained in Arcana …, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice" is not implemented, so the feat OVER-GRANTS. Measured by building characters: a dragonblood fighter (Arcana untrained) taking the feat and answering the effectChoice with Society ends up {arcana:trained, society:trained} — two skills where the text grants one. featGrantsAuto.ts:55 reads `'arcane-dragonblood': { skills: { arcana: 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true` (the flag ~60 sibling entries carry and build.ts:3384 reads), so `character.skillFallbacks` is null on every host and the effectChoices picker is rendered and applied UNCONDITIONALLY rather than only when another source trains Arcana. Builder half, second defect: the record declares TWO pickers for this one clause. `record.choice {flag:'arcaneDragonbloodFallback', kind:'skills'}` renders a "Replacement skill" list of 12 options that are the skills the host is ALREADY trained in ("Arcana (E), Crafting (E), … Thievery (T)") — `kind:'skills'` resolves through trainedSkillOptions, i.e. Assurance's "pick a skill you're trained in", which is the exact inverse of "become trained in a skill" — and its answer is consumed by nothing (verdict echo-only, `answerDeadButSheetMoves`). Per Q20 that is not acceptable label-only: the app plainly models the consequence (the other picker moves skills.*), so a dead picker here is a defect, and no grep in src/ finds `arcaneDragonbloodFallback` anywhere. Delivered correctly: Arcana trained, and the Arcane Sense grant (featFeatGrants.ts:64) lands with its own innate Detect Magic and `grantedBy:'arcane-dragonblood'`. Also unbuilt, secondary: "if you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an arcane dragon" — the only exemplar picker in src/ is the sorcerer Draconic bloodline's `dragonChoice` (builder/shared.tsx:2964), which offers all four traditions to a character holding this feat, and no picker at all consumes the 44-entry `draconicExemplar` collection, so the Q9 filter has nothing to attach to for a non-sorcerer.

defects.name: Arcane Eye
defects.detail: See the Unseen is ENHANCEMENT-ONLY text ("**Enhancement** … You can cast See the Unseen as an arcane innate spell once per hour"), but the record grants it flatly: `innateSpells:[{spellId:'see-the-unseen',tradition:'arcane'}]`, and the sheetDiff confirms a 1st-level taker gets `spellcasting[innate-casting].repertoire.2[0]='see-the-unseen'` plus `grantedSpells[0]`. Every other automaton Enhancement feat authors only its BASE benefit (automaton-armament = the strike, energy-beam = the beam, reinforced-chassis = the action, magical-resistance = resistance 5) and leaves the Enhancement as prose behind Lesser/Greater Augmentation's picker — this one is the outlier, so a 1st-level automaton reads an innate spell they cannot cast, and nothing on the record marks the clause as not-yet-held. Second, the frequency is wrong: the grant carries neither `usesPerDay` nor `usesPer`, so build.ts:4699-4700 defaults it and SpellsTab prints "rank 2 · 1/day · from Arcane Eye". The hourly lane exists and is in use — feats/primal-proportions carries `usesPer:'hour'` and innateCadence renders it — so "once per hour" is authorable and simply absent; as printed the use returns at daily preparations instead. Delivered correctly: darkvision (`senses:[{name:'darkvision'}]`) and the arcane tradition/source line on the spell card. One further display defect: deriveDefenses keys senses by name and never supersedes, so an automaton (ancestry vision = low-light-vision, which is this feat's own prerequisite) reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision" — Q13 says show only darkvision.

defects.name: Awakened Jewel
defects.detail: CONFIRMED BY BUILDING THE CHARACTER: an OCCULT grant is filed under an ARCANE (or divine) innate entry. The pick-a-cantrip path pushes `{spellId: chosen}` with no tradition (build.ts:4651), and the single pooled 'innate-casting' entry takes its tradition from the majority of `content.spells[id].traditions[0]` (build.ts:4703-4706). Every one of the 28 options has traditions[0] of arcane or divine — NOT ONE resolves to occult. Built a level-20 sarangay fighter: bullhorn → tradition 'arcane', warp-step → 'arcane', forbidding-ward → 'divine'. SpellsTab.tsx:1849 prints exactly that as the section header — 'innate spells (Arcane)' — which is exemplar 10's pooled-header defect verbatim, and it is what the harness saw as `stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].tradition` moving between two answers. `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` already exists and is honoured; `CantripPickSpec` has no field to set it. ALSO MISSING (sheet): (1) 'A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up' does not happen for an innate-only character — SpellsTab.tsx:1195 computes `maxRank` from prepared/spontaneous entries plus focus ONLY, so with no class casting it is 0 and the detail view shows the cantrip frozen at base rank, while a main pool correctly labels 'at will · heightened to 10th' (SpellsTab.tsx:1268/1299). (2) The head-gem possession condition is written nowhere: no `spellNotes` on the record, and `SpellNote.spellId` (types.ts:338) names a FIXED spell, so the N2/Q7 lane cannot attach a note to whichever cantrip the player picked. ALSO MISSING (builder): the option list is a frozen Foundry snapshot rather than the occult cantrip list — 6 COMMON occult cantrips the app ships and shows by default are unofferable (approximate, infectious-enthusiasm, protect-companion, read-the-air, tame, wash-your-luck). Correctly excluded: ghost-sound (edition 'superseded', always hidden). CORRECT: cantrips only, one pick, permanent, and the entry reads 'at will' with no use pip (SpellsTab.tsx:1798).

defects.name: Awakened Magic
defects.detail: Same confirmed defect as Awakened Jewel, and here the text names the tradition outright ('as an primal innate spell'). Built a level-20 awakened-animal fighter: caustic-blast → innate entry tradition 'arcane', vitality-lash → 'divine'. Never primal. Cause: build.ts:4651 pushes the pick as `{spellId}` with no tradition and build.ts:4705 derives the pooled entry's tradition from `spells[id].traditions[0]`; all 34 options have a traditions[0] of arcane or divine, so NO pick can ever produce a primal entry. SpellsTab.tsx:1849 renders that as the header 'innate spells (Arcane)'. `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` exists and would fix it; CantripPickSpec cannot express it. ALSO MISSING (sheet): the ceil(level/2) heightening never applies to this grant — SpellsTab.tsx:1195 builds `maxRank` from prepared/spontaneous entries and focus only, so an awakened animal with no other spellcasting views the cantrip at base rank instead of 10th, while a class pool correctly prints 'at will · heightened to 10th'. ALSO MISSING (builder): the primal option list is a frozen Foundry snapshot, not the app's primal cantrip list — 4 COMMON primal cantrips the app ships and shows by default cannot be picked (approximate, healing-plaster, protect-companion, tame). Correctly excluded: acid-splash and ray-of-frost (edition 'superseded'). CORRECT: one picker only (no second question about tradition/rank/uses), cantrips only, and the entry reads 'at will' with no pip.

defects.name: Aberration Kinship
defects.detail: The innate half is right: sheetDiff adds Mindlink to the innate entry at rank 1 (its own base rank, no override asserted), tradition occult, spellSources.mindlink = "Aberration Kinship", and SpellsTab.tsx:1807 renders it as "rank 1 · 1/day · from Aberration Kinship" with a spendable pip (build.ts:4699 leaves innateUses absent because absent means the default 1/day). What is missing is the clause "but you can target only aberrations": the record carries no `spellNotes`, so nothing is written into Mindlink's description. This is the N2 lane and it is built and populated — 64 feats carry `spellNotes`, and azarketi-purification's "You can cast Cleanse Cuisine from this feat only on liquids" is the identical restriction shape, printed under the granting record's name by build.ts:3947 → spellNotesFor → SpellsTab.tsx:2155. As shipped, a player reading Mindlink from this feat sees the spell as printed and would legally target a non-aberration. Builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and nothing should be asked.

defects.name: Acrobatic Performer
defects.detail: The +1 is delivered correctly: situationalBonuses.ts:99 puts it on Acrobatics as "+1 circumstance" (right type — the printed "circumstances" is a typo) with the restriction in `when` and outside the flat total, which is Ruling B. The SUBSTITUTION is delivered nowhere. The record carries no `skillSubstitutions`, so "You can roll an Acrobatics check instead of a Performance check when using the Perform action" reaches nothing — deriveSkill/explain.ts never see it, and the Perform action never reads as rollable with Acrobatics. The lane exists and 26 feats carry it in exactly this shape (versatile-performance: use Performance instead of Diplomacy to Make an Impression; natural-medicine; sly-disarm). Worse, the single star the feat does produce reads "when you Perform, if trained in both Acrobatics and Performance" with a +1 attached, which welds the substitution's condition to the BONUS's condition: a character trained in Acrobatics but not Performance may still substitute, and the sheet tells them nothing.

defects.name: Acupuncturist
defects.detail: silentOnBothHalves with no harnessLimits, and DECIDED SCOPE does not excuse it — the lanes doc explicitly keeps "the action's EXISTENCE" as the `grantsAction` lane. The feat teaches a named downtime activity (a day of study, needles stored in healer's tools, one ally, Medicine vs a standard DC for the ALLY'S level) and the app surfaces it as an activity nowhere: the record has no `grantsActions`, there is no `acupuncturist` entry in content.actions, and SKILL_ACTIONS.medicine (skillActions.ts) has no entry for it — that list is precisely where feat-gated Medicine activities live (Battle Medicine, feat: true/featName), and the sibling downtime feat Train Animal is there under Nature. So the activity, its requirement and the ally-level DC are readable only inside the feat's own description on the Feats tab. Measured, this is the pattern rather than a one-off: all 12 downtime-trait feats carry no mechanical field at all. The ally-side +2/+1/-1 and the 1-week lockout correctly produce nothing on this sheet (Ruling F), and the four degrees are present in the feat's own description text, so the only defect is the activity's absence from the activities/skill-action surface.

defects.name: Acute Vision
defects.detail: The core grant works and the empty sheetDiff is expected: `whileActive:[{state:'rage',senses:[darkvision precise]}]` is read by activeStateGrants (derive.ts:931) and pushed into deriveDefenses' sense map (derive.ts:1991) only while classResources.rage is on, so darkvision arrives with rage and leaves with it — exactly what the text says, and the harness measured a non-raging character. Two ruled requirements are not delivered. (1) Principle C: the rage entry does not reflect the feat. Rage is a bare state toggle (VitalsRail.tsx:935-960) whose only text is the static note in classResources.ts:71 ("Raging: lasts 1 min / until the encounter ends"); nothing aggregates whileActive grants into it, so a barbarian who is not raging can see nowhere that raging will give them darkvision. (2) Q13: senses are stored in a map keyed by NAME with a best-acuity merge and no supersede step, and VitalsRail.tsx:730 prints every entry — so an elf/gnome barbarian raging reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision" where the owner ruled to show only darkvision. docs/gold-set-final.md line 270 records this as a change to shipped behaviour that has not been made; grep confirms no suppression exists. Builder half correct — nothing is asked and nothing should be.

defects.name: Adrenaline Rush
defects.detail: One of the three sheet requirements is delivered, two are not. Delivered: the Athletics star, situationalBonuses.ts:102 — "+1 status … while Raging, to lift heavy objects, Escape, or Force Open" — correct type, correct restriction, and correctly NOT fanned out to Acrobatics or the unarmed Escape. Missing: (1) "increase your encumbered and maximum Bulk limits by 2" reaches nothing. The lane exists and is read — deriveBulk (src/rules/derive.ts:4094-4136) sums feats' bulkLimitBonus into both encumberedAt (5+Str+bonus) and max (10+Str+bonus), which is exactly the two numbers this clause moves — and this record carries no such field, so a raging barbarian's Bulk thresholds are unchanged and the encumbered/overloaded state never recomputes. Note the field as it stands is unconditional (authored for Beast of Burden), so a flat bulkLimitBonus:2 would be spurious here: the clause needs the rage gate the app already has for other numbers (whileState:'rage', types.ts:630, resource 'rage' in classResources.ts:71). (2) No marker on the actions. The RecordMarker lane is live (17 entries with on:'action' in situationalBonuses.ts, e.g. black-powder-boost marking Leap) and both action records exist as 'escape' and 'force-open' in core.json, but nothing marks either for this feat, so a player reading the Escape or Force Open entry sees no sign of the +1 (Ruling D / Q2's "both"). (3) Nothing ties the feat to the Rage state: it appears in no mode — the barbarian Rage mode is cat-rage (src/rules/modes.ts:219) and carries no mention of it, and there is no modeAdjust row in scripts/data — so the mode the player toggles does not carry this feat's text (Principle B / Q11). Builder correctly asks nothing.

defects.name: Agile Shield Grip
defects.detail: grantsAction is delivered — the diff inserts "Agile Shield Grip" into the actions list as a 1-action activity, and its description carries the "**Requirements** You are wielding a shield with a shield boss or shield spikes in one hand" block plus the switch-back sentence, which satisfies Principle E. The builder half is correctly silent (the feat names no build-time choice). Everything below that is absent: (1) "You reduce your shield boss and shield spikes weapon damage die to 1d4" — no `weaponTraits`/`setDie` rider anywhere; the Strike rows for shield boss and shield spikes keep their printed die (Principle L: reach/die is a VALUE, not an annotation); (2) "your shield boss and shield spike Strikes gain the agile weapon trait" — no trait added, so the row's three attack numbers never recompute onto the agile −4/−8 progression; (3) "You can use Agile Shield Grip again to switch to a normal grip" — per Q11 this is a MODE (it can explicitly be shut down) and no mode exists: `scripts/data/toggle-modes.json` (258 modes) contains no Agile Shield Grip entry, and no registry mentions the feat (`registries: []`). Nothing in the record hints at any of it. ⚠ Note for the fix: the `weaponRider` lane can say it (`WeaponRider.setDie` + `add:['agile']`, match on the two shield weapons) but is always-on, and `ModeDef` has NO weaponTraits/setDie field today (0 of 258 modes carry one), so the toggleable form needs a small field extension — authoring the rider on the feat alone would make the reduced die unconditional, which is the text's own condition removed.

defects.name: Alchemical Assessment
defects.detail: Silent on both halves, and the builder silence is correct (the feat asks nothing). The sheet half delivers none of its only content. "When using the Crafting skill to Identify Alchemy on an alchemical item you hold, you can do so as a single action, rather than spending 10 minutes" is exactly the owner's Quick Recognition specification (Principle H — the action appears under BOTH costs with the explanation in the popup), and Identify Alchemy still shows only its native cost: src/rules/actions.ts:109 lists it as an exploration action and src/rules/skillActions.ts:294 prints `costText: "10 minutes"`, with no 1-action form and no mark from this feat. `registries: []` confirms no RECORD_MARKERS entry, so the Ruling D / Q8 marker on the modified action (carrying the two conditions — alchemical item, held) does not exist either. The record's only surface is a description cross-link (`r: [{label:'Identify Alchemy', key:'actions'}]`) on the feat's own popup, which is the reverse direction from what Ruling D asks: the mark belongs on Identify Alchemy, the thing the player is looking at when it matters. The lane exists — RECORD_MARKERS/`actionRider` already render `{on:'action', id, value, note}` rows for other records — so this is unauthored, not unbuildable. Correctly NOT reported: no `*` is owed on the Crafting row (no number moves).

defects.name: Alchemical Familiar
defects.detail: The companion-tab harness limit explains the silent diff, so I judged from source. The familiar itself is granted (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['alchemical-familiar'], a synthetic Companions-tab card), but three of the feat's four clauses fail. (1) MISSING, sheet: 'The familiar uses your Intelligence modifier to determine its Perception, Acrobatics, and Stealth modifiers' has no surface at all — FamiliarBlock (src/rules/companions.ts:576-683) has no Acrobatics or Stealth field, and its Perception is copied wholesale from the master via masterDefenses() (Wisdom + the master's proficiency), so the Int rule is neither applied nor shown, and it cannot track Int as it changes. (2) SPURIOUS, sheet: the grant is authored lockedAbilities: ['construct','tough'], but the text says Construct here 'doesn't require the familiar to have the Tough familiar ability'. Tough is therefore handed over unasked, and deriveFamiliar's hasTough raises the familiar to (5+2) x level HP — a benefit the printed waiver denies. The card's own note repeats the error: 'It always has Construct (a construct-trait familiar; requires and includes Tough).' (3) MISSING, builder: 'doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2)' is not modelled. `abilityBudget: 2` is read by nothing in src/ — CompanionsTab.tsx:1457 seeds only lockedAbilities, and it seeds them INTO cfg.abilities, the same array the player's own picks live in. FamiliarAbilityPicker shows only '2 chosen' with no budget and no remaining count, so the count reads as fully spent before the player has chosen anything — precisely the failure mode the clause exists to prevent — and nothing marks Construct as permanent, so the player can toggle it off. Minor: the card attributes it as 'Granted by a feat' without naming Alchemical Familiar (grant.label is never rendered; kindMeta returns the generic 'Familiar').

defects.name: Alchemical Scholar
defects.detail: The two formula clauses work; the redundancy clause does not exist. VERIFIED WORKING: a hobgoblin fighter gets Alchemical Crafting as a bonus feat (grantedBy 'alchemical-scholar') and its four filtered slots fire from the grant, plus 1 slot for the 'additional common 1st-level alchemical formula' and level-1 slots for the per-level clause (6 slots at level 7), all writing into the granted book. MISSING (builder + sheet): 'If you would automatically gain that feat… you instead gain a different 1st-level Crafting skill feat.' Nothing implements it. FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS is documented as 'Deduped against feats the character already has', and featGrantsAuto's `redundantFallback` is a SKILL-training fallback, not a feat one. Measured: a level-7 hobgoblin ALCHEMIST with Alchemical Scholar ends up with alchemical-crafting granted by 'alchemy' (the class feature) and Alchemical Scholar's grant silently swallowed — no picker is offered, no substitute feat appears, and the player loses a whole 1st-level Crafting skill feat with no sign anything happened. The option list the text specifies (Crafting skill feats of level 1, Alchemical Crafting excluded) exists nowhere. SECONDARY, spurious width (builder): the per-level clause says 'one common alchemical formula OF THAT LEVEL', but FORMULA_GRANTS['alchemical-scholar'].parts[1] uses maxLevel 'self', so every one of the six slots on a 7th-level character offers the same 369-item pool spanning levels 0-7 rather than one 2nd-level pick, one 3rd, and so on — a list wider than the feat's own restriction (Q9), and materially more generous.

defects.name: Alghollthu Bound
defects.detail: The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and nothing is rendered. On the sheet, Will carries two lines (confirmed by calling explainStat on an azarketi holding the feat): '+2 circumstance from Alghollthu Bound — against mental effects that would make you controlled' (situationalBonuses.ts:107, correctly outside the flat total per Ruling B) and 'a success is a critical success instead … unless the effect originates from an alghollthu' (the record's own degreeShifts entry, in the one registry, correctly scoped to will). Two things are missing, and they are the same half of the sentence. (a) The second, OPPOSITE-SIGNED entry — '-2 circumstance … against mental effects from alghollthus' — has no entry anywhere: no situational row, no note, on any save. Per Ruling H the text names no roll ('against mental effects', not 'to Will saves'), so it should surface on every save it could plausibly apply to; today it surfaces on none. (b) The +2 line's `when` omits the alghollthu carve-out that the degreeShift line does carry, so the star reads '+2 circumstance … against mental effects that would make you controlled' with no exception stated — false at exactly the table where an azarketi's flavour makes it likeliest to come up. This is the Round-10 Dragon's Presence shape: the record shipped with the good news and hid the bad.

defects.name: All of the Animal
defects.detail: Silent on both halves, with no harness limit to explain it — and the builder silence is correct (Principle M2: the corpse is an object in the fiction, re-chosen every use, so no picker and no free-text field is owed). The sheet half delivers nothing. Confirmed by driving the real display paths on a fighter holding the feat: explainStat(skill: survival).situational is [] and recordMarkersFor(action 'subsist') is [] — the record carries no `situational`, no RECORD_MARKERS entry, and appears in no registry (registries: []). Both owed surfaces are absent: the `*` on SURVIVAL carrying the clause (owed under Q20's refinement even though no number moves — the clause names a specific stat, the Assurance shape), and the marker on the SUBSIST action itself (Q2 'both', Ruling D — a player about to Subsist is looking at Subsist). The 'subsist' action id exists in core.json and StatDetailModal already renders action marks from RECORD_MARKERS, so the lane is built and simply unused here. Note that the app's other Subsist-modifying skill feats (Forager, Planar Survival) each have a row in SKILL_ACTIONS.survival; All of the Animal has neither a row nor a mark, so it exists only in the feats list.

defects.name: Ammunition Thaumaturgy
defects.detail: The clause "You can Interact to reload a weapon using the hand holding your implement" reaches no surface but the feat's own description. The record carries no fields beyond level/category/rarity/actionCost/edition/aonId, `registries` is empty, and grepping src/, scripts/data/ and test/ for `ammunition-thaumaturgy` returns NOTHING — so no note, no marker, no rider. Ruling D as confirmed by Q8 ("Yes — mark the action the feat modifies") is unambiguous for this shape, and both the lane and its target already exist: RECORD_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3332) renders `{on:'action', id, note}` through recordMarkersFor (src/rules/explain.ts:465), and core.json actions contains BOTH `reload` and `interact`. Nearby precedents in the same registry mark exactly this kind of permission — 'feather-step' on `step`, 'sure-feet' on `balance`/`climb`, 'perfect-readiness' whose note even says "the extra action can be used only to Step or to Interact to reload". The builder half is correct (the feat rightly asks nothing — which weapon and which implement are facts of the moment). Fix is one RECORD_MARKERS entry on `reload` (and/or `interact`).

defects.name: Anadi Lore
defects.detail: The redundancy clause is not built. src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:28 reads `'anadi-lore': { skills: { crafting: 'trained', survival: 'trained', 'lore:anadi': 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true` — while the same file gives that flag to every sibling carrying the identical sentence: `android-lore` (line 30), `azarketi-lore` (65), `conrasu-lore` (97), `automaton-lore` (61), `awakened-animal-lore` (63). AoN feat-2762 confirms the clause is printed: "If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you become trained in a skill of your choice." src/rules/build.ts:3384 is the only site that acts on it — it pushes `skillFallbacks` (which Builder.tsx:1862 turns into the substitute picker) and applies `<featId>:fallback:<skill>`, both guarded on `g.redundantFallback`. So for any anadi whose class or background already trains Crafting or Survival: BUILDER — the substitute-skill picker never renders, the player is never asked (this is why `presentsChoices` is empty; the harness host was a fighter, for whom the clause does not fire, so the empty picker list there is expected and proves nothing either way); SHEET — no replacement skill is trained, and the grant is silently lost. The other three grants ARE correct: Crafting and Survival move in the diff, and `lore:anadi` reaches the sheet as its own row (MainTab.tsx:182 builds Lore rows from stored proficiencies) — its absence from sheetDiff is a harness gap, since scripts/feat-evidence.mjs:127 snapshots only the 16 core SKILLS. Note the engine's existing shape already handles the reader's flagged double-overlap case (one fallback pushed per redundant key, each with its own answer slot), so the fix really is the one missing flag.

defects.name: Ancestral Blood Magic
defects.detail: Nothing is delivered on either requirement. The record carries no fields at all, `registries` is empty, and `ancestral-blood-magic` appears NOWHERE in src/, scripts/data/ or test/. (1) Principle C — the record whose grant this widens says nothing about it. Blood magic is surfaced today on the bloodline features themselves (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:996-1001: `bloodline-draconic` → "for 1 round after your blood magic triggers…", and 20-odd siblings), and those entries are unchanged and unattributed, so a sorcerer reading their bloodline still sees only the printed triggers. (2) Q8 / Principle N2 — no mark on the qualifying spells. ⚠ The two halves are not equally buildable, and I am separating them rather than lumping them: the SPELL half has a real route (build.ts:3939 `pushSpellNote` + spellNotesFor → SpellsTab.tsx:2155), it simply needs a derived pass because the qualifying set is per-character (non-cantrip spells whose source is a heritage or an ancestry feat) and the static `spellNotes` array is keyed by literal spellId; that is unauthored work, not a missing capability. The FEATURE half may be a genuine field gap: `GrantModification` (types.ts:1042) can only say `innateUsesPerDay`, `actionRider` (which renders as a RecordMarker on an ACTION or CONDITION row) or `deityDomainsFromChoice`, and blood magic is a class feature, not an action or a condition — so there is no gated way today to add a line to another FEATURE's entry. Per the doc's own Round-10 lesson, that is the field being unable to say it rather than the text not saying it. Builder half is correct: the feat rightly asks nothing.

defects.name: Ancient Memories
defects.detail: The skill grant works — sheetDiff moves acrobatics untrained→trained and its modifier 1→23 — but every rule the text puts AROUND that grant is undelivered, and the app asks the one question twice. (1) The daily pick is never asked at Daily preparations. The record's `choice` is `{ kind: 'skills', daily: true }`, and askedAtDailyPrep (derive.ts:976) requires kind 'array'/'text'/'open', so dailyChoicesFor skips it — the app's own comment names this record: 'Ancient Memories is the one record in that state today'. Measured: 58 feats carry choice.daily and this is the only one with kind 'skills'. So per Q23 it renders in the wrong place (the builder) and never in the right one. (2) That builder picker's OPTION LIST is inverted. kind 'skills' resolves through trainedSkillOptions (build.ts:1159/1303), which returns the skills the character is ALREADY trained in — the evidence's 12 options are Arcana (E), Crafting (E), … Acrobatics (T) — i.e. every option is a wasted grant (Q21/Q27) and no untrained skill, the only kind the feat can help, can be picked at all. Its answer moves nothing (verdict 'daily', echoed). (3) A SECOND picker asks the same question: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['ancient-memories'] = { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] } (featGrantsAuto.ts:29) renders 'Trained skill' with all 16 skills, its answer IS read (moves intimidation), and it silently defaults — pickersLeftBlank 2, silentDefaults on both, and the unanswered build still trains Acrobatics (featSkillChoiceValue defaults to the slot's first option). (4) The rank it writes is PERMANENT and indistinguishable from a real one: it lands in stored.proficiencies.skills, which is what the prerequisite test and skill increases read, so the two exclusions the text makes — not a prerequisite for a permanent option, not a base a skill increase raises — are both violated, and nothing on the skill row says 'until you prepare again' (the temporary note lives on the dead daily picker, not on the grant that moved the sheet). Sheet half: the number moves (correct) but reads permanent (missing). Builder half: asked in the wrong place, asked twice, and with an option list that excludes the only useful answers.

defects.name: Angelkin
defects.detail: Two of the four promises are undelivered. SHEET — 'You know the Empyrean language' never reaches the sheet: the record carries no grantsLanguages, no feat in core.json carries that field at all (only 2 heritages do), and a probe build of a human fighter holding Angelkin returns languages ['common']. build.ts:5065 already reads content.feats[id].grantsLanguages, so the lane exists and the record is simply unauthored — grantsLanguages:['empyrean'] ('empyrean' is a live id in the 120-entry languages bucket). BUILDER — the redundancy clause is not registered: featGrantsAuto.ts:31 is 'angelkin': { skills: { society: 'trained' } } with NO redundantFallback:true (android-lore, whose clause is identical in shape, has it). Probe with Society already trained: skillFallbacks is null, no replacement picker is rendered, and the grant is silently wasted — the player is never asked. Delivered correctly: Society trained (diff 0->22) and the granted skill feat, which lands as a real owned feat (stored.feats[multilingual].grantedBy = 'angelkin') whose own two language slots flow through recordLanguageSlots, so the granted feat's choice is offered.

defects.name: Animal Companion (Ranger)
defects.detail: The companion half is delivered (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['animal-companion-ranger'] = { kind:'animal' } -> auto card, young by default, full type picker and young stat block with support + advanced maneuver). What is missing is the second sentence: 'When you Hunt Prey, your animal companion gains the action's benefits and your hunter's edge benefit if you have one.' It appears nowhere. The record carries no `note`; the only mention of this id in all of src/ is companionGrants.ts:50, whose note is the generic 'Grants an animal companion — choose its type and advance it in the Edit tab' and says nothing about Hunt Prey or the edge; registries lists companionGrants only, so situationalBonuses has no entry. Both routes the owner's rulings call for already exist and are unused here: an action marker on Hunt Prey (situationalBonuses.ts:3441 shows the exact shape — swift-prey uses { on:'action', id:'hunt-prey', note }, Ruling D / Q8), and a note on the COMPANION's own card (COMPANION_MODS[...].note, rendered through modNotes in companions.ts:519). So a precision ranger's companion shares the precision damage, and a flurry ranger's companion its MAP progression, with nothing on either sheet saying so. Missing, not no_lane. The 'if you have one' conditional means the authored note must name the edge the character actually has.

defects.name: Animal Elocutionist
defects.detail: The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and renders no picker. One of three sheet clauses is delivered: "+1 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on animals" is in FEAT_SITUATIONAL (situationalBonuses.ts:116) as a Diplomacy entry, when="to Make an Impression on animals", bonus="+1 circumstance" — right type, right restriction, kept out of the Diplomacy total per Ruling B. Two clauses are undelivered. (1) "You hear animal sounds as conversations… and you can respond in turn" / "you can ask questions of, receive answers from… animals" reaches no surface at all: the record carries no grantsLanguages, no note, no second situational entry, so nothing on the Details tab, the Vitals rail or the Diplomacy row tells the player they can speak with animals. This is a 24-record family (burrow-elocutionist, green-tongue, aquatic-conversationalist, reptile-speaker, croak-talker, wave-speaker, plant-empathy, natural-ambassador, familiars-language …) sharing the phrase and carrying nothing; the earlier audit-500 pass reached the same finding on ratspeak. The lane exists (mechanic-lanes D: `language` = "You can speak with Y"; lane J: `note` for a clause worth printing but not computable), so this is promised-but-empty, not a missing lane — the owner still has to choose the shape (a pill in the languages/senses row vs a printed note), since core.languages has 120 real language slugs and no animal-speech one. (2) Q2/Q8: the ACTION half is absent. Make an Impression is a rendered row inside the Diplomacy stat-detail modal (skillActions.ts SKILL_ACTIONS.diplomacy → StatDetailModal.tsx:185 recordMarkersFor(…,'action',…)), and RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3332, 106 entries) has no entry for this feat and no `make-an-impression` mark at all, so the value never appears where the player reads that action.

defects.name: Animal Empathy
defects.detail: silentOnBothHalves, and only one half of that is correct. The builder correctly asks nothing (no choice, no effectChoices, no picker — the text offers no options). The sheet delivers nothing at all: storedFields carry only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/aonId, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and the harness reports no harnessLimits — so the emptiness is the app, not the measurement. Two things are owed. (1) The rudimentary two-way animal communication ("ask questions of, receive answers from") has no surface — same 24-record family gap as Animal Elocutionist, and the word RUDIMENTARY has to survive to the player so this does not read as full conversation. (2) A `*` on Diplomacy saying Diplomacy can be used on animals: FEAT_SITUATIONAL has no entry for this id, so the Diplomacy row carries nothing back to the feat. Correct by omission, and worth stating so nobody "fixes" it: this feat grants NO bonus, so the absence of any modifier on Diplomacy is right — only the star and the communication statement are missing.

defects.name: Animal Empathy (Druid)
defects.detail: Mechanically identical to Animal Empathy and identically empty: no registries, no stored mechanical fields, empty sheetDiff, no harnessLimits. Builder correctly asks nothing (the "Archetypes Beastmaster (Level 4), Mammoth Lord (Level 4)" line is availability metadata and is correctly NOT rendered as a picker).
