Missing: the rudimentary animal-communication statement, and the `*` on Diplomacy for "you can use Diplomacy with animals" — no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry exists for this id. Again correctly no modifier, since the feat grants no bonus. Two record-level observations the owner should see with this one: (a) the description begins with a bibliographic header glued to the rules prose — "Animal Empathy (Druid) Source Player Core pg. 127 Archetypes Beastmaster (Level 4), Mammoth Lord (Level 4)" — import damage of the Exemplar-Dedication family, rendered to the player as if it were rules text; (b) it shares aonId feat-4709 with `animal-empathy` and prints the same rules, so the feat list offers the same feat twice under two names.

defects.name: Apparition Sense
defects.detail: The sense half is right and observed: defenses.senses gains {name:'apparition sight', acuity:'imprecise', range:30}, so the player reads "Apparition Sight (imprecise 30 ft)" off the Senses row. What is not delivered is the second sentence's activity: "As an activity that takes 10 minutes, you can act as a link between disembodied souls and their mortal bodies." The record carries no `grantsActions`, its own actionCost is {type:'passive'}, and nothing in db.actions is attributed to it — so no entry appears anywhere in the actions list and the procedure (contact with both spirit and body for the full 10 minutes; it does NOT raise the dead; the displaced occupant's Will save vs your spell DC) survives only inside the raw feat description. Note for whoever fixes it: authoring the activity is not enough on its own — ActionCost {type:'duration'; text} exists in types.ts:136 but ZERO records in public/core.json use it, and MainTab.tsx's isActionCost gate (actions|reaction|free|variable only, MainTab.tsx:226) drops a duration-cost record, so the display filter needs widening too. Secondary and much smaller: the standing "a spirit or undead otherwise incapable of speech can speak through you (while in direct contact)" capability has no `note` field, so it too is only in the description. The Will-save sentence correctly gets no surface (it lands on another creature and quotes a DC that already has a row). The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and the harness observed no picker.

defects.name: Arcane Communication
defects.detail: "You gain touch telepathy … as long as you share a language" reaches nothing. The record's stored fields are only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `senses`, no `note`, no `passiveEffects` — `registries` is empty and `sheetDiff` is `[]` (crossChecks.silentOnBothHalves, with NO harnessLimits to excuse it). The builder correctly asks nothing, so the whole feat is silent. A route exists and is in daily use: `senses[]` is free-form and already carries non-vision entries across the corpus (thoughtsense, lifesense, apparition sight, "ignores concealment from smoke"), and `note` is the lane for a clause worth printing but not computable; derive.ts even built a dedicated `breathesWater` flag for exactly this shape ("a permanent capability with no number attached … every record saying it did nothing at all"). So this is an empty lane, not a missing one. The Enhancement tier (10-ft range) is likewise unrecorded — and note the app DOES model the tier elsewhere: feats/lesser-augmentation and feats/greater-augmentation carry an `effectChoices` picker listing arcane-communication by name, so the tier could be gated. Nothing on the sheet distinguishes base from Enhancement here because nothing is on the sheet at all.

defects.name: Arcane Sense
defects.detail: The at-will half is right and the rank half is absent. Delivered: `innateSpells:[{spellId:'detect-magic',tradition:'arcane',atWill:true}]` produces an innate entry headed "Innate spells · innate spells (Arcane)", and atWill sets innateUses=0 so there is no pip and nothing to restore — the positive "at will" statement the text makes. Missing: "If you're a master in Arcana, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank; if you're legendary, 4th" is modelled nowhere. `InnateSpellGrant` can express `rank`, `heightenHalfLevel` and `heightenAt` (level-keyed steps), but nothing keyed to a SKILL proficiency, and the record authors no heighten at all — so the printed rank never moves when Arcana rises, which is the whole second sentence of the feat. Compounding it, this app's Detect Magic record is the legacy CANTRIP (rank 0, `cantrip` trait) rather than the Remaster 1st-rank spell the feat's own text names, so the grant lands in `spellcasting[innate-casting].cantrips[0]` and SpellsTab's cantrip branch renders it as meta="at will" with NO rank at all and — unlike the repertoire branch, which appends "· from <source>" — WITHOUT the "from Arcane Sense" attribution, even though `spellSources.detect-magic='Arcane Sense'` is populated (a write-only field for this one shape). So the player reads an unranked, unattributed Detect Magic. Two sibling records need the same proficiency-keyed ladder and also lack it (rivethun-devotion, rivethun-adept), so the field limitation is real rather than a one-off authoring miss. Builder half is correct: the feat asks nothing.

defects.name: Armor Assist
defects.detail: Nothing at all is delivered on the sheet. The record carries no situational, no note and no other mechanical field (storedFields is level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only), and src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts has no 'armor-assist' key. Required: a `*` on BOTH skills the text names — Athletics and the specific Warfare Lore subskill (ruling C / principle D: star every skill that could perform the named action) — carrying what the check achieves (halve your own donning time) and the GM's DC guidance (usually 15 common / 20 uncommon / 25 rare), with click-through. Both targets are demonstrably in lane: situationalBonuses.ts already stars a named Lore this exact way (siege-ritualist, targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'lore:warfare'}] at line 2239). The ally half correctly owes no second number (ruling F) but per principle A must still be readable in the same star's note and the description. The builder half is right: the Athletics-or-Warfare-Lore choice is made per attempt at the table, and the builder renders no picker (choiceCount 0). ⚠ The harnessLimits entry 'pick-a-feat-grant' on this feat is a FALSE trigger and must not be used to excuse the empty diff: armor-assist grants no feat — it only appears inside OTHER feats' option lists (src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:140 and :193, Pitborn's six-feat pick). The silentOnBothHalves shape here is real.

defects.name: Armor Regiment Training
defects.detail: One of three sheet clauses is delivered; two are absent. DELIVERED — bulkIgnore: the record carries armorBulkReduction { by: 1, categories: ['heavy'] } and it is genuinely read, at src/rules/derive.ts:4103 inside deriveBulk, applied only to worn items of itemType 'armor' whose category is heavy, floored at the item's own Bulk so it cannot go negative, and subtracted from the total that feeds the encumbered/maximum thresholds. The empty sheetDiff does not contradict this — the reference host wears no heavy armour and Bulk is not one of the diffed values. MISSING — situational: no `*` on the Speed row for the exploration-mode travel clause. The record has no `situational` field and situationalBonuses.ts has no key for it, yet this is the app's most well-worn shape: horizon-walker-dedication (line 647), scouts-speed (721), legendary-guide (733) and constant-crosier (1994) all star the Speed row with a travel-only `when` that explicitly says it is not the encounter Speed. The star must carry the ally half as text (ruling F + principle A) and must NOT strip the armour Speed penalty from the printed Speed. MISSING — note: "you can rest normally while wearing armor of any type" has no marker anywhere. Per ruling D it belongs on the Rest / daily-preparations flow, and the app already writes this exact clause into a mode note for a comparable record (guardians-armor in toggle-modes.json: "You can also rest normally in medium and heavy armor"). Mitigating: nothing in src/ models an armoured-rest penalty at all (only the glossary's 'comfort' trait blurb), so no wrong number is produced — the loss is the marker, which is why this half is low severity on its own. Builder half correct: the feat asks nothing and renders no picker.

defects.name: Armored Regiment Training
defects.detail: Only one of the three clauses is delivered. The bulk clause is real: `armorBulkReduction {by:1, categories:['heavy']}` (authored in effect-backfill.json) is read by deriveBulk at src/rules/derive.ts:4103 and subtracted from the carried total. The other two clauses reach nothing. (1) "you can rest normally while wearing armor of any type" — the record carries no `note`, `registries` is empty, and nothing anywhere marks Rest/daily preparations; the app knows the concept (glossary.ts:147 explains the Comfort armour trait as exactly this), so the player of a commander in full plate is left under the general rule with no indication it stopped applying. (2) "In exploration mode, you and your allies use your normal Speeds without including your armors' Speed penalties" — no `situational` field and no situationalBonuses entry, so the Speed row (which already has the armour's Speed penalty subtracted) carries no `*`. sheetDiff is empty and the diff DOES cover situational notes, so both absences are observed, not inferred. Both lanes exist and are heavily used (`note`; `situational` targets kind 'speed'), so this is unbuilt data, not a missing capability. The ally half correctly needs nothing (Ruling F). Builder half is correct: the feat asks nothing and the app asks nothing. Secondary, smaller: `armorRelief` (derive.ts:4119) returns 0 unless `inv.worn`, so heavy armour carried but not worn gets no reduction — the text conditions on the armour being heavy, not on wearing it.

defects.name: Automaton Armament
defects.detail: Everything except the Enhancement is right. The picker offers exactly two options (Claw, Pincer), the answer is read, and both strikes land correctly on the Strikes tab, measured: Claw = 1d4+5 S, traits agile/finesse/unarmed, group brawling, mapStep 4; Pincer = 1d6+5 P, traits grapple/unarmed, group brawling, mapStep 5 — the die, type, group, the agile MAP step and the absence of agile/finesse on the pincer all reach the row. Re-choosing swaps the row cleanly (Ruling K covers the rest), and the record's own level 1 means the "select at any level" clause needs no separate gate. THE ENHANCEMENT IS NOT APPLIED. It is recorded — Lesser Augmentation and Greater Augmentation each carry an `effectChoices` picker listing `automaton-armament` — but that answer reaches nothing: no `src/` file mentions lesser/greater-augmentation, and the picker's own prompt says "(prose benefit — read that feat's Enhancement entry)". Measured: a fighter/automaton at level 9 holding Automaton Armament (claw) AND Lesser Augmentation pointed at it still shows Claw 1d4+5 S. Per Principle C the die step (claw 1d4→1d6, pincer 1d6→1d8, everything else untouched) has to be reflected in the strike this feat granted, attributed to the Enhancement.

defects.name: Avowed Insight
defects.detail: DELIVERED: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:748 stars AC and, via {kind:'save', detail:'all'}, all three saves with '+1 circumstance' and the 1-round condition in the `when` — Q1 (indication only) and Q2 (all three saves) both satisfied, and the sheetDiff confirms four star rows. The free-text Lore answer really does reach a skill row: build.ts:3436 writes `lore:<subject>` at trained. TWO DEFECTS. (a) MISSING, sheet: nothing is starred on the TRIGGER side. The reward is bought by a successful Recall Knowledge, and your own answer #6 (Mastermind's Eye) is this exact shape — 'a * in every skill that can recall knolladge so the user can see what happens when he checks his recall knowledge number' — reinforced by Ruling C, Ruling H and Q2's 'star the skill AND the action'. The record's only situational targets are ac and save:all; there is no skill target, no marker on the Recall Knowledge action, and no star on the Lore this feat itself grants. (b) SPURIOUS, builder: the pick is an UNRESTRICTED free-text box (featGrantsAuto.ts:62 'avowed-insight': {loreChoices: 1} → Builder.tsx:1896, label 'Trained Lore', placeholder 'Lore subject (e.g. Warfare)…'), while the text restricts it to a creature type NAMED BY THAT CHARACTER'S VOW. Measured against the data: only 2 of the 6 yaksha heritages name a creature type — deny-the-firstborn-pursuit (fey; the answer is forced, so per the Exemplar Dedication rule no question should be posed at all, just a stated fact) and deny-the-traitors-rebirth (rakshasas and asuras; a 2-option pick). featGrantsAuto.ts's own header admits the gap: 'Restricted skill choices are surfaced as options: any … the exact list restriction is not modeled'. Q9's Domain Fluency shape applies.

defects.name: Awakened Animal Lore
defects.detail: DELIVERED: BOTH Arcana and Nature reach trained with computed modifiers (sheetDiff: arcana untrained→trained mod 22, nature likewise) — the half-delivery trap is avoided. The redundancy fallback is right in shape: build.ts:3384 fires it PER SKILL (the evidence's single 'Already trained in arcana — replacement skill' picker is the arcana slot alone), the answer is read (movedPaths show a real skill rank moving), and Builder.tsx:1866 greys every already-trained option with the reason 'Already <rank> — pick a skill you are untrained in' — Q27 satisfied, so the raw 16-option list in the evidence is not a Q9 width defect. No phantom 'choose a Lore' question is posed for the granted feat, which is correct. MISSING: 'You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Awakened Animal Lore' is a NAME ON A LIST and nothing else. featFeatGrants.ts:69 grants `additional-lore`, whose own content is featGrantsAuto.ts:22 {loreChoices: 1} — an unanswered Lore slot. Builder.tsx's grantedChoicePicker only handles a record `choice` def (additional-lore has none), so no picker is rendered for a granted feat's FEAT_GRANTS lore slot, and no FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE entry pre-answers it. Grepped: no `lore:awakened-animal` anywhere in src/ or scripts/data/, and the sheetDiff shows no Lore row at all. The binding mechanism already exists (FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE {kind:'fixed', skill} for eidetic-ear) but has no fixed-LORE shape, so the field is part of why this could not be authored. COLLATERAL, outside this feat: `additional-lore` also carries no rankUpgrade, so even a normally-taken Additional Lore never reaches the skill increases its text promises at 3rd/7th/15th.

defects.name: Axiomatic Lore
defects.detail: Clause: "If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills … you instead become trained in a skill of your choice." The redundancy fallback is never asked. `featGrantsAuto.ts:64` authors `'axiomatic-lore': { skills: { diplomacy: 'trained', society: 'trained', 'lore:axis': 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true` — the very next line (65), azarketi-lore, has it. `redundantFallback` is the only trigger for the picker (build.ts:3384 pushes onto `Character.skillFallbacks`, which is what the builder renders and what the builder harness reported for azarketi-lore). Rebuilt to confirm rather than inferred: an investigator (Society is a fixed class skill) and a commander (same) each take Axiomatic Lore and get `skillFallbacks = null` — no prompt, no options, and the redundant Society training is silently swallowed by `maxRank`. The pack's empty `presentsChoices` is NOT evidence either way, because its host is a fighter/human on the acolyte background, for whom neither named skill is redundant (correct behaviour). The sheet-side half of the same clause ("the chosen skill reads trained") fails only as a consequence — there is no answer to apply. The other three requirements are delivered and observed: Diplomacy and Society read trained (+22 each) and Axis Lore is trained. One-line fix, same shape as line 65.

defects.name: Azarketi Weapon Familiarity
defects.detail: Clause: "For the purpose of determining your proficiency, martial azarketi weapons are simple weapons and advanced azarketi weapons are martial weapons." The remap is flattened into a fixed rank. `featGrantsAuto.ts:66` authors `weaponFamiliarity: { weapons: ['crossbow','hand-crossbow','longspear','spear','trident','boarding-axe','gill-hook'], rank: 'trained' }` — so the two azarketi weapons in content (boarding-axe and gill-hook, both MARTIAL, both uncommon) get a flat `trained` override instead of resolving to the character's SIMPLE rank. Observed, not inferred: a level-11 azarketi psychic (simple = expert, martial = untrained) equipping a Gill Hook derives the Strike at rank `trained`, attack +14/+9/+4; the remap the text prints makes it expert, +16. The gap is live for every class that outruns martial with simple — sorcerer L20, animist L11+, psychic L11+, cloistered casters generally — and widens to 4 points at master. This is a data gap, not a lane gap: build.ts:4038-4060 already handles several clauses per record and `mirrorCategory` is the exact field (`advanced-bow-training` uses `mirrorCategory: 'martial'`), so the record wants a second clause `{ weapons: ['boarding-axe','gill-hook'], mirrorCategory: 'simple' }`; because overrides are applied with `maxRank` and deriveStrike maxes again against the weapon's own category, Q10's "only when it makes the player better" still holds. Delivered correctly: the five named weapons are trained (observed as weaponOverrides), the access clause owes nothing (Q5), and the builder correctly asks nothing. ⚠ The pack's `companion-tab?` limit is a false positive — it matched the word "familiar" in "You are familiar with weapons"; no companion is involved.

defects.name: Bardic Lore
defects.detail: The trained grant works; the three clauses after it do not. First, the empty sheetDiff is a HOST artifact and not a defect, and the pack's `pick-a-feat-grant` limit explains it for the wrong reason (it fired because featPickGrants.ts:190 lists 'bardic-lore' in Natural Ambition's EXCLUDE array): the sheet host is a bard whose subclass is `options[0]` = the ENIGMA muse, which already grants the Bardic Lore feat, so the 'before' character already had `lore:bardic` trained. Rebuilt on maestro/polymath/warrior/zoophonia, taking the feat does grant `lore:bardic` trained (featGrantsAuto.ts:69). What fails: (1) SHEET, rankUpgrade — "If you have legendary proficiency in Occultism, you gain expert proficiency in Bardic Lore" is not modelled anywhere; a bard driven to legendary Occultism via skill increases still reads `lore:bardic` = trained (the record carries only a flat `skills` map; `conditionalSkills` keys off the same skill's own prior rank, not off Occultism, so no existing field expresses it). (2) BUILDER, the hard exclusion — "you can't increase your proficiency rank in Bardic Lore by any other means" is not enforced: Builder.tsx:1418 builds the skill-increase list as `[...SKILLS, ...loreKeys]` from every owned lore, so Bardic Lore is offered live, un-greyed and with no reason (Q27), and three skill increases spent on it were observed to raise it to MASTER. (3) SHEET, note — nothing states that this Lore is Recall-Knowledge-only on any topic, or why its rank cannot move; the record carries no `note` and no situational entry, so the row behaves unlike every neighbouring Lore with no explanation, which is exactly the "reads as a broken app" shape.

defects.name: Bargain Hunter
defects.detail: Silent on both halves with NO harness limit — and the builder half is correct (the feat owes no question and asks none), so the whole defect is the sheet. Nothing of the three clauses is delivered. (1) "You can Earn Income using Diplomacy": the record carries no `skillSubstitutions`, no `situational` entry and no `note` (storedFields = level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only; registries empty; the only mention of `bargain-hunter` anywhere in src/ or scripts/data is a background's `grantedFeatId`). The Earn Income downtime record at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/actions.ts:123 still reads `skill: 'Crafting'`, and the Diplomacy row gets no `*` — the lane plainly exists and is used for this exact shape elsewhere (situationalBonuses.ts:262 `leaf-transformation`, when: "using Deception to Earn Income"). (2) The second use — run Earn Income with Diplomacy and take the proceeds as a discount on one item, free if the income meets its Price — appears on no surface but the feat's own blurb, which fails Principle A. (3) The +2 gp at 1st-level character creation has no lane at all: `startingWealthGp` (src/rules/wealth.ts) is a flat level table with no per-feat term. ⚠ Worth the owner knowing: the app already derives currency as budget minus purchases (build.ts:5168 `cpToCoins(startingWealthGp(level)*100 - inventory)`), so a +2 gp term IS expressible in that model and stays correct after the player spends it — the reader's "one-time write, never derived" worry does not apply here.

defects.name: Bestial Manifestation
defects.detail: Sheet half is correct: `grantedStrikes` carries all four rows with the printed die, damage type, group brawling and trait lines (Claw d4 slashing agile/finesse/unarmed/versatile-p; Hoof d6 bludgeoning; Jaws d6 piercing; Tail d4 bludgeoning agile), keyed by `choiceValue`, and the answer is read — strikes[0].name/damage/traits all move. Two builder-half failures. (1) The picker shows four BARE WORDS. The `choice.options` carry only value+label and no `description`, and `buildChoiceOptions` (build.ts:1291) fills a description only for `def.ownsFeature` choices, so PopupSelect renders "Claw / Hoof / Jaws / Tail" with no die, damage type or traits — the only things that distinguish them — at a pick the feat says is permanent. The data is already on the same record (`grantedStrikes`, matched by `choiceValue`); the picker option's `description` field exists and is unauthored. (2) The Special clause has NO ROUTE anywhere in the app: nothing expresses "selectable only in a 1st-level slot" and nothing locks an answered choice. `maxLevel` exists only on featPickGrants specs and item filters, not as a ceiling on which slot may take a feat; grep for onlyAtLevel/firstLevelOnly/noRetrain/'only at 1st' in src/ returns nothing. So the feat is offerable in a 5th/9th/13th/17th-level ancestry slot and the attack stays freely re-choosable forever. This is a lane gap, not a per-record omission — 28 live feats print "You can select this feat only at 1st level" (round-ears, tusks, quadruped, elf-atavism, orc-sight, draconic-aspect, scaly-hide, gravesight …) and none can say it.

defects.name: Blowgun Poisoner
defects.detail: silentOnBothHalves with NO harnessLimits: sheetDiff is empty, storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/actionCost/archetype, and registries is [] — nothing in situationalBonuses.ts, no note, no RecordMarker. The builder half is correct (the feat states no choice and none is rendered), so the whole defect is the sheet. Owed and absent: (a) a `*` on STEALTH carrying the third clause — "if you make a blowgun Strike while hidden or undetected, you don't automatically become observed. Instead, immediately attempt a Stealth check against the Perception DC of the target" — Stealth is where the player looks up the number this clause makes them roll, and Q2 says star the skill AND the action; (b) a marker on the blowgun Strike rows carrying all three rules: injury poisons apply even when resistance zeroes the damage, the crit-success misfortune that worsens the target's initial save by one degree (target-side, so correctly no `degreeShifts` entry on the character's own stats), and the hidden/undetected Stealth clause. Both surfaces exist as lanes today (`situational` targets kind 'skill' and 'strikeAttack'; RecordMarker marks actions) and neither is authored, so all three clauses live only inside the feat's own text.

defects.name: Bodyguard
defects.detail: Builder half is CORRECT and should not be reported: the charge is authored as `choice {flag:'bodyguardCharge', kind:'text', daily:true}` — free text is the right answer type (Principle I) — and Builder.tsx guards every choice site on `askedAtDailyPrep` (Builder.tsx:1441/1549/1621/1815), so it does not render in the builder and is asked at Daily preparations instead (Q23); it stays re-editable because Daily preparations can be reopened, satisfying the 10-minute re-choice clause. The evidence's `presentsChoices` row is the harness resolving the declared choice, not the builder rendering it. Sheet half is empty and owes two things. (1) No marker on TAUNT: `actions/taunt` exists in core.json and the shipped lane for exactly this is a RecordMarker `{on:'action', id:'taunt'}` (the same route as furious-focus → vicious-swing), but nothing records that this feat raises the taunted enemy's penalty to –2 against your charge. Correctly no skill star — Taunt is a 1-action guardian activity with no check, so Ruling C's conditional does not fire. (2) The daily answer has no consumer: `bodyguardCharge` is matched by no file under src/ (only data files), so the charge's name is readable only inside the daily-prep dialog's "Keeping your last choices" line (CharacterSheet.tsx:851, and only when dailyPrepPrompt === 'reuse'), never on the sheet where the Taunt rule is read.

defects.name: Bouncy Goblin
defects.detail: DELIVERED: Acrobatics → trained with the modifier moving 2 → 24 (the +2 is NOT folded in, Ruling B), and the restricted bonus surfaces as a star on Acrobatics carrying "to Tumble Through a foe's space / +2 circumstance" (situationalBonuses.ts:134). MISSING: the fallback clause '(or another skill of your choice, if you were already trained in Acrobatics)' is not modelled. featGrantsAuto.ts:77 reads `'bouncy-goblin': { skills: { acrobatics: 'trained' } }` — no `redundantFallback`. Its Remaster sibling, the identical clause, does: featGrantsAuto.ts:133 `'extra-squishy': { skills: { acrobatics: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }`. The whole route exists and works (build.ts:3384 pushes Character.skillFallbacks and applies featSkillChoices `<featId>:fallback:<skill>`; Builder.tsx:1862 renders the picker), so this is one absent flag. Consequence: a goblin already trained in Acrobatics is asked NOTHING (builder half — the conditional question never appears) and gains NOTHING (sheet half — no substitute skill is ever trained), silently losing a skill training. The evidence pack cannot show this: the harness host was untrained in Acrobatics, so `presentsChoices: []` is the correct behaviour for that host and the defect is only visible in the record. SECONDARY: per Q2/Q8 the Tumble Through action row should also carry the mark; RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3332) has no bouncy-goblin entry, so the star lives on the skill only.

defects.name: Adroit Manipulation
defects.detail: The sheet half is correct: Thievery moves untrained→trained (skills.thievery.modifier 2→24), and `degreeShifts:[{successToCrit, when:"on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock", skills:[thievery], actions:[pick-a-lock]}]` is Q2's both-surfaces exactly — I confirmed in src/rules/explain.ts that one entry fans out to a Thievery star (authoredSituational, line ~367) AND a pick-a-lock action marker (degreeShiftMarkers, line ~311). The empty situational diff is a HARNESS blind spot, not a gap: feat-evidence.mjs snapshots stars via `featSituationalFor(ids, ref)` with no third argument, so it reads FEAT_SITUATIONAL only and can never see a degreeShifts-derived star. The builder half is where the defect is. The text poses ONE conditional question, and the app renders TWO pickers. (1) The working one is derived: `redundantFallback:true` in featGrantsAuto.ts:23 → Character.skillFallbacks → Builder.tsx:1862, which fires only when the Thievery grant was redundant, is consumed (answerIsRead verdict "read"), and correctly greys every already-trained skill including Thievery ("Already <rank> — pick a skill you are untrained in"), satisfying Q27. (2) Beside it the record's own `choice {flag:'adroitSkill', prompt:'Replacement skill', kind:'skills'}` renders a second "Replacement skill" picker — for EVERY holder, including one untrained in Thievery for whom the text asks nothing — and its 12 options are `trainedSkillOptions(character,'trained')`, i.e. the skills the character is ALREADY trained in (Arcana (E), Crafting (E), Occultism (E), Religion (E), Acrobatics (T) … Scribing Lore (T), Thievery (T)). That is the exact inverse of the legal list (any skill you are NOT trained in, and never Thievery itself), and the answer reaches nothing: `adroitSkill` appears in no file under src/, FEAT_GRANTS['adroit-manipulation'] carries no skillChoices for choiceGrantFor to read, and the harness confirms verdict "echo-only". This is the Exemplar Dedication shape from Round 5 — a phantom question the owner ruled should be deleted. Fix: drop the record's `choice` block from effect-backfill.json and leave the fallback lane to ask the question.

defects.name: Alabaster Eyes
defects.detail: The grant itself works: `senses:[{name:'darkvision'}]` is authored and the diff shows defenses.senses[1] ← "darkvision". Two things happen that the feat's text does not call for. SHEET: the vishkanya ancestry's low-light vision is still printed beside it — the diff adds darkvision at index 1 while index 0 (the ancestry `vision: 'low-light-vision'` baseline added at derive.ts:2039) is untouched, and neither `deriveDefenses` nor VitalsRail.tsx:730 / DetailsTab.tsx:443 suppresses a superseded sense, so the row reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision". Q13 rules exactly this case ("Show only darkvision when it supersedes low-light", 9 feats) — the supersede exists nowhere in the app, so no darkvision-granting feat on a low-light ancestry obeys it. BUILDER: "**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level" is not enforced — no field in src/rules/types.ts can express a take-at-this-level-only restriction (searched: no onlyAtLevel/maxTakeLevel/firstLevelOnly; `maxLevel` is a choice-option filter), so this level-1 ancestry feat is offered in the 5th/9th/13th/17th-level ancestry slots too, an option list wider than the feat's own printed restriction (Q9). The retraining half of the same clause is moot rather than broken — the app has no retraining feature at all (only one incidental mention, in featUses.ts). That availability restriction is a genuine "no lane at all" candidate; the sense-supersede is a built-lane display fix.

defects.name: Ancestral Mind
defects.detail: The app does implement a retune — `entryRetune: [{ scope: 'innate', tradition: 'occult', keyAbilityFromClass: 'psychic' }]` (scripts/backfill-entry-retune.mjs:23) — but it is applied FAR wider than the text. build.ts:4762 resolves scope 'innate' as `spellcasting.find(e => e.type === 'innate')`, and there is exactly ONE pooled 'innate-casting' entry (build.ts:4713) that collects innate spells from the heritage (4617), the BACKGROUND (4625), every INVESTED ITEM (4634), every FEAT including class feats (4641), resolved effect-choices and pick-a-cantrip grants. The text's filter — 'innate spells you know from an ancestry feat or heritage' — is the load-bearing part of the requirement, and nothing honours it: a psychic with an Astrological Augur background (divine Augury) or an invested Cloak of Elvenkind (arcane Ghost Sound) has THOSE spells relabelled occult and re-based onto the psychic attribute too. Wrong tradition is a wrong value, not a cosmetic one. Two further gaps on the same half: (1) no attribution anywhere — the record carries no `spellNotes`, and entryRetune only mutates tradition/keyAbility, so nothing on the Spells page names Ancestral Mind as the reason (requirement 1, principle N2/C, and the 'why does this DC differ' half of requirement 3); (2) the attribute remap is a no-op as shipped, because the pooled innate entry already defaults to `keyAbility: caster?.keyAbility` (build.ts:4715) — a psychic's innate spells use the psychic attribute with or without this feat, so the feat's own benefit is invisible and Q10's 'apply the remap only when it makes the player better' is untestable. ⚠ The per-subset scope may need a lane rather than data: one pooled innate entry cannot carry two traditions, though `innateSource`/`spellSources` already records WHICH record granted each innate spell, so the information to split them exists. ⚠ Evidence note: sheetDiff is empty because the psychic host owns no innate spells (a host-owns-nothing shape the harness did not flag); everything above is read from the code path, not observed.

defects.name: Armor Proficiency
defects.detail: The SHEET half is fully and correctly built — no defect there. src/rules/featGrants.ts:326 carries { armorCascade: true, rankUpgrade: { level: 13, rank: 'expert' } }; build.ts:3408 trains the first of light→medium→heavy still untrained at the moment the take applies, so repeat takes advance; the granted rank becomes expert on reaching 13th (keyed to current level, not the level taken); and each take records fc.choice = { label: 'Light armor' }, which the Feats tab prints as "Armor Proficiency (Light armor)" (src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:87) and the builder shows as a "Trains you in" sub-card (Builder.tsx:1793) — so the computed category is identifiable on both surfaces, which was the requirement most at risk. maxTakable 3 keeps it repeatable. The empty sheetDiff is only because the harness host is a level-20 fighter already trained in every armour category. THE DEFECT is that same case: builder.eligibleHosts lists all six reference hosts including fighter/human, for whom the feat is a guaranteed no-op at every level — there is no "next type" left, and no later scaling can rescue it (the 13th-level clause upgrades only a category this feat granted). Per Q21 that pick is wasted across the character's whole career and should be filtered; per Q27's table ("already trained… shown, greyed, and it says why") it must at minimum not render live and silently inert. src/rules/featSlots.ts:35 applies no such test, and the take then "grants nothing and stays bare" (build.ts comment) — a general feat slot spent on nothing, with the row not even carrying a category label to explain it. The app's own test blesses this as "a harmless no-op for a fighter" (test/feat-grants.test.ts), which is the exact shape the owner called bad design. Same defect on the 3rd take for any class already trained in light (only two takes can ever do anything).

defects.name: Artisanal Crafter
defects.detail: The Q9 case in its plainest form. The feat grants Specialty Crafting "in your choice of blacksmithing, leatherworking, or stonemasonry" — three options. The builder renders Specialty Crafting's OWN full list of twelve: Alchemy, Artistry, Blacksmithing, Bookmaking, Glassmaking, Leatherworking, Pottery, Shipbuilding, Stonemasonry, Tailoring, Weaving, Woodworking (picker key `specialty-crafting`, storage grantedFeatChoices, optionCount 12, optionsTruncated 0). A player can take Alchemy or Shipbuilding through a feat that never offered them — the same shape the owner already ruled a defect on Manifold Modifications (Round 5). The app has a route for BINDING a granted feat's answer (FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE, featFeatGrants.ts) but none for NARROWING it to a subset; backgroundGrants.ts records this explicitly for `toymaker` ("6 of 12"), calling it "ruling Q9's filtering lane rather than this one, and is unbuilt" — so this record is one of a family, and one narrowing shape fixes all of them. Everything else is right: the sheet half grants Crafting trained (rank + modifier move), the fallback picker exists and its answer is read (it trains the chosen skill), Specialty Crafting is owned with grantedBy = artisanal-crafter and its own situational Crafting bonus live, and the specialty answer being echo-only is legitimate here (the app models no per-specialty number, and the pick is written onto the granted feat's own entry, so the player can read which specialty they hold from Specialty Crafting itself).

defects.name: Ash-piercing Gaze
defects.detail: The feat is modelled as a SENSE the character does not have. The record carries `senses: [{name: "ignores concealment from smoke and mist"}]` and the diff confirms it lands as a sense row (defenses.senses[1].name), beside darkvision and low-light — SenseEntry's own doc comment says `name` is "the sense selector, e.g. darkvision, scent, tremorsense". The text grants no sense: the creature stays concealed, you do not see through the smoke, and only the flat check to TARGET it is auto-succeeded. As printed on the senses list it claims a perception capability that would also read as covering Seek, and as making the creature not concealed for every other purpose. Meanwhile the clause never reaches the thing it modifies — `registries` is empty, so there is no situationalBonuses entry at all — even though the app's own near-identical twin is authored correctly: `firesight` = [{ targets: [{kind:'strikeAttack'}], when: "targeting a creature concealed only by smoke and fire", bonus: "automatically succeed at the flat check" }], with `fire-lung` and `uncanny-bombs` in the same shape, and `multisensory-mask` demonstrating the `on:'condition', id:'concealed'` marker Ruling D asks for. So the fix is to move the clause from the sense list to a strike-row star and/or a Concealed-condition marker carrying the smoke-or-mist-only restriction. Builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and the app asks nothing.

defects.name: Benefactor's Resistance
defects.detail: The sheet half is delivered: `effectChoices[breath-type]` grants `resistances:[{type, value:'max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))'}]` and the answer moves defenses.resistances + defenses.sources.resistance:<type>, one line only, on a live formula. But the record ALSO renders a SECOND damage-type picker the text never asks for: `choice` (flag `nonPhysicalResistance`, prompt literally "Choose an option", 5 options acid/cold/fire/electricity/sonic). `nonPhysicalResistance` has ZERO consumers in src/ (grep returns nothing) — the harness confirms it: verdict echo-only, silentDefault true. So the player is shown two damage-type questions on one feat, and the one whose option list exactly matches the feat's printed five is the DEAD one: answer only that and the character gets no resistance at all, silently. It also carries no `choice.inert` and no `choice.note`, so it breaks the app's own coded rule at Builder.tsx:485 ("A pick that records but grants nothing must say so — never silently show a pick that does nothing") and Q27. Fix is to delete the `choice` block (the effectChoice already does the work). Two smaller notes, neither driving the verdict: (a) the live picker adds Poison to the five, which is legitimate for clause 1 (a poison-breathing benefactor) and matches the Elementheart Kobold six, but its own prompt tells a physical-breath player to pick from five while offering six — poison is not a legal answer in that branch; (b) the value uses max(1,…) at level 1, the app-wide convention copied from Elementheart Kobold, whose text prints "(minimum 1)" — this feat's text does not, so a 1st-level kobold shows resistance 1 where RAW gives 0.

defects.name: Blessed Blood (Sorcerer)
defects.detail: The list-widening itself works: `spellListAdditions {from:'deity', max:3, as:'list'}` resolves against the build's own deity in build.ts:3822 and is read by BOTH spell-selection surfaces — Builder.tsx:665 `listAdditions` (repertoire building) and SpellsTab.tsx:286 `useTraditionSpells` (Manage Spells / Learn a Spell) — so the spells become legal repertoire options at their own ranks, and `as:'list'` keeps them OUT of the repertoire, satisfying the negative requirement (the `note` says so in words too). The defect is the cap. `max` is read only on the whole-TRADITION branch; the deity branch does `[...new Set([...spells, ...fromDeity])]` with no slice, so `max:3` is enforced by nothing. Measured against the app's own deity data: 460 of 485 deities grant exactly 3 (harmless), but 12 grant MORE and every one of them is over-granted — Nethys, Nalinivati, Abraxas, Yuelral, Isis, the three Nyarlathotep entries and Zeaki grant 9 spells (a Nethys sorcerer gets all 9 added, three times the printed cap), and Brixori plus two others grant 4. Builder half: the "up to three" choice is never asked at all — declared [], presentsChoices [], choiceCount 0; the app auto-adds the deity's whole list, so a player who wanted one or two has no way to say so and no way to see which three the feat is responsible for beyond the note's prose. The picker route already exists (both readers key off the resolved deity, so its option list is available).

defects.name: Bounce Boost
defects.detail: SHEET HALF IS FINE: the reaction reaches the reactions list (sheetDiff actions[0] = 'Bounce Boost'), and its popup text carries the Trigger line, the full +1/+2/+3/+4 Athletics ladder and the 2ft/5ft Leap clause — Principle E plus Ruling F, so correctly no star and no number on your own Athletics (registries: [], no situational entry). BUILDER DEFECT (Q9): the feat's printed 'Prerequisites Trained in Athletics' is not stored. public/core.json feats/bounce-boost has no `prerequisites` array at all, and prerequisites are the only input to the gate (build.ts:6066 `for (const line of feat.prerequisites ?? [])`, which DOES enforce the 'trained in <skill>' pattern) and to the 'Requires:' chip (Builder.tsx:2370). So the slot offers Bounce Boost to a tripkee untrained in Athletics — an option list wider than the feat's own restriction — and never tells the player the requirement exists. Systemic, not one-off: measured 167 live feats whose description still prints an un-parsed 'Prerequisites …' line and whose record carries no array (bounce-boost, litany-against-wrath, the six ancestry weapon-expertise feats, …). SECONDARY, not counted against the verdict: the popup shows the whole tier ladder rather than the tier this character's Athletics rank produces; the app has no field that computes a value into ally-facing prose, and Ruling F/Principle E make the reaction entry the whole surface, so I did not treat that as owed.

defects.name: Animal Soul Siblings
defects.detail: Nearly correct — one half of one clause is missing. Delivered: Speak with Animals arrives as an innate spell with THIS spell's own tradition (stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].tradition='primal'), at the spell's own base rank (repertoire.2), attributed (spellSources['speak-with-animals']='Animal Soul Siblings'), and grantedSpells carries innate:speak-with-animals. The "once per day" is delivered even though nothing appears in the limitedUses diff: innate cadence is not tracked there — build.ts:4699 records only DEVIATIONS from 1/day, and SpellsTab.tsx:1813 prints "rank 2 · 1/day · from Animal Soul Siblings" with a spendable pip; no innate grant in this batch produces a limitedUses row, including ones with usesPerDay:1 authored explicitly, so the absence is the harness, not the app. The +1 is correctly typed and correctly restricted: situationalBonuses.ts:118, Diplomacy, when="to Gather Information from animals", "+1 circumstance", outside the total per Ruling B, starring the one skill that performs the action per Ruling C. Builder correctly asks nothing. MISSING: the second surface Q2/Q8 requires — the Gather Information ACTION carries no mark. That row renders inside the Diplomacy stat-detail modal (SKILL_ACTIONS.diplomacy → StatDetailModal.tsx:185) and supports marks, but RECORD_MARKERS has no entry for this feat; the only `gather-information` mark in the whole registry belongs to Streetwise. One-line fix, same pattern as Animal Elocutionist's Make an Impression mark. Separately worth the owner's eye (a Spells-page concern, not this record's): all innate grants pool into a single 'Innate spells' entry whose tradition is a majority vote across grants (build.ts:4708), so a character with primal and arcane innate spells would have one of them labelled with the other's tradition.

defects.name: Battle Medicine
defects.detail: The grantsAction lane IS delivered — sheetDiff shows `actions[0] = Battle Medicine`, the record carries actionCost {actions:1} and the healing/manipulate traits, and its description opens with "**Requirements** You're holding or wearing a healer's toolkit" and names the Medicine check at Treat Wounds' DC. It correctly puts no star on Medicine and no use pip for the per-target immunity (Ruling F). The defect is the immunity clause itself: the stored description reads "The target is then to your Battle Medicine for 1 day" — the word `immune` was dropped in import. AoN feat-5125 in the local archive reads "The target is then immune to your Battle Medicine for 1 day", so the sentence the requirement says must live in the popup is unreadable. The SAME bug hits the record the popup links to: `actions/treat-wounds` reads "The target is then temporarily to Treat Wounds actions for 1 hour". I scanned every description in public/core.json + public/core-descriptions.json for the pattern and got exactly these two records — a two-record fix, and the two a Battle Medicine player reads together. Secondary, not charged: the DC→healing table and the expert/master/legendary tiers ARE readable (the popup's `r` link resolves to actions/treat-wounds, which prints DC 15 / DC 20 +10 / DC 30 +30 / DC 40 +50 and the 4d8/2d8/1d8 outcomes), but they are printed flat rather than gated to this character's Medicine rank, so a trained-only character reads tiers they cannot attempt.

defects.name: Bon Mot
defects.detail: Almost everything is delivered: the activity is listed (it is a curated skill action, so MainTab dedupes it out of the feat list on purpose), the enemy-facing –3/–2 correctly touches no row of the sheet (decided scope / Q4), no `*` is put on Diplomacy (correct — the feat uses the check, it does not change it), and the app RESOLVES the crit-failure back-reference rather than printing it: situationalBonuses.ts:2435 gives `bon-mot` targets perception + will, bonus "-2 status (penalty)", when "for 1 minute after you critically fail your own Bon Mot…". What is missing is that this half is only a star. The clause is self-facing, runs 1 minute (not a round) and has an explicit end condition ("ends after 1 minute or if you issue another Bon Mot and succeed"), which is Q1's "a longer duration gets a mode" plus Q11's "if the effect can be shut down, it is a mode" — and Q15 does not excuse it, since it fires on a critical FAILURE. There is no mode: toggle-modes.json holds 258 modes and 0 mentions of bon-mot, while the same file already models self-inflicted penalties as modes (curse-of-creeping-ashes-2 carries a −2 circumstance modifier). So the player who critically fails can never make their Perception and Will actually drop for the minute; they can only read that they should.

defects.name: Ancestral Insight
defects.detail: The two grants are delivered — sheetDiff shows stored.proficiencies.skills['lore:alghollthu'] and ['lore:azlanti'] both moving null→trained (src/rules/featGrantsLane.ts:17), the rows render with full modifiers (MainTab.tsx:182 lists every lore: key), and the builder correctly asks nothing. The defect is the SCOPE of the degree shift. The record's degreeShifts entry (core.json, from scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs:402) is authored `skills: ['lore']`, and targetMatches (situationalBonuses.ts:2996-3008) reads the bare detail 'lore' as a WILDCARD: `if (detail === 'lore' || detail === 'lore:*') return skill.startsWith('lore:')`. So the critical-failure→failure star is painted on EVERY Lore row the character owns — Warfare Lore, Sea Shanties Lore, any lore the player typed — where the text names exactly two. The clause 'on an Alghollthu Lore or Azlanti Lore check to Recall Knowledge' survives in the note's `when`, so the star is self-limiting in prose, but the rows it marks are wider than the feat's own restriction, which is the spurious shape (Ruling C does not widen a clause whose text names its skills). Fixable in the data alone: the same matcher supports exact keys (`detail.startsWith('lore:')` → case-insensitive equality), and featGrantsLane grants exactly those two keys, so `skills: ['lore:alghollthu','lore:azlanti']` would land on the two rows only. The Recall Knowledge action marker (degreeShiftMarkers, explain.ts:308) is correct as authored. ⚠ Harness blind spot, reported not judged: the snapshot's situational sweep iterates only the 16 core SKILLS, so no lore star of any kind appears in sheetDiff — the star's presence and its width were both read from the code path, not observed.

defects.name: Assurance
defects.detail: Sheet half is correct: the chosen skill carries the star and its note reads "take 10 + your proficiency bonus instead of rolling from Assurance — you forgo the roll; no other bonus, penalty or modifier applies" (situationalBonuses.ts:3247), which is exactly the Q20 worked case. Builder half is correct on three of four points — `trainedSkillOptions` (build.ts:1159) offers only trained-or-better skills and includes Lores ("Scribing Lore (T)" in the pack), `maxTakable: null` keeps the feat offered for a second take, and each instance stores its answer under its own slot key so the first pick is not overwritten (measured: two instances at 2:skill:1 and 4:skill:1, both starred). The defect is the Special clause: "Each time, choose a different skill." Measured with Assurance already taken for Athletics, the SECOND instance's picker still lists `athletics` as a live option (12 options: arcana, crafting, occultism, religion, acrobatics, athletics, deception, diplomacy, lore:scribing, medicine, stealth, thievery). `choiceOptionsFor`'s `distinct` filter only removes answers within ONE choice def's picks, and the `kind: 'skills'` branch of `buildChoiceOptions` (build.ts:1303) returns before any narrowing runs — so nothing excludes a skill an earlier Assurance already claimed. The list is wider than the feat's own printed restriction, and the player can build an illegal double-Assurance on one skill.

defects.name: Breath Control
defects.detail: The two mechanical clauses are delivered exactly and are the model case: the +1 stars ALL THREE saves rather than being narrowed to Fortitude (Ruling H / Q2) and is kept out of the flat totals (Ruling B — sheetDiff moves only situational.*), and the success→critical-success upgrade is in the one registry it belongs in (`degreeShifts: [{shift:'successToCrit', when:'on a save against an inhaled threat…', saves:['all']}]`). The '25 times as long' clause needs nothing further: a feat's `note` renders as a 'Note:' paragraph appended to that feat's own description (FeatsTab.tsx:77), which already prints the sentence, and there is no suffocation action or condition for a RecordMarker to attach to — no comparable record (inner-breath, internal-respirator, aqueous-dragonblood) carries one either. THE DEFECT is a duplicate: situationalBonuses.ts:135 hand-copies the shift into its own trigger — when: "against inhaled threats (success becomes critical success)" — while the degreeShifts field states the same rule again. Both land in the same star list for each save (explain.ts:439/564 merge FEAT_SITUATIONAL with the degreeShift-derived entries), so every save popup tells the player the crit upgrade twice, in two different wordings, from two registries that can drift. This is precisely the cleanup the project already made elsewhere — see the comment above 'conceited-mindset' (situationalBonuses.ts:640) where the degree half was stripped out of the `when` once the field could hold it, and the ⚠ on the `degreeShift` lane in docs/mechanic-lanes.md. Fix is to trim the parenthesis so the line carries only '+1 circumstance … against inhaled threats'.

defects.name: Blood Rising
defects.detail: The core of the feat IS delivered: sheetDiff adds actions[0] = "Blood Rising" at its reaction cost, and the popup carries the printed text — Trigger, the blood-magic-off-schedule clause, the two legal targets, the AC/save clause and the duration override. Per Principle E (Minor Omen) that is often the whole requirement, and Q1 keeps the round-scale duration out of the numbers. Builder correctly asks nothing (choiceCount 0). Two residual requirements have no route in this engine. (1) "**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of your bloodline": the record's displayed traits are the static ["sorcerer"] and no field derives a RECORD's own trait line per character — `grantsCreatureTraits` puts traits on YOU, not on the record — so the computed arcane/divine/occult/primal trait can never appear. (2) Principle C's mark on the thing it modifies: blood magic is not a record at all, only a paragraph inside each bloodline class feature's description (`classFeatures/bloodline-draconic` → "**Blood Magic—Scaly Hide** … +1 status bonus to AC for 1 round"), and the shipped marker lanes (`RecordMarker.on` is `'action' | 'condition'` only, `modifiesGrant.actionRider`) cannot target a class feature, so neither the "lasts until the beginning of your next turn" override nor "that bonus applies against the triggering spell" can be written where the player reads their blood magic. Same reason the trigger cannot resolve "the same tradition as your bloodline" to a concrete tradition.

uncertain.name: Adhyabhau
uncertain.detail: Everything measurable is delivered: the Will row carries "+1 circumstance from Adhyabhau — against emotion effects" (situationalBonuses.ts:101, save 'will' only, outside the printed total per Ruling B) and "a success is a critical success instead from Adhyabhau — on a save against an emotion effect" from a single degreeShifts entry (saves:['will']); the sentence is not duplicated across registries, and Fortitude/Reflex carry nothing from this feat. Builder correctly asks nothing. The one unsettled point is the scope the requirements flagged: the promotion clause says "when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect", not "a Will save", so read at its word it also covers a Fortitude or Reflex save against an emotion effect, and Ruling H (where the rules are open, stay open — star everything plausible) points at all three rows. The app has narrowed it to Will, which matches Foundry's own build of this feat (.import-src/.../dhampir/adhyabhau.json gates its AdjustDegreeOfSuccess on selector "will") and matches the sentence's first half; but the narrowing is a ruling and Ruling H says not to make one silently. Changing it is a one-word edit (saves:['will'] -> ['all']) either way.
uncertain.question: Adhyabhau's second clause says "when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect" without naming Will. Should the success-to-critical-success promotion star all three saves against emotion effects (Ruling H — stay open, printed trigger in the note), or stay Will-only as it is built now, matching Foundry and the sentence's first half?

uncertain.name: Ask the Bones
uncertain.detail: The mechanics are delivered: Ask the Bones appears in the actions list as its own entry (actions[0]), the once-per-day frequency gets a real use pip (limitedUses "Ask the Bones: {max:1, per:day}") as Principle O2 requires of a per-day resource, and the +1 circumstance bonus is authored with its trigger. Builder correctly asks nothing. What I cannot settle is the STAR PLACEMENT, where two of the owner's own decisions point opposite ways. The app authors `ask-the-bones` as [{ targets: [{kind:'skill', detail:'all'}], when: "once per day, on the Recall Knowledge check made with Ask the Bones…" , bonus: "+1 circumstance" }], which puts a star on all sixteen skills (the diff shows all sixteen situational entries). Principle P (Posse, Round 4) says a benefit gated behind a deliberate action needs no star because the player already knows they did the thing — and this +1 exists only inside an activity the player deliberately spends, whose popup already carries the sentence. But Mastermind's Eye (answer 6) and Principle C say a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it, and the app has a standing precedent for the exact shape here (`vomit-stomach`: "once per day, on the immediate save Vomit Stomach grants…" stars Fortitude). Both readings are defensible from the record as it stands, so I will not call sixteen stars either correct or spurious. Note the star's `when` is capped with "…" per the capped-notes ruling, so the GM-adjudicated trigger ("if the bones belonged to a person particularly knowledgeable on the subject") is only in the click-through, not on the star line.
uncertain.question: Ask the Bones' +1 circumstance bonus exists only on the Recall Knowledge check made with the feat's own once-per-day activity, and the app currently stars all sixteen skills with it. Principle P (Posse) says a benefit gated behind a deliberate action needs no star; Mastermind's Eye says star every skill that can Recall Knowledge. For a bonus that lives INSIDE a feat's own activity, should the stars stay on every skill, or should it live only in the activity's popup?

uncertain.name: Avenge in Glory
uncertain.detail: DELIVERED: the reaction reaches the actions list (Principle E) with Trigger/Frequency/Access in its description popup; storedFields.limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'} gives the once-per-day pip (sheetDiff shows both); and src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:563 stars BOTH halves of every Strike — targets [{kind:'strikeAttack'}] and [{kind:'strikeDamage'}], bonus '+1 circumstance', when 'while you still have the temporary HP from Avenge in Glory…' — rendered at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:460. (The evidence pack's empty `situational` block is a harness limit: scripts/feat-evidence.mjs:152 only samples ac/perception/save/skill refs, never strike refs.) Builder half is correct: nothing is asked and nothing should be. NOT DELIVERED: the 1-minute state has no mode — no entry in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, no `modes` registry hit — so the temporary Hit Points equal to your level are granted nowhere; the player types them into the temp-HP box by hand. The field could not say it today either: `tempHp` exists only on BattleForm (src/rules/types.ts:3107) and only as a FIXED number, so 'equal to your level' is unauthorable as things stand. I cannot settle whether that absence is a defect because two of your decisions point opposite ways (see question).
uncertain.question: Avenge in Glory is a reaction that grants temporary Hit Points equal to your level for 1 minute, plus a +1 circumstance bonus to attack and damage while you still have them. Q1 ('a longer duration gets a mode') and the Shield the Faithful precedent (1 minute, includes YOU, so its mode carries real numbers) say this should be a MODE that grants tempHp = your level on entry and takes it back on exit — the shape Round 10 built for BattleForm.tempHp. But Q15 says 'temporary Hit Points alone are not complicated', and Principle E says a reaction's entry in the reactions list is often the whole requirement. Today the app gives the reaction row, the 1/day pip and the +1 as a star on both strike rows, and grants no temp HP. Which governs — build the mode (which also needs `tempHp` to accept a level-scaled value outside `battleForm`), or is what ships already the finished shape?

verdicts.name: Aberration Kinship
verdicts.detail: The innate half is right: sheetDiff adds Mindlink to the innate entry at rank 1 (its own base rank, no override asserted), tradition occult, spellSources.mindlink = "Aberration Kinship", and SpellsTab.tsx:1807 renders it as "rank 1 · 1/day · from Aberration Kinship" with a spendable pip (build.ts:4699 leaves innateUses absent because absent means the default 1/day). What is missing is the clause "but you can target only aberrations": the record carries no `spellNotes`, so nothing is written into Mindlink's description. This is the N2 lane and it is built and populated — 64 feats carry `spellNotes`, and azarketi-purification's "You can cast Cleanse Cuisine from this feat only on liquids" is the identical restriction shape, printed under the granting record's name by build.ts:3947 → spellNotesFor → SpellsTab.tsx:2155. As shipped, a player reading Mindlink from this feat sees the spell as printed and would legally target a non-aberration. Builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and nothing should be asked.

verdicts.name: Acrobatic Performer
verdicts.detail: The +1 is delivered correctly: situationalBonuses.ts:99 puts it on Acrobatics as "+1 circumstance" (right type — the printed "circumstances" is a typo) with the restriction in `when` and outside the flat total, which is Ruling B. The SUBSTITUTION is delivered nowhere. The record carries no `skillSubstitutions`, so "You can roll an Acrobatics check instead of a Performance check when using the Perform action" reaches nothing — deriveSkill/explain.ts never see it, and the Perform action never reads as rollable with Acrobatics. The lane exists and 26 feats carry it in exactly this shape (versatile-performance: use Performance instead of Diplomacy to Make an Impression; natural-medicine; sly-disarm). Worse, the single star the feat does produce reads "when you Perform, if trained in both Acrobatics and Performance" with a +1 attached, which welds the substitution's condition to the BONUS's condition: a character trained in Acrobatics but not Performance may still substitute, and the sheet tells them nothing.

verdicts.name: Acupuncturist
verdicts.detail: silentOnBothHalves with no harnessLimits, and DECIDED SCOPE does not excuse it — the lanes doc explicitly keeps "the action's EXISTENCE" as the `grantsAction` lane. The feat teaches a named downtime activity (a day of study, needles stored in healer's tools, one ally, Medicine vs a standard DC for the ALLY'S level) and the app surfaces it as an activity nowhere: the record has no `grantsActions`, there is no `acupuncturist` entry in content.actions, and SKILL_ACTIONS.medicine (skillActions.ts) has no entry for it — that list is precisely where feat-gated Medicine activities live (Battle Medicine, feat: true/featName), and the sibling downtime feat Train Animal is there under Nature. So the activity, its requirement and the ally-level DC are readable only inside the feat's own description on the Feats tab. Measured, this is the pattern rather than a one-off: all 12 downtime-trait feats carry no mechanical field at all. The ally-side +2/+1/-1 and the 1-week lockout correctly produce nothing on this sheet (Ruling F), and the four degrees are present in the feat's own description text, so the only defect is the activity's absence from the activities/skill-action surface.

verdicts.name: Acute Vision
verdicts.detail: The core grant works and the empty sheetDiff is expected: `whileActive:[{state:'rage',senses:[darkvision precise]}]` is read by activeStateGrants (derive.ts:931) and pushed into deriveDefenses' sense map (derive.ts:1991) only while classResources.rage is on, so darkvision arrives with rage and leaves with it — exactly what the text says, and the harness measured a non-raging character. Two ruled requirements are not delivered. (1) Principle C: the rage entry does not reflect the feat. Rage is a bare state toggle (VitalsRail.tsx:935-960) whose only text is the static note in classResources.ts:71 ("Raging: lasts 1 min / until the encounter ends"); nothing aggregates whileActive grants into it, so a barbarian who is not raging can see nowhere that raging will give them darkvision. (2) Q13: senses are stored in a map keyed by NAME with a best-acuity merge and no supersede step, and VitalsRail.tsx:730 prints every entry — so an elf/gnome barbarian raging reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision" where the owner ruled to show only darkvision. docs/gold-set-final.md line 270 records this as a change to shipped behaviour that has not been made; grep confirms no suppression exists. Builder half correct — nothing is asked and nothing should be.

verdicts.name: Adapted Cantrip
verdicts.detail: The whole feat is inert. The record's choice carries `inert: "Recorded only: the cantrip is not added to your prepared options or your repertoire — add it yourself…"`, and the harness confirms it: verdict inert-declared, two different answers moved nothing (`moved:false`, `movedPaths:[]`), silentDefault true, sheetDiff empty. So none of the three delivery clauses land — no addition to the prepared-cantrip options (the dailyChoice lane, which per Q23 belongs in Daily preparations and is not offered there either), no repertoire replacement, and the chosen cantrip is castable nowhere in the class entry. This is not a lane gap: `grantedRepertoire`/grantedRepertoireAdds (build.ts:3796, 3980) already adds spells into a caster's entry, and FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS already grants a chosen cantrip from a filtered list. Builder half fails twice more. (a) Q9 — the picker offers all 115 cantrips with no tradition filter; the record's own note admits it ("the picker can't filter that, because your tradition depends on your class"), yet `OpenChoiceFrom.traditions` exists and the resolver already runs against a concrete character, so a caster is shown their OWN tradition's cantrips, which the feat forbids. (b) the repertoire branch's mandatory question — which cantrip known is given up — is never asked: choiceCount is 1 and no picker over the character's own repertoire is rendered, so a repertoire caster is left in a state the feat does not describe. Noted in passing: the feat prints "spellcasting class feature" as a prerequisite and eligibleHosts still returns fighter/human.

verdicts.name: Adaptive Vision
verdicts.detail: Both clauses are delivered and nothing extra happens. Observed by building a dwarf fighter and reading each save row through explainStat: Fortitude, Reflex and Will all carry "+1 circumstance from Adaptive Vision — against visual effects" AND "a success is a critical success instead from Adaptive Vision — on a save against a visual effect". The +1 lives in situational only (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:100, targets [{kind:'save',detail:'all'}]), outside the printed save totals, which is Ruling B for a restricted bonus, and the bonus type is stated for stacking. The promotion is ONE degreeShifts entry on the record ({shift:'successToCrit', when:'on a save against a visual effect', saves:['all']}) and is NOT also copied into situationalBonuses — the two-registries-drifting failure is avoided. The sheetDiff shows only the situational half because the harness's snapshot calls featSituationalFor (the static registry) and never authoredSituational, so degreeShifts entries are invisible to it; they were verified live instead. Builder correctly asks nothing: the Access line is a prerequisite (Q5) and the record declares no choice.

verdicts.name: Additional Lore
verdicts.detail: Only the first sentence is built. FEAT_GRANTS['additional-lore'] is {loreChoices:1} (src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:22) — a free-text Lore subject, granted trained. THREE things the text promises are absent. (1) "At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory": the record carries no rankUpgrade, and the Lore grant loop (src/rules/build.ts:3435-3441) hardcodes maxRank(cur,'trained') and never applies the `at()` level-upgrade helper the other grants use — so no extra increase is offered at 3/7/15 and the rank never rises. Observed: a level-20 fighter with the feat and subject "Warfare" reads Warfare Lore rank "trained", +22, timeline a single "Trained" at level 1. (2) The repeatable clause is broken at the storage key: maxTakable is null so the feat stays offerable, but the builder binds every instance's input to `${featId}:${index}` (Builder.tsx:1894 loreKey2, read back at build.ts:3436), so two takes share the key `additional-lore:0`. Observed: two takes with subjects Warfare and Sailing produced exactly one lore skill, lore:warfare — the second instance grants nothing and the two instances cannot hold different subcategories, which is the one filtering the text DOES require ("you must select a new subcategory"). (3) The answer is not legible on the feat: the FeatChoice carries no `choice`, so the feat entry reads "Additional Lore" with no subject (twice, if taken twice), and the skill breakdown names the source "a trained skill" rather than the feat. The Lore-already-trained non-filter is fine — free text cannot over-filter.

verdicts.name: Adhyabhau
verdicts.detail: Everything measurable is delivered: the Will row carries "+1 circumstance from Adhyabhau — against emotion effects" (situationalBonuses.ts:101, save 'will' only, outside the printed total per Ruling B) and "a success is a critical success instead from Adhyabhau — on a save against an emotion effect" from a single degreeShifts entry (saves:['will']); the sentence is not duplicated across registries, and Fortitude/Reflex carry nothing from this feat. Builder correctly asks nothing. The one unsettled point is the scope the requirements flagged: the promotion clause says "when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect", not "a Will save", so read at its word it also covers a Fortitude or Reflex save against an emotion effect, and Ruling H (where the rules are open, stay open — star everything plausible) points at all three rows. The app has narrowed it to Will, which matches Foundry's own build of this feat (.import-src/.../dhampir/adhyabhau.json gates its AdjustDegreeOfSuccess on selector "will") and matches the sentence's first half; but the narrowing is a ruling and Ruling H says not to make one silently. Changing it is a one-word edit (saves:['will'] -> ['all']) either way.
verdicts.question: Adhyabhau's second clause says "when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect" without naming Will. Should the success-to-critical-success promotion star all three saves against emotion effects (Ruling H — stay open, printed trigger in the note), or stay Will-only as it is built now, matching Foundry and the sentence's first half?

verdicts.name: Adopted Ancestry
verdicts.detail: The feat's whole payload is unbuilt, and the record says so itself: its choice carries inert = "Recorded only: the chosen ancestry's feats aren't yet offered in your ancestry feat slots — add them through Setup -> Overrides". Confirmed by grep: nothing in src/ reads the `adoptedAncestry` flag, and eligibleFeatsForSlot (src/rules/featSlots.ts:88-99) gates an ancestry slot on f.traits.includes(build.ancestryId), the versatile heritage's own id, heritage-level extraAncestryFeatTraits (the half-elf/half-orc route) or the universal-ancestry trait — there is no hook for a feat-chosen ancestry, so "You can select ancestry feats from the ancestry you chose, in addition to your character's own ancestry" never widens any slot, now or at any later level. The picker itself is also wrong at both edges. Too narrow: its options are a hardcoded 8 (Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Human, Leshy, Orc) with the note "Only ancestries marked common in the app's data are listed" — the app marks 20 ancestries uncommon and 22 rare, including catfolk, hobgoblin, kholo, kobold, lizardfolk, ratfolk, tengu and tripkee, so "another ancestry to which you have access" is hard-blocked rather than reachable with its rarity shown (Ruling H). Too wide: the character's OWN ancestry is offered live — the fighter/human host is shown "Human", the one pick that buys nothing across the whole career (Q21), and it is neither excluded nor greyed with a reason (Q27). The answer IS echoed onto the feat's label, so the "name the adopted ancestry" requirement is met; the sheet half of the grant cannot be judged because the route into it does not exist.

verdicts.name: Adrenaline Rush
verdicts.detail: One of the three sheet requirements is delivered, two are not. Delivered: the Athletics star, situationalBonuses.ts:102 — "+1 status … while Raging, to lift heavy objects, Escape, or Force Open" — correct type, correct restriction, and correctly NOT fanned out to Acrobatics or the unarmed Escape. Missing: (1) "increase your encumbered and maximum Bulk limits by 2" reaches nothing. The lane exists and is read — deriveBulk (src/rules/derive.ts:4094-4136) sums feats' bulkLimitBonus into both encumberedAt (5+Str+bonus) and max (10+Str+bonus), which is exactly the two numbers this clause moves — and this record carries no such field, so a raging barbarian's Bulk thresholds are unchanged and the encumbered/overloaded state never recomputes. Note the field as it stands is unconditional (authored for Beast of Burden), so a flat bulkLimitBonus:2 would be spurious here: the clause needs the rage gate the app already has for other numbers (whileState:'rage', types.ts:630, resource 'rage' in classResources.ts:71). (2) No marker on the actions. The RecordMarker lane is live (17 entries with on:'action' in situationalBonuses.ts, e.g. black-powder-boost marking Leap) and both action records exist as 'escape' and 'force-open' in core.json, but nothing marks either for this feat, so a player reading the Escape or Force Open entry sees no sign of the +1 (Ruling D / Q2's "both"). (3) Nothing ties the feat to the Rage state: it appears in no mode — the barbarian Rage mode is cat-rage (src/rules/modes.ts:219) and carries no mention of it, and there is no modeAdjust row in scripts/data — so the mode the player toggles does not carry this feat's text (Principle B / Q11). Builder correctly asks nothing.

verdicts.name: Adroit Manipulation
verdicts.detail: The sheet half is correct: Thievery moves untrained→trained (skills.thievery.modifier 2→24), and `degreeShifts:[{successToCrit, when:"on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock", skills:[thievery], actions:[pick-a-lock]}]` is Q2's both-surfaces exactly — I confirmed in src/rules/explain.ts that one entry fans out to a Thievery star (authoredSituational, line ~367) AND a pick-a-lock action marker (degreeShiftMarkers, line ~311). The empty situational diff is a HARNESS blind spot, not a gap: feat-evidence.mjs snapshots stars via `featSituationalFor(ids, ref)` with no third argument, so it reads FEAT_SITUATIONAL only and can never see a degreeShifts-derived star. The builder half is where the defect is. The text poses ONE conditional question, and the app renders TWO pickers. (1) The working one is derived: `redundantFallback:true` in featGrantsAuto.ts:23 → Character.skillFallbacks → Builder.tsx:1862, which fires only when the Thievery grant was redundant, is consumed (answerIsRead verdict "read"), and correctly greys every already-trained skill including Thievery ("Already <rank> — pick a skill you are untrained in"), satisfying Q27. (2) Beside it the record's own `choice {flag:'adroitSkill', prompt:'Replacement skill', kind:'skills'}` renders a second "Replacement skill" picker — for EVERY holder, including one untrained in Thievery for whom the text asks nothing — and its 12 options are `trainedSkillOptions(character,'trained')`, i.e. the skills the character is ALREADY trained in (Arcana (E), Crafting (E), Occultism (E), Religion (E), Acrobatics (T) … Scribing Lore (T), Thievery (T)). That is the exact inverse of the legal list (any skill you are NOT trained in, and never Thievery itself), and the answer reaches nothing: `adroitSkill` appears in no file under src/, FEAT_GRANTS['adroit-manipulation'] carries no skillChoices for choiceGrantFor to read, and the harness confirms verdict "echo-only". This is the Exemplar Dedication shape from Round 5 — a phantom question the owner ruled should be deleted. Fix: drop the record's `choice` block from effect-backfill.json and leave the fallback lane to ask the question.

verdicts.name: Advanced Weaponry
verdicts.detail: Two of the feat's three requirements are undelivered, and the record says so itself. BUILDER: the text's first question — "Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks" — is never asked. `declared` is `record.choice` only, choiceCount 1, and that one picker is the TRAIT picker. Its 8 options are exactly right (disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, versatile bludgeoning/piercing/slashing — versatile correctly split three ways), so the second question is fine; the first has no picker at all. This is not a lane gap: the sibling evolution feats pushing-attack and weighty-impact both carry `choice {flag:'pushingAttack', prompt:'Eidolon attack', kind:'array', options:[primary, secondary]}` in effect-backfill.json, which is the same question in the same words. SHEET: the picked trait is never written onto the chosen attack. The record's own `inert` string is the admission — "Recorded only — the app doesn't track traits added to an eidolon's unarmed attacks. Note in your eidolon's notes WHICH attack (primary or secondary) you chose; Grasping Limbs later needs the attack that gained grapple" — and grep confirms `advanced-weaponry`/`advancedWeaponry` appear nowhere under src/. The companion harness limit explains the empty diff but establishes nothing, and the surface plainly exists: deriveEidolon in src/rules/companions.ts builds attacks[0]/attacks[1] each with a `traits: string[]` line, and COMPANION_MODS already lets an owner feat reach them (Ranged Combatant's grantedStrikes, Dual Energy Heart's evoNote, and Pushing Attack's note that NAMES the chosen attack from the player's own answer). Same shape, same file, one entry short. A versatile pick additionally has to make that damage type selectable on the attack, which is the whole mechanical content of three of the eight options. This is the Ranged Combatant ruling again — a companion feat whose entire content is a picker whose answer the eidolon never receives.

verdicts.name: Aegis of the Dissolution
verdicts.detail: The feat's one clause is delivered exactly as Q2 and Ruling B specify, and nothing else happens. All three saves gain a star — situational.fortitude / .reflex / .will each with id `aegis-of-the-dissolution`, `when: "against darkness or shadow effects"`, `bonus: "+1 circumstance"`. The type matches the text (circumstance, not status), the value matches (+1, and textNumbers agrees), the restriction stays in the `when` and is NOT folded into any save total, which is the correct display for a restricted flat bonus. The builder correctly asks nothing (choiceCount 0, no declared choices), which is right: the feat cannot be shut down, so per Q11 it is a passive/situational bonus rather than a mode. No harness limits apply and the diff is complete (sheetDiffTruncated 0).

verdicts.name: Aeonbound
verdicts.detail: Only the resource is built; both mechanical clauses are absent. The record carries exactly one authored field — `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` — and that is the sole entry for `aeonbound` in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (verified by scanning the file; there is no second row). The per-day pip is correctly owed and correctly delivered. MISSING 1 — the degree shift. "When someone rolls a failure or a critical failure on a check to Treat your Wounds, you can... increase the degree of success by one step" is a textbook `degreeShifts` entry (`shift: 'oneBetter'`, `when: 'on a check to Treat your Wounds'`, `skills:['medicine']`, `actions:['treat-wounds']`), which per Q2 would produce both surfaces — a Medicine star and a Treat Wounds marker — from one authored entry. The record has no `degreeShifts` field at all, so neither surface exists, and Q15 does not exempt it (that governs crit-SUCCESS triggers; this fires on a failure).
