Note it must cover BOTH entry degrees, failure and critical failure — the Dragon's Presence omission from Round 10. MISSING 2 — the toolkit waiver. "You and your allies can Treat your Wounds without a healer's toolkit" gets no `note`, no `situational`, and the record appears in no registry (`registries: []`), so the sheet says nothing. Ruling D governs its placement (a clause with no stat row of its own marks the thing it modifies — the Magic Hands/Treat Wounds shape), and Principle A means the ally-facing half still owes an indication on the record it modifies rather than nothing. Wording must keep the narrow scope: it waives the kit only for treating THIS character's wounds. The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and the app asks nothing. The `forced-placement` limit affects only whether this host is offered the feat, not any of the above.

verdicts.name: Aerial Boomerang
verdicts.detail: The impulse does reach the actions list (sheetDiff inserts "Aerial Boomerang" at actions[0], with its 2-action cost and its air/impulse/kineticist/primal traits), but the three numbers the player reads off that entry are gone from the app's own text, and I confirmed this is real damage rather than a truncated evidence pack: public/core-descriptions.json stores "races away from you in a . Each creature in the area takes damage with a save against your class DC." The pristine archive record (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-4206.json) reads "in a 60-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 2d4 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC." So the AREA (60-foot line), the DAMAGE (2d4 slashing) and the SAVE (basic Reflex) were all stripped at import — the signature of the @Template/@Damage/@Check cleaner deleting the value along with the markup. The entry therefore prints an impulse with no area, no dice and no save name, and the heightening line "Level (+2) The damage increases by 1d4" has no base to build on, so a level-20 kineticist who should read 11d4 reads nothing. Two further gaps, both smaller: the record carries no scaling field, so even with the base restored the entry would print the 1st-level line and leave the +1d4-per-2-levels arithmetic to the player; and the 1-action concentrate RETURN action gets no entry of its own (only one action row was added), with its requirements — line of effect to the boomerang, within 60 feet of it — living only in the prose. The record has no entry in effect-backfill.json at all. Nothing else is owed: the damage to creatures in the area and the whirling square land on enemies and the battlefield, the until-end-of-next-turn duration is a Q1 non-implementation, and the class DC already has its own row so no specialStatistic is due. The builder correctly asks nothing.

verdicts.name: Ageless Spirit
verdicts.detail: The record delivers NOTHING on either half. core.json feats/ageless-spirit carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `choice`, no daily choice, no skill grant — and the evidence agrees (`declared: []`, `presentsChoices: []`, `sheetDiff: []`, `silentOnBothHalves: true`, no harnessLimits). Builder/daily half: "During your daily preparations… gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice" is never asked, in the builder OR at Daily preparations. Sheet half: "This proficiency lasts until you prepare again" — no skill row ever moves and nothing is sourced to the feat. The lane is built and the template already exists: its twin `ancient-memories` (ghoran, identical text) carries `choice {flag:'ancientMemoriesSkill', prompt:'Skill remembered from a past life', kind:'skills', daily:true, note:'Trained in this skill until your next daily preparations…'}`. ⚠ Two caveats for whoever authors it: (a) `askedAtDailyPrep` (src/rules/derive.ts:975) deliberately excludes `kind:'skills'` from the Rest sheet, so copying that shape asks the question in the BUILDER, not at daily prep as Q23 requires — the code comment admits "Ancient Memories is the one record in that state today"; (b) `dailyChoiceGrants` (derive.ts:1365) only reads `options[].grant`, so a `kind:'skills'` daily answer grants no rank at all — the twin's answer is prose-only, so copying it would leave the sheet half still dead. The third clause ("you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option") has no lane — the twin carries it as note text only.

verdicts.name: Agile Shield Grip
verdicts.detail: grantsAction is delivered — the diff inserts "Agile Shield Grip" into the actions list as a 1-action activity, and its description carries the "**Requirements** You are wielding a shield with a shield boss or shield spikes in one hand" block plus the switch-back sentence, which satisfies Principle E. The builder half is correctly silent (the feat names no build-time choice). Everything below that is absent: (1) "You reduce your shield boss and shield spikes weapon damage die to 1d4" — no `weaponTraits`/`setDie` rider anywhere; the Strike rows for shield boss and shield spikes keep their printed die (Principle L: reach/die is a VALUE, not an annotation); (2) "your shield boss and shield spike Strikes gain the agile weapon trait" — no trait added, so the row's three attack numbers never recompute onto the agile −4/−8 progression; (3) "You can use Agile Shield Grip again to switch to a normal grip" — per Q11 this is a MODE (it can explicitly be shut down) and no mode exists: `scripts/data/toggle-modes.json` (258 modes) contains no Agile Shield Grip entry, and no registry mentions the feat (`registries: []`). Nothing in the record hints at any of it. ⚠ Note for the fix: the `weaponRider` lane can say it (`WeaponRider.setDie` + `add:['agile']`, match on the two shield weapons) but is always-on, and `ModeDef` has NO weaponTraits/setDie field today (0 of 258 modes carry one), so the toggleable form needs a small field extension — authoring the rider on the feat alone would make the reduced die unconditional, which is the text's own condition removed.

verdicts.name: Air Cushion
verdicts.detail: All four requirements are delivered and nothing extra happens. The reaction enters the actions list (diff: actions[0] ← "Air Cushion", actionCost type 'reaction'), and its description carries the "**Trigger** A creature within 60 feet is falling" meta line plus the full effect text, which per Principle E and Q4 is the whole surface for an effect that lands on the falling creature. No number moves anywhere on the sheet — correct: the target is another creature (Ruling F) and fall damage is HP (Ruling E). "You can't use Air Cushion again while you have one in effect" is carried as printed text with NO `limitedUses` on the record — correct per Principle O2/M2 (a duration-gated restriction is not a per-day resource, so a use pip would have been the defect). Considered and not reported: the "**Level (8th)** The range is 120 feet…" block is printed verbatim to every kineticist rather than resolved for the character's level (nothing in src/ gates description blocks by level; the `innateGate`/minLevel lane covers spell GRANTS, not an action's own text). I judged this delivered rather than defective — the block is explicitly labelled with its level, which is how the book and AoN print it, and no owner ruling covers level-gated description text. Flagging it here in case the owner wants that as a new display lane, since it would apply to every kineticist impulse.

verdicts.name: Alabaster Eyes
verdicts.detail: The grant itself works: `senses:[{name:'darkvision'}]` is authored and the diff shows defenses.senses[1] ← "darkvision". Two things happen that the feat's text does not call for. SHEET: the vishkanya ancestry's low-light vision is still printed beside it — the diff adds darkvision at index 1 while index 0 (the ancestry `vision: 'low-light-vision'` baseline added at derive.ts:2039) is untouched, and neither `deriveDefenses` nor VitalsRail.tsx:730 / DetailsTab.tsx:443 suppresses a superseded sense, so the row reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision". Q13 rules exactly this case ("Show only darkvision when it supersedes low-light", 9 feats) — the supersede exists nowhere in the app, so no darkvision-granting feat on a low-light ancestry obeys it. BUILDER: "**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level" is not enforced — no field in src/rules/types.ts can express a take-at-this-level-only restriction (searched: no onlyAtLevel/maxTakeLevel/firstLevelOnly; `maxLevel` is a choice-option filter), so this level-1 ancestry feat is offered in the 5th/9th/13th/17th-level ancestry slots too, an option list wider than the feat's own printed restriction (Q9). The retraining half of the same clause is moot rather than broken — the app has no retraining feature at all (only one incidental mention, in featUses.ts). That availability restriction is a genuine "no lane at all" candidate; the sense-supersede is a built-lane display fix.

verdicts.name: Alchemical Assessment
verdicts.detail: Silent on both halves, and the builder silence is correct (the feat asks nothing). The sheet half delivers none of its only content. "When using the Crafting skill to Identify Alchemy on an alchemical item you hold, you can do so as a single action, rather than spending 10 minutes" is exactly the owner's Quick Recognition specification (Principle H — the action appears under BOTH costs with the explanation in the popup), and Identify Alchemy still shows only its native cost: src/rules/actions.ts:109 lists it as an exploration action and src/rules/skillActions.ts:294 prints `costText: "10 minutes"`, with no 1-action form and no mark from this feat. `registries: []` confirms no RECORD_MARKERS entry, so the Ruling D / Q8 marker on the modified action (carrying the two conditions — alchemical item, held) does not exist either. The record's only surface is a description cross-link (`r: [{label:'Identify Alchemy', key:'actions'}]`) on the feat's own popup, which is the reverse direction from what Ruling D asks: the mark belongs on Identify Alchemy, the thing the player is looking at when it matters. The lane exists — RECORD_MARKERS/`actionRider` already render `{on:'action', id, value, note}` rows for other records — so this is unauthored, not unbuildable. Correctly NOT reported: no `*` is owed on the Crafting row (no number moves).

verdicts.name: Alchemical Crafting
verdicts.detail: Both halves deliver, and the empty `builder.presentsChoices` in the pack is a HARNESS BLIND SPOT, not a defect: scripts/builder-evidence.mjs never scans FORMULA_GRANTS, which is where this feat's picker is declared. Verified by driving the real resolvers (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/formulaBook.ts + src/builder/shared.tsx FormulaBookCard): a level-1 fighter taking the feat gets exactly 4 slots labelled 'Common 1st-level alchemical item', each offering a 138-item pool that is 100% alchemical, 100% common, max level 1 — the printed restriction, filtered (Q9) — and the count stays 4 at level 5, so the one-time 'when you select this feat' grant does not scale. The sheetDiff's inventory write (formula-book-blank, grantedBy 'Alchemical Crafting') is Q14 #6. The picks are written into the BOOK's own state (build.ts:4517) against a separate spent ledger (formulaPicks), so losing the book loses them and the feat does not re-grant (Q14 #9); FormulaBookPanel gives reference-only rows '<item> formula', remove, search, capacity 100, and empty slots that open this feat's filtered list (Q14 #1-#5, #8). The Craft permission is a real, feat-gated surface: SKILL_ACTIONS.crafting carries an 'Alchemical Crafting' row (feat: true) reading 'lets you use the Craft activity to create alchemical items… Without it you cannot Craft alchemical items', and Q19's craftable pool is wired (craftableFormulas -> AlchemyPanel). Two nuances I could see but would not call defects: the Craft ROW itself carries no `*` (RECORD_MARKERS has no 'craft' entry) — the app's convention for skill feats that modify an activity is a row of their own, used identically for Forager/PlanarЫрogether with Magical Crafting; and the builder pool does not grey a formula the book already holds, so picking the same item in two slots silently collapses to one write (a Q27 display gap in the shared formula picker, not specific to this feat).

verdicts.name: Alchemical Familiar
verdicts.detail: The companion-tab harness limit explains the silent diff, so I judged from source. The familiar itself is granted (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['alchemical-familiar'], a synthetic Companions-tab card), but three of the feat's four clauses fail. (1) MISSING, sheet: 'The familiar uses your Intelligence modifier to determine its Perception, Acrobatics, and Stealth modifiers' has no surface at all — FamiliarBlock (src/rules/companions.ts:576-683) has no Acrobatics or Stealth field, and its Perception is copied wholesale from the master via masterDefenses() (Wisdom + the master's proficiency), so the Int rule is neither applied nor shown, and it cannot track Int as it changes. (2) SPURIOUS, sheet: the grant is authored lockedAbilities: ['construct','tough'], but the text says Construct here 'doesn't require the familiar to have the Tough familiar ability'. Tough is therefore handed over unasked, and deriveFamiliar's hasTough raises the familiar to (5+2) x level HP — a benefit the printed waiver denies. The card's own note repeats the error: 'It always has Construct (a construct-trait familiar; requires and includes Tough).' (3) MISSING, builder: 'doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2)' is not modelled. `abilityBudget: 2` is read by nothing in src/ — CompanionsTab.tsx:1457 seeds only lockedAbilities, and it seeds them INTO cfg.abilities, the same array the player's own picks live in. FamiliarAbilityPicker shows only '2 chosen' with no budget and no remaining count, so the count reads as fully spent before the player has chosen anything — precisely the failure mode the clause exists to prevent — and nothing marks Construct as permanent, so the player can toggle it off. Minor: the card attributes it as 'Granted by a feat' without naming Alchemical Familiar (grant.label is never rendered; kindMeta returns the generic 'Familiar').

verdicts.name: Alchemical Scholar
verdicts.detail: The two formula clauses work; the redundancy clause does not exist. VERIFIED WORKING: a hobgoblin fighter gets Alchemical Crafting as a bonus feat (grantedBy 'alchemical-scholar') and its four filtered slots fire from the grant, plus 1 slot for the 'additional common 1st-level alchemical formula' and level-1 slots for the per-level clause (6 slots at level 7), all writing into the granted book. MISSING (builder + sheet): 'If you would automatically gain that feat… you instead gain a different 1st-level Crafting skill feat.' Nothing implements it. FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS is documented as 'Deduped against feats the character already has', and featGrantsAuto's `redundantFallback` is a SKILL-training fallback, not a feat one. Measured: a level-7 hobgoblin ALCHEMIST with Alchemical Scholar ends up with alchemical-crafting granted by 'alchemy' (the class feature) and Alchemical Scholar's grant silently swallowed — no picker is offered, no substitute feat appears, and the player loses a whole 1st-level Crafting skill feat with no sign anything happened. The option list the text specifies (Crafting skill feats of level 1, Alchemical Crafting excluded) exists nowhere. SECONDARY, spurious width (builder): the per-level clause says 'one common alchemical formula OF THAT LEVEL', but FORMULA_GRANTS['alchemical-scholar'].parts[1] uses maxLevel 'self', so every one of the six slots on a 7th-level character offers the same 369-item pool spanning levels 0-7 rather than one 2nd-level pick, one 3rd, and so on — a list wider than the feat's own restriction (Q9), and materially more generous.

verdicts.name: Alghollthu Bound
verdicts.detail: The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and nothing is rendered. On the sheet, Will carries two lines (confirmed by calling explainStat on an azarketi holding the feat): '+2 circumstance from Alghollthu Bound — against mental effects that would make you controlled' (situationalBonuses.ts:107, correctly outside the flat total per Ruling B) and 'a success is a critical success instead … unless the effect originates from an alghollthu' (the record's own degreeShifts entry, in the one registry, correctly scoped to will). Two things are missing, and they are the same half of the sentence. (a) The second, OPPOSITE-SIGNED entry — '-2 circumstance … against mental effects from alghollthus' — has no entry anywhere: no situational row, no note, on any save. Per Ruling H the text names no roll ('against mental effects', not 'to Will saves'), so it should surface on every save it could plausibly apply to; today it surfaces on none. (b) The +2 line's `when` omits the alghollthu carve-out that the degreeShift line does carry, so the star reads '+2 circumstance … against mental effects that would make you controlled' with no exception stated — false at exactly the table where an azarketi's flavour makes it likeliest to come up. This is the Round-10 Dragon's Presence shape: the record shipped with the good news and hid the bad.

verdicts.name: All of the Animal
verdicts.detail: Silent on both halves, with no harness limit to explain it — and the builder silence is correct (Principle M2: the corpse is an object in the fiction, re-chosen every use, so no picker and no free-text field is owed). The sheet half delivers nothing. Confirmed by driving the real display paths on a fighter holding the feat: explainStat(skill: survival).situational is [] and recordMarkersFor(action 'subsist') is [] — the record carries no `situational`, no RECORD_MARKERS entry, and appears in no registry (registries: []). Both owed surfaces are absent: the `*` on SURVIVAL carrying the clause (owed under Q20's refinement even though no number moves — the clause names a specific stat, the Assurance shape), and the marker on the SUBSIST action itself (Q2 'both', Ruling D — a player about to Subsist is looking at Subsist). The 'subsist' action id exists in core.json and StatDetailModal already renders action marks from RECORD_MARKERS, so the lane is built and simply unused here. Note that the app's other Subsist-modifying skill feats (Forager, Planar Survival) each have a row in SKILL_ACTIONS.survival; All of the Animal has neither a row nor a mark, so it exists only in the feats list.

verdicts.name: All This Will Happen Again
verdicts.detail: Both halves delivered. Sheet: the reaction enters the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0]), its popup carries the verbatim Trigger and BOTH halves of the effect (the reroll and "you must use the second result, even if it's worse"), and the +1 status sits in `situational.will` with when="reroll a failed save vs an emotion effect (keep the 2nd result)" — Ruling B's shape, and the diff shows saves.will is unmoved, so nothing was folded into the total. The Minor Omen ruling ("no need for it to impact the sheet in another way") is permissive, not prohibitive, so the extra Will star is not spurious. Builder: correctly asks nothing. ⚠ ONE DATA OBSERVATION, not a defect in delivery: the requirement-reader concluded "the text prints no Frequency line, so no per-day use pip is owed" — that premise is wrong, and it is wrong because of the app's own copy. AoN feat-6894 prints "**Frequency** once per day" (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-6894.json), so `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` and the use pip are RIGHT. But the description in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core-descriptions.json drops that line, while 549 other feat descriptions keep it — including its own sibling all-this-has-happened-before, same book, which reads "**Frequency** once per day\n\n**Trigger** …". Worth a one-record text fix so the popup states the limit in words as well as in pips.

verdicts.name: Ambersoul
verdicts.detail: `silentOnBothHalves` is legitimate here, on two settled rulings rather than on an absence of evidence. The only number the feat states — a –1 circumstance penalty on ATTACK ROLLS WITH THAT WEAPON — lands on the creature that hit you, and DECIDED SCOPE / Ruling F+N covers target-side numbers exactly ("this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm"); it also expires at the end of that creature's turn, which Q1 puts in the indication-only bucket. Q11 correctly makes it a passive rather than a mode (the sap cannot be shut down). The `note` requirement is met by the feat's own description, which survives intact with all four conditions (slashing OR piercing, melee Strike, each time, attaches to the weapon not the creature), and there is no other record of the character's to mark. Contrast its sibling `brightsoul`, whose penalty falls on the character's OWN Stealth and which correctly does carry a situational entry — the registries differ because the texts differ. Builder correctly asks nothing. REACHABILITY, checked rather than assumed, because `nativeHostEligible:false` looks alarming: the Ardande versatile heritage ships (core.json heritages.ardande, versatile:true, grantsCreatureTraits:['ardande']) and featSlots.ts:91 admits a versatile heritage's own feats into ancestry slots, so the feat is takeable. The false eligibility reading is the `forced-placement` harness limit — the host was a plain human.

verdicts.name: Ammunition Thaumaturgy
verdicts.detail: The clause "You can Interact to reload a weapon using the hand holding your implement" reaches no surface but the feat's own description. The record carries no fields beyond level/category/rarity/actionCost/edition/aonId, `registries` is empty, and grepping src/, scripts/data/ and test/ for `ammunition-thaumaturgy` returns NOTHING — so no note, no marker, no rider. Ruling D as confirmed by Q8 ("Yes — mark the action the feat modifies") is unambiguous for this shape, and both the lane and its target already exist: RECORD_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3332) renders `{on:'action', id, note}` through recordMarkersFor (src/rules/explain.ts:465), and core.json actions contains BOTH `reload` and `interact`. Nearby precedents in the same registry mark exactly this kind of permission — 'feather-step' on `step`, 'sure-feet' on `balance`/`climb`, 'perfect-readiness' whose note even says "the extra action can be used only to Step or to Interact to reload". The builder half is correct (the feat rightly asks nothing — which weapon and which implement are facts of the moment). Fix is one RECORD_MARKERS entry on `reload` (and/or `interact`).

verdicts.name: Anadi Lore
verdicts.detail: The redundancy clause is not built. src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:28 reads `'anadi-lore': { skills: { crafting: 'trained', survival: 'trained', 'lore:anadi': 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true` — while the same file gives that flag to every sibling carrying the identical sentence: `android-lore` (line 30), `azarketi-lore` (65), `conrasu-lore` (97), `automaton-lore` (61), `awakened-animal-lore` (63). AoN feat-2762 confirms the clause is printed: "If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you become trained in a skill of your choice." src/rules/build.ts:3384 is the only site that acts on it — it pushes `skillFallbacks` (which Builder.tsx:1862 turns into the substitute picker) and applies `<featId>:fallback:<skill>`, both guarded on `g.redundantFallback`. So for any anadi whose class or background already trains Crafting or Survival: BUILDER — the substitute-skill picker never renders, the player is never asked (this is why `presentsChoices` is empty; the harness host was a fighter, for whom the clause does not fire, so the empty picker list there is expected and proves nothing either way); SHEET — no replacement skill is trained, and the grant is silently lost. The other three grants ARE correct: Crafting and Survival move in the diff, and `lore:anadi` reaches the sheet as its own row (MainTab.tsx:182 builds Lore rows from stored proficiencies) — its absence from sheetDiff is a harness gap, since scripts/feat-evidence.mjs:127 snapshots only the 16 core SKILLS. Note the engine's existing shape already handles the reader's flagged double-overlap case (one fallback pushed per redundant key, each with its own answer slot), so the fix really is the one missing flag.

verdicts.name: Ancestral Blood Magic
verdicts.detail: Nothing is delivered on either requirement. The record carries no fields at all, `registries` is empty, and `ancestral-blood-magic` appears NOWHERE in src/, scripts/data/ or test/. (1) Principle C — the record whose grant this widens says nothing about it. Blood magic is surfaced today on the bloodline features themselves (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:996-1001: `bloodline-draconic` → "for 1 round after your blood magic triggers…", and 20-odd siblings), and those entries are unchanged and unattributed, so a sorcerer reading their bloodline still sees only the printed triggers. (2) Q8 / Principle N2 — no mark on the qualifying spells. ⚠ The two halves are not equally buildable, and I am separating them rather than lumping them: the SPELL half has a real route (build.ts:3939 `pushSpellNote` + spellNotesFor → SpellsTab.tsx:2155), it simply needs a derived pass because the qualifying set is per-character (non-cantrip spells whose source is a heritage or an ancestry feat) and the static `spellNotes` array is keyed by literal spellId; that is unauthored work, not a missing capability. The FEATURE half may be a genuine field gap: `GrantModification` (types.ts:1042) can only say `innateUsesPerDay`, `actionRider` (which renders as a RecordMarker on an ACTION or CONDITION row) or `deityDomainsFromChoice`, and blood magic is a class feature, not an action or a condition — so there is no gated way today to add a line to another FEATURE's entry. Per the doc's own Round-10 lesson, that is the field being unable to say it rather than the text not saying it. Builder half is correct: the feat rightly asks nothing.

verdicts.name: Ancestral Insight
verdicts.detail: The two grants are delivered — sheetDiff shows stored.proficiencies.skills['lore:alghollthu'] and ['lore:azlanti'] both moving null→trained (src/rules/featGrantsLane.ts:17), the rows render with full modifiers (MainTab.tsx:182 lists every lore: key), and the builder correctly asks nothing. The defect is the SCOPE of the degree shift. The record's degreeShifts entry (core.json, from scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs:402) is authored `skills: ['lore']`, and targetMatches (situationalBonuses.ts:2996-3008) reads the bare detail 'lore' as a WILDCARD: `if (detail === 'lore' || detail === 'lore:*') return skill.startsWith('lore:')`. So the critical-failure→failure star is painted on EVERY Lore row the character owns — Warfare Lore, Sea Shanties Lore, any lore the player typed — where the text names exactly two. The clause 'on an Alghollthu Lore or Azlanti Lore check to Recall Knowledge' survives in the note's `when`, so the star is self-limiting in prose, but the rows it marks are wider than the feat's own restriction, which is the spurious shape (Ruling C does not widen a clause whose text names its skills). Fixable in the data alone: the same matcher supports exact keys (`detail.startsWith('lore:')` → case-insensitive equality), and featGrantsLane grants exactly those two keys, so `skills: ['lore:alghollthu','lore:azlanti']` would land on the two rows only. The Recall Knowledge action marker (degreeShiftMarkers, explain.ts:308) is correct as authored. ⚠ Harness blind spot, reported not judged: the snapshot's situational sweep iterates only the 16 core SKILLS, so no lore star of any kind appears in sheetDiff — the star's presence and its width were both read from the code path, not observed.

verdicts.name: Ancestral Linguistics
verdicts.detail: The record delivers nothing at all, on either half. core.json carries only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `choice`, no `dailyChoices`, no `languageChoices`, no `passiveEffects.grantsLanguages`. registries is empty, no src file mentions the id, sheetDiff is empty and the builder renders zero pickers (crossChecks.silentOnBothHalves = true, and no harnessLimit excuses it: the harness did NOT flag `daily-choice`, because there is no daily choice on the record to flag). BUILDER half: 58 feats carry `choice.daily`; this is not one, so the language pick is asked NOWHERE — not in the builder (which is correct per Q23) and not at Daily preparations (dailyChoicesFor walks ownedDailyChoiceRecords looking for `choice.daily`, finds nothing here). The two-tier legal list the text specifies (every common language, plus any other language you have access to) therefore does not exist either. SHEET half: no language ever reaches the languages list, so the 'you know this language until you prepare again' temporary marking and the clear-and-re-pick at the next preparation have nothing to attach to; and the 'can't be used as a prerequisite for a permanent character option' exclusion is moot because no grant is ever made. A 1st-level elf ancestry feat that is completely inert.

verdicts.name: Ancestral Longevity
verdicts.detail: Completely inert, same shape as Ancestral Linguistics. core.json carries no `choice`, no `dailyChoices`, no `trainedSkillChoice`; FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS (src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts) has no 'ancestral-longevity' key — its near-twin 'ancient-memories' at line 29 does; registries is empty; sheetDiff is empty; the builder renders zero pickers; crossChecks.silentOnBothHalves = true with no harnessLimit. BUILDER half: the daily skill pick is asked nowhere. It cannot be asked at Daily preparations (dailyChoicesFor only reaches records with `choice.daily`), and it is not asked in the builder either, so the 'one skill of your choice' pick, the skippable 'you CAN', and the re-ask every day are all absent. SHEET half: no skill row ever moves, so the trained rank, its recomputed modifier, the 'lasts until you prepare again' marking, and the two prerequisite exclusions (not a base for a skill increase, not a prerequisite for a permanent option) are all undelivered. ⚠ Worth the owner's attention as a family: the follow-up Expert Longevity DOES carry a `choice`, so the record it is defined against grants nothing for it to upgrade.

verdicts.name: Ancestral Mind
verdicts.detail: The app does implement a retune — `entryRetune: [{ scope: 'innate', tradition: 'occult', keyAbilityFromClass: 'psychic' }]` (scripts/backfill-entry-retune.mjs:23) — but it is applied FAR wider than the text. build.ts:4762 resolves scope 'innate' as `spellcasting.find(e => e.type === 'innate')`, and there is exactly ONE pooled 'innate-casting' entry (build.ts:4713) that collects innate spells from the heritage (4617), the BACKGROUND (4625), every INVESTED ITEM (4634), every FEAT including class feats (4641), resolved effect-choices and pick-a-cantrip grants. The text's filter — 'innate spells you know from an ancestry feat or heritage' — is the load-bearing part of the requirement, and nothing honours it: a psychic with an Astrological Augur background (divine Augury) or an invested Cloak of Elvenkind (arcane Ghost Sound) has THOSE spells relabelled occult and re-based onto the psychic attribute too. Wrong tradition is a wrong value, not a cosmetic one. Two further gaps on the same half: (1) no attribution anywhere — the record carries no `spellNotes`, and entryRetune only mutates tradition/keyAbility, so nothing on the Spells page names Ancestral Mind as the reason (requirement 1, principle N2/C, and the 'why does this DC differ' half of requirement 3); (2) the attribute remap is a no-op as shipped, because the pooled innate entry already defaults to `keyAbility: caster?.keyAbility` (build.ts:4715) — a psychic's innate spells use the psychic attribute with or without this feat, so the feat's own benefit is invisible and Q10's 'apply the remap only when it makes the player better' is untestable. ⚠ The per-subset scope may need a lane rather than data: one pooled innate entry cannot carry two traditions, though `innateSource`/`spellSources` already records WHICH record granted each innate spell, so the information to split them exists. ⚠ Evidence note: sheetDiff is empty because the psychic host owns no innate spells (a host-owns-nothing shape the harness did not flag); everything above is read from the code path, not observed.

verdicts.name: Ancient Memories
verdicts.detail: The skill grant works — sheetDiff moves acrobatics untrained→trained and its modifier 1→23 — but every rule the text puts AROUND that grant is undelivered, and the app asks the one question twice. (1) The daily pick is never asked at Daily preparations. The record's `choice` is `{ kind: 'skills', daily: true }`, and askedAtDailyPrep (derive.ts:976) requires kind 'array'/'text'/'open', so dailyChoicesFor skips it — the app's own comment names this record: 'Ancient Memories is the one record in that state today'. Measured: 58 feats carry choice.daily and this is the only one with kind 'skills'. So per Q23 it renders in the wrong place (the builder) and never in the right one. (2) That builder picker's OPTION LIST is inverted. kind 'skills' resolves through trainedSkillOptions (build.ts:1159/1303), which returns the skills the character is ALREADY trained in — the evidence's 12 options are Arcana (E), Crafting (E), … Acrobatics (T) — i.e. every option is a wasted grant (Q21/Q27) and no untrained skill, the only kind the feat can help, can be picked at all. Its answer moves nothing (verdict 'daily', echoed). (3) A SECOND picker asks the same question: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['ancient-memories'] = { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] } (featGrantsAuto.ts:29) renders 'Trained skill' with all 16 skills, its answer IS read (moves intimidation), and it silently defaults — pickersLeftBlank 2, silentDefaults on both, and the unanswered build still trains Acrobatics (featSkillChoiceValue defaults to the slot's first option). (4) The rank it writes is PERMANENT and indistinguishable from a real one: it lands in stored.proficiencies.skills, which is what the prerequisite test and skill increases read, so the two exclusions the text makes — not a prerequisite for a permanent option, not a base a skill increase raises — are both violated, and nothing on the skill row says 'until you prepare again' (the temporary note lives on the dead daily picker, not on the grant that moved the sheet). Sheet half: the number moves (correct) but reads permanent (missing). Builder half: asked in the wrong place, asked twice, and with an option list that excludes the only useful answers.

verdicts.name: Android Lore
verdicts.detail: Both halves deliver. SHEET: sheetDiff moves crafting and thievery untrained->trained (modifier 1->23, 2->24) and adds stored.proficiencies.skills['lore:android'] = trained; MainTab.tsx:183 renders every 'lore:' proficiency key as its own rollable skill row, so Android Lore appears on the skills list. BUILDER: featGrantsAuto['android-lore'] carries redundantFallback:true and build.ts:3384 fires it only when the character's existing rank already equals the grant (maxRank(cur,at(r))===cur) — verified by probe: a fighter already trained in crafting+thievery yields skillFallbacks [{crafting},{thievery}], one replacement picker each, and both answers are 'read' (the picked skill becomes trained); the redundant grant is skipped by `continue`, so the training moves rather than stacking. The 16-skill option list includes already-trained skills, which is the SHOWN-AND-GREYED bucket of Q27, not a Q9 filtering defect, and this evidence cannot see greying. One nuance noted, not counted as a defect: when BOTH named skills are already trained the app grants TWO replacement picks; the printed text ('one of those skills') does not state the double case, but per-skill conversion is the natural reading.

verdicts.name: Angelkin
verdicts.detail: Two of the four promises are undelivered. SHEET — 'You know the Empyrean language' never reaches the sheet: the record carries no grantsLanguages, no feat in core.json carries that field at all (only 2 heritages do), and a probe build of a human fighter holding Angelkin returns languages ['common']. build.ts:5065 already reads content.feats[id].grantsLanguages, so the lane exists and the record is simply unauthored — grantsLanguages:['empyrean'] ('empyrean' is a live id in the 120-entry languages bucket). BUILDER — the redundancy clause is not registered: featGrantsAuto.ts:31 is 'angelkin': { skills: { society: 'trained' } } with NO redundantFallback:true (android-lore, whose clause is identical in shape, has it). Probe with Society already trained: skillFallbacks is null, no replacement picker is rendered, and the grant is silently wasted — the player is never asked. Delivered correctly: Society trained (diff 0->22) and the granted skill feat, which lands as a real owned feat (stored.feats[multilingual].grantedBy = 'angelkin') whose own two language slots flow through recordLanguageSlots, so the granted feat's choice is offered.

verdicts.name: Animal Accomplice
verdicts.detail: The empty sheetDiff is the companion-tab harness limit, not silence: FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['animal-accomplice'] = { kind:'familiar', abilityBudget:2 }, and CompanionsTab.tsx:1455 materialises a card for every such grant the moment the feat is owned, with the familiar-ability picker (2, the general familiar allotment) and its own inventory. Nothing lands on the character's own stat rows, which is the standing companion ruling rather than a gap. The 'type of animal is up to you' clause is served by the card's free-text Name field (Principle I) and is NOT filtered to burrowing animals — no filter of any kind is applied and no burrow Speed is granted, which is what the text (advice, not a restriction) requires. The rapport sentence promises nothing and nothing is invented for it.

verdicts.name: Animal Companion
verdicts.detail: Both harness limits (pick-a-feat-grant, companion-tab) explain the empty diff; read from the source instead. FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['animal-companion'] = { kind:'animal' } auto-creates a companion card seeded maturity 'young' (CompanionsTab.tsx:187/1457) — the feat's own word, and the maturity segment defaults to young until a Mature/Incredible feat raises the floor via COMPANION_MODS.maturityFloor. The mandatory 'which animal' question IS asked, on the companion's Edit tab (CompanionsTab.tsx:1231 'Companion type' select over all 98 animalCompanions records, construct types split out); no class-specific narrowing is invented. The stat block is full and rollable — deriveAnimalCompanion computes AC, HP, saves, Perception, Speeds, senses and unarmed attacks per maturity, and the card prints the type's Support benefit and Advanced maneuver (CompanionsTab.tsx:742-756). Nothing lands on the character's own rows, per the companion ruling.

verdicts.name: Animal Companion (Ranger)
verdicts.detail: The companion half is delivered (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['animal-companion-ranger'] = { kind:'animal' } -> auto card, young by default, full type picker and young stat block with support + advanced maneuver). What is missing is the second sentence: 'When you Hunt Prey, your animal companion gains the action's benefits and your hunter's edge benefit if you have one.' It appears nowhere. The record carries no `note`; the only mention of this id in all of src/ is companionGrants.ts:50, whose note is the generic 'Grants an animal companion — choose its type and advance it in the Edit tab' and says nothing about Hunt Prey or the edge; registries lists companionGrants only, so situationalBonuses has no entry. Both routes the owner's rulings call for already exist and are unused here: an action marker on Hunt Prey (situationalBonuses.ts:3441 shows the exact shape — swift-prey uses { on:'action', id:'hunt-prey', note }, Ruling D / Q8), and a note on the COMPANION's own card (COMPANION_MODS[...].note, rendered through modNotes in companions.ts:519). So a precision ranger's companion shares the precision damage, and a flurry ranger's companion its MAP progression, with nothing on either sheet saying so. Missing, not no_lane. The 'if you have one' conditional means the authored note must name the edge the character actually has.

verdicts.name: Animal Elocutionist
verdicts.detail: The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and renders no picker. One of three sheet clauses is delivered: "+1 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on animals" is in FEAT_SITUATIONAL (situationalBonuses.ts:116) as a Diplomacy entry, when="to Make an Impression on animals", bonus="+1 circumstance" — right type, right restriction, kept out of the Diplomacy total per Ruling B. Two clauses are undelivered. (1) "You hear animal sounds as conversations… and you can respond in turn" / "you can ask questions of, receive answers from… animals" reaches no surface at all: the record carries no grantsLanguages, no note, no second situational entry, so nothing on the Details tab, the Vitals rail or the Diplomacy row tells the player they can speak with animals. This is a 24-record family (burrow-elocutionist, green-tongue, aquatic-conversationalist, reptile-speaker, croak-talker, wave-speaker, plant-empathy, natural-ambassador, familiars-language …) sharing the phrase and carrying nothing; the earlier audit-500 pass reached the same finding on ratspeak. The lane exists (mechanic-lanes D: `language` = "You can speak with Y"; lane J: `note` for a clause worth printing but not computable), so this is promised-but-empty, not a missing lane — the owner still has to choose the shape (a pill in the languages/senses row vs a printed note), since core.languages has 120 real language slugs and no animal-speech one. (2) Q2/Q8: the ACTION half is absent. Make an Impression is a rendered row inside the Diplomacy stat-detail modal (skillActions.ts SKILL_ACTIONS.diplomacy → StatDetailModal.tsx:185 recordMarkersFor(…,'action',…)), and RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3332, 106 entries) has no entry for this feat and no `make-an-impression` mark at all, so the value never appears where the player reads that action.

verdicts.name: Animal Empathy
verdicts.detail: silentOnBothHalves, and only one half of that is correct. The builder correctly asks nothing (no choice, no effectChoices, no picker — the text offers no options). The sheet delivers nothing at all: storedFields carry only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/aonId, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and the harness reports no harnessLimits — so the emptiness is the app, not the measurement. Two things are owed. (1) The rudimentary two-way animal communication ("ask questions of, receive answers from") has no surface — same 24-record family gap as Animal Elocutionist, and the word RUDIMENTARY has to survive to the player so this does not read as full conversation. (2) A `*` on Diplomacy saying Diplomacy can be used on animals: FEAT_SITUATIONAL has no entry for this id, so the Diplomacy row carries nothing back to the feat. Correct by omission, and worth stating so nobody "fixes" it: this feat grants NO bonus, so the absence of any modifier on Diplomacy is right — only the star and the communication statement are missing.

verdicts.name: Animal Empathy (Druid)
verdicts.detail: Mechanically identical to Animal Empathy and identically empty: no registries, no stored mechanical fields, empty sheetDiff, no harnessLimits. Builder correctly asks nothing (the "Archetypes Beastmaster (Level 4), Mammoth Lord (Level 4)" line is availability metadata and is correctly NOT rendered as a picker). Missing: the rudimentary animal-communication statement, and the `*` on Diplomacy for "you can use Diplomacy with animals" — no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry exists for this id. Again correctly no modifier, since the feat grants no bonus. Two record-level observations the owner should see with this one: (a) the description begins with a bibliographic header glued to the rules prose — "Animal Empathy (Druid) Source Player Core pg. 127 Archetypes Beastmaster (Level 4), Mammoth Lord (Level 4)" — import damage of the Exemplar-Dedication family, rendered to the player as if it were rules text; (b) it shares aonId feat-4709 with `animal-empathy` and prints the same rules, so the feat list offers the same feat twice under two names.

verdicts.name: Animal Senses
verdicts.detail: What works: the effectChoice picker ("Choose a sense from your inherent animal") offers exactly the three printed options and the answer is READ — picking scent moves defenses.senses[1].name/.range/.acuity to scent / 30 / imprecise, so the sense shape prints completely. Four defects around it. (1) BUILDER, spurious duplicate: the record also carries a top-level `choice` (flag `animalSenses`, prompt stored literally as "Prompt") which the builder renders as a SECOND dropdown for the same question (Builder.tsx:1817 renderChoice, key `1:ancestry:0`), and its answer is read by nothing — no occurrence of `animalSenses` anywhere in src/, and featChoices[<slot>] has no reader for this flag. Verdict echo-only with silentDefault: the player answers the sense question twice, one answer is inert. Exemplar Dedication's precedent applies — delete it, or make it the per-taking store (see 3). (2) BUILDER, missing gate: "You must have low-light vision before you can gain darkvision with this feat" is enforced nowhere. EffectChoice options (types.ts:1332) have no gate/disabled/reason field, and the picker (Builder.tsx:1974) renders every option live, so the harness's human fighter — normal vision — was offered Darkvision as a live pick. This is the Q9 half (Manifold Modifications shape), not the Q27 display half. (3) BOTH HALVES, repeat clause broken: maxTakable:null → maxTakes()=Infinity, so the feat CAN be taken again, but the working answer is stored at `animal-senses:sense` — one key per RECORD (build.ts:3505 `build.effectChoices[`${recordId}:${ch.id}`]`) — so the second taking cannot record a different sense and the sheet can never accumulate two. Note the inert picker in (1) is the one keyed per slot. (4) SHEET, Q13 not delivered: senses are a Map keyed by sense name (derive.ts:2029 addSense) with no supersede rule, and both DetailsTab and VitalsRail print every entry, so a low-light ancestry plus this feat's darkvision lists Low-light vision AND Darkvision side by side. NOT a defect: the "inherent animal typically has that sense" restriction is unfilterable by design — the beastkin heritage stores `inherentAnimal` as free text and its own note says the feats let you pick the sense — and the picker prompt does name the inherent animal. harnessLimits: forced-placement (host lacked the beastkin heritage), which explains eligibleHosts=[] only.

verdicts.name: Animal Soul Siblings
verdicts.detail: Nearly correct — one half of one clause is missing. Delivered: Speak with Animals arrives as an innate spell with THIS spell's own tradition (stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].tradition='primal'), at the spell's own base rank (repertoire.2), attributed (spellSources['speak-with-animals']='Animal Soul Siblings'), and grantedSpells carries innate:speak-with-animals. The "once per day" is delivered even though nothing appears in the limitedUses diff: innate cadence is not tracked there — build.ts:4699 records only DEVIATIONS from 1/day, and SpellsTab.tsx:1813 prints "rank 2 · 1/day · from Animal Soul Siblings" with a spendable pip; no innate grant in this batch produces a limitedUses row, including ones with usesPerDay:1 authored explicitly, so the absence is the harness, not the app. The +1 is correctly typed and correctly restricted: situationalBonuses.ts:118, Diplomacy, when="to Gather Information from animals", "+1 circumstance", outside the total per Ruling B, starring the one skill that performs the action per Ruling C. Builder correctly asks nothing. MISSING: the second surface Q2/Q8 requires — the Gather Information ACTION carries no mark. That row renders inside the Diplomacy stat-detail modal (SKILL_ACTIONS.diplomacy → StatDetailModal.tsx:185) and supports marks, but RECORD_MARKERS has no entry for this feat; the only `gather-information` mark in the whole registry belongs to Streetwise. One-line fix, same pattern as Animal Elocutionist's Make an Impression mark. Separately worth the owner's eye (a Spells-page concern, not this record's): all innate grants pool into a single 'Innate spells' entry whose tradition is a majority vote across grants (build.ts:4708), so a character with primal and arcane innate spells would have one of them labelled with the other's tradition.

verdicts.name: Apparition Sense
verdicts.detail: The sense half is right and observed: defenses.senses gains {name:'apparition sight', acuity:'imprecise', range:30}, so the player reads "Apparition Sight (imprecise 30 ft)" off the Senses row. What is not delivered is the second sentence's activity: "As an activity that takes 10 minutes, you can act as a link between disembodied souls and their mortal bodies." The record carries no `grantsActions`, its own actionCost is {type:'passive'}, and nothing in db.actions is attributed to it — so no entry appears anywhere in the actions list and the procedure (contact with both spirit and body for the full 10 minutes; it does NOT raise the dead; the displaced occupant's Will save vs your spell DC) survives only inside the raw feat description. Note for whoever fixes it: authoring the activity is not enough on its own — ActionCost {type:'duration'; text} exists in types.ts:136 but ZERO records in public/core.json use it, and MainTab.tsx's isActionCost gate (actions|reaction|free|variable only, MainTab.tsx:226) drops a duration-cost record, so the display filter needs widening too. Secondary and much smaller: the standing "a spirit or undead otherwise incapable of speech can speak through you (while in direct contact)" capability has no `note` field, so it too is only in the description. The Will-save sentence correctly gets no surface (it lands on another creature and quotes a DC that already has a row). The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and the harness observed no picker.

verdicts.name: Appraiser's Eye
verdicts.detail: All four printed promises are delivered and observed. innateSpells:[{spellId:'read-aura', tradition:'primal', atWill:true, heightenHalfLevel:true}] produces an 'Innate spells' entry with tradition primal, read-aura in `cantrips` (not in a per-day repertoire slot) and spellSources['read-aura'] = "Appraiser's Eye", so the spell is attributed to this feat where the player reads it. "At will" is honoured by the cantrip path — no limitedUses on the record, no innateUses entry, nothing to spend or restore. heightenHalfLevel is documented as exactly ceil(level/2) and overrides any base rank (mechanic-lanes.md, section E), which is the general cantrip rule resolving through the general path rather than a frozen number. The skill-feat grant lands too: stored.feats['quick-identification'] appears with grantedBy:'appraisers-eye', and featFeatGrants adds granted feats as bonuses with no slot consumed and no prerequisite test (featFeatGrants.ts header), which is exactly the "even if you don't meet the prerequisites" waiver. One app-wide shape I checked and am NOT reporting as this feat's defect: build.ts:4708 gives the single 'innate-casting' entity ONE tradition, the majority tradition across all innate grants, so a character with more innate spells of another tradition would see the block labelled with that one. That is a pre-existing property of the innate block rather than anything this record does, and the spell's own popup prints Read Aura's real tradition list.

verdicts.name: Aquatic Elf Warrior
verdicts.detail: Two defects, both on the sheet half. (1) The proficiency remap is authored as a FLAT rank instead of mirroring the simple category: featGrantsAuto.ts:34 has weaponFamiliarity {weapons:[crossbow, heavy-crossbow, dagger, longspear, spear, trident], rank:'trained'}. The text says to treat the martial ones AS SIMPLE WEAPONS, i.e. use the character's own simple-weapon rank, and 11 classes have simple > martial at high level (cleric/druid/witch/sorcerer/oracle/animist/psychic/summoner/kineticist expert; alchemist/monk master). Measured by building the characters: a level-20 elf CLERIC (simple expert, martial untrained) wielding a trident prints +22/+17/+12 at rank trained where the feat entitles them to expert, +24; an elf MONK (simple master) also prints +22 where master gives +26. maxRank keeps it from ever lowering a rank, so Q10 is satisfied — it just under-delivers by 2 to 4 on the attack row. The app already has the exact right shape and uses it elsewhere: mirrorCategory:'simple' (jotunborn-weapon-familiarity, advanced-monastic-weaponry, explosive-savant). (2) "You don't take a -2 circumstance penalty to melee slashing or bludgeoning attacks while underwater" has no surface at all: the feat id appears in no entry of situationalBonuses.ts (registries list only featGrantsAuto), so no melee Strike row carries a `*` for it. The lane exists and is live — situationalBonuses supports {kind:'strikeAttack'} and MainTab.tsx:460 renders the star per strike instance — it is simply unauthored. (Underwater Marauder carries nothing for the same clause either, so this is a small family, not a one-off.) Builder half correct: the feat asks nothing and no picker was rendered.

verdicts.name: Aquatic Eyes
verdicts.detail: The feat grants DARKVISION to every character on the FIRST taking, and lists it beside low-light vision. Observed by building the characters: a level-20 human (ancestry vision 'normal') with Aquatic Eyes shows senses "normal, low-light-vision, darkvision"; an elf shows "low-light-vision, darkvision". The cause is a double authoring — effect-backfill.json carries TWO rows for this id, one writing conditionalSenses [{ifPresent:'low-light-vision', base:low-light-vision, upgraded:darkvision}] (line 9523) and a second writing a flat senses:[{name:'low-light-vision'}] (line 68227) — and derive.ts:2129-2138 evaluates "already have" against the senses gathered SO FAR plus the ancestry's vision. The flat grant lands first, so the feat satisfies its own "if your ancestry already has low-light vision" test and upgrades itself. Two things are wrong at once: darkvision is granted where the text conditions it on the ancestry, and both senses are shown where Q13 rules that only darkvision is displayed when it supersedes low-light. Fix is one deletion (drop the flat `senses` backfill row); the conditionalSenses lane alone is already correct and tested (test/fix-campaign.test.ts 'conditional sense upgrades'). Builder half also fails, differently: maxTakable:2 lets the feat be taken a second time UNCONDITIONALLY, where the Special gates the repeat on "your ancestry has neither low-light vision nor darkvision" (Q9 — an illegal second taking should not be offered), and "You can't retrain out of this feat" is modelled nowhere. Note the second taking is moot today anyway, since the first already hands out darkvision.

verdicts.name: Aqueous Dragonblood
verdicts.detail: Only the base swim Speed arrives; three of the four clauses are unbuilt and the one picker is dead. (1) The branch "if you already have a base swim Speed, it increases by 5 feet" never fires — measured: a character holding Wavetouched Paragon (swim 15) who then takes Aqueous Dragonblood still shows swim 15, where the text gives 20. The record carries only speeds:{swim:15} and speeds are combined by max, not by the printed +5. (2) The builder's picker is the same defect from the other side: `choice` {flag:'choice', prompt:'Choose an option', options Yes / No} storing existing-swim-speed / no-swim-speed, answered both ways with nothing moving (verdict echo-only, silentDefault true) — those two values appear nowhere in src/. It is also a phantom question in the Round-5 / Exemplar Dedication sense: the app can read whether the character already has a base swim Speed, so this should be computed rather than asked, and the prompt "Choose an option" tells the player nothing. (3) "you take only a -1 circumstance melee penalty to slashing or bludgeoning attacks that pass through water (instead of -2)" has no situational entry — the feat id is in no registry at all — so no melee Strike row carries the `*`, though the {kind:'strikeAttack'} star lane is live (MainTab.tsx:460). (4) "hold your breath underwater for 10 minutes" has no `note`, so it is readable only in the raw description. The draconic-exemplar narrowing is inert for a different reason and I am not counting it as this feat's defect: the choiceOptionLimits lane exists (derive.ts:1246 effectiveChoiceLimits / narrowChoiceOptions) but NO record in the app offers a draconic-exemplar pick and the 44 draconicExemplar records are name-only stubs with no swim data — there is nothing to filter yet.

verdicts.name: Arcane Communication
verdicts.detail: "You gain touch telepathy … as long as you share a language" reaches nothing. The record's stored fields are only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `senses`, no `note`, no `passiveEffects` — `registries` is empty and `sheetDiff` is `[]` (crossChecks.silentOnBothHalves, with NO harnessLimits to excuse it). The builder correctly asks nothing, so the whole feat is silent. A route exists and is in daily use: `senses[]` is free-form and already carries non-vision entries across the corpus (thoughtsense, lifesense, apparition sight, "ignores concealment from smoke"), and `note` is the lane for a clause worth printing but not computable; derive.ts even built a dedicated `breathesWater` flag for exactly this shape ("a permanent capability with no number attached … every record saying it did nothing at all"). So this is an empty lane, not a missing one. The Enhancement tier (10-ft range) is likewise unrecorded — and note the app DOES model the tier elsewhere: feats/lesser-augmentation and feats/greater-augmentation carry an `effectChoices` picker listing arcane-communication by name, so the tier could be gated. Nothing on the sheet distinguishes base from Enhancement here because nothing is on the sheet at all.

verdicts.name: Arcane Dragonblood
verdicts.detail: The "instead" in "If you would automatically become trained in Arcana …, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice" is not implemented, so the feat OVER-GRANTS. Measured by building characters: a dragonblood fighter (Arcana untrained) taking the feat and answering the effectChoice with Society ends up {arcana:trained, society:trained} — two skills where the text grants one. featGrantsAuto.ts:55 reads `'arcane-dragonblood': { skills: { arcana: 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true` (the flag ~60 sibling entries carry and build.ts:3384 reads), so `character.skillFallbacks` is null on every host and the effectChoices picker is rendered and applied UNCONDITIONALLY rather than only when another source trains Arcana. Builder half, second defect: the record declares TWO pickers for this one clause. `record.choice {flag:'arcaneDragonbloodFallback', kind:'skills'}` renders a "Replacement skill" list of 12 options that are the skills the host is ALREADY trained in ("Arcana (E), Crafting (E), … Thievery (T)") — `kind:'skills'` resolves through trainedSkillOptions, i.e. Assurance's "pick a skill you're trained in", which is the exact inverse of "become trained in a skill" — and its answer is consumed by nothing (verdict echo-only, `answerDeadButSheetMoves`). Per Q20 that is not acceptable label-only: the app plainly models the consequence (the other picker moves skills.*), so a dead picker here is a defect, and no grep in src/ finds `arcaneDragonbloodFallback` anywhere. Delivered correctly: Arcana trained, and the Arcane Sense grant (featFeatGrants.ts:64) lands with its own innate Detect Magic and `grantedBy:'arcane-dragonblood'`. Also unbuilt, secondary: "if you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an arcane dragon" — the only exemplar picker in src/ is the sorcerer Draconic bloodline's `dragonChoice` (builder/shared.tsx:2964), which offers all four traditions to a character holding this feat, and no picker at all consumes the 44-entry `draconicExemplar` collection, so the Q9 filter has nothing to attach to for a non-sorcerer.

verdicts.name: Arcane Eye
verdicts.detail: See the Unseen is ENHANCEMENT-ONLY text ("**Enhancement** … You can cast See the Unseen as an arcane innate spell once per hour"), but the record grants it flatly: `innateSpells:[{spellId:'see-the-unseen',tradition:'arcane'}]`, and the sheetDiff confirms a 1st-level taker gets `spellcasting[innate-casting].repertoire.2[0]='see-the-unseen'` plus `grantedSpells[0]`. Every other automaton Enhancement feat authors only its BASE benefit (automaton-armament = the strike, energy-beam = the beam, reinforced-chassis = the action, magical-resistance = resistance 5) and leaves the Enhancement as prose behind Lesser/Greater Augmentation's picker — this one is the outlier, so a 1st-level automaton reads an innate spell they cannot cast, and nothing on the record marks the clause as not-yet-held. Second, the frequency is wrong: the grant carries neither `usesPerDay` nor `usesPer`, so build.ts:4699-4700 defaults it and SpellsTab prints "rank 2 · 1/day · from Arcane Eye". The hourly lane exists and is in use — feats/primal-proportions carries `usesPer:'hour'` and innateCadence renders it — so "once per hour" is authorable and simply absent; as printed the use returns at daily preparations instead. Delivered correctly: darkvision (`senses:[{name:'darkvision'}]`) and the arcane tradition/source line on the spell card. One further display defect: deriveDefenses keys senses by name and never supersedes, so an automaton (ancestry vision = low-light-vision, which is this feat's own prerequisite) reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision" — Q13 says show only darkvision.

verdicts.name: Arcane Fists
verdicts.detail: Three of the four sheet clauses reach nothing; `sheetDiff` is `[]` with no harnessLimits, and the record carries only critSpec/critSpecLevel/critSpecWeapons. Built a magus and read deriveStrikes with and without the feat — the Fist row is identical in both: damage "1d4+1 B", traits [agile,finesse,nonlethal,unarmed]. (1) "The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6" — not applied. derive.ts:3810 hardcodes the d4→d6 upgrade to powerful-fist / warrior-automaton / warrior-jotunborn only; the general lane is `unarmedTraits` with `setDie` (24 feats use unarmedTraits today, e.g. syu-tak-nwas-deadly-hair with match+stepDie), and this record carries none. (2) "Your unarmed attacks gain the arcane trait, making them magical" — no trait added and no magical flag; `unarmedTraits:[{add:['arcane']}]` is exactly the shape and is unused. (3) "You don't take the normal −2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack" — no `note`, no `situational`; `registries` is empty and grep finds no arcane-fists in src/, so the clause exists nowhere the player can read it on the strike row (Ruling D / the textNumbers pack even extracts "−2 circumstance" from the text). Delivered: the crit-spec clause — critSpecSources gains `{level:5, weapons:{groups:['brawling']}}` from the feat and matches both brawling unarmed attacks and brawling weapons via group. "This critical specialization effect uses your spell DC instead of your class DC" has nothing to bind to, since CRIT_SPEC prose prints no DC at all ("must succeed at a Fortitude save"), which is a display gap rather than a wrong number.

verdicts.name: Arcane Sense
verdicts.detail: The at-will half is right and the rank half is absent. Delivered: `innateSpells:[{spellId:'detect-magic',tradition:'arcane',atWill:true}]` produces an innate entry headed "Innate spells · innate spells (Arcane)", and atWill sets innateUses=0 so there is no pip and nothing to restore — the positive "at will" statement the text makes. Missing: "If you're a master in Arcana, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank; if you're legendary, 4th" is modelled nowhere. `InnateSpellGrant` can express `rank`, `heightenHalfLevel` and `heightenAt` (level-keyed steps), but nothing keyed to a SKILL proficiency, and the record authors no heighten at all — so the printed rank never moves when Arcana rises, which is the whole second sentence of the feat. Compounding it, this app's Detect Magic record is the legacy CANTRIP (rank 0, `cantrip` trait) rather than the Remaster 1st-rank spell the feat's own text names, so the grant lands in `spellcasting[innate-casting].cantrips[0]` and SpellsTab's cantrip branch renders it as meta="at will" with NO rank at all and — unlike the repertoire branch, which appends "· from <source>" — WITHOUT the "from Arcane Sense" attribution, even though `spellSources.detect-magic='Arcane Sense'` is populated (a write-only field for this one shape). So the player reads an unranked, unattributed Detect Magic. Two sibling records need the same proficiency-keyed ladder and also lack it (rivethun-devotion, rivethun-adept), so the field limitation is real rather than a one-off authoring miss. Builder half is correct: the feat asks nothing.

verdicts.name: Arcane Tattoos
verdicts.detail: Both halves deliver. BUILDER: one picker, prompt "Choose a cantrip", optionCount 7 — Shield / Tangle Vine / Daze / Electric Arc / Ghost Sound / Void Warp / Sigil, exactly the closed list the text welds to the seven Thassilonian schools, no wider (src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:20). It asks for the cantrip rather than the school name, which is the same one-to-one question in the form the player can actually choose on — the requirement's worry (a bare school name) is the shape the app avoided. The school is not recorded anywhere, and the only records that would consume it (ornate-tattoo, virtue-forged-tattoos, "the same school as your Arcane Tattoos") are themselves excluded, so nothing is left dangling. Access clause correctly gates nothing (prerequisites: [], Q5). SHEET: answerIsRead verdict 'read' — the pick lands at stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].cantrips[0] with spellSources.<spell> naming the feat (rendered at src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:1597). Tradition resolves to arcane: build.ts takes the grant's tradition from the spell's first listed tradition and all seven list arcane first (verified in core.json). At-will with no use pip — a rank-0 grant goes into innateCantrips and never touches innateUses, so no counter and nothing to restore. The empty sheetDiff is the unanswered-picker shape (crossChecks.sheetSilentButBuilderAsks), not an absent effect. ⚠ CONTEXT, not a defect: the record is on EXCLUDED_FEATS (src/data/index.ts:30, with ornate-tattoo, virtue-forged-tattoos, hag-magic), so it is deleted from the live database and no player can reach any of the above — that is the owner's own "8 judgment call feats" decision (test/judgment-calls.test.ts:82). The audit harness resolved options from the raw content and bypassed that filter, so other excluded feats in this batch will also read as live.

verdicts.name: Armor Assist
verdicts.detail: Nothing at all is delivered on the sheet. The record carries no situational, no note and no other mechanical field (storedFields is level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only), and src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts has no 'armor-assist' key. Required: a `*` on BOTH skills the text names — Athletics and the specific Warfare Lore subskill (ruling C / principle D: star every skill that could perform the named action) — carrying what the check achieves (halve your own donning time) and the GM's DC guidance (usually 15 common / 20 uncommon / 25 rare), with click-through. Both targets are demonstrably in lane: situationalBonuses.ts already stars a named Lore this exact way (siege-ritualist, targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'lore:warfare'}] at line 2239). The ally half correctly owes no second number (ruling F) but per principle A must still be readable in the same star's note and the description. The builder half is right: the Athletics-or-Warfare-Lore choice is made per attempt at the table, and the builder renders no picker (choiceCount 0). ⚠ The harnessLimits entry 'pick-a-feat-grant' on this feat is a FALSE trigger and must not be used to excuse the empty diff: armor-assist grants no feat — it only appears inside OTHER feats' option lists (src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:140 and :193, Pitborn's six-feat pick). The silentOnBothHalves shape here is real.

verdicts.name: Armor in Earth
verdicts.detail: Only the grantsAction half arrives — the sheetDiff shows the impulse entering the action list (actions[0] 'Armor in Earth') and nothing else. Everything the stone armour does is absent: there is NO mode for this feat anywhere (no entry in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, no hit for 'armor-in-earth' in src/, scripts/data/ or effect-backfill.json; the record itself carries zero mechanical fields). So there is no toggle, no Dismiss, no self-exclusion, no 10-minute duration text, no AC Bonus +4, no Dex Cap +1, no Check Penalty −2, no Speed Penalty −10 ft, no Str 3 / Bulk 1 / group plate, no armour specialization, no suppression-and-replication of the worn armour's runes, no 'uses your highest armour proficiency', and no 3rd-level rewrite to heavy / +5 / bulwark. The builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and renders no picker, and the level-3 upgrade is not rendered as a second pick. This is a skipped record rather than a missing capability: the two sibling impulses of identical shape ARE authored as display-only modes carrying the full statistics in their note — `metal-carapace` and `hardwood-armor` in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, both with duration "10 minutes (Dismissible; using the impulse again ends the old one)" and both ending "The app cannot swap armor statistics automatically — unequip your worn armor while this is active." Judged against that precedent, the mode + full-text note is squarely in lane and owed; only the automatic armour-statistic SWAP (and with it the Dex-cap/armour-spec/rune-replication numbers) is the part the app has already conceded it has no route for, so that sub-half is closer to no_lane than to a build task.

verdicts.name: Armor Proficiency
verdicts.detail: The SHEET half is fully and correctly built — no defect there. src/rules/featGrants.ts:326 carries { armorCascade: true, rankUpgrade: { level: 13, rank: 'expert' } }; build.ts:3408 trains the first of light→medium→heavy still untrained at the moment the take applies, so repeat takes advance; the granted rank becomes expert on reaching 13th (keyed to current level, not the level taken); and each take records fc.choice = { label: 'Light armor' }, which the Feats tab prints as "Armor Proficiency (Light armor)" (src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:87) and the builder shows as a "Trains you in" sub-card (Builder.tsx:1793) — so the computed category is identifiable on both surfaces, which was the requirement most at risk. maxTakable 3 keeps it repeatable. The empty sheetDiff is only because the harness host is a level-20 fighter already trained in every armour category. THE DEFECT is that same case: builder.eligibleHosts lists all six reference hosts including fighter/human, for whom the feat is a guaranteed no-op at every level — there is no "next type" left, and no later scaling can rescue it (the 13th-level clause upgrades only a category this feat granted). Per Q21 that pick is wasted across the character's whole career and should be filtered; per Q27's table ("already trained… shown, greyed, and it says why") it must at minimum not render live and silently inert. src/rules/featSlots.ts:35 applies no such test, and the take then "grants nothing and stays bare" (build.ts comment) — a general feat slot spent on nothing, with the row not even carrying a category label to explain it. The app's own test blesses this as "a harmless no-op for a fighter" (test/feat-grants.test.ts), which is the exact shape the owner called bad design. Same defect on the 3rd take for any class already trained in light (only two takes can ever do anything).

verdicts.name: Armor Regiment Training
verdicts.detail: One of three sheet clauses is delivered; two are absent. DELIVERED — bulkIgnore: the record carries armorBulkReduction { by: 1, categories: ['heavy'] } and it is genuinely read, at src/rules/derive.ts:4103 inside deriveBulk, applied only to worn items of itemType 'armor' whose category is heavy, floored at the item's own Bulk so it cannot go negative, and subtracted from the total that feeds the encumbered/maximum thresholds. The empty sheetDiff does not contradict this — the reference host wears no heavy armour and Bulk is not one of the diffed values. MISSING — situational: no `*` on the Speed row for the exploration-mode travel clause. The record has no `situational` field and situationalBonuses.ts has no key for it, yet this is the app's most well-worn shape: horizon-walker-dedication (line 647), scouts-speed (721), legendary-guide (733) and constant-crosier (1994) all star the Speed row with a travel-only `when` that explicitly says it is not the encounter Speed. The star must carry the ally half as text (ruling F + principle A) and must NOT strip the armour Speed penalty from the printed Speed. MISSING — note: "you can rest normally while wearing armor of any type" has no marker anywhere. Per ruling D it belongs on the Rest / daily-preparations flow, and the app already writes this exact clause into a mode note for a comparable record (guardians-armor in toggle-modes.json: "You can also rest normally in medium and heavy armor"). Mitigating: nothing in src/ models an armoured-rest penalty at all (only the glossary's 'comfort' trait blurb), so no wrong number is produced — the loss is the marker, which is why this half is low severity on its own. Builder half correct: the feat asks nothing and renders no picker.

verdicts.name: Armored Regiment Training
verdicts.detail: Only one of the three clauses is delivered. The bulk clause is real: `armorBulkReduction {by:1, categories:['heavy']}` (authored in effect-backfill.json) is read by deriveBulk at src/rules/derive.ts:4103 and subtracted from the carried total. The other two clauses reach nothing. (1) "you can rest normally while wearing armor of any type" — the record carries no `note`, `registries` is empty, and nothing anywhere marks Rest/daily preparations; the app knows the concept (glossary.ts:147 explains the Comfort armour trait as exactly this), so the player of a commander in full plate is left under the general rule with no indication it stopped applying. (2) "In exploration mode, you and your allies use your normal Speeds without including your armors' Speed penalties" — no `situational` field and no situationalBonuses entry, so the Speed row (which already has the armour's Speed penalty subtracted) carries no `*`. sheetDiff is empty and the diff DOES cover situational notes, so both absences are observed, not inferred. Both lanes exist and are heavily used (`note`; `situational` targets kind 'speed'), so this is unbuilt data, not a missing capability. The ally half correctly needs nothing (Ruling F). Builder half is correct: the feat asks nothing and the app asks nothing. Secondary, smaller: `armorRelief` (derive.ts:4119) returns 0 unless `inv.worn`, so heavy armour carried but not worn gets no reduction — the text conditions on the armour being heavy, not on wearing it.

verdicts.name: Artisanal Crafter
verdicts.detail: The Q9 case in its plainest form. The feat grants Specialty Crafting "in your choice of blacksmithing, leatherworking, or stonemasonry" — three options. The builder renders Specialty Crafting's OWN full list of twelve: Alchemy, Artistry, Blacksmithing, Bookmaking, Glassmaking, Leatherworking, Pottery, Shipbuilding, Stonemasonry, Tailoring, Weaving, Woodworking (picker key `specialty-crafting`, storage grantedFeatChoices, optionCount 12, optionsTruncated 0). A player can take Alchemy or Shipbuilding through a feat that never offered them — the same shape the owner already ruled a defect on Manifold Modifications (Round 5). The app has a route for BINDING a granted feat's answer (FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE, featFeatGrants.ts) but none for NARROWING it to a subset; backgroundGrants.ts records this explicitly for `toymaker` ("6 of 12"), calling it "ruling Q9's filtering lane rather than this one, and is unbuilt" — so this record is one of a family, and one narrowing shape fixes all of them. Everything else is right: the sheet half grants Crafting trained (rank + modifier move), the fallback picker exists and its answer is read (it trains the chosen skill), Specialty Crafting is owned with grantedBy = artisanal-crafter and its own situational Crafting bonus live, and the specialty answer being echo-only is legitimate here (the app models no per-specialty number, and the pick is written onto the granted feat's own entry, so the player can read which specialty they hold from Specialty Crafting itself).

verdicts.name: As in Life, So in Death
verdicts.detail: Both halves miss a different requirement, and the grant itself is the only thing delivered (Adopted Ancestry is owned, level 1, grantedBy = as-in-life-so-in-death, no slot charged). BUILDER: the feat's whole point is "You can choose any ancestry", overriding Adopted Ancestry's common-ancestry restriction. The rendered picker offers exactly the 8 common ancestries — Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Human, Leshy, Orc (optionCount 8, optionsTruncated 0) — so a skeleton who was a kobold, hobgoblin or tengu in life cannot record it. Nothing in the app can widen a granted feat's list (FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE only pins a fixed answer). The answer is also echo-only in a way that matters: featSlots.ts:87-99 gates ancestry-feat slots on build.ancestryId, a versatile heritage's id, `extraAncestryFeatTraits` and `universal-ancestry`, and never reads the adopted-ancestry pick — so Adopted Ancestry's own effect (select that ancestry's feats when you gain an ancestry feat) is not live, which Principle G requires of a grant. SHEET: the auto-success clause — "you do not have to attempt Deception checks against a creature's Perception DC to successfully Impersonate yourself as a member of that ancestry" — plus its two carve-outs (no protection against divination; no benefit against a creature actively attempting Perception) reach nothing. registries lists only featFeatGrants, the record carries no `situational` and no `note`, and the diff shows no situational entry. This is not a capability gap: eight sibling feats carry precisely this shape (childlike-plant +4 "to Impersonate a human version of yourself", round-ears, sinister-appearance, feathered-cloak…), and `on:'action'` markers already exist for hide/sneak/avoid-notice, so the Impersonate marker Q8 asks for is one row of data.

verdicts.name: Ash-piercing Gaze
verdicts.detail: The feat is modelled as a SENSE the character does not have. The record carries `senses: [{name: "ignores concealment from smoke and mist"}]` and the diff confirms it lands as a sense row (defenses.senses[1].name), beside darkvision and low-light — SenseEntry's own doc comment says `name` is "the sense selector, e.g. darkvision, scent, tremorsense". The text grants no sense: the creature stays concealed, you do not see through the smoke, and only the flat check to TARGET it is auto-succeeded.
