As printed on the senses list it claims a perception capability that would also read as covering Seek, and as making the creature not concealed for every other purpose. Meanwhile the clause never reaches the thing it modifies — `registries` is empty, so there is no situationalBonuses entry at all — even though the app's own near-identical twin is authored correctly: `firesight` = [{ targets: [{kind:'strikeAttack'}], when: "targeting a creature concealed only by smoke and fire", bonus: "automatically succeed at the flat check" }], with `fire-lung` and `uncanny-bombs` in the same shape, and `multisensory-mask` demonstrating the `on:'condition', id:'concealed'` marker Ruling D asks for. So the fix is to move the clause from the sense list to a strike-row star and/or a Concealed-condition marker carrying the smoke-or-mist-only restriction. Builder half is correct — the feat asks nothing and the app asks nothing.

verdicts.name: Ask the Bones
verdicts.detail: The mechanics are delivered: Ask the Bones appears in the actions list as its own entry (actions[0]), the once-per-day frequency gets a real use pip (limitedUses "Ask the Bones: {max:1, per:day}") as Principle O2 requires of a per-day resource, and the +1 circumstance bonus is authored with its trigger. Builder correctly asks nothing. What I cannot settle is the STAR PLACEMENT, where two of the owner's own decisions point opposite ways. The app authors `ask-the-bones` as [{ targets: [{kind:'skill', detail:'all'}], when: "once per day, on the Recall Knowledge check made with Ask the Bones…" , bonus: "+1 circumstance" }], which puts a star on all sixteen skills (the diff shows all sixteen situational entries). Principle P (Posse, Round 4) says a benefit gated behind a deliberate action needs no star because the player already knows they did the thing — and this +1 exists only inside an activity the player deliberately spends, whose popup already carries the sentence. But Mastermind's Eye (answer 6) and Principle C say a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it, and the app has a standing precedent for the exact shape here (`vomit-stomach`: "once per day, on the immediate save Vomit Stomach grants…" stars Fortitude). Both readings are defensible from the record as it stands, so I will not call sixteen stars either correct or spurious. Note the star's `when` is capped with "…" per the capped-notes ruling, so the GM-adjudicated trigger ("if the bones belonged to a person particularly knowledgeable on the subject") is only in the click-through, not on the star line.
verdicts.question: Ask the Bones' +1 circumstance bonus exists only on the Recall Knowledge check made with the feat's own once-per-day activity, and the app currently stars all sixteen skills with it. Principle P (Posse) says a benefit gated behind a deliberate action needs no star; Mastermind's Eye says star every skill that can Recall Knowledge. For a bonus that lives INSIDE a feat's own activity, should the stars stay on every skill, or should it live only in the activity's popup?

verdicts.name: Assurance
verdicts.detail: Sheet half is correct: the chosen skill carries the star and its note reads "take 10 + your proficiency bonus instead of rolling from Assurance — you forgo the roll; no other bonus, penalty or modifier applies" (situationalBonuses.ts:3247), which is exactly the Q20 worked case. Builder half is correct on three of four points — `trainedSkillOptions` (build.ts:1159) offers only trained-or-better skills and includes Lores ("Scribing Lore (T)" in the pack), `maxTakable: null` keeps the feat offered for a second take, and each instance stores its answer under its own slot key so the first pick is not overwritten (measured: two instances at 2:skill:1 and 4:skill:1, both starred). The defect is the Special clause: "Each time, choose a different skill." Measured with Assurance already taken for Athletics, the SECOND instance's picker still lists `athletics` as a live option (12 options: arcana, crafting, occultism, religion, acrobatics, athletics, deception, diplomacy, lore:scribing, medicine, stealth, thievery). `choiceOptionsFor`'s `distinct` filter only removes answers within ONE choice def's picks, and the `kind: 'skills'` branch of `buildChoiceOptions` (build.ts:1303) returns before any narrowing runs — so nothing excludes a skill an earlier Assurance already claimed. The list is wider than the feat's own printed restriction, and the player can build an illegal double-Assurance on one skill.

verdicts.name: Athamaru Lore
verdicts.detail: Two of the four clauses are undelivered. (1) REDUNDANT FALLBACK, builder half — `featGrantsAuto.ts:60` carries `{ skills: { athletics: 'trained', nature: 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true`, unlike its twin automaton-lore on the next line. Measured on a druid/athamaru already trained in Athletics and Nature: `character.skillFallbacks` is null, `pickersFor` renders nothing, and the trained-skill set with the feat is byte-identical to the set without it. The player is never asked for a replacement and simply loses both grants — the text's "you instead become trained in a skill of your choice" is silently swallowed, and it should be able to fire twice. (2) THE LORE ITSELF, sheet half — `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS` grants `additional-lore` (it does appear on the sheet as a bonus feat with `grantedBy: athamaru-lore`), but no ATHAMARU LORE skill ever appears. Additional Lore's subject lives in `FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['additional-lore'] = { loreChoices: 1 }`, and Builder.tsx:1896 renders that Lore text box only for the feat PICKED IN A SLOT — never for a granted bonus feat — so `featLoreChoices['additional-lore:0']` is never written and build.ts:3435 trains nothing. The fix the sibling records already use is a `'lore:athamaru': 'trained'` entry on this feat (compare `anadi-lore`, `android-lore`, `nagaji-lore`), which would also satisfy the builder requirement that the subject arrive pre-filled rather than asked. Correct today: Athletics and Nature both read trained. Secondary and systemic rather than specific to this feat — the skill breakdown's timeline names a background or class source but never a feat, so neither grant says where it came from.

verdicts.name: Athamaru Weapon Familiarity
verdicts.detail: The first and primary clause — the martial-to-simple proficiency remap — has no field on the record at all and no registry entry (`registries: []`; every other ancestry familiarity feat carries `weaponFamiliarity`, e.g. `azarketi-weapon-familiarity`, `centaur-weapon-familiarity`, `conrasu-weapon-familiarity` in featGrantsAuto.ts). Measured directly: a wizard/athamaru (trained simple, untrained martial) holding a Trident rolls +2/-3/-8 at rank `untrained` both WITH and WITHOUT the feat, at level 1 and at level 5. Nothing remaps, so nothing can name the feat in the breakdown either. The named set that should be remapped is athamaru-trait weapons plus crossbow, heavy crossbow, longspear, spear, trident, restricted to the martial members and applied only where it improves the rank (Q10). The empty `sheetDiff` in the pack is not the evidence for this — the reference host owns no weapon — the direct build is. The SECOND clause is correct and needs no change: `critSpec: true`, `critSpecLevel: 5`, `critSpecWeapons: { traits: ['athamaru'], bases: ['crossbow','heavy-crossbow','longspear','spear','trident'] }`, and `critSpecSources` filters `s.level <= c.level`. Measured: the Trident shows no crit spec at level 1 and shows it at level 5, and the set is not narrowed to martial, matching the sentence.

verdicts.name: Automaton Armament
verdicts.detail: Everything except the Enhancement is right. The picker offers exactly two options (Claw, Pincer), the answer is read, and both strikes land correctly on the Strikes tab, measured: Claw = 1d4+5 S, traits agile/finesse/unarmed, group brawling, mapStep 4; Pincer = 1d6+5 P, traits grapple/unarmed, group brawling, mapStep 5 — the die, type, group, the agile MAP step and the absence of agile/finesse on the pincer all reach the row. Re-choosing swaps the row cleanly (Ruling K covers the rest), and the record's own level 1 means the "select at any level" clause needs no separate gate. THE ENHANCEMENT IS NOT APPLIED. It is recorded — Lesser Augmentation and Greater Augmentation each carry an `effectChoices` picker listing `automaton-armament` — but that answer reaches nothing: no `src/` file mentions lesser/greater-augmentation, and the picker's own prompt says "(prose benefit — read that feat's Enhancement entry)". Measured: a fighter/automaton at level 9 holding Automaton Armament (claw) AND Lesser Augmentation pointed at it still shows Claw 1d4+5 S. Per Principle C the die step (claw 1d4→1d6, pincer 1d6→1d8, everything else untouched) has to be reflected in the strike this feat granted, attributed to the Enhancement.

verdicts.name: Automaton Lore
verdicts.detail: Two clauses land and two do not. CORRECT: Arcana and Crafting read trained; and the redundancy fallback is genuinely built (`featGrantsAuto.ts:61` carries `redundantFallback: true`) — measured on a wizard/automaton trained in both from class, it renders TWO pickers ("Already trained in arcana — replacement skill", "Already trained in crafting — replacement skill"), each answer trains its skill (answering medicine + survival produced exactly two extra trained skills), and Builder.tsx:1878 already greys options the character is trained in with a reason, per Q27. MISSING (sheet): no AUTOMATON LORE skill ever appears. Additional Lore is granted as a bonus feat with `grantedBy: automaton-lore`, but its subject lives in `FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['additional-lore'] = { loreChoices: 1 }` and Builder.tsx:1896 renders that Lore box only for a slot-PICKED feat, never a granted one, so `featLoreChoices` is never written and no Lore is trained — same shape as Athamaru Lore; the sibling records solve it with a `'lore:automaton': 'trained'` entry, which also keeps the subject unaskable as the text requires. MISSING (builder + sheet): the whole **Enhancement** clause. No picker anywhere asks "Arcana or Crafting" — the only pickers this feat renders are the two fallbacks — and no rank moves: measured at level 9 with Lesser Augmentation pointed at automaton-lore, Arcana and Crafting both stay trained. The clause needs a two-option picker with BOTH options always live (Q21: an option the character is already expert in is the one that becomes master) and a set/upgrade that reads the rank held at the time, never a flat set to expert.

verdicts.name: Avenge in Glory
verdicts.detail: DELIVERED: the reaction reaches the actions list (Principle E) with Trigger/Frequency/Access in its description popup; storedFields.limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'} gives the once-per-day pip (sheetDiff shows both); and src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:563 stars BOTH halves of every Strike — targets [{kind:'strikeAttack'}] and [{kind:'strikeDamage'}], bonus '+1 circumstance', when 'while you still have the temporary HP from Avenge in Glory…' — rendered at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:460. (The evidence pack's empty `situational` block is a harness limit: scripts/feat-evidence.mjs:152 only samples ac/perception/save/skill refs, never strike refs.) Builder half is correct: nothing is asked and nothing should be. NOT DELIVERED: the 1-minute state has no mode — no entry in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, no `modes` registry hit — so the temporary Hit Points equal to your level are granted nowhere; the player types them into the temp-HP box by hand. The field could not say it today either: `tempHp` exists only on BattleForm (src/rules/types.ts:3107) and only as a FIXED number, so 'equal to your level' is unauthorable as things stand. I cannot settle whether that absence is a defect because two of your decisions point opposite ways (see question).
verdicts.question: Avenge in Glory is a reaction that grants temporary Hit Points equal to your level for 1 minute, plus a +1 circumstance bonus to attack and damage while you still have them. Q1 ('a longer duration gets a mode') and the Shield the Faithful precedent (1 minute, includes YOU, so its mode carries real numbers) say this should be a MODE that grants tempHp = your level on entry and takes it back on exit — the shape Round 10 built for BattleForm.tempHp. But Q15 says 'temporary Hit Points alone are not complicated', and Principle E says a reaction's entry in the reactions list is often the whole requirement. Today the app gives the reaction row, the 1/day pip and the +1 as a star on both strike rows, and grants no temp HP. Which governs — build the mode (which also needs `tempHp` to accept a level-scaled value outside `battleForm`), or is what ships already the finished shape?

verdicts.name: Avowed Insight
verdicts.detail: DELIVERED: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:748 stars AC and, via {kind:'save', detail:'all'}, all three saves with '+1 circumstance' and the 1-round condition in the `when` — Q1 (indication only) and Q2 (all three saves) both satisfied, and the sheetDiff confirms four star rows. The free-text Lore answer really does reach a skill row: build.ts:3436 writes `lore:<subject>` at trained. TWO DEFECTS. (a) MISSING, sheet: nothing is starred on the TRIGGER side. The reward is bought by a successful Recall Knowledge, and your own answer #6 (Mastermind's Eye) is this exact shape — 'a * in every skill that can recall knolladge so the user can see what happens when he checks his recall knowledge number' — reinforced by Ruling C, Ruling H and Q2's 'star the skill AND the action'. The record's only situational targets are ac and save:all; there is no skill target, no marker on the Recall Knowledge action, and no star on the Lore this feat itself grants. (b) SPURIOUS, builder: the pick is an UNRESTRICTED free-text box (featGrantsAuto.ts:62 'avowed-insight': {loreChoices: 1} → Builder.tsx:1896, label 'Trained Lore', placeholder 'Lore subject (e.g. Warfare)…'), while the text restricts it to a creature type NAMED BY THAT CHARACTER'S VOW. Measured against the data: only 2 of the 6 yaksha heritages name a creature type — deny-the-firstborn-pursuit (fey; the answer is forced, so per the Exemplar Dedication rule no question should be posed at all, just a stated fact) and deny-the-traitors-rebirth (rakshasas and asuras; a 2-option pick). featGrantsAuto.ts's own header admits the gap: 'Restricted skill choices are surfaced as options: any … the exact list restriction is not modeled'. Q9's Domain Fluency shape applies.

verdicts.name: Awakened Animal Lore
verdicts.detail: DELIVERED: BOTH Arcana and Nature reach trained with computed modifiers (sheetDiff: arcana untrained→trained mod 22, nature likewise) — the half-delivery trap is avoided. The redundancy fallback is right in shape: build.ts:3384 fires it PER SKILL (the evidence's single 'Already trained in arcana — replacement skill' picker is the arcana slot alone), the answer is read (movedPaths show a real skill rank moving), and Builder.tsx:1866 greys every already-trained option with the reason 'Already <rank> — pick a skill you are untrained in' — Q27 satisfied, so the raw 16-option list in the evidence is not a Q9 width defect. No phantom 'choose a Lore' question is posed for the granted feat, which is correct. MISSING: 'You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Awakened Animal Lore' is a NAME ON A LIST and nothing else. featFeatGrants.ts:69 grants `additional-lore`, whose own content is featGrantsAuto.ts:22 {loreChoices: 1} — an unanswered Lore slot. Builder.tsx's grantedChoicePicker only handles a record `choice` def (additional-lore has none), so no picker is rendered for a granted feat's FEAT_GRANTS lore slot, and no FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE entry pre-answers it. Grepped: no `lore:awakened-animal` anywhere in src/ or scripts/data/, and the sheetDiff shows no Lore row at all. The binding mechanism already exists (FEAT_GRANT_BOUND_CHOICE {kind:'fixed', skill} for eidetic-ear) but has no fixed-LORE shape, so the field is part of why this could not be authored. COLLATERAL, outside this feat: `additional-lore` also carries no rankUpgrade, so even a normally-taken Additional Lore never reaches the skill increases its text promises at 3rd/7th/15th.

verdicts.name: Awakened Jewel
verdicts.detail: CONFIRMED BY BUILDING THE CHARACTER: an OCCULT grant is filed under an ARCANE (or divine) innate entry. The pick-a-cantrip path pushes `{spellId: chosen}` with no tradition (build.ts:4651), and the single pooled 'innate-casting' entry takes its tradition from the majority of `content.spells[id].traditions[0]` (build.ts:4703-4706). Every one of the 28 options has traditions[0] of arcane or divine — NOT ONE resolves to occult. Built a level-20 sarangay fighter: bullhorn → tradition 'arcane', warp-step → 'arcane', forbidding-ward → 'divine'. SpellsTab.tsx:1849 prints exactly that as the section header — 'innate spells (Arcane)' — which is exemplar 10's pooled-header defect verbatim, and it is what the harness saw as `stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].tradition` moving between two answers. `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` already exists and is honoured; `CantripPickSpec` has no field to set it. ALSO MISSING (sheet): (1) 'A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up' does not happen for an innate-only character — SpellsTab.tsx:1195 computes `maxRank` from prepared/spontaneous entries plus focus ONLY, so with no class casting it is 0 and the detail view shows the cantrip frozen at base rank, while a main pool correctly labels 'at will · heightened to 10th' (SpellsTab.tsx:1268/1299). (2) The head-gem possession condition is written nowhere: no `spellNotes` on the record, and `SpellNote.spellId` (types.ts:338) names a FIXED spell, so the N2/Q7 lane cannot attach a note to whichever cantrip the player picked. ALSO MISSING (builder): the option list is a frozen Foundry snapshot rather than the occult cantrip list — 6 COMMON occult cantrips the app ships and shows by default are unofferable (approximate, infectious-enthusiasm, protect-companion, read-the-air, tame, wash-your-luck). Correctly excluded: ghost-sound (edition 'superseded', always hidden). CORRECT: cantrips only, one pick, permanent, and the entry reads 'at will' with no use pip (SpellsTab.tsx:1798).

verdicts.name: Awakened Magic
verdicts.detail: Same confirmed defect as Awakened Jewel, and here the text names the tradition outright ('as an primal innate spell'). Built a level-20 awakened-animal fighter: caustic-blast → innate entry tradition 'arcane', vitality-lash → 'divine'. Never primal. Cause: build.ts:4651 pushes the pick as `{spellId}` with no tradition and build.ts:4705 derives the pooled entry's tradition from `spells[id].traditions[0]`; all 34 options have a traditions[0] of arcane or divine, so NO pick can ever produce a primal entry. SpellsTab.tsx:1849 renders that as the header 'innate spells (Arcane)'. `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` exists and would fix it; CantripPickSpec cannot express it. ALSO MISSING (sheet): the ceil(level/2) heightening never applies to this grant — SpellsTab.tsx:1195 builds `maxRank` from prepared/spontaneous entries and focus only, so an awakened animal with no other spellcasting views the cantrip at base rank instead of 10th, while a class pool correctly prints 'at will · heightened to 10th'. ALSO MISSING (builder): the primal option list is a frozen Foundry snapshot, not the app's primal cantrip list — 4 COMMON primal cantrips the app ships and shows by default cannot be picked (approximate, healing-plaster, protect-companion, tame). Correctly excluded: acid-splash and ray-of-frost (edition 'superseded'). CORRECT: one picker only (no second question about tradition/rank/uses), cantrips only, and the entry reads 'at will' with no pip.

verdicts.name: Axiomatic Lore
verdicts.detail: Clause: "If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills … you instead become trained in a skill of your choice." The redundancy fallback is never asked. `featGrantsAuto.ts:64` authors `'axiomatic-lore': { skills: { diplomacy: 'trained', society: 'trained', 'lore:axis': 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true` — the very next line (65), azarketi-lore, has it. `redundantFallback` is the only trigger for the picker (build.ts:3384 pushes onto `Character.skillFallbacks`, which is what the builder renders and what the builder harness reported for azarketi-lore). Rebuilt to confirm rather than inferred: an investigator (Society is a fixed class skill) and a commander (same) each take Axiomatic Lore and get `skillFallbacks = null` — no prompt, no options, and the redundant Society training is silently swallowed by `maxRank`. The pack's empty `presentsChoices` is NOT evidence either way, because its host is a fighter/human on the acolyte background, for whom neither named skill is redundant (correct behaviour). The sheet-side half of the same clause ("the chosen skill reads trained") fails only as a consequence — there is no answer to apply. The other three requirements are delivered and observed: Diplomacy and Society read trained (+22 each) and Axis Lore is trained. One-line fix, same shape as line 65.

verdicts.name: Azarketi Lore
verdicts.detail: All four requirements delivered. Sheet: Athletics and Nature read trained (modifiers recomputed 0→22 and −1→21), Azarketi Lore is trained, and every grant goes through `maxRank`, so an existing higher rank is never lowered. Builder: `redundantFallback: true` (featGrantsAuto.ts:65) makes the fallback fire ONCE PER COLLIDED SKILL — the harness host had Athletics already trained and Nature not, and exactly one picker rendered ("Already trained in athletics — replacement skill"), which is the conditional behaviour the text asks for. The answer is consumed, not echoed: the widened sample moved `stored.proficiencies.skills.intimidation` / `skills.intimidation.rank` / `.modifier` (the two-answer probe found nothing only because the level-20 host was already trained in acrobatics and thievery). Two observations, neither reported as a defect against this feat: (1) the fallback list is the 16 core SKILLS with no Lore subjects, because build.ts:3387 applies the pick only `if (SKILLS.includes(picked))` — RAW "a skill of your choice" would admit a Lore, but this is the shape of every redundantFallback record in the app, not this record's doing; (2) whether the already-trained option is greyed (Q27) is a display fact this evidence cannot see, so it is not judged.

verdicts.name: Azarketi Weapon Familiarity
verdicts.detail: Clause: "For the purpose of determining your proficiency, martial azarketi weapons are simple weapons and advanced azarketi weapons are martial weapons." The remap is flattened into a fixed rank. `featGrantsAuto.ts:66` authors `weaponFamiliarity: { weapons: ['crossbow','hand-crossbow','longspear','spear','trident','boarding-axe','gill-hook'], rank: 'trained' }` — so the two azarketi weapons in content (boarding-axe and gill-hook, both MARTIAL, both uncommon) get a flat `trained` override instead of resolving to the character's SIMPLE rank. Observed, not inferred: a level-11 azarketi psychic (simple = expert, martial = untrained) equipping a Gill Hook derives the Strike at rank `trained`, attack +14/+9/+4; the remap the text prints makes it expert, +16. The gap is live for every class that outruns martial with simple — sorcerer L20, animist L11+, psychic L11+, cloistered casters generally — and widens to 4 points at master. This is a data gap, not a lane gap: build.ts:4038-4060 already handles several clauses per record and `mirrorCategory` is the exact field (`advanced-bow-training` uses `mirrorCategory: 'martial'`), so the record wants a second clause `{ weapons: ['boarding-axe','gill-hook'], mirrorCategory: 'simple' }`; because overrides are applied with `maxRank` and deriveStrike maxes again against the weapon's own category, Q10's "only when it makes the player better" still holds. Delivered correctly: the five named weapons are trained (observed as weaponOverrides), the access clause owes nothing (Q5), and the builder correctly asks nothing. ⚠ The pack's `companion-tab?` limit is a false positive — it matched the word "familiar" in "You are familiar with weapons"; no companion is involved.

verdicts.name: Bamboo and Silt Repose
verdicts.detail: Both printed clauses are undelivered — the feat is entirely inert. The record in core.json carries only id/name/level/category/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId: no `note`, no `situational`, and `registries: []` (it appears in none of the eight id-keyed registries). Nothing is marked on the Speed row and nothing on Stride, so a player who takes it sees the feat's name and nothing else. `silentOnBothHalves` here is genuine: no harness limit applies, the host is a native yaksha, and the builder correctly asks nothing (the feat names its own terrain types). The app has the lane and uses it for the identical sentence elsewhere — situationalBonuses.ts:3444 `'unimpeded-journey': [{ on: 'action', id: 'stride', note: 'Unimpeded Journey: you ignore the effects of difficult terrain, and treat greater difficult terrain as difficult terrain.' }]`, with the same shape at 3437 rite-of-passage, 3439 stonestep-shisk, 3447 wildwood-halfling and 3408 water-dancer. So this is one missing authored entry, and it must carry BOTH halves plus both qualifiers — non-magical only, and only light undergrowth / shallow bogs, mud and water — since carrying just the "ignore" half is the documented Dragon's Presence failure mode.

verdicts.name: Bardic Lore
verdicts.detail: The trained grant works; the three clauses after it do not. First, the empty sheetDiff is a HOST artifact and not a defect, and the pack's `pick-a-feat-grant` limit explains it for the wrong reason (it fired because featPickGrants.ts:190 lists 'bardic-lore' in Natural Ambition's EXCLUDE array): the sheet host is a bard whose subclass is `options[0]` = the ENIGMA muse, which already grants the Bardic Lore feat, so the 'before' character already had `lore:bardic` trained. Rebuilt on maestro/polymath/warrior/zoophonia, taking the feat does grant `lore:bardic` trained (featGrantsAuto.ts:69). What fails: (1) SHEET, rankUpgrade — "If you have legendary proficiency in Occultism, you gain expert proficiency in Bardic Lore" is not modelled anywhere; a bard driven to legendary Occultism via skill increases still reads `lore:bardic` = trained (the record carries only a flat `skills` map; `conditionalSkills` keys off the same skill's own prior rank, not off Occultism, so no existing field expresses it). (2) BUILDER, the hard exclusion — "you can't increase your proficiency rank in Bardic Lore by any other means" is not enforced: Builder.tsx:1418 builds the skill-increase list as `[...SKILLS, ...loreKeys]` from every owned lore, so Bardic Lore is offered live, un-greyed and with no reason (Q27), and three skill increases spent on it were observed to raise it to MASTER. (3) SHEET, note — nothing states that this Lore is Recall-Knowledge-only on any topic, or why its rank cannot move; the record carries no `note` and no situational entry, so the row behaves unlike every neighbouring Lore with no explanation, which is exactly the "reads as a broken app" shape.

verdicts.name: Bargain Hunter
verdicts.detail: Silent on both halves with NO harness limit — and the builder half is correct (the feat owes no question and asks none), so the whole defect is the sheet. Nothing of the three clauses is delivered. (1) "You can Earn Income using Diplomacy": the record carries no `skillSubstitutions`, no `situational` entry and no `note` (storedFields = level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only; registries empty; the only mention of `bargain-hunter` anywhere in src/ or scripts/data is a background's `grantedFeatId`). The Earn Income downtime record at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/actions.ts:123 still reads `skill: 'Crafting'`, and the Diplomacy row gets no `*` — the lane plainly exists and is used for this exact shape elsewhere (situationalBonuses.ts:262 `leaf-transformation`, when: "using Deception to Earn Income"). (2) The second use — run Earn Income with Diplomacy and take the proceeds as a discount on one item, free if the income meets its Price — appears on no surface but the feat's own blurb, which fails Principle A. (3) The +2 gp at 1st-level character creation has no lane at all: `startingWealthGp` (src/rules/wealth.ts) is a flat level table with no per-feat term. ⚠ Worth the owner knowing: the app already derives currency as budget minus purchases (build.ts:5168 `cpToCoins(startingWealthGp(level)*100 - inventory)`), so a +2 gp term IS expressible in that model and stays correct after the player spends it — the reader's "one-time write, never derived" worry does not apply here.

verdicts.name: Battle Medicine
verdicts.detail: The grantsAction lane IS delivered — sheetDiff shows `actions[0] = Battle Medicine`, the record carries actionCost {actions:1} and the healing/manipulate traits, and its description opens with "**Requirements** You're holding or wearing a healer's toolkit" and names the Medicine check at Treat Wounds' DC. It correctly puts no star on Medicine and no use pip for the per-target immunity (Ruling F). The defect is the immunity clause itself: the stored description reads "The target is then to your Battle Medicine for 1 day" — the word `immune` was dropped in import. AoN feat-5125 in the local archive reads "The target is then immune to your Battle Medicine for 1 day", so the sentence the requirement says must live in the popup is unreadable. The SAME bug hits the record the popup links to: `actions/treat-wounds` reads "The target is then temporarily to Treat Wounds actions for 1 hour". I scanned every description in public/core.json + public/core-descriptions.json for the pattern and got exactly these two records — a two-record fix, and the two a Battle Medicine player reads together. Secondary, not charged: the DC→healing table and the expert/master/legendary tiers ARE readable (the popup's `r` link resolves to actions/treat-wounds, which prints DC 15 / DC 20 +10 / DC 30 +30 / DC 40 +50 and the 4d8/2d8/1d8 outcomes), but they are printed flat rather than gated to this character's Medicine rank, so a trained-only character reads tiers they cannot attempt.

verdicts.name: Battleblooded
verdicts.detail: Both halves verified by driving the build, not by reading fields. Sheet: Intimidation goes untrained→trained, and Intimidating Glare is OWNED (`stored.feats[intimidating-glare].grantedBy = battleblooded`, no slot consumed) with its own mechanics landing — `situational.intimidation[intimidating-glare]` carries "when you Demoralize" / visual-instead-of-auditory. Builder: the redundancy fallback is conditional and live, not frozen — built with the Lost and Alone background (trained in Intimidation) the character reports `skillFallbacks: [{featId: battleblooded, skill: intimidation}]` and answering it trains the chosen skill; built without that background it does not appear at all. `featGrantsAuto.ts:71` carries `redundantFallback: true` and build.ts:3384 evaluates it against the accumulated build, and Builder.tsx:1862 renders the picker over all 16 skills with the already-trained ones `disabled` and a spelled-out reason ("Already trained — pick a skill you are untrained in"), which is Q27's shape. No picker is offered for the named Intimidating Glare grant, correctly. The evidence pack's `nativeHostEligible: false` / forced-placement is a host artifact only: brute-forcing every ancestry × heritage shows a nephilim-heritage character IS offered the feat (heritage id `nephilim` equals its trait).

verdicts.name: Beast Trainer
verdicts.detail: The builder half is right — the picker offers EXACTLY Pet and Train Animal, both live, no repeats. The answer reaches nothing: `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS['beast-trainer'] = ['train-animal']` (src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:73) is a flat unconditional map, and `grantedFeatByChoice` is honoured for BACKGROUNDS only (`bg?.grantedFeatByChoice`, src/rules/build.ts:430). Measured by rebuilding an orc fighter three ways: choice=pet → granted ['train-animal'], no companion; choice=train-animal → ['train-animal']; unanswered → ['train-animal']. So a player who picks Pet is silently given Train Animal instead — a missing grant AND a spurious one in the same act, and the Pet branch's whole point (a Tiny minion on the Companions tab) never appears even though the target is ready to receive it: `companionGrants.ts:81` already carries `'pet': {kind:'familiar', abilityBudget:2}`. This is Round 5's worked shape (Ranged Combatant) exactly — an answer that changes only the label. The Nature grant is correct (untrained→trained, attributed) and, correctly per the printed text, no redundancy fallback is invented for it.

verdicts.name: Beastbrood
verdicts.detail: Every sheet lane works when the feat is forced onto a character — Society untrained→trained, Courtly Graces owned (`grantedBy: beastbrood`, no slot) with both of its situational bonuses reaching Deception and Diplomacy, and the redundancy fallback firing only when another source already trains Society (measured with the Pathfinder Hopeful and Trade Consortium Underling backgrounds; answering it trains the chosen skill). But NO CHARACTER CAN TAKE IT. I brute-forced every ancestry × every legal heritage at level 20 over the ancestry/general/skill slots: Beastbrood is offered by no host, while Battleblooded, Beast Trainer, Bargain Hunter and Battle Medicine all resolve to one. Cause: the versatile-heritage gate at src/rules/featSlots.ts:91 tests `f.traits.includes(her.id)`, and the Tiefling heritage's id is `aon-tiefling` while its trait is `tiefling`. Nephilim passes only because its id and trait are the same string. ⚠ This is not one feat: six versatile heritages have an id that is not among their traits — aon-tiefling (16 feats), aon-aasimar (20), aon-aphorite, aon-ganzi, aon-ifrit and hungerseed (trait `oni`) — and each adds ZERO ancestry feats (measured: human bare 49 eligible, +nephilim 100, +aon-tiefling 49, +aon-aasimar 49). Legacy edition is not the explanation: legacy-era content is hidden only when the per-character "Hide legacy data" toggle is on. The fix is to match the heritage's TRAITS as well as its id.

verdicts.name: Benefactor's Resistance
verdicts.detail: The sheet half is delivered: `effectChoices[breath-type]` grants `resistances:[{type, value:'max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))'}]` and the answer moves defenses.resistances + defenses.sources.resistance:<type>, one line only, on a live formula. But the record ALSO renders a SECOND damage-type picker the text never asks for: `choice` (flag `nonPhysicalResistance`, prompt literally "Choose an option", 5 options acid/cold/fire/electricity/sonic). `nonPhysicalResistance` has ZERO consumers in src/ (grep returns nothing) — the harness confirms it: verdict echo-only, silentDefault true. So the player is shown two damage-type questions on one feat, and the one whose option list exactly matches the feat's printed five is the DEAD one: answer only that and the character gets no resistance at all, silently. It also carries no `choice.inert` and no `choice.note`, so it breaks the app's own coded rule at Builder.tsx:485 ("A pick that records but grants nothing must say so — never silently show a pick that does nothing") and Q27. Fix is to delete the `choice` block (the effectChoice already does the work). Two smaller notes, neither driving the verdict: (a) the live picker adds Poison to the five, which is legitimate for clause 1 (a poison-breathing benefactor) and matches the Elementheart Kobold six, but its own prompt tells a physical-breath player to pick from five while offering six — poison is not a legal answer in that branch; (b) the value uses max(1,…) at level 1, the app-wide convention copied from Elementheart Kobold, whose text prints "(minimum 1)" — this feat's text does not, so a 1st-level kobold shows resistance 1 where RAW gives 0.

verdicts.name: Bestial Manifestation
verdicts.detail: Sheet half is correct: `grantedStrikes` carries all four rows with the printed die, damage type, group brawling and trait lines (Claw d4 slashing agile/finesse/unarmed/versatile-p; Hoof d6 bludgeoning; Jaws d6 piercing; Tail d4 bludgeoning agile), keyed by `choiceValue`, and the answer is read — strikes[0].name/damage/traits all move. Two builder-half failures. (1) The picker shows four BARE WORDS. The `choice.options` carry only value+label and no `description`, and `buildChoiceOptions` (build.ts:1291) fills a description only for `def.ownsFeature` choices, so PopupSelect renders "Claw / Hoof / Jaws / Tail" with no die, damage type or traits — the only things that distinguish them — at a pick the feat says is permanent. The data is already on the same record (`grantedStrikes`, matched by `choiceValue`); the picker option's `description` field exists and is unauthored. (2) The Special clause has NO ROUTE anywhere in the app: nothing expresses "selectable only in a 1st-level slot" and nothing locks an answered choice. `maxLevel` exists only on featPickGrants specs and item filters, not as a ceiling on which slot may take a feat; grep for onlyAtLevel/firstLevelOnly/noRetrain/'only at 1st' in src/ returns nothing. So the feat is offerable in a 5th/9th/13th/17th-level ancestry slot and the attack stays freely re-choosable forever. This is a lane gap, not a per-record omission — 28 live feats print "You can select this feat only at 1st level" (round-ears, tusks, quadruped, elf-atavism, orc-sight, draconic-aspect, scaly-hide, gravesight …) and none can say it.

verdicts.name: Blast Lock
verdicts.detail: Both halves deliver and nothing extra happens. Sheet: the activity reaches the actions list at its printed cost (`actionCost {actions:1}`, sheetDiff actions[0] = "Blast Lock"), and its stored description is the complete printed text — the Requirements line ("You're wielding a loaded firearm"), the 10-foot range, "attack roll against the DC required to Pick the Lock", and all four degrees of success including the −2 and −4 circumstance penalty lines — with a live ref-link to Pick the Lock. No new statistic is invented, correctly: the attack is the firearm Strike the Strikes tab already prints and the DC belongs to the lock. Critically, the −2/−4 attach to nothing on this character: `registries` is empty, so no `situationalBonuses` star or `degreeShifts` entry hangs a standing penalty on Thievery or Pick a Lock — which is the right call (the penalty belongs to the lock that was shot) and is also the shape an over-eager pass would have got wrong. Builder: choiceCount 0, declared [], presentsChoices [] — the feat asks nothing, exactly as the text requires.

verdicts.name: Blessed Blood (Sorcerer)
verdicts.detail: The list-widening itself works: `spellListAdditions {from:'deity', max:3, as:'list'}` resolves against the build's own deity in build.ts:3822 and is read by BOTH spell-selection surfaces — Builder.tsx:665 `listAdditions` (repertoire building) and SpellsTab.tsx:286 `useTraditionSpells` (Manage Spells / Learn a Spell) — so the spells become legal repertoire options at their own ranks, and `as:'list'` keeps them OUT of the repertoire, satisfying the negative requirement (the `note` says so in words too). The defect is the cap. `max` is read only on the whole-TRADITION branch; the deity branch does `[...new Set([...spells, ...fromDeity])]` with no slice, so `max:3` is enforced by nothing. Measured against the app's own deity data: 460 of 485 deities grant exactly 3 (harmless), but 12 grant MORE and every one of them is over-granted — Nethys, Nalinivati, Abraxas, Yuelral, Isis, the three Nyarlathotep entries and Zeaki grant 9 spells (a Nethys sorcerer gets all 9 added, three times the printed cap), and Brixori plus two others grant 4. Builder half: the "up to three" choice is never asked at all — declared [], presentsChoices [], choiceCount 0; the app auto-adds the deity's whole list, so a player who wanted one or two has no way to say so and no way to see which three the feat is responsible for beyond the note's prose. The picker route already exists (both readers key off the resolved deity, so its option list is available).

verdicts.name: Blessing of the Five
verdicts.detail: Delivered: the ability reaches the actions list at 3 actions (sheetDiff actions[0]), its stored description carries the Frequency line, the full effect text, the five-excluded-creatures sentence and the whole alternative revival use (with ref-links to Heal, The Godclaw and Doomed 1), and `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` produces the single daily pip (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]) — one use covering both halves of the ability, correctly. Missing: the Heal itself. The record carries NO `innateSpells`, so the spell is never castable or reachable from the ability and the rank the whole ability turns on — (ceil(level/2))−1, i.e. rank 4 at 10th, rank 9 at 19th — is printed NOWHERE on the sheet; the player must compute it by hand every level. With no grant there is also nothing for the "up to five creatures remain unaffected" clause to attach to, so the `spellNotes` requirement (principle N2 — write the feat's text into the granted spell's description under the feat's name) fails with it. This is a data omission, not a lane gap, and its own family proves it: three sibling Hellknight-order records carry exactly the fields needed — `devil-allies` has innateSpells with `heightenAt` steps plus a spellNote, `righteous-resistance` has innateSpells + spellNote, `locate-lawbreakers` has innateSpells with usesPerDay. `heightenAt {level, rank}[]` (types.ts:1521, applied at build.ts:4673) can express the −1 formula as explicit steps (3→1, 5→2, … 19→9). Note when authoring: the 3-action version and the base rank 0 at levels 1–2 both need saying, and the daily use should not be double-counted between `usesPerDay` and the existing `limitedUses`.

verdicts.name: Blood Rising
verdicts.detail: The core of the feat IS delivered: sheetDiff adds actions[0] = "Blood Rising" at its reaction cost, and the popup carries the printed text — Trigger, the blood-magic-off-schedule clause, the two legal targets, the AC/save clause and the duration override. Per Principle E (Minor Omen) that is often the whole requirement, and Q1 keeps the round-scale duration out of the numbers. Builder correctly asks nothing (choiceCount 0). Two residual requirements have no route in this engine. (1) "**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of your bloodline": the record's displayed traits are the static ["sorcerer"] and no field derives a RECORD's own trait line per character — `grantsCreatureTraits` puts traits on YOU, not on the record — so the computed arcane/divine/occult/primal trait can never appear. (2) Principle C's mark on the thing it modifies: blood magic is not a record at all, only a paragraph inside each bloodline class feature's description (`classFeatures/bloodline-draconic` → "**Blood Magic—Scaly Hide** … +1 status bonus to AC for 1 round"), and the shipped marker lanes (`RecordMarker.on` is `'action' | 'condition'` only, `modifiesGrant.actionRider`) cannot target a class feature, so neither the "lasts until the beginning of your next turn" override nor "that bonus applies against the triggering spell" can be written where the player reads their blood magic. Same reason the trigger cannot resolve "the same tradition as your bloodline" to a concrete tradition.

verdicts.name: Blowgun Poisoner
verdicts.detail: silentOnBothHalves with NO harnessLimits: sheetDiff is empty, storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/actionCost/archetype, and registries is [] — nothing in situationalBonuses.ts, no note, no RecordMarker. The builder half is correct (the feat states no choice and none is rendered), so the whole defect is the sheet. Owed and absent: (a) a `*` on STEALTH carrying the third clause — "if you make a blowgun Strike while hidden or undetected, you don't automatically become observed. Instead, immediately attempt a Stealth check against the Perception DC of the target" — Stealth is where the player looks up the number this clause makes them roll, and Q2 says star the skill AND the action; (b) a marker on the blowgun Strike rows carrying all three rules: injury poisons apply even when resistance zeroes the damage, the crit-success misfortune that worsens the target's initial save by one degree (target-side, so correctly no `degreeShifts` entry on the character's own stats), and the hidden/undetected Stealth clause. Both surfaces exist as lanes today (`situational` targets kind 'skill' and 'strikeAttack'; RecordMarker marks actions) and neither is authored, so all three clauses live only inside the feat's own text.

verdicts.name: Bodyguard
verdicts.detail: Builder half is CORRECT and should not be reported: the charge is authored as `choice {flag:'bodyguardCharge', kind:'text', daily:true}` — free text is the right answer type (Principle I) — and Builder.tsx guards every choice site on `askedAtDailyPrep` (Builder.tsx:1441/1549/1621/1815), so it does not render in the builder and is asked at Daily preparations instead (Q23); it stays re-editable because Daily preparations can be reopened, satisfying the 10-minute re-choice clause. The evidence's `presentsChoices` row is the harness resolving the declared choice, not the builder rendering it. Sheet half is empty and owes two things. (1) No marker on TAUNT: `actions/taunt` exists in core.json and the shipped lane for exactly this is a RecordMarker `{on:'action', id:'taunt'}` (the same route as furious-focus → vicious-swing), but nothing records that this feat raises the taunted enemy's penalty to –2 against your charge. Correctly no skill star — Taunt is a 1-action guardian activity with no check, so Ruling C's conditional does not fire. (2) The daily answer has no consumer: `bodyguardCharge` is matched by no file under src/ (only data files), so the charge's name is readable only inside the daily-prep dialog's "Keeping your last choices" line (CharacterSheet.tsx:851, and only when dailyPrepPrompt === 'reuse'), never on the sheet where the Taunt rule is read.

verdicts.name: Bon Mot
verdicts.detail: Almost everything is delivered: the activity is listed (it is a curated skill action, so MainTab dedupes it out of the feat list on purpose), the enemy-facing –3/–2 correctly touches no row of the sheet (decided scope / Q4), no `*` is put on Diplomacy (correct — the feat uses the check, it does not change it), and the app RESOLVES the crit-failure back-reference rather than printing it: situationalBonuses.ts:2435 gives `bon-mot` targets perception + will, bonus "-2 status (penalty)", when "for 1 minute after you critically fail your own Bon Mot…". What is missing is that this half is only a star. The clause is self-facing, runs 1 minute (not a round) and has an explicit end condition ("ends after 1 minute or if you issue another Bon Mot and succeed"), which is Q1's "a longer duration gets a mode" plus Q11's "if the effect can be shut down, it is a mode" — and Q15 does not excuse it, since it fires on a critical FAILURE. There is no mode: toggle-modes.json holds 258 modes and 0 mentions of bon-mot, while the same file already models self-inflicted penalties as modes (curse-of-creeping-ashes-2 carries a −2 circumstance modifier). So the player who critically fails can never make their Perception and Will actually drop for the minute; they can only read that they should.

verdicts.name: Bone Magic
verdicts.detail: Two builder defects and one sheet defect. BUILDER (1) — the Special clause "Choose when you gain this feat whether your innate spells are primal or occult" is NEVER ASKED. `builder.declared` is only `registry.FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS`; the record carries no `choice` and no `effectChoices`, so there is no second picker at all (not a dead picker — an absent one). BUILDER (2) — the cantrip list is NARROWER than the feat's own restriction. featCantripGrants.ts:24 hardcodes 33 options, but the union of the occult and primal cantrip lists in core.json is 49 common, current-edition cantrips. Never offered: musical-accompaniment, deep-breath, slashing-gust, glass-shield, tremor-signs, eat-fire, illuminate, detect-metal, needle-darts, draw-moisture, rousing-splash, root-reading, take-root, timber, live-wire, glamorize — and the app itself lists every one of those under `awakened-magic` (primal) or `awakened-jewel` (occult), so this is a stale list rather than a ruling. Q9/Q21 cannot justify the omission: none of the 16 is illegal or wasted. SHEET — because the tradition is never asked, the innate entry's tradition falls back to the SPELL's first tradition (build.ts:4705, `g.tradition ?? spells[id].traditions[0]`), so picking Electric Arc (traditions [arcane, primal]) labels the character's innate casting ARCANE, a tradition this feat never allows (Q12 — the sheet must not say something false about the spell); and the downstream lizardfolk feat `bone-investiture`, whose prerequisite is Bone Magic, hardcodes `tradition:'primal'` on its Dinosaur Form grant instead of following the answer, which is exactly the clause "this choice applies to all innate spells you gain from lizardfolk ancestry feats that have Bone Magic as a prerequisite". Delivered correctly: the cantrip picker's answer IS read (verdict read, reaches spellcasting[innate-casting].cantrips), it is at-will with no use pips, and cantrips auto-heighten to ceil(level/2) (SpellsTab.tsx:1267). The empty sheetDiff is the unanswered-picker shape, not a dead grant.

verdicts.name: Bounce Boost
verdicts.detail: SHEET HALF IS FINE: the reaction reaches the reactions list (sheetDiff actions[0] = 'Bounce Boost'), and its popup text carries the Trigger line, the full +1/+2/+3/+4 Athletics ladder and the 2ft/5ft Leap clause — Principle E plus Ruling F, so correctly no star and no number on your own Athletics (registries: [], no situational entry). BUILDER DEFECT (Q9): the feat's printed 'Prerequisites Trained in Athletics' is not stored. public/core.json feats/bounce-boost has no `prerequisites` array at all, and prerequisites are the only input to the gate (build.ts:6066 `for (const line of feat.prerequisites ?? [])`, which DOES enforce the 'trained in <skill>' pattern) and to the 'Requires:' chip (Builder.tsx:2370). So the slot offers Bounce Boost to a tripkee untrained in Athletics — an option list wider than the feat's own restriction — and never tells the player the requirement exists. Systemic, not one-off: measured 167 live feats whose description still prints an un-parsed 'Prerequisites …' line and whose record carries no array (bounce-boost, litany-against-wrath, the six ancestry weapon-expertise feats, …). SECONDARY, not counted against the verdict: the popup shows the whole tier ladder rather than the tier this character's Athletics rank produces; the app has no field that computes a value into ally-facing prose, and Ruling F/Principle E make the reaction entry the whole surface, so I did not treat that as owed.

verdicts.name: Bouncy Goblin
verdicts.detail: DELIVERED: Acrobatics → trained with the modifier moving 2 → 24 (the +2 is NOT folded in, Ruling B), and the restricted bonus surfaces as a star on Acrobatics carrying "to Tumble Through a foe's space / +2 circumstance" (situationalBonuses.ts:134). MISSING: the fallback clause '(or another skill of your choice, if you were already trained in Acrobatics)' is not modelled. featGrantsAuto.ts:77 reads `'bouncy-goblin': { skills: { acrobatics: 'trained' } }` — no `redundantFallback`. Its Remaster sibling, the identical clause, does: featGrantsAuto.ts:133 `'extra-squishy': { skills: { acrobatics: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }`. The whole route exists and works (build.ts:3384 pushes Character.skillFallbacks and applies featSkillChoices `<featId>:fallback:<skill>`; Builder.tsx:1862 renders the picker), so this is one absent flag. Consequence: a goblin already trained in Acrobatics is asked NOTHING (builder half — the conditional question never appears) and gains NOTHING (sheet half — no substitute skill is ever trained), silently losing a skill training. The evidence pack cannot show this: the harness host was untrained in Acrobatics, so `presentsChoices: []` is the correct behaviour for that host and the defect is only visible in the record. SECONDARY: per Q2/Q8 the Tumble Through action row should also carry the mark; RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3332) has no bouncy-goblin entry, so the star lives on the skill only.

verdicts.name: Breath Control
verdicts.detail: The two mechanical clauses are delivered exactly and are the model case: the +1 stars ALL THREE saves rather than being narrowed to Fortitude (Ruling H / Q2) and is kept out of the flat totals (Ruling B — sheetDiff moves only situational.*), and the success→critical-success upgrade is in the one registry it belongs in (`degreeShifts: [{shift:'successToCrit', when:'on a save against an inhaled threat…', saves:['all']}]`). The '25 times as long' clause needs nothing further: a feat's `note` renders as a 'Note:' paragraph appended to that feat's own description (FeatsTab.tsx:77), which already prints the sentence, and there is no suffocation action or condition for a RecordMarker to attach to — no comparable record (inner-breath, internal-respirator, aqueous-dragonblood) carries one either. THE DEFECT is a duplicate: situationalBonuses.ts:135 hand-copies the shift into its own trigger — when: "against inhaled threats (success becomes critical success)" — while the degreeShifts field states the same rule again. Both land in the same star list for each save (explain.ts:439/564 merge FEAT_SITUATIONAL with the degreeShift-derived entries), so every save popup tells the player the crit upgrade twice, in two different wordings, from two registries that can drift. This is precisely the cleanup the project already made elsewhere — see the comment above 'conceited-mindset' (situationalBonuses.ts:640) where the degree half was stripped out of the `when` once the field could hold it, and the ⚠ on the `degreeShift` lane in docs/mechanic-lanes.md. Fix is to trim the parenthesis so the line carries only '+1 circumstance … against inhaled threats'.

verdicts.name: Breath of the Dragon
verdicts.detail: Nothing but the raw sentence is delivered. The action row exists only because the record has `actionCost {actions:2}` (sheetDiff actions[0]); storedFields carry no grantsActions, no specialStatistic, no damage scaling, no traits beyond dragonblood/magical, and registries is empty. Four requirements unmet on the SHEET half: (1) shape, damage type and save are printed as the generic 'match those of your draconic exemplar (see above)' — the app's own draconicExemplar collection is 44 name-only stubs (id/name/aonId, no descriptions, no shape/damage/save columns), so the lookup table the '(see above)' points at does not exist here; (2) the DC is never printed as a number, although the lane that fits it exactly is built — `specialStatistic` with `basis: {higherOfClassDcOrSpellDc}`, the same shape as the chronoskimmer and deviation DCs (docs/mechanic-lanes.md §K, 11 records); (3) no level scaling — the popup says 1d4 to a 19th-level character who should read 10d4; (4) no resolved damage-type trait, so the player cannot tell whether a target's resistance bites. BUILDER half: the answer this feat is supposed to consume is recorded nowhere — grep finds no draconic-exemplar pick on any record (the dragonblood heritage grants only the trait and a fear degreeShift; the lineage feats ask only their skill fallbacks). The app's own precedent for this is `draconic-resistance`, which asks its consumer-side question outright ('Choose the damage type associated with your draconic exemplar', effectChoices with a per-option resistance grant) — Breath of the Dragon asks nothing and reads nothing. CORRECT as-is: no use pip for the 1d4-round recharge (O2). MINOR display: the description still carries the AoN chrome trailer 'Breath of the Dragon leads to… Debilitating Breath, Energize Bite, …' (the leading 'Source … pg. 45' header is handled by AstRenderer's meta block).

verdicts.name: Breath of the Dragon (Dragonblood)
verdicts.detail: Same unbuilt record as its general-feat sibling, and worse in one respect. THE TEXT ITSELF HAS LOST BOTH AREA VALUES: public/core-descriptions.json feats/breath-of-the-dragon-dragonblood reads 'you can exhale a torrent of energy in a or a , dealing 1d4 damage' — the sibling record prints 'a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line'. Since the record carries no area field either, the ancestry version — the one a dragonblood character actually takes — shows an area of nothing at all, and the values have to be recovered from the source (an import defect in the description, not a rendering one). Everything else matches the sibling: storedFields hold only rarity/level/category/actionCost/aonId, registries empty, so the shape, damage type and save stay the generic 'match those of your draconic exemplar' sentence; the 'higher of your class DC or spell DC' is never printed as a number although the `specialStatistic` lane with `basis:{higherOfClassDcOrSpellDc}` exists for exactly that shape; the damage never scales past the printed 1d4; and the action's trait list carries no resolved damage-type trait. BUILDER half: the pick it is supposed to read does not exist anywhere in the app (no draconic-exemplar choice on the dragonblood heritage or any lineage feat; core.json's 44 draconicExemplar records are name-only stubs), so the feat correctly presents no picker of its own and correspondingly has no answer to resolve. The 1d4-round recharge needs only its sentence (O2) and has it. Harness note: `forced-placement` — no rendered slot offered this dragonblood ancestry feat to the fighter/human host, so eligibility is unevidenced either way; the sheet half was still measured and the defects above are read off the record and its own description.

requirements.what: Mindlink appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell with tradition OCCULT, reachable and readable from the entry, with this feat named as the source that granted it. The text names no rank, so it is cast at Mindlink's own base rank — no rank override is stated and none should be asserted.
requirements.clause: You can cast Mindlink as an innate occult spell once per day

requirements.what: One spendable use per day shown beside the innate spell entry: consumed when the spell is cast, restored at daily preparations. The entry must not read as unlimited/at-will.
requirements.clause: once per day

requirements.what: The targeting restriction must be written INTO Mindlink's description as the player reads it here, attributed to Aberration Kinship and visually separated from the spell's own printed rules (principle N2). This is load-bearing rather than decorative: Mindlink as normally printed targets a creature generally, so a player reading the unmodified description would legally target a non-aberration. The restriction applies to THIS grant only.
requirements.clause: but you can target only aberrations

requirements.what: No builder requirement. The feat names the spell, the tradition and the frequency, and restricts the targets itself — the player is asked nothing at build time.
requirements.clause: (whole feat)

requirements.what: The Perform action must show that an Acrobatics check is a legal roll in place of a Performance check — the substitution surfaces on the action the feat modifies (Ruling D/G: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). It is a substitution, not an added bonus: Performance remains legal too, so both skills must read as usable for Perform.
requirements.clause: You can roll an Acrobatics check instead of a Performance check when using the Perform action.

requirements.what: A `*` on the ACROBATICS skill row saying it can be rolled for the Perform action. Ruling C — a benefit named after an action stars every skill that could perform it, because the skill row is where the player looks the number up; the Perform action's own entry alone does not reach them there.
requirements.clause: You can roll an Acrobatics check instead of a Performance check when using the Perform action.

requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus restricted to Acrobatics checks made to Perform: a `*` on Acrobatics carrying the value and the restriction in its `when`, NEVER folded into the flat Acrobatics total (Ruling B — a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is correct). The Perform action entry should carry the same +1 inline. The bonus is GATED on being trained in both Acrobatics and Performance — a condition the sheet can compute — so it must not be shown as live for a character trained in only one; if it renders at all in that case it must state the condition and look inactive (Q27: an inert marker must look inert). Note the printed "+1 circumstances bonus" is a typo for circumstance.
requirements.clause: If you are trained in both Acrobatics and Performance, you gain a +1 circumstances bonus on Acrobatics checks made to Perform.

requirements.what: No builder requirement. Both skills are named by the feat; nothing is chosen and no option list exists. The trained-in-both clause is a condition on the bonus, not a prerequisite question to ask the player.
requirements.clause: (whole feat)

requirements.what: The feat teaches a named downtime activity that must appear in the character's actions/activities list with: its time cost (a full day of study), its requirement (healer's tools — the feat's needles are stored in them, so a character without healer's tools cannot perform it), its target (one ally), and the check it calls for — a Medicine check against a standard DC set by the ALLY'S level, not the acting character's. The DC scaling off someone else's level is the detail a generic "attempt a Medicine check" entry would lose.
requirements.clause: You spend a day studying an ally to attempt a Medicine check to improve their qi against a standard DC for your ally's level.

requirements.what: All four degrees of success must be readable in that activity's popup, including the CRITICAL FAILURE (the ally takes a -1 circumstance penalty to all downtime skill checks for a week) — an outcome that harms the target, which a summary showing only the good results would hide. This is an outcome table, NOT the `degreeShift` lane: nothing here changes a degree of success into another degree, so no degree-shift entry and no star on saves is owed.
requirements.clause: **Critical Success** ... **Success** ... **Critical Failure** ...

requirements.what: The +2/+1 circumstance bonus to a downtime skill check, the roll-twice-against-afflictions fortune effect, and the -1 penalty all land on the ALLY'S sheet. Ruling F: an effect on a teammate produces no number, no star and no modifier on your own sheet — the activity's own description already tells the player what the ally gets. Do not report the ally's bonus failing to reach anyone as a defect.
requirements.clause: You grant your ally the choice of a +2 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check ... this is a fortune effect.

requirements.what: The choice offered on a critical success belongs to the ALLY and is made at the table when the activity resolves, not at build time. It is not a builder picker.
requirements.clause: You grant your ally the choice of a +2 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check within the next week, or the ability to roll twice on their next saving throw ...

requirements.what: A per-target lockout tracked on someone else's sheet across a week. No use pip, no per-day counter and no resource on the acting character — the feat imposes no limit on how often YOU may use it, only on how often a given ally may benefit. It is text in the activity's popup and nothing more.
requirements.clause: The ally is then immune to all uses of Acupuncturist for 1 week.

requirements.what: An access clause. Q5: access does not gate a picker or a shop, and an access line owes no requirement of its own.
requirements.clause: **Access** Tian Xia origin

requirements.what: Darkvision must appear in the character's senses WHILE RAGING and be absent otherwise. The grant is conditional on a state the app already turns on and off, so it cannot be written as a permanent sense — a rager who is not raging would then read as having darkvision at all times, which is false. The sense arrives with the rage state and leaves with it.
requirements.clause: When you are raging, your visual senses improve, granting you darkvision.

requirements.what: The RAGE state's own entry must list darkvision among what it currently does. Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — and Principle B — a mode carries the full text of what it does. A player toggling rage must be able to see that this feat is part of what rage now gives them, on rage's record, not only in the feat's own description.
requirements.clause: When you are raging, your visual senses improve, granting you darkvision.

requirements.what: Q13: where the granted darkvision supersedes a low-light vision the character already has, show only darkvision while raging rather than both. The senses line must not read as two competing senses.
requirements.clause: granting you darkvision

requirements.what: No builder requirement. The sense, the trigger and the duration are all fixed by the feat; nothing is chosen.
requirements.clause: (whole feat)

requirements.what: Ask the player to pick ONE cantrip. The legal options are the load-bearing half: cantrips ONLY (not spells of any rank), and only those from a magical tradition OTHER than the character's own — every cantrip belonging to the character's own tradition is excluded, and where the character casts from more than one tradition, all of their own traditions are excluded. Per Q9 the list is filtered to what may legally be picked, and each option's tradition must be legible in the picker so the player can see why it qualifies. One pick, not a repeatable one.
requirements.clause: Choose one cantrip from a magical tradition other than your own.

requirements.what: For a PREPARED caster, the chosen cantrip must be offered as a legal option when preparing cantrips — ADDED to the existing option pool, not replacing anything ("in addition to your other options"). Per Q23 this question belongs to daily preparations and must not render in the builder, and it defaults to the last choice made. Preparing it must remain optional: the feat lets the player choose it, it never forces it into a slot.
requirements.clause: If you prepare spells, you can choose this spell when you prepare your cantrips, in addition to your other options.

requirements.what: For a REPERTOIRE caster, ask WHICH cantrip known is given up. The legal options are exactly the cantrips currently in that character's repertoire — no other list. This clause is mandatory for a repertoire caster ("replace"), unlike the prepared branch, so the question cannot be skipped without leaving the repertoire in a state the feat does not describe.
requirements.clause: If you have a spell repertoire, replace one of your cantrips known with the chosen spell.

requirements.what: For a REPERTOIRE caster the sheet must show the swap in the repertoire: the replaced cantrip GONE from the cantrips known, and the chosen cantrip in its place and castable. A grant that only adds the new cantrip without removing the old one gives the character one cantrip more than the feat allows.
requirements.clause: replace one of your cantrips known with the chosen spell

requirements.what: The two branches are mutually exclusive by caster type. Ask only the branch matching the character's spellcasting: a prepared caster must never be asked which cantrip known to give up, and a repertoire caster must never be shown a prepare-list addition. An inapplicable question rendered live reads as a broken app (Q27).
requirements.clause: If you prepare spells ... If you have a spell repertoire ...

requirements.what: The chosen cantrip must be presented as a spell of the CHARACTER'S class tradition — it sits in the character's own spellcasting entry and uses that entry's spell attack roll and DC, and its tradition must not be displayed as the alternate tradition it was taken from, which would state something false about how the player casts it. Per Q12, whichever presentation leaves the player least confused; if the origin tradition is shown at all it must be attributed to this feat and clearly not the tradition it is cast as.
requirements.clause: You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class's tradition.

requirements.what: The pick is re-choosable later, and the option filter is re-applied from scratch when it is: the replacement may come from the SAME alternate tradition or a DIFFERENT one, so the list must not be locked to the tradition chosen the first time. It stays filtered to traditions other than the character's own. Per principle K, re-choosing in the builder needs no sheet surface of its own.
requirements.clause: If you swap or retrain this cantrip later, you can choose its replacement from the same alternate tradition or a different one.
**Access** You are from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar.
requirements.what: NOTHING. An access line is a prerequisite, not a choice — the feat asks the player no question here, and nothing else in this feat asks one either. Whether the character is from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar is a fact about the character, not an answer the feat collects. (Prerequisites/access clauses are explicitly NOT a lane; Q5 further settles that an access clause on its own owes nothing.)

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against visual effects.
requirements.what: A `*` on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — carrying "+1 circumstance bonus against visual effects" and naming this feat. Q2: the clause names no single save, so it applies to saves generally and all three are starred. Ruling B: because the rules restrict it to visual effects it must live in the situational list with the restriction in its `when`, and must NOT be added into the printed save totals — a restricted bonus sitting outside the total is the correct behaviour. Bonus type is circumstance, which the star must state so the stacking display can compare it against another circumstance bonus with the same `when`.

requirements.clause: If you roll a success on a saving throw against a visual effect, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.what: A SECOND, SEPARATE requirement from the +1 — a success-to-critical-success upgrade, conditioned on "against a visual effect", surfaced on all three saves (Q2 again: no single save is named). The player must be able to read, at the save row, that a success promotes. ⚠ It must be one registry entry, not the sentence copied into a situational note as well — that is the two-registries-drifting failure the degreeShifts field exists to prevent. Note also that the two clauses have the same trigger but are different mechanics: folding the promotion into the +1 star's text and calling that one requirement loses the fact that the degree changes.

requirements.clause: Choose a Lore skill subcategory.
requirements.what: Ask which Lore subcategory. LEGAL OPTIONS: the text places no restriction whatever — any Lore subcategory, not the deity's, not one tied to a background, not one you lack. Lore subcategories are open-ended in the rules, so the picker must accept one the app's list does not carry (principle I — free-text player input is a legitimate choice type). ⚠ It must NOT filter out a Lore the character is already trained in: Q21's test is "wasted across the character's whole career", and the 3rd/7th/15th increases below make such a pick worthwhile even when the training itself is redundant — Canny Acumen exactly. On a repeat taking (see the Special clause) the subcategories already chosen through this feat are the ones that ARE illegal; per Q27 they are shown greyed with the reason, never rendered live and silently inert.

requirements.clause: You become trained in it.
requirements.what: The chosen Lore appears in the skill list at trained, with its modifier computed and this feat named as its source. The answer to the picker must also be legible on the feat itself — with two instances of a repeatable feat, an entry reading only "Additional Lore" makes the two indistinguishable and hides which Lores the character actually chose (Q20: a choice with a modelled consequence must show its answer).

requirements.clause: At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory.
requirements.what: At character levels 3, 7 and 15 the builder must offer an EXTRA skill increase — one over and above the class's normal skill increases — whose only legal target is this feat's own chosen Lore. Two things must be true and are easy to get wrong: it must not be spendable on any other skill (a one-option increase, not an entry into the general pool), and it must not consume the character's normal skill increase for that level. ⚠ OPEN READING, flagged rather than assumed: the text does not say what happens when the feat is taken after level 3, 7 or 15. "you gain the additional skill increases to that subcategory for the listed levels" reads as owing the passed ones immediately; the alternative is that only future listed levels pay out. Someone must rule this; do not let the builder decide it silently.

requirements.clause: At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory.
requirements.what: As those increases are applied the chosen Lore's rank rises — trained to expert to master to legendary — and the Lore's row shows the new rank and the recomputed modifier. This is the half the player reads off the sheet; the builder half above is only the offer.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you must select a new subcategory of Lore and you gain the additional skill increases to that subcategory for the listed levels.
requirements.what: The feat is REPEATABLE: after it is taken it must stay selectable at later feat slots rather than being greyed as already owned, and each new instance asks its own Lore question. "you must select a new subcategory" is a hard restriction on that question's option list — every subcategory already chosen through a previous instance of this feat is excluded (greyed with the reason, per Q27). This is the one place the picker DOES filter, and it is the opposite of the already-trained case above.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you must select a new subcategory of Lore and you gain the additional skill increases to that subcategory for the listed levels.
requirements.what: Each instance carries its OWN independent 3rd/7th/15th increase track for its OWN subcategory. Two instances mean two Lore rows each climbing separately — not one shared pool of increases the player can pour into a single Lore, and not one instance's increases silently applying to the other's subcategory.

requirements.clause: You descend from the rare psychic vampires known as vetalaranas. Your forebear gained sustenance from the mental and emotional energy of living creatures, which manifests in you as powerful resistance to such effects.
requirements.what: NOTHING. This is flavour — lineage and origin — and the feat asks the player no question anywhere in its text. No picker, no free-text field, no daily choice. Recorded explicitly so that the absence reads as measured rather than overlooked.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait,
requirements.what: A `*` on the WILL save only — this clause names Will, so Q2's "all three saves" does not apply to it — carrying "+1 circumstance bonus against effects with the emotion trait" and naming this feat. Ruling B: the emotion restriction keeps it out of the printed Will total and inside the situational list with the restriction in its `when`. The bonus type (circumstance) must be stated for the stacking display.

requirements.clause: and when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.what: A separate success-to-critical-success upgrade, conditioned on effects with the emotion trait, readable at the save row. ⚠ THE SCOPE IS THE OPEN QUESTION and must not be answered by accident: this second clause says "a saving throw", not "a Will save" — read at its word it covers Fortitude and Reflex saves against emotion effects too, and Ruling H (where the rules are open, stay open — star everything plausible, printed trigger in the note) points at starring all three. The narrower reading inherits "Will" from the first half of the sentence. Whoever builds it must choose deliberately and put the printed trigger in the note; narrowing it silently would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's. Either way this is a DIFFERENT requirement from the +1 star, on a different mechanic, and the sentence must not be duplicated into a situational note as well.

requirements.clause: Choose a common ancestry or another ancestry to which you have access.
requirements.what: Ask which ancestry is adopted. LEGAL OPTIONS, exactly as the text draws them: every COMMON ancestry unconditionally, plus any non-common ancestry the character has access to. Access is a table-level permission the app cannot verify, so per Ruling H the uncommon/rare entries stay reachable with their rarity shown rather than hard-blocked — and per Q5 rarity by itself gates nothing. ⚠ The character's OWN ancestry is the single pick that buys nothing (its feats are already available), so it fails Q21's "wasted across the whole career" test — it is excluded, or shown greyed saying why (Q27). The text gives no repeat clause, so this is one ancestry, chosen once.

requirements.clause: Choose a common ancestry or another ancestry to which you have access.
requirements.what: The feat entry must name the adopted ancestry. The choice has a real mechanical consequence, so it needs an answer the player can read back — an entry saying only "Adopted Ancestry" leaves the character sheet unable to state which culture was adopted, and the player cannot check what widened their feat list.

requirements.clause: You can select ancestry feats from the ancestry you chose, in addition to your character's own ancestry,
requirements.what: The real payload, and it is entirely a builder requirement: at EVERY ancestry-feat slot the character has, now and at every later level, the option list must be the chosen ancestry's ancestry feats MERGED with the character's own — level-gated and prerequisite-gated as normal, additive ("in addition to"), never replacing the native list. A label recording the answer is not enough here: Q20's first test is whether the app models a mechanical consequence, and this one it does.

requirements.clause: You can select ancestry feats from the ancestry you chose, in addition to your character's own ancestry,
requirements.what: An ancestry feat taken through this route must land on the sheet exactly as a native one does — its senses, speeds, granted actions, stars, resistances and any pickers of its own all reach the sheet under their own lanes.
