A borrowed-ancestry feat that appears in the feat list but whose effects are inert because its ancestry does not match the character's is the failure mode this requirement exists to name.

requirements.clause: as long as the ancestry feats don't require any physiological feature that you lack, as determined by the GM.
requirements.what: NOTHING — and deliberately so. "as determined by the GM" hands this to the table; a physiology filter must not be built, because the app would be inventing rulings the book declines to make. If any feat is nonetheless withheld from the list, Q27 requires it to say why rather than sit inert. No sheet surface either.

requirements.clause: In the heat of battle, you are capable of amazing feats of strength. While you are Raging,
requirements.what: NOTHING. The feat asks the player no question — no pick, no free text, no daily choice. Raging is a state entered in play, not an answer collected while building.

requirements.clause: While you are Raging,
requirements.what: Both benefits below are scoped to the Rage state and must be surfaced as part of it, not baked into the character's baseline numbers. Q11's test decides it: the effect can be shut down (Rage ends), so it is a toggleable state rather than a passive bonus — and the state must carry this feat's full printed text so the player can read what it does while it runs (Principle B). The player must be able to tell, at a glance, that these two numbers are only true while raging.

requirements.clause: increase your encumbered and maximum Bulk limits by 2;
requirements.what: While raging, BOTH carrying thresholds rise by 2 — the encumbered limit and the maximum Bulk limit — and the encumbered/overloaded state recomputes against the raised numbers, so a character who is encumbered at rest may read as unencumbered while raging. Two numbers, not one. ⚠ NAMED AS A POSSIBLE UNBUILT LANE: the lane vocabulary has no entry for a character-side Bulk-limit change. The nearest, `bulkIgnore`, is item-only ("ignore N Bulk", "this counts as Light") and is about an item's own bulk, not the carrier's thresholds. This is the "clearly mechanical, no lane at all" shape and is worth checking before it is filed under `note`.

requirements.clause: you also gain a +1 status bonus to Athletics checks to lift heavy objects, Escape, and Force Open.
requirements.what: A `*` on ATHLETICS carrying "+1 status bonus while Raging, on checks to lift heavy objects, to Escape, and to Force Open". Bonus type is status, which the star must state for stacking. "Lift heavy objects" names no action, so it survives only as text inside this star. ⚠ Ruling C ("a bonus named after an ACTION stars every skill that could perform it") must NOT be applied blindly here: the bonus is worded as a bonus to ATHLETICS CHECKS to Escape, so an Escape rolled with Acrobatics or with an unarmed attack modifier does not get it, and starring those would state something false.

requirements.clause: you also gain a +1 status bonus to Athletics checks to lift heavy objects, Escape, and Force Open.
requirements.what: The second half of Q2's "both": besides the skill star, the ACTIONS Escape and Force Open each carry a marker showing this feat modifies them, value inline, star linking back to the feat (Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). Each marker must say the bonus applies only to the Athletics version of that action and only while Raging, otherwise a player reading the Escape entry with Acrobatics in mind takes a bonus they do not have.

requirements.clause: **Access** Mihrini ethnicity
requirements.what: Nothing owed. An access clause is eligibility prose, not a mechanic (mechanic-lanes, "NOT lanes": prerequisites and access clauses). It may gate who is offered the feat, but it asks the player no question and puts nothing on the sheet.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Thievery (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Thievery).
requirements.what: A CONDITIONAL question, asked only when the character is already trained in Thievery: "which other skill do you become trained in instead?" If they are not already trained in Thievery there is no question at all — the grant is flat. Legal options: any skill other than Thievery. One pick, no repeats, no later-level scaling. Per Q27 (the owner's own bug report is literally this picker) skills the character is already trained in must LOOK unpickable — greyed and saying why — never rendered live and silently inert; per Q21 they are genuinely wasted here, since nothing in this feat upgrades at a later level, so they are correctly unavailable rather than kept live.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Thievery (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Thievery).
requirements.what: Thievery reads trained on the skills list — or, when the fallback fired, the substituted skill reads trained instead and Thievery is untouched. The rank is a real proficiency change (it moves the skill's modifier), and this feat must be named as its source in that skill's breakdown.

requirements.clause: If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.what: A success becomes a critical success, restricted to Pick a Lock. Per Q2 this is BOTH surfaces from one entry: a `*` on Thievery — the skill the player looks the number up on — carrying the clause, AND a marker on the Pick a Lock action itself (Ruling D / Q8: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). Thievery is the only skill that performs Pick a Lock, so Ruling C's "star every skill that could perform it" resolves to Thievery alone. It moves no number — the restriction stays in the star's `when`, never folded into the Thievery total (Ruling B). ⚠ If the substituted-skill fallback fired, this clause is unaffected: it names Thievery explicitly and still stars Thievery, even for a character who took the feat's proficiency in something else.

requirements.clause: Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks.
requirements.what: Ask which attack. The legal list is tightly restricted and all three restrictions do work: the eidolon's own attacks (not the character's), MELEE only (a ranged eidolon attack is not legal), UNARMED only, and STARTING only — the attacks the eidolon began with, not ones added later by other feats or evolutions. Per Q9 the picker offers only those; per Q27 anything shown but unpickable must be greyed with its reason. One pick. A character with no eidolon has no legal option, and the picker must say that rather than render empty.

requirements.clause: It gains one of the following traits, chosen when you gain the feat: disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, or versatile bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
requirements.what: Ask which trait. The list is CLOSED and has EIGHT entries, not six — "versatile bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing" is three separate options (versatile B, versatile P, versatile S), and collapsing them to one "versatile" option would lose the damage type the player picked. One pick, no repeats, no later-level scaling. "chosen when you gain the feat" fixes it at build time — it is not a daily choice (Q23) and not re-asked in play; per Principle K, re-choosing it is a builder action needing no sheet surface.

requirements.clause: It gains one of the following traits, chosen when you gain the feat: disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, or versatile bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
requirements.what: The picked trait must be written onto THAT SPECIFIC attack and be readable in its trait line — Principle C, a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing. Both answers have to land together: the trait belongs to the one chosen attack, not to the eidolon generally, so an eidolon with two starting melee unarmed attacks must show it on one and not the other. A versatile pick additionally makes that damage type selectable on the attack, which is the whole mechanical content of the option. Per the companion ruling in DECIDED SCOPE this lives on the EIDOLON's stat block and attack entry, never on the character's own strikes — its absence from the character's sheet is correct, not a gap.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects with the darkness or shadow traits.
requirements.what: A `*` on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — each carrying "+1 circumstance bonus against effects with the darkness or shadow traits". Q2 is explicit: when a bonus applies to saves generally rather than to one named save, star all three. The +1 must NOT be added into the printed save totals: it is a flat bonus the rules restrict, so per Ruling B it lives in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, and a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is the correct display. The feat has exactly one mechanical clause and asks the player nothing — no choice, no resource, no action, no mode (it cannot be shut down, so per Q11 it is a passive/situational bonus rather than a toggle).

requirements.clause: You and your allies can Treat your Wounds without a healer's toolkit.
requirements.what: A marker on the Treat Wounds action stating that no healer's toolkit is needed to treat THIS character's wounds, and a `*` on Medicine carrying the same — Q2's "both", with Ruling C resolving "every skill that could perform Treat Wounds" to Medicine alone. Ruling D governs the placement: a clause with no stat row of its own attaches to the thing it modifies (Magic Hands marks Treat Wounds, and this is the same shape). ⚠ The scope is narrow and the wording must keep it: it waives the toolkit only when the wounds being treated are YOURS. It does not let this character treat someone else without a kit. The half where an ally is the one rolling is still owed a surface here rather than nothing — Principle A: an ally-facing effect still needs an indication on the record it modifies. It moves no number.

requirements.clause: Once per day, when someone rolls a failure or a critical failure on a check to Treat your Wounds, you can focus on your internal cohesion to increase the degree of success by one step.
requirements.what: A one-degree-better shift on failure and critical failure, restricted to checks to Treat this character's Wounds. Per Q2 one entry produces both surfaces: a marker on the Treat Wounds action and a `*` on Medicine. Q15 does not apply — that governs effects firing on a CRITICAL SUCCESS; this fires on a failure, so it is implemented. Note it upgrades from failure AND from critical failure (two entry degrees), so a surface that only says "a failure becomes a success" hides half the clause — the same both-directions omission Round 10 caught on Dragon's Presence.

requirements.clause: Once per day, when someone rolls a failure or a critical failure on a check to Treat your Wounds, you can focus on your internal cohesion...
requirements.what: A per-day resource on this character's sheet: one spendable use, shown beside the feat, spent when the player uses it, restored at daily preparations. This is a per-DAY frequency, so O2's "per-round frequencies get no use pip" does not exempt it — the pip is owed. The resource belongs to this character even when an ally is the one who rolled the failed check, because "you can focus" is this character's ability.

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NOTHING in the builder. No skill choice, no option list, no free text, no daily choice. Both of its mechanical clauses are automatic consequences of owning it; the only player decision is the in-play one to spend the daily use, which is the sheet-side pip above, not a build-time question.

requirements.clause: A blade of shearing wind races away from you in a . Each creature in the area takes damage with a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: The impulse must appear as a usable entry in the character's actions/impulses list, with its action cost, its traits, its area, its damage and its save type readable, and its full text reachable from the entry — the same shape Ruling E gives a reaction (the entry, with its trigger and requirements in the popup, is the surface). ⚠ THE TEXT AS SUPPLIED CANNOT SATISFY ITS OWN DISPLAY REQUIREMENT: three values have been stripped by an unsubstituted-template defect — the area ("races away from you in a ." — the line's length is missing), the damage dice ("takes damage"), and the save ("with a save", type unstated). Those three numbers are exactly what the player reads off this entry, so the requirement is unmeetable until the source text is repaired. Stating the requirement from what remains would silently specify an entry that prints no area, no dice and no save name.

requirements.clause: On your next turn, you can use a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to return the boomerang to you... You must have line of effect to the boomerang and be within 60 feet of it.
requirements.what: A SECOND, separate action entry — one action, concentrate trait — to return the boomerang, with its requirements (line of effect to the boomerang, and within 60 feet of it) written in its popup. This is the Minor Omen shape: the entry plus its requirements in the popup is the whole surface. It is a distinct entry from the impulse above and must not be collapsed into it; Principle H's "one action under both costs" is the wrong shape here, because this is a different action with a different cost, not the same action at two costs.

requirements.clause: the boomerang whirls in place until the end of your next turn... then the impulse ends.
requirements.what: No mode, and no tracking of whether the boomerang is out. Q1 settles it: an effect lasting until the end of your next turn is about a round, and effects lasting 1 round are not implemented — indication only; a mode is for something longer. So the return action above is simply listed, its availability window left to the player. Likewise nothing is owed for the damage to creatures in the area, the whirling square, or a creature ending its turn there — those land on enemies and on the battlefield, which mechanic-lanes excludes explicitly.

requirements.clause: with a save against your class DC
requirements.what: No new statistic. This points at a number that already has its own row on the sheet — the class DC — which is precisely the exclusion recorded for `specialStatistic` ("a record pointing at a statistic that already has a row"). The impulse's entry should name which DC it uses so the player knows where to read it, but no second DC and no separate breakdown row is owed.

requirements.clause: **Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d4.
requirements.what: The damage shown in the impulse entry must be the value for THIS character's level, not the base line alone — base damage plus 1d4 for every 2 levels of heightening. A heightening line printed as static prose beneath an unscaled number makes the player do the arithmetic the sheet exists to do. ⚠ Unmeetable as written for the same reason as the entry above: the base damage was stripped from the text, so there is no floor for the +1d4 steps to build on.

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NOTHING in the builder. It names no choice, no option list, no free text and no daily choice — every decision it contains (whether to return the boomerang, when) is made at the table with the action entries above.

requirements.clause: During your daily preparations, you can meditate upon fragmentary memories of your past lives to gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The player must be asked "which skill do you become trained in?" — and asked at DAILY PREPARATIONS, not in the builder (Q23: daily choices must not render in the builder; they appear when the player presses Daily preparations and default to the last choice made). Legal options: ANY one skill — the text puts no restriction on the list, so it is not limited to the leshy's own skills or to a class list. The pick is re-made every day and may be changed each time; it is not locked in at the level the feat was taken. Per Q27 a skill the character is already trained in or better must not be rendered as a live option — the grant would be genuinely wasted (no later-level scaling exists here to rescue it, so Q21's exception does not apply): show it greyed and say why, never identical to a live option and silently inert. The picker also needs an "unpicked" state — the meditation is optional ("you CAN meditate"), so no pick is a legal outcome.

requirements.clause: …to gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice. This proficiency lasts until you prepare again.
requirements.what: The chosen skill's row must actually move: proficiency rank trained, with the trained proficiency folded into the printed modifier, sourced to Ageless Spirit in the breakdown. It must also read as TEMPORARY where the player looks at it — the rank is gone at the next daily preparation, so a rank shown identically to a permanent one lies about the character. Concretely: the grant is cleared on rest/daily prep and re-applied only from that day's pick.

requirements.clause: Since this proficiency is temporary, you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat.
requirements.what: The temporary rank must be invisible to every eligibility test: a feat whose prerequisite is "trained in X" must stay unavailable, and a skill increase must not treat the skill as already trained. So the same character has two answers to "am I trained in X?" — yes for the modifier the sheet prints, no for anything the builder gates on. ⚠ No lane in mechanic-lanes.md covers a proficiency that counts for rolls but not for prerequisites; this is a "no lane at all, but clearly mechanical" candidate, and the failure mode is silent (the feat list would simply offer one feat too many).

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are wielding a shield with a shield boss or shield spikes in one hand. --- You change your grip on the shield… You can use Agile Shield Grip again to switch to a normal grip, returning the damage to the usual amount and removing the agile trait.
requirements.what: Agile Shield Grip must appear in the actions list as a 1-action activity, with its Requirement ("wielding a shield with a shield boss or shield spikes in one hand") printed in its popup, and the popup must state that using it again switches back. This is the Minor Omen shape applied to an action rather than a reaction (Principle E): the entry plus its trigger/requirement text is a requirement in its own right, independent of the numbers below.

requirements.clause: You can use Agile Shield Grip again to switch to a normal grip, returning the damage to the usual amount and removing the agile trait.
requirements.what: The changed grip is a state the player turns on and off, so per Q11 it is a MODE, not a passive bonus — the text explicitly says it can be shut down and restored. The mode must be visibly running (the player has to be able to tell which grip they are in, since both grips print different Strike numbers), and turning it off must restore the weapon's printed die and remove the trait rather than leaving the reduced values stuck.

requirements.clause: You reduce your shield boss and shield spikes weapon damage die to 1d4.
requirements.what: While the mode is on, the Strike rows for shield boss and shield spikes must PRINT 1d4 as the damage die — it replaces the weapon's own printed die rather than adding a note beside it (the same "it is a value, not an annotation" shape the owner ruled for reach, Principle L). It applies to both weapons, not one chosen weapon, and only to those two — no other Strike changes.

requirements.clause: As long as the weapon damage die is 1d4, your shield boss and shield spike Strikes gain the agile weapon trait.
requirements.what: The agile trait must appear on those two Strike rows AND its consequence must follow through: agile changes the multiple attack penalty for those Strikes to the agile progression (−4/−8 rather than −5/−10), so the three numbers the Strike row prints must recompute. The trait is conditional on the die being 1d4 — it rides on the same mode, and if any other source ever restores a larger die the trait must go with it.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No builder question. The feat names nothing the player chooses at build time — no weapon pick, no skill, no option list. Toggling the grip is play-time interaction with the sheet, not a build choice.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet is falling.
requirements.what: Air Cushion must appear in the reactions list (it is a kineticist impulse taken as a reaction), with its trigger — a creature within 60 feet is falling — in its popup. Per the owner's Minor Omen answer (Principle E) and Q4, for an effect that lands on the falling creature the reaction entry IS the surface; nothing further is owed.

requirements.clause: Air currents flow upward to slow the target's fall to 60 feet per round. The cushion ends when the target reaches the ground, and the creature takes no damage from the fall.
requirements.what: The effect text must be readable in the reaction's popup, and it must move NO number on the sheet. The target is another creature (Ruling F — an effect landing on someone else gets no star and no modifier), and even where the target is the caster, fall damage is HP, which never moves sheet stats (Ruling E). Do not report the absent fall-damage immunity as a gap; the full text in the popup is the specified behaviour.

requirements.clause: You can't use Air Cushion again while you have one in effect.
requirements.what: Printed in the popup as a restriction — NOT a use counter. It is not a per-day or per-hour resource (which is what a limited-uses pip is for); it is gated on a duration the app cannot observe, since the cushion ends when the target lands or after a minute. The app supplies the capability and the player supplies the timing (Principle M2), the same reason a per-round frequency gets no pip (Principle O2).

requirements.clause: **Level (8th)** The range is 120 feet, and you can create cushions for up to 5 falling creatures with one reaction.
requirements.what: The entry the player reads must state the numbers for THIS character's level: below 8th, range 60 feet and one falling creature; at 8th and above, range 120 feet and up to 5 creatures with one reaction. Showing the 8th-level line to a 1st-level kineticist, or hiding it from a 10th-level one, both make the sheet state something false about the character (Q12 — whichever leaves the player least confused). This is the same shape as an innate-spell ladder gated by minLevel, applied to an action's own text.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No builder question. The feat names no choice — no target picked at build time, no option list, no element pick beyond the air gate the feat's own trait already presumes.

requirements.clause: You gain darkvision.
requirements.what: Darkvision must appear on the character's senses line, sourced to Alabaster Eyes. Per Q13, where the character's ancestry already gives low-light vision, show ONLY darkvision — darkvision supersedes it, and printing both invites the player to think they are two separate senses.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain out of this feat or into this feat.
requirements.what: Two builder restrictions the feat states about itself. (1) It may be offered only for a 1st-level ancestry feat slot; at every later slot it is not a legal pick — per Q9 filtered out of the list, and per Q27, anywhere it IS shown it must look unpickable and say why, never render identically to a live option and refuse silently. (2) It must be excluded from retraining in BOTH directions: a character who has it cannot swap it away, and a character who lacks it cannot retrain into it. ⚠ No lane in mechanic-lanes.md covers a per-feat availability/retraining restriction; the nearest is dedicationGate, which is a different clause. This is a "no lane at all" candidate.

requirements.clause: In place of the normal vishkanyan golden eyes, you were born with especially perceptive snow-white eyes.
requirements.what: No choice is asked. The eye-colour sentence is flavour; the feat replaces nothing the player picks and offers no options list. The only builder work this feat creates is the availability rule above.

requirements.clause: When using the Crafting skill to Identify Alchemy on an alchemical item you hold, you can do so as a single action, rather than spending 10 minutes.
requirements.what: Identify Alchemy must appear under BOTH costs — its native 10-minute form and the 1-action form this feat enables — with the explanation in the popup. This is exactly the owner's Quick Recognition specification (Principle H: "an action whose cost changes conditionally appears under both costs, with the explanation in the popup"), and both must remain visible because the 1-action form is conditional and the 10-minute form still applies when it is not met.

requirements.clause: …on an alchemical item you hold…
requirements.what: The condition must be carried in the popup with the 1-action cost: it applies only to Identify Alchemy, only on an ALCHEMICAL item, and only one you are HOLDING. Without it the sheet would advertise a 1-action Identify Alchemy for every item, which is a different rule from the one the feat prints. The mark belongs on the Identify Alchemy action itself — the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D, Q8) — attributed to Alchemical Assessment so it is not mistaken for the action's own printed rules.

requirements.clause: You can identify alchemical items quickly.
requirements.what: Nothing is owed on the Crafting skill row. No number moves — the feat changes how long the activity takes, not the check — so this is not a situational star: Principle J puts stars on the specific skill or action AFFECTED, and what is affected here is the action's cost, which the action entry already carries. Do not report a missing `*` on Crafting as a defect.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No builder question. The feat asks the player nothing — no skill choice, no option list, no free text.

requirements.clause: You can use the Craft activity to create alchemical items.
requirements.what: The Craft activity carries a marker naming this feat: alchemical items are now legal Craft targets for this character. Ruling D / Q8 — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and Craft is the record this clause modifies. A player reading Craft otherwise has no way to know the four formulas this same feat gave them are usable.

requirements.clause: You can use the Craft activity to create alchemical items.
requirements.what: The permission is a real gate, not prose. The app must be able to record 'this character may Craft alchemical items' and read it wherever craftability is decided, so an alchemical formula in the book is CRAFTABLE rather than an inert reference. Q19 settled this shape for the same sentence elsewhere: formulas a feat writes into the book are craftable and join the craft/prepare pools as pool membership, never an inventory copy. Without the gate being readable, this feat's own four formulas do nothing.

requirements.clause: When you select this feat, you immediately add the formulas for four common 1st-level alchemical items to your formula book.
requirements.what: FOUR picks, asked in the builder (Q14 #7). Legal options are filtered, not the whole item list (Q9): items that are alchemical AND common AND exactly 1st level. Four DISTINCT items — a formula the book already holds must be shown greyed with the reason rather than rendered live and silently inert (Q27). The grant fires once, 'when you select this feat' — no repeats, no later-level scaling.

requirements.clause: …add the formulas for four common 1st-level alchemical items to your formula book.
requirements.what: The four picks are written INTO a formula book and listed there as '<item name> formula' — a reference, never a copy in inventory (Q14 #1–#2). It is a ONE-TIME WRITE severed from the feat once chosen: the book owns them, deleting the book loses them permanently and the feat will not re-grant (Q14 #9), so the book's contents must be its own state and not derived from the owned feat — the opposite shape from every other grant. Removable, searchable, counted against a capacity of 100 (Q14 #3–#5). ⚠ mechanic-lanes.md carries no lane for a formula book at all, although Q14 specifies the system in full.

requirements.clause: …to your formula book.
requirements.what: The character must HAVE a formula book for the four to land in — taking a feat that writes formulas ensures one exists; if they have none, add it (Q14 #6). Any of the four left unpicked renders as an EMPTY SLOT in the book's popup, and pressing that slot opens this feat's filtered selection (Q14 #8), so a player who skipped the builder can still see and settle what they are owed.

requirements.clause: You gain a familiar…
requirements.what: A familiar appears in the Companions tab, attributed to this feat, with its own stat block. Per DECIDED SCOPE (★ Companions) every number below belongs on the COMPANION's sheet and not on the character's — that placement is the specification, and its absence from the character sheet is correct rather than a gap.

requirements.clause: …doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2).
requirements.what: The feat's own words presuppose that a familiar-ability budget exists and is chosen by the player. The player must be asked which familiar abilities they take, with the budget (typically 2) shown and the remaining count visible.

requirements.clause: …which has the Construct familiar ability; this is permanent…
requirements.what: Construct appears on the familiar as a granted, PERMANENT ability, attributed to this feat — not one of the player's chosen abilities, and not something they can spend away, swap out on a daily re-selection, or lose.

requirements.clause: …doesn't require the familiar to have the Tough familiar ability…
requirements.what: Construct's normal prerequisite is WAIVED for this grant. If the app validates familiar-ability prerequisites, Construct here must be legal with Tough absent, and Tough must not be auto-taken to satisfy it — auto-taking it would silently consume one of the two free picks the next clause exists to protect.

requirements.clause: …doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2).
requirements.what: The ability budget must EXCLUDE this grant. The player is still asked for the full usual number of picks and the remaining-picks count must read that way — Construct occupying a slot is the failure mode, and it would be invisible unless the count is computed with the grant held outside it.

requirements.clause: The familiar uses your Intelligence modifier to determine its Perception, Acrobatics, and Stealth modifiers.
requirements.what: Three numbers on the familiar's stat block — Perception, Acrobatics, Stealth — computed from the CHARACTER's Intelligence modifier, REPLACING whatever the default familiar rule uses for them. They must track the character's Intelligence as it changes (a level-up boost, an apex item), not be frozen at the moment the familiar was created.

requirements.clause: You gain the Alchemical Crafting feat.
requirements.what: Alchemical Crafting appears on the character as a granted feat with its details readable and attributed to this feat. Principle G: a granted record needs its details surfaced AND its choices offered — printing the name alone is not the grant. Everything Alchemical Crafting itself does must fire from here: the Craft-alchemical-items permission and its four formulas.

requirements.clause: You gain the Alchemical Crafting feat.
requirements.what: The granted feat itself asks a question, so this grant asks it too: the four common 1st-level alchemical formula picks must be offered in the builder, sourced to this grant. A grant that fires the granted feat's numbers but swallows its picker leaves four formulas unchosen and invisible.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically gain that feat (from your background or the alchemist class, for example), you instead gain a different 1st-level Crafting skill feat.
requirements.what: When Alchemical Crafting already arrives from an AUTOMATIC source — the text's trigger is 'would automatically gain', naming background and the alchemist class, not merely 'already have it' — the grant flips to a picker. Legal options: skill feats of the Crafting skill, exactly 1st level, with Alchemical Crafting itself excluded. The player must be ASKED; a silent no-op here costs them a whole feat, and an option they cannot take must look untakeable rather than be inert (Q27).

requirements.clause: …you instead gain a different 1st-level Crafting skill feat.
requirements.what: Whichever feat actually results — Alchemical Crafting or the substitute — is the one shown on the sheet, with its own details surfaced and its own grants fired. The substitute is a real feat with real consequences, not a label.

requirements.clause: Add an additional common 1st-level alchemical formula to your formula book when you take this feat.
requirements.what: ONE further pick, filtered to common AND alchemical AND exactly 1st level (Q9, Q14 #7). 'Additional' is load-bearing: it is a fifth formula on top of Alchemical Crafting's four, never a replacement for them. And this sentence does not depend on the previous one — it must still be offered when the redundancy clause replaced Alchemical Crafting with a different feat.

requirements.clause: Add an additional common 1st-level alchemical formula to your formula book…
requirements.what: That formula is written into the formula book as a reference (Q14 #1–#2), a one-time write the book then owns (Q14 #9). Unpicked, it shows as an empty slot in the book's popup that opens this feat's filtered list when pressed (Q14 #8).

requirements.clause: Each time you gain a level beyond 1st, add one common alchemical formula of that level to your formula book.
requirements.what: A RECURRING pick — once at every level from 2nd to 20th, 19 further picks over a career, offered at each level-up rather than bundled into one prompt. Each level's list is filtered to common alchemical items whose level EQUALS the level just gained: the text says 'of that level', not 'of that level or lower', so a 7th-level character is choosing among 7th-level formulas only.

requirements.clause: Each time you gain a level beyond 1st, add one common alchemical formula of that level to your formula book.
requirements.what: Each level's formula is written into the book (one-time write, Q14 #9). Levels whose pick was skipped show as EMPTY SLOTS (Q14 #8), so a 12th-level character can see the eleven grants he never settled instead of losing them silently. Capacity 100 (Q14 #5) is genuinely in play here: this feat alone writes 24 formulas across a full career.

requirements.clause: You receive a +2 circumstance bonus to Will saves against mental effects that would make you controlled…
requirements.what: A `*` on the WILL save carrying '+2 circumstance' with the printed trigger. It must NOT be added into the flat Will total — Ruling B: a bonus the rules restrict belongs in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, and sitting outside the total is the correct result, not a missing number.

requirements.clause: …and if you roll a success against such an effect, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.what: A success→critical-success degree shift on the Will save, scoped to the same trigger ('such an effect' = a mental effect that would make you controlled). Q2 puts the entry on the statistic the player reads the number off; this one names Will specifically, so it lands on Will alone — the 'star all three saves' half of Q2 is for a clause that applies to saves generally, which this is not. ⚠ It must live in the one degree-shift registry alongside the bonus's own entry, not be retyped as prose in a second place.

requirements.clause: However, you gain none of these benefits against effects originating from alghollthus…
requirements.what: The alghollthu carve-out must ride on BOTH entries above, in their `when`/note text. A star reading '+2 vs mental control, success becomes critical success' with no exception stated says something false at precisely the table where the feat's flavour makes it likeliest to matter. The app cannot know whether a source is an alghollthu, so this is text the player reads rather than a computation — but it is not optional text.

requirements.clause: …and instead take a -2 circumstance penalty against mental effects from alghollthus.
requirements.what: A second, opposite-signed entry: −2 circumstance, trigger 'mental effects from alghollthus'. Two things about it. (a) Its `when` differs from the +2's, so both display — the stacking rule shows both when the triggers differ and makes no attempt to reason about overlap. (b) ⚠ The text names no roll for this half — it says 'against mental effects', not 'to Will saves' — so per Ruling H (where the rules are open, stay open: star everything plausible, printed trigger in the note) it should surface on every save it could plausibly apply to rather than being narrowed to Will on the app's own authority. Narrowing it would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: NOTHING is owed here. The feat asks the player no question at any point — no option list, no free-text field, no level-scaling pick, no re-selection. Its entire delivery is the four sheet surfaces above.

requirements.clause: Choose a Large or larger corpse of an animal that died within the past day.
requirements.what: NOT a builder question, despite the word 'choose'. The thing chosen is an object in the fiction whose existence the app cannot know, and it is re-chosen every time the feat is used rather than once at selection. Principle M2: the app supplies the capability, the player supplies the timing and the target. No picker — and no free-text field either, unlike Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location, because that one is chosen once and kept while this one is not. The corpse's constraints (Large or larger, animal, dead within the past day) are text the player reads in the clause, not options the app enumerates.

requirements.clause: While using Survival to Subsist near the carcass, you always receive enough food for yourself and one additional Medium creature, using up the meat from the carcass to do so.
requirements.what: A `*` on SURVIVAL carrying the clause. Only Survival is starred even though Subsist can also be attempted with Society — Ruling C's 'star every skill that could perform the action' is overridden here by the feat's own restriction, which names Survival explicitly. It moves NO number: the outcome is guaranteed rather than modified. Q20's refinement is what makes the star owed anyway — the clause names a specific stat, so that stat carries a `*` back to the feat whether or not a number moves (the Assurance shape). ⚠ Principle P (Posse: a benefit behind a deliberate out-of-combat action needs no star) does not apply — there the bonus lands on a LATER roll the player has already earned; here the modified roll IS the deliberate action, so the star sits on the row being read at the moment it matters (Ruling D).

requirements.clause: While using Survival to Subsist near the carcass…
requirements.what: A marker on the SUBSIST activity itself, with the clause in its popup. Q2: both — star the skill AND mark the action; Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and a player about to Subsist is looking at Subsist, not at the skill list. The note must carry the carcass conditions so the player can tell when the guarantee is live.

requirements.clause: …enough food for yourself and one additional Medium creature…
requirements.what: The ally's half of the food produces no number on your sheet (Ruling F), and food is not a modelled resource for you either. Principle A — an ally-facing effect still needs an indication on the record it modifies — is already satisfied by the Survival star and the Subsist marker required above; nothing further is owed for this half.

requirements.clause: Since you're using all of the animal, others can't use the carcass's meat for any other purpose, including their own use of All of the Animal.
requirements.what: NO requirement. It restricts other characters and the state of an object in the world, neither of which is on this sheet, and it is table adjudication in any case. It stays as the feat's own description text and needs no surface.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You fail or critically fail a Will save against an emotion effect.
requirements.what: The feat appears as a triggered ability in the reactions list, with its trigger printed verbatim in its popup. The trigger has three parts the popup must keep: it fires on a failure OR a critical failure (not failure alone), only on a WILL save, and only against an EMOTION effect. This is the exact shape of the Minor Omen exemplar, where the owner ruled the entry in the reactions list is the whole surface. Note the text prints no Frequency line, so no per-day use pip is owed.

requirements.clause: Reroll the triggering saving throw with a +1 status bonus. You must use the second result, even if it's worse.
requirements.what: The popup carries the full effect text, both halves. The +1 status bonus moves no row on the sheet: it exists only on the reroll made inside this reaction, never on an ordinary Will save, so it must not be added to the Will save total. And the downside — 'you must use the second result, even if it's worse' — has to be shown, not dropped; a record that prints a cost and a benefit in one sentence and surfaces only the benefit is the failure the two both-directions degreeShift records made.

requirements.clause: You fail or critically fail a Will save against an emotion effect.
requirements.what: No `*` on Will saves, and no degree-of-success surface. The owner ruled the identical shape (Minor Omen: 'Trigger You fail a Reflex save… Reroll the failed save') needs nothing beyond the reaction entry — 'there isnt a need for it to imact the sheet in another way.' A reroll is also in Round 9's no-implementation bucket.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No question to ask. The feat names no option, no list, no free text and no later-level scaling — nothing the player chooses. Legitimately zero builder requirements.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No question to ask. The feat offers no option, no damage-type pick, no scaling — the sap and its penalty are fixed. Legitimately zero builder requirements.

requirements.clause: The creature takes a –1 circumstance penalty on attack rolls with that weapon or unarmed attack until the end of its turn.
requirements.what: No number and no star anywhere on the character's own rows. The penalty lands on the ENEMY's attack roll — a target-side number the app does not model (DECIDED SCOPE: 'this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm') — and it expires at the end of that creature's turn, which Q1 puts in the indication-only bucket. In particular this is NOT an AC bonus: the character's AC is unchanged, and expressing the –1 as +1 AC would be wrong twice (it is per-weapon, and it persists after the triggering Strike).

requirements.clause: Sticky, golden sap runs through your veins instead of blood.
requirements.what: No mode. Q11's test — can the effect be shut down? — answers no: the sap is always present and the effect fires automatically on being hit, so it is a passive rather than a toggle. And the passive has no number of its own to carry. The 'instead of blood' sentence states no mechanical consequence in this text (no trait, no immunity, no resistance), so nothing may be derived from it.

requirements.clause: Each time a creature deals slashing or piercing damage to you with a melee Strike, your sap coats its weapon or unarmed attack.
requirements.what: The trigger must remain readable in the feat's own entry, with its four conditions intact — slashing OR piercing only, melee Strike only, each time (it can apply to several attackers at once), and the penalty attaches to the specific weapon or unarmed attack that struck you, not to the creature. ⚠ There is no other record to mark: unlike an ally-facing feat under Principle A, this feat modifies no spell, action or class feature of the character's, so there is no host record to carry an indication and the feat's own text is the entire surface.

requirements.clause: You can Interact to reload a weapon using the hand holding your implement.
requirements.what: A marker on the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D, confirmed by Q8): the reload entry of every weapon the character carries that has a reload value, and/or the Reload/Interact action itself, carrying this clause — the Interact to reload may be performed with the hand that is holding your implement. Per Ruling C's shape it belongs on every place that could perform the reload, not on one arbitrary weapon.

requirements.clause: You can Interact to reload a weapon using the hand holding your implement.
requirements.what: It moves no number and grants no action. The reload value is unchanged, no bonus or penalty is stated, and no new activity is taught — Reload/Interact already exists. The feat only lifts a hands restriction, so it is a mark on an existing action rather than a new entry in the actions list, and no free-hand or hands-occupied model is implied by this text.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No question to ask. The feat names no option and no list; which weapon is reloaded and which implement is held are facts of the moment at the table, never build-time picks. Legitimately zero builder requirements.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Crafting and Survival.
requirements.what: BOTH skills read trained on the sheet with their modifiers recomputed — Crafting and Survival, two grants from one clause. Neither is a choice; the feat names them.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A substitute skill picker, asked ONLY when another source already trains the character in Crafting or Survival. Which options are legal: ANY skill — the text places no restriction on the substitute — minus those the character is already trained in, since training cannot be taken twice; per Q27 an unpickable option is shown greyed with the reason rather than rendered live and silently inert. The redundancy is a fact about the rest of the build ('from your background or class, for example' is illustrative, not exhaustive — any automatic source counts), so the picker must appear, disappear and revalidate whenever the player changes background, class or another skill grant. ⚠ Reading, flagged not assumed: the text is singular ('one of those skills'), but a character trained in both from elsewhere should get the clause once per redundant skill, with the two picks required to differ — otherwise a double overlap quietly costs the player a grant.

requirements.clause: you become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: Whatever skill the player picks reads trained on the sheet, with its modifier recomputed and this feat named as its source.

requirements.clause: You also become trained in Anadi Lore.
requirements.what: Anadi Lore appears as a trained Lore skill in its own right, with its own row and modifier — a third skill grant, separate from the Crafting/Survival clause and not subject to the redundancy fallback (the fallback says 'one of those skills', meaning Crafting or Survival only).

requirements.clause: You also become trained in Anadi Lore.
requirements.what: No question here. The Lore subject is named by the feat, so this must NOT render as a Lore picker — the only choice this feat ever asks is the conditional substitute above.

requirements.clause: You gain your blood magic effect when you cast a non-cantrip spell you gained from a heritage or an ancestry feat, in addition to the normal circumstances that trigger your blood magic.
requirements.what: Principle C — this feat changes what ANOTHER record granted, so the change must be reflected in that record: the blood magic class feature's own entry must state that its trigger set is widened by this feat, attributed to it. Without that, a player reading their blood magic feature sees only the printed triggers and never learns the set grew.

requirements.clause: when you cast a non-cantrip spell you gained from a heritage or an ancestry feat
requirements.what: Per Ruling D/Q8 the mark also belongs where the player looks when it matters — on each qualifying spell entry, saying that casting it triggers your blood magic, written under this feat's name and visually separated from the spell's own printed rules (Principle N2). The qualifying set is fully computable and must be exactly it: spells whose source is a HERITAGE or an ANCESTRY FEAT, and only those of 1st rank or higher. Cantrips from those same sources must NOT be marked, and spells from any other source (class, items, other archetypes) must not be either — the value of the marker is that it names the small set the player would otherwise have to work out per spell.

requirements.clause: in addition to the normal circumstances that trigger your blood magic
requirements.what: Nothing is removed and no number moves. 'In addition to' means the existing triggers all survive, and the blood magic effect itself belongs to the bloodline record and is unchanged here — this feat states no bonus, resistance, damage, resource or duration of its own, so it owes no value anywhere. Its whole content is which casts count.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No question to ask. The feat names no option and no list; which spells qualify is derived from where the character got them, never asked of the player. Legitimately zero builder requirements.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Alghollthu Lore and Azlanti Lore.
requirements.what: TWO named Lore skills, both granted unconditionally: Alghollthu Lore and Azlanti Lore each appear as their own row on the skills list at trained rank, with the full modifier computed (proficiency + level + the governing attribute), sourced to this feat. Two grants, not one — a record carrying only one of them silently loses the other. Neither is chosen, so nothing is filtered and no redundancy fallback exists: the text gives no alternative if the character is somehow already trained in one.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Alghollthu Lore and Azlanti Lore.
requirements.what: NO requirement. The text names both Lores outright — there is no picker, no 'Lore of your choice', no free-text field. Anything that asks the player which Lore they get would be a phantom question.

requirements.clause: If you roll a critical failure on an Alghollthu Lore or Azlanti Lore check to Recall Knowledge, you get a failure instead.
requirements.what: A critical-failure-becomes-failure shift, and per Q2 it lands in BOTH places: a `*` on the Alghollthu Lore row AND on the Azlanti Lore row carrying the clause, plus a marker on the Recall Knowledge action itself. Scope is doubly restricted and both restrictions must survive into the note: only those two Lores (Ruling C's 'star every skill that could perform the action' does NOT widen this — the text names its skills), and only on Recall Knowledge checks, not on every check made with those Lores. This is the same one-registry point the manual makes: the shift is one entry that produces the skill star and the action mark, not a sentence copied into a situational-bonus table beside it.

requirements.clause: During your daily preparations, you can recede into old memories to become fluent in one common language or one other language you have access to.
requirements.what: A language pick asked at DAILY PREPARATIONS, not in the builder (Q23) — the builder must not render it — and it defaults to the last choice made. Legal options are exactly two tiers: every COMMON language, plus any other language the character has access to (uncommon/rare unlocked by ancestry, region, deity, or another feat) — not the unfiltered language list, and not common-only. It is 'you CAN' — declining is legal, so the pick must be skippable rather than forced. It is re-asked every day and the same language may be picked again on any later day (no once-ever restriction). A language the character already speaks permanently is wasted and nothing at a later level redeems it (the Canny Acumen exception does not apply), so per Q21/Q27 it should be filtered out, or shown greyed with the reason — never rendered live and silently inert.

requirements.clause: …to become fluent in one common language or one other language you have access to.
requirements.what: The chosen language appears in the character's languages list on the sheet, attributed to Ancestral Linguistics, indistinguishable in function from a known language for the day.

requirements.clause: You know this language until you prepare again.
requirements.what: The granted language must READ as temporary where it is listed — marked as lasting only until the next daily preparations — and must be cleared and re-picked at the next preparation, so the list can never show yesterday's language. A permanent-looking entry on the languages list is a false statement about the character.

requirements.clause: Since this knowledge is temporary, you can't use it as a prerequisite for a permanent character option.
requirements.what: The temporary language must be excluded from the builder's eligibility test: wherever a permanent character option is gated on knowing a language, this day's language must not satisfy that gate. It is a real rule about which options the builder offers, not flavour — and it means the grant has to be flagged as temporary at the point the prerequisite test reads it, not merely labelled on screen.

requirements.clause: During your daily preparations, you can reflect upon your life experiences to gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A skill pick asked at DAILY PREPARATIONS, not in the builder (Q23) — the builder must not render it — defaulting to the last choice made. The text restricts the list in no way: 'one skill of your choice' means any skill. It is 'you CAN', so declining is legal and the pick must be skippable. It is re-asked every day and the same skill may be picked again on any later day. A skill the character is already trained or better in gains nothing and no later level redeems it (unlike Canny Acumen, this feat never upgrades the pick), so per Q21/Q27 those options should be filtered out, or shown greyed saying why — never live and inert.

requirements.clause: …gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The chosen skill's row moves to trained and its modifier is recomputed (proficiency + level, plus its attribute), with Ancestral Longevity named as the source in the breakdown. The number the player reads off the sheet must actually change — a note saying 'you are trained in something today' is not the requirement.

requirements.clause: This proficiency lasts until you prepare again.
requirements.what: The grant must READ as temporary on the skill row — until the next daily preparations — and must be withdrawn and re-picked at the next preparation, so yesterday's skill cannot linger as a permanent-looking trained rank.

requirements.clause: …you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat.
requirements.what: Two exclusions the builder must honour, and they are different: (1) the temporary trained rank must not satisfy the prerequisite of any permanent option such as a skill feat; (2) it must not serve as the BASE a skill increase raises — a skill increase applied on top of it must behave as though the character were untrained. This means the temporary rank has to be distinguishable from a real one wherever rank is read, not only where it is displayed.

requirements.clause: You can cast any innate spells you know from an ancestry feat or heritage using your psychic spellcasting and thoughtforms.
requirements.what: Every qualifying innate spell entry carries a note, attributed to Ancestral Mind and visually separated from the spell's own printed rules (principle N2/C — a feat that changes another record's granted thing is reflected in that thing), stating it may be cast with your psychic spellcasting and thoughtforms. ⚠ The filter is the SOURCE of the innate spell, and it is the load-bearing part of the requirement: only innate spells from an ANCESTRY FEAT or a HERITAGE qualify. Innate spells from a class feat, an item, a background, a deity or an archetype must NOT be marked, and the marking has to be recomputed as the character gains or loses ancestry feats.

requirements.clause: When you do so, the spell's tradition becomes occult, if it wasn't already…
requirements.what: A VALUE change, not a note: the tradition shown for those innate spells must be occult. 'if it wasn't already' means it is a set, not a toggle — an already-occult spell is unaffected and must not be double-labelled. Wherever the sheet states the tradition of these spells it must state occult, including any pooled/grouped heading that asserts one tradition for a set of innate spells; a heading that names a different tradition while these spells sit under it states something false about them (Q12 — whichever spelling leaves the player least confused).

requirements.clause: …and you can use your psychic spellcasting attribute modifier instead of Charisma to determine your spell attack modifier and spell DC.
requirements.what: The spell attack modifier and spell DC PRINTED FOR THOSE INNATE SPELLS are recomputed from the psychic spellcasting attribute rather than Charisma, with the breakdown naming Ancestral Mind as the reason — the player must be able to see why this spell's DC differs from another innate spell's. Two details the text forces: it applies only to the qualifying ancestry/heritage innate spells (the character's other innate spells keep their Charisma-based numbers, so ONE character can legitimately show two different innate spell DCs), and it is 'you CAN … instead', an option rather than a replacement — so by the precedent of Q10 (apply a remap only when it makes the player better) the sheet should present the better of the two rather than strictly overwriting a higher Charisma-based number. ⚠ NO LANE IN THE MANUAL EXPRESSES THIS: nothing listed under Magic or Proficiency re-bases a spell attack modifier and spell DC onto a different attribute for a SUBSET of a character's spells — `profSpell` moves a rank, `spellNote` writes prose. This is a candidate 'no lane at all, but the text is clearly mechanical'.

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: NO requirement. Nothing is chosen — no list, no free-text, no per-level pick. Which spells qualify is decided by the character's own ancestry feats and heritage, and which attribute is used is decided by their psychic spellcasting, so every question this feat could raise is already answered elsewhere on the build. The prerequisite (being a psychic) is a prerequisite, not a choice.

requirements.clause: During your daily preparations, you can explore your memories of your past lives to become trained in one skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A skill pick asked at DAILY PREPARATIONS, not in the builder (Q23) — the builder must not render it — defaulting to the last choice made. The text restricts the list in no way: 'one skill of your choice' means any skill. It is 'you CAN', so declining is legal and the pick must be skippable. Re-asked every day; the same skill may be picked again on later days. Skills the character is already trained or better in gain nothing and no later level redeems the pick, so per Q21/Q27 they should be filtered out or shown greyed with the reason rather than rendered live and inert. ⚠ This is mechanically the same question Ancestral Longevity asks, so a character holding both feats must be asked TWICE and get two skills — the two picks are independent and the second must not be able to name the skill the first just took (it would gain nothing).

requirements.clause: …become trained in one skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The chosen skill's row moves to trained and its modifier is recomputed (proficiency + level + attribute), with Ancient Memories named as the source in the breakdown — the number on the sheet actually changes.

requirements.clause: This proficiency lasts until you prepare again.
requirements.what: The grant must READ as temporary on the skill row — until the next daily preparations — and must be withdrawn and re-picked at the next preparation, so a stale trained rank can never persist looking permanent.

requirements.clause: …you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat.
requirements.what: Two exclusions the builder must honour: the temporary trained rank must not satisfy the prerequisite of any permanent option such as a skill feat, and it must not act as the base a skill increase raises (an increase applied over it must treat the skill as untrained). The temporary rank therefore has to be distinguishable from a real one wherever rank is READ, not only where it is displayed.
Crafting and Thievery both read TRAINED on the skills list, attributed to this feat. Two named skills, no question asked — the player picks nothing here.
requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Crafting and Thievery.

requirements.what: When another source (background, class, ancestry) would already make the character trained in Crafting or Thievery, the builder must ASK for a replacement skill instead of silently wasting the grant. Legal options: any skill the character is not already trained in — the point of the clause is that a redundant grant is converted, so an option that would itself be redundant must not be offered as live (Q9 filters it; Q27 says anything still shown must LOOK unpickable and say why). The text does not narrow the list any further. Repeats: the clause is written singular ('one of those skills'), so it fires once per redundant skill; if BOTH Crafting and Thievery are already granted, the printed text does not say what happens — flag it, do not assume two picks.
requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

requirements.what: The skill chosen by the fallback reads TRAINED on the skills list, attributed to this feat, and the superseded skill (Crafting or Thievery) is NOT counted twice — the grant moved, it did not stack.
requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice

requirements.what: 'Android Lore' appears as its own Lore skill on the skills list at TRAINED, with a rollable modifier. It is a fixed named Lore — the player is asked nothing.
requirements.clause: You also become trained in Android Lore.

requirements.what: Society reads TRAINED on the skills list, attributed to this feat. Named skill, no question asked.
requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Society.

requirements.what: When another source would already make the character trained in Society, the builder must ASK for a replacement skill. Legal options: any skill the character is not already trained in (the clause exists precisely to avoid a wasted grant, so an already-trained option is not a legal answer — filtered per Q9, and if shown at all it must be greyed with a stated reason per Q27). The text puts no other restriction on the list.
requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in Society (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

requirements.what: The replacement skill reads TRAINED, attributed to this feat, and Society is not granted in addition — the grant is redirected, not duplicated.
requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice

requirements.what: Empyrean appears in the character's languages list, attributed to this feat. Fixed language, no choice offered.
requirements.clause: You know the Empyrean language

requirements.what: The granted skill feat must be a REAL owned feat — it appears in the character's feat list with its full details reachable and its source named as Angelkin — not a line of prose inside this feat's description, and it must not consume one of the character's own skill-feat slots. ⚠ THE TEXT AS SUPPLIED NAMES NO FEAT: 'you gain the skill feat' has lost the feat's name (a definite article with no antecedent — import damage). The requirement is therefore certain in shape and unresolvable in content from this text alone; the specific feat must be recovered from the source record before it can be built. Do not guess a feat name.
requirements.clause: and you gain the skill feat.

requirements.what: CONDITIONAL on resolving the feat's name: if the granted skill feat carries a choice of its own (many skill feats name a skill, a language or a subject), that choice must be offered in the builder as part of taking Angelkin — a granted thing needs its details surfaced AND its choice offered (Principle G). Unknowable from this text until the feat is named.
requirements.clause: and you gain the skill feat.

requirements.what: A real familiar exists as a companion record the player can open — its own entry with the familiar's statistics and its familiar/master ability allotment, per the general familiar rules — not a note on the feat saying a familiar was gained. The feat grants a plain familiar with no modifications, so nothing is added to the CHARACTER's own stat rows; a companion's numbers, and items bought for it, belong to the companion (standing companion ruling).
requirements.clause: You gain a familiar.

requirements.what: Ask the player what animal the familiar is. The list is UNRESTRICTED — 'up to you' — so this is free-text / open input (Principle I), not a fixed picker. Critically, the burrow-Speed sentence is ADVICE about what most gnomes pick, not a legal restriction: the options must NOT be filtered to burrowing animals, and choosing one grants no burrow Speed.
requirements.clause: The type of animal is up to you, but most gnomes choose animals with a burrow Speed.

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. The rapport/bonding sentence and the 'most gnomes choose…' remark are flavour and advice — they promise no number, no marker and no restriction.
requirements.clause: You build a rapport with an animal, which becomes magically bonded to you. … but most gnomes choose animals with a burrow Speed.

requirements.what: Ask WHICH animal companion. A companion cannot be delivered without one being named, so this question is mandatory even though the sentence does not contain the word 'choose'. Legal options: the animal companion types the character has access to; the feat is shared by druid and ranger (its traits) and the text imposes no class-specific narrowing of the list, so do not invent one. Maturity is fixed at YOUNG — 'young' is the feat's own word, not a player choice, so no mature/nimble/savage option belongs on this pick.
requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young animal companion

requirements.what: The chosen animal companion appears as its own companion record with a full young-companion stat block the player can read and roll from — AC, Hit Points, Speeds, senses, unarmed attacks with their damage, its support benefit and its advanced maneuver. Per the standing companion ruling nothing lands on the character's own stat rows; the companion's numbers live on the companion's sheet and its gear in its own inventory.
requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young animal companion that travels with you on your adventures

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. 'obeys any simple commands you give it to the best of its abilities' restates the general animal-companion action economy (the companion acts when commanded); it is a general rule, not a promise this feat makes.
requirements.clause: and obeys any simple commands you give it to the best of its abilities.

requirements.what: Ask WHICH animal companion — the same mandatory pick as the generic feat. Legal options: the animal companion types the character has access to; maturity is fixed at YOUNG by the feat's own word and is not part of the question.
requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young animal companion

requirements.what: The chosen animal companion appears as its own companion record with a readable, rollable young-companion stat block (AC, HP, Speeds, senses, unarmed attacks and damage, support benefit, advanced maneuver). Nothing lands on the ranger's own stat rows.
requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young animal companion that travels with you and obeys simple commands.

requirements.what: A marker on the HUNT PREY action itself, stating that the companion also gains the action's benefits and — only when the character actually has one — the hunter's edge benefit. The mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D / Q8): Hunt Prey is what they read and press, so the rider belongs there rather than on a general stat. The 'if you have one' conditional must be honoured — do not assert a hunter's edge benefit for a ranger who has none, and name the edge the character actually has (precision / flurry / outwit) rather than repeating the generic phrase.
requirements.clause: When you Hunt Prey, your animal companion gains the action's benefits and your hunter's edge benefit if you have one.

requirements.what: The same rider must ALSO be visible on the COMPANION's record, because the companion is who receives it — a companion's benefit marks the companion, never the master. A player reading the animal's stat block must be able to see that it shares Hunt Prey's benefits and the hunter's edge; if the edge is flurry (a multiple-attack-penalty progression) or outwit (skill and AC changes), the companion's block is the only place those could ever be read.
requirements.clause: your animal companion gains the action's benefits and your hunter's edge benefit if you have one

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. 'travels with you and obeys simple commands' restates the general companion action economy.
requirements.clause: that travels with you and obeys simple commands.

requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — no option list, no free text, no repeat clause, no daily pick. There is legitimately NO builder requirement here.
requirements.clause: (whole feat)

requirements.what: Two-way communication with animals must be readable on the sheet: an entry stating the character understands animal sounds as speech and can answer in kind, attributed to this feat. It is a communication capability, not a named language the player picks, and it grants no other tongue — so it belongs wherever the sheet lists what the character can speak with / understand, worded as animals only.
requirements.clause: You hear animal sounds as conversations instead of unintelligent noise, and you can respond in turn.

requirements.what: A `*` on Diplomacy carrying the clause: Diplomacy may be used on animals at all, and you can ask questions of and receive answers from them. No number moves — the clause changes who is a LEGAL TARGET of the skill — and per Ruling D / the Round-5 refinement a clause that names a specific stat stars that stat even when nothing moves, because Diplomacy is where the player looks this up.
requirements.clause: You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals.

requirements.what: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus. Per Ruling B it sits in the situational list with its restriction in the `when` ("to Make an Impression on animals") and NOT folded into the Diplomacy total. Per Ruling C it stars every skill that could perform the named action — Make an Impression is a Diplomacy action, so the `*` lands on Diplomacy. Per Ruling D / Q2 / Q8 the Make an Impression ACTION also carries a mark with the value inline (+1 circumstance vs animals) and a click-through to the feat. Both surfaces, not one.
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on animals.

requirements.what: No requirement. This is GM adjudication of an exploration/social situation — explicitly a NOT-lane. Nothing on the sheet.
requirements.clause: In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case.

requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — no options, no free text, no repeat clause. There is legitimately NO builder requirement.

requirements.what: Rudimentary two-way communication with animals must be readable on the sheet — an entry stating the character can ask animals questions and receive answers, attributed to this feat. The word that must survive to the player is RUDIMENTARY: this is a weaker grant than a full conversational one, and the sheet must not present it as speaking with animals freely.
requirements.clause: You have a connection to the creatures of the natural world that allows you to communicate with them on a rudimentary level. You can ask questions of, receive answers from…

requirements.what: A `*` on Diplomacy saying Diplomacy can be used on animals. NO number moves anywhere in this feat — unlike Animal Elocutionist it grants no +1, so any modifier appearing on Diplomacy from this record would be wrong. The star exists because the clause names Diplomacy specifically and Diplomacy is where the player looks (Ruling D, Round-5 refinement).
requirements.clause: …and use the Diplomacy skill with animals.

requirements.what: No requirement. GM adjudication of a social/exploration situation — a NOT-lane.
requirements.clause: In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case.

requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — no options, no free text, no repeat clause. There is legitimately NO builder requirement. (The "Archetypes Beastmaster (Level 4), Mammoth Lord (Level 4)" line in the text is availability metadata, not a choice the feat offers — it must never be rendered as a picker.)

requirements.what: Rudimentary two-way communication with animals readable on the sheet — the character can ask animals questions and receive answers, attributed to this feat. Mechanically identical to Animal Empathy; the sheet must state the rudimentary level, not a full conversational grant.
requirements.clause: You have a connection to the creatures of the natural world that allows you to communicate with them on a rudimentary level. You can ask questions of, receive answers from…

requirements.what: A `*` on Diplomacy saying Diplomacy can be used on animals. No number moves — this feat grants no bonus at all, so a modifier on Diplomacy sourced from this record would be a defect. The star is owed because the clause names Diplomacy and that is where the player reads the number (Ruling D).
requirements.clause: …and use the Diplomacy skill with animals.

requirements.what: No requirement. GM adjudication — a NOT-lane.
requirements.clause: In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case.

requirements.what: OBSERVATION, not a rules clause: the record's text opens with a bibliographic header — the feat's own name, "Source Player Core pg. 127", and the archetype/level availability line — glued to the rules prose. That is import damage of the same family as Exemplar Dedication's mangled "Class DCAbility Score". The description the player reads must be the rules text; a citation header rendered as though it were rules prose states nothing false but reads as a broken record (Q27's spirit). No mechanical requirement follows from it.
