requirements.what: The player MUST be asked which sense they gain. Exactly three options are printed and no others are legal: darkvision, low-light vision, and scent (imprecise) 30 feet. The picker must offer these three and nothing else — not the app's general sense list.
requirements.clause: You gain one of the following senses available to your inherent animal: darkvision, low-light vision, or scent (imprecise) 30 feet.

requirements.what: A gate on ONE option inside that picker: darkvision is legal only if the character already has low-light vision. Per Q9 the builder shows only what may legally be picked, and per Q27 an option that is shown but cannot be taken must LOOK unpickable — greyed, and saying why ("requires low-light vision"). Rendering darkvision identically to the live options and silently refusing it is the failure Q27 names. Note this is a now-question, not a career-question (Q21): the character can gain low-light later and then take the feat again for darkvision, so the gate is re-evaluated per taking, never used to filter the feat out of existence.
requirements.clause: You must have low-light vision before you can gain darkvision with this feat.

requirements.what: A second restriction on the same option list: the three options must be narrowed to senses the character's INHERENT ANIMAL typically has. The legal set is therefore per-character, keyed to whatever gave the character an inherent animal, not a fixed three. Where an option is excluded on these grounds it must be greyed with that reason stated (Q27) rather than silently absent, because the player needs to know the restriction exists — and if the inherent animal's sense list is not something the app can resolve, the restriction still has to be PUT IN FRONT OF the player at the picker.
requirements.clause: If your inherent animal doesn't typically have a specific type of sense, you can't gain that sense with this feat.

requirements.what: The feat is REPEATABLE: it must remain selectable after the character already owns it, and each taking asks its own sense question. On every taking after the first, senses already chosen through this feat are not legal answers ("a different sense each time") — shown greyed with that reason, per Q27, rather than offered and refused. Each instance's answer is stored separately so the sheet can attribute each sense to its own taking.
requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat multiple times, choosing a different sense each time.

requirements.what: The chosen sense appears in the character's senses, attributed to this feat. All three shapes must print completely: darkvision; low-light vision; and scent with BOTH its acuity (imprecise) and its range (30 feet) — a scent entry missing either is incomplete. Because the feat repeats, several senses from several takings must accumulate on the sheet rather than one overwriting another.
requirements.clause: You gain one of the following senses available to your inherent animal: darkvision, low-light vision, or scent (imprecise) 30 feet.

requirements.what: Display consequence of the darkvision branch (Q13): when this feat's darkvision is added to a character who has low-light vision — which the feat's own prerequisite guarantees is always the case — the sheet shows only darkvision, since it supersedes low-light. Both must not be listed side by side.
requirements.clause: You must have low-light vision before you can gain darkvision with this feat.

requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — the spell is named, the tradition is named, the bonus is fixed. No option list, no free text, no repeat. There is legitimately NO builder requirement.

requirements.what: Speak with Animals appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell with the primal tradition, at the spell's own base rank (the text names no rank, so the printed rank must be the spell's), its details reachable from the entry, and this feat named as the source. The tradition the player reads must be THIS spell's own — primal — wherever the entry is presented; a pooled innate section that asserts a single tradition across grants of differing traditions would state something false about this spell, which Q12 forbids ("whichever spelling leaves the player least confused"). That half is owed by the Spells page, not by the feat record.
requirements.clause: You gain Speak with Animals as a primal innate spell that you can cast once per day.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations. The entry must not read as at-will.
requirements.clause: …that you can cast once per day.

requirements.what: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus. Per Ruling B it lives in the situational list with the restriction in its `when` ("to Gather Information from animals") and is NOT added into the Diplomacy total. Per Ruling C the `*` goes on every skill that could perform the named action — Gather Information is a Diplomacy action, so Diplomacy is starred. Per Ruling D / Q2 / Q8 the Gather Information ACTION also carries a mark with the value inline and a click-through to this feat. Two surfaces from one clause.
requirements.clause: You get a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks to Gather Information from animals.
You have apparition sight, an imprecise sense that allows you to detect the presence of invisible or hidden spirits, haunts, and undead within 30 feet of you.
requirements.what: A named sense must appear in the character's senses list: "apparition sight", precision IMPRECISE, range 30 feet, stating what it detects (invisible or hidden spirits, haunts and undead). All three parts are printed VALUES the player reads off the sheet, not prose buried in the feat popup — the name, the precision and the 30 ft are what distinguish this from darkvision or scent. It is unconditional (no ancestry branch, no toggle), so per Q7 it carries no `*`; the source feat must still be nameable from the entry.

requirements.clause: As an activity that takes 10 minutes, you can act as a link between disembodied souls and their mortal bodies. As long as you are in contact with both a spirit and a living body that belonged to it in life during that entire time, the spirit can use you to return to that body; this does not allow you to bring the dead back to life, but can assist in restoring a disembodied soul to a still-living body.
requirements.what: The text says "As an activity", so a new named activity must appear in the actions list with a 10-minute cost (a duration cost, not an action-glyph cost) and its full procedure in the popup: contact with BOTH the spirit and the body maintained for the whole 10 minutes, and the explicit limit that it does not raise the dead — it only returns a soul to a still-living body. Per the manual, only the activity's EXISTENCE is the lane; the steps inside it are the player's to perform.

requirements.clause: You can allow a spirit or undead otherwise incapable of speech to speak through you as long as you are in direct contact with it.
requirements.what: A standing capability with no number and no action cost. It must be legible as something the character CAN DO — printed alongside the apparition-sight sense or the feat's surfaced text — including its condition (direct contact with the spirit or undead). Nothing computes; the requirement is only that the player can find it without re-reading the rulebook.

requirements.clause: If the body is occupied by another spirit or soul, that entity must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC or be cast from the body when its original owner is returned.
requirements.what: No new statistic and no new row. The save lands on ANOTHER creature (a NOT-lane: effects on someone else), and the DC named is your spell DC, which already has a row on the sheet — so per the specialStatistic exclusion ("a record pointing at a statistic that already has a row") this must NOT create a second labelled number. The sentence belongs in the 10-minute activity's popup so the player knows which of their own DCs to quote at the table.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. The feat asks the player nothing — no pick, no free text, no branch; the sense, the speech capability and the activity all arrive fixed. A builder question here would be invented.

requirements.clause: You can cast the read aura cantrip as a primal innate spell at will.
requirements.what: Read Aura must appear on the Spells page as an INNATE spell with tradition PRIMAL, marked as a cantrip, with its own description reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source. The tradition must be legible where the player reads THIS spell — a character holding other innate grants of a different tradition must not see Read Aura filed under theirs (Q12: the sheet must not state something false about the spell).

requirements.clause: …as a primal innate spell at will.
requirements.what: "At will" is the OPPOSITE of a resource: no use pip, no per-day count, nothing spent when cast and nothing to restore at daily preparations. The entry must read as at-will rather than defaulting to a once-per-day pip, and it must never become unavailable after casting.

requirements.clause: A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: The rank shown beside this innate cantrip must be ceil(character level / 2) and must move on its own as the character levels — the player reads the current rank off the entry, not a base rank of 1. This restates the general cantrip rule rather than adding a feat-specific one, so it must resolve through the same auto-heighten path every cantrip uses; a fixed rank written onto this grant would be wrong twice (wrong number, and frozen).

requirements.clause: You also gain the Quick Identification skill feat, even if you don't meet the prerequisites.
requirements.what: Quick Identification must appear in the character's feats as a granted feat attributed to Appraiser's Eye, with its own details reachable AND its own mechanical effects live on the sheet (a granted feat that is a label only is a dead grant). The grant must survive the prerequisite check — the text explicitly waives it — so an ineligible character must still receive it rather than getting an empty or inert slot (Q27: nothing may be shown that looks present but does nothing).

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. No question is asked: the spell is named (Read Aura), the tradition is named (primal), the frequency is fixed (at will), and the granted feat is named (Quick Identification). Nothing here is a picker.

requirements.clause: You have familiarity with crossbows, heavy crossbows, daggers, longspears, spears, and tridents—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
requirements.what: A proficiency remap on a NAMED, CLOSED list of six weapons — crossbow, heavy crossbow, dagger, longspear, spear, trident — and on nothing else. For each of those weapons the proficiency used to compute the attack modifier steps one category down: martial is read as simple, advanced is read as martial. The remapped rank must reach the Strike row's attack NUMBER itself, not merely a note; if the character wields a trident or heavy crossbow the printed modifier must already include it.

requirements.clause: …for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
requirements.what: Per Q10 the remap applies ONLY WHERE IT MAKES THE PLAYER BETTER. A character already trained (or better) in martial weapons must not have a trident's rank pulled down to the simple track, and a weapon on the list that is already simple (dagger, longspear, spear, crossbow) must be unaffected. The comparison is rank-vs-rank, taking the higher; a strict replacement would silently downgrade a martial-proficient character.

requirements.clause: You don't take a –2 circumstance penalty to melee slashing or bludgeoning attacks while underwater.
requirements.what: A `*` on every melee Strike row that could deal slashing or bludgeoning damage, carrying the clause: no –2 circumstance penalty for that attack while underwater. It cannot be a flat modifier — the app cannot know the character is underwater, and the general rule imposing the penalty is the circumstance being cancelled — so it lives as a situational marker where the player looks the attack number up (Ruling D / principle J), not on a general stat and not only inside the feat's text.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. No choice is offered: the six weapons are enumerated by the feat and the underwater clause is automatic — the builder must not present a weapon picker here.

requirements.clause: You gain low-light vision, or you gain darkvision if your ancestry already has low-light vision.
requirements.what: A branching sense grant resolved against the ANCESTRY, not against senses from any other source: if the ancestry already has low-light vision the character gains DARKVISION; otherwise low-light vision. The resulting sense must appear in the senses list as a value, and per Q13 only DARKVISION is shown when it supersedes low-light — the sheet must not list both.

requirements.clause: **Special** If your ancestry has neither low-light vision nor darkvision, you can take this ancestry feat a second time to gain darkvision.
requirements.what: The feat must be selectable A SECOND TIME, and only under a stated condition: the ancestry has NEITHER low-light vision NOR darkvision. So the ancestry-feat picker must permit exactly one repeat, gated on that ancestry test, while still forbidding a third taking and forbidding the repeat for any ancestry that has either sense. Per Q9 an illegal second taking should not be offered; per Q27, if it is shown it must be greyed with the reason rather than rendered live and silently inert. ⚠ "May be taken again under a condition printed on the feat" is not one of the lanes the manual lists.

requirements.clause: …you can take this ancestry feat a second time to gain darkvision.
requirements.what: After the second taking, DARKVISION must appear in the senses list and, per Q13, supersede the low-light vision the first taking granted — the sheet shows darkvision alone rather than both, and the change follows from owning the feat twice rather than from any new pick.

requirements.clause: You can't retrain out of this feat.
requirements.what: Once taken, the builder must not offer to retrain or swap this feat away, and the block must be VISIBLE — greyed with the reason rather than a control that silently refuses (Q27). ⚠ A per-record retraining restriction read from the feat's own printed text is not one of the lanes the manual lists.

requirements.clause: You gain a swim Speed of 15 feet; if you already have a base swim Speed, it increases by 5 feet.
requirements.what: A swim Speed must appear in the Speeds list as a resolved NUMBER, and the branch must actually be computed: 15 feet for a character with no base swim Speed, but existing base swim Speed + 5 feet for one who already has one. A flat 15 is wrong for the second case and a flat +5 wrong for the first. It is unconditional once granted, so per Q7 it needs no `*` — it is a permanent speed, not a conditional one.

requirements.clause: You can hold your breath underwater for 10 minutes before needing air
requirements.what: A printed statement that this character's breath-holding time is 10 minutes, replacing the general rule's derived duration. There is no stat row for breath-holding, so per Ruling D it attaches to the thing it modifies — it belongs beside the swim Speed / senses area where an underwater character looks, and must be findable without opening the feat. No existing number moves.

requirements.clause: you take only a –1 circumstance melee penalty to slashing or bludgeoning attacks that pass through water (instead of –2)
requirements.what: A `*` on every melee Strike row that could deal slashing or bludgeoning damage, carrying the reduced penalty: –1 circumstance instead of –2 when the attack passes through water. It must state the replacement (–1 in place of –2), not merely 'reduced'. It cannot be a flat modifier, because the app cannot know the attack passed through water; the marker lives on the strike rows where the player reads the attack number (principle J), not on a general stat.

requirements.clause: If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose a dragon with a swim Speed.
requirements.what: This creates no question of its own — it CONSTRAINS a draconic-exemplar pick made elsewhere. Wherever that dragon choice is offered, owning this feat must narrow the legal options to dragons that have a swim Speed. Per Q9 the illegal dragons should not be offered; per Q27 any still shown must be greyed with the reason ('this feat requires a dragon with a swim Speed') rather than selectable and silently wrong. If the character never takes a draconic exemplar, the clause does nothing.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT beyond the filter above. The feat itself asks the player nothing — the swim Speed, the breath duration and the penalty reduction all arrive fixed.

requirements.clause: You gain touch telepathy, allowing you to communicate silently and mentally with any creature you're touching, as long as you share a language.
requirements.what: Touch telepathy appears on the sheet as a named sense/communication ability, sourced to this feat, carrying BOTH conditions the text states: the target must be touched, and you must share a language with it. ⚠ It grants no language — it is a channel for languages you already have — so the languages list must gain nothing from this clause; adding a language would state something false.

requirements.clause: You gain touch telepathy…
requirements.what: No builder question. The base benefit is unconditional and unchosen — the feat asks the player nothing here.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** You can send your messages even further. Your telepathy gains a range of 10 feet, but you still have to share a language with your target.
requirements.what: When the enhancement is active, the telepathy entry reads a 10-foot range and REPLACES the touch-only entry rather than sitting beside it (Principle G — an upgrade replaces what it upgrades). The shared-language condition survives the upgrade and must still be shown; only the range clause changes.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** …
requirements.what: The Enhancement text must be readable from the feat's own record AND visibly marked as a benefit the character does not have yet, so a character holding only the base feat never reads 10-foot telepathy off their sheet. The feat prints two tiers in one block; showing both undifferentiated makes the sheet assert a range the character does not have.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** …
requirements.what: ⚠ FLAGGED, not asserted: the feat distinguishes a base benefit from an Enhancement benefit, so which tier the character holds has to be recordable somewhere in the build — otherwise the sheet cannot choose between the two entries above. This feat's own text names no trigger, cost or level for gaining the enhancement, so nothing in the text I was given specifies what asks the question or when. Stated as an open dependency rather than invented as a picker.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Arcana.
requirements.what: Arcana reads trained, with this feat named as the source in the skill's breakdown.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in Arcana (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A skill question that appears ONLY when Arcana is already being trained by another source — the condition is 'would automatically become trained', a fact about other grants, not about the player's taste. Legal options: any skill (the text places no restriction beyond 'of your choice'); repeats of skills the character is already trained in cannot be taken, and per Q27 must be shown greyed with the reason rather than rendered live and silently inert. No level scaling.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in Arcana …, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The substituted skill reads trained with this feat named as the source, and in that case this feat must NOT also be listed as a source of Arcana's training — the text says 'instead', so the Arcana grant is replaced, not stacked. A character who triggers the fallback ends up trained in Arcana (from the other source) plus one chosen skill, never Arcana twice.

requirements.clause: You gain the Arcane Sense skill feat.
requirements.what: Arcane Sense appears in the character's feat list, named as granted by this feat, with its full details reachable from the entry. A named grant, so the builder asks nothing.

requirements.clause: You gain the Arcane Sense skill feat.
requirements.what: The granted feat's OWN effects must land, not just its name: at-will 1st-rank arcane Detect Magic on the Spells page, heightening with this character's Arcana proficiency rank (see the arcane-sense entry). A granted feat that produces none of its own sheet effects is a label, not a grant.

requirements.clause: If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an arcane dragon.
requirements.what: A restriction this feat places on a choice offered ELSEWHERE: for a character with this feat, the draconic-exemplar picker must offer only arcane dragons (Q9 — the builder shows only what the player may legally pick; Q27 — anything shown-but-unpickable must look unpickable and say why). ⚠ The legal set is 'dragons of the arcane category', which this text does not enumerate — 'such as a fortune dragon or mirage dragon' sits in the flavour sentence and is illustrative, so it must not be read as the option list. The restriction is conditional ('if you choose'): a character who takes no draconic exemplar is asked nothing.

requirements.clause: If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an arcane dragon.
requirements.what: No sheet surface of its own. It constrains a picker; once the pick is made it is the exemplar's own record that shows on the sheet, and per Principle K a restriction the player re-satisfies in the builder needs no marker.

requirements.clause: Your eye has been magically enhanced to pierce darkness. You gain darkvision.
requirements.what: Darkvision appears in the senses list, sourced to this feat. Per Q13, where it supersedes an existing low-light vision, show only darkvision rather than both.

requirements.clause: You gain darkvision.
requirements.what: No builder question — the sense is unconditional and unchosen.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** Your eye can see invisible creatures in brief spurts. You can cast See the Unseen as an arcane innate spell once per hour.
requirements.what: When the enhancement is active, See the Unseen appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the arcane tradition, at its base rank (the text names no rank and no heightening, so the spell's own rank is what prints), with this feat named as its source and its arcane tradition legible where the player reads the spell entry. Absent the enhancement the spell must not appear at all — this whole clause is behind the Enhancement tier.

requirements.clause: … once per hour.
requirements.what: One spendable use shown beside the innate spell, consumed on casting and returning every hour — NOT at daily preparations, and not an unlimited/at-will entry. ⚠ O2 (per-round frequencies get no pip) does not exempt this: once per hour runs out across a scene, which is exactly the resource shape a pip exists for. The refresh cadence the text states is hourly, so whatever restores it must be able to say 'hour' rather than 'day'.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** …
requirements.what: The Enhancement text must be readable from the feat's own record and visibly marked as a benefit not yet held, so a character with only the base feat does not read an innate spell they cannot cast.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** …
requirements.what: ⚠ FLAGGED, not asserted: as with the other Enhancement feat, which tier the character holds has to be recordable, because the innate spell above exists only in the enhanced tier. This feat's text names no trigger, level or cost for gaining the enhancement, so this text alone specifies no builder question — recorded as an open dependency rather than invented.

requirements.clause: The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4.
requirements.what: The Fist strike prints 1d6 as its damage die — a VALUE replacement on the strike row, not a note beside it (the shape Principle L sets for reach: the player reads the number they will roll). ⚠ Scope is the fist specifically; the other unarmed attacks named later in the feat keep their own dice.

requirements.clause: You don't take the normal -2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other unarmed attacks.
requirements.what: Across ALL of the character's unarmed strikes (the text says 'your fist or any other unarmed attacks'), the -2 circumstance penalty for making a lethal attack with a nonlethal unarmed attack must not be applied, and the strike must carry the mark saying the normally-applicable penalty is waived — Ruling D, the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters. If the lethal/nonlethal choice is not something the sheet models, this is a `*` on the unarmed strike rows carrying the clause; it is not nothing.

requirements.clause: Your unarmed attacks gain the arcane trait, making them magical.
requirements.what: Two things, both on every unarmed strike: the arcane trait is listed among that strike's traits, AND the strike counts as magical wherever magical matters (overcoming resistances and weaknesses that key on it). Showing the trait without the magical consequence delivers half the sentence.

requirements.clause: At 5th level, you also gain the critical specialization effects of unarmed attacks in the brawling group and weapons in the brawling group.
requirements.what: From character level 5 and not before, both brawling-group unarmed attacks and brawling-group WEAPONS show that they have critical specialization, with the effect's text reachable from the strike. Two populations, not one — a build that grants it to unarmed attacks only drops half the clause. Below level 5 nothing appears.

requirements.clause: This critical specialization effect uses your spell DC instead of your class DC.
requirements.what: Where that critical specialization effect prints a DC, the number shown is this character's SPELL DC, not the class DC. Scope is limited to the crit spec effect this feat grants — it does not restate any other DC on the sheet.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No builder requirement. Every clause is unconditional or level-gated; the feat asks the player nothing and offers no options.

requirements.clause: You can cast 1st-rank Detect Magic at will as an arcane innate spell.
requirements.what: Detect Magic appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the arcane tradition at rank 1, with this feat named as its source and the arcane tradition legible on the entry the player reads (not inferred from a pooled section header that may belong to another tradition).

requirements.clause: … at will …
requirements.what: AT WILL, explicitly: no use pip, no per-day count, no consumption on casting and nothing to restore at daily preparations. The entry must read as unlimited, which is a positive statement the text makes rather than an absence.

requirements.clause: If you're a master in Arcana, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank; if you're legendary, it is heightened to 4th rank.
requirements.what: The rank printed on that innate Detect Magic is computed from the character's ARCANA proficiency rank — not character level, not spellcasting rank: 1st at trained or expert, 3rd at master, 4th at legendary. The heightened rank REPLACES the printed rank rather than appearing alongside it (Principle G), and it must move on its own when Arcana's rank later rises, since nothing re-asks the player.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No builder requirement. The spell is named, the tradition is named, and the rank is derived from a proficiency the character already has — the feat asks the player nothing.

requirements.clause: **Access** Varisian ethnicity or New Thassilon nationality
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. An access clause is not a lane (mechanic-lanes, NOT-lanes list: "prerequisites, access clauses"), and Q5 settles that access text does not gate anything the player picks from. It must not become a prerequisite gate on the feat.

requirements.clause: Choose one of the following schools of magic: abjuration (Shield), conjuration (Tangle Vine), enchantment (Daze), evocation (Electric Arc), illusion (Ghost Sound), necromancy (Void Warp), or transmutation (Sigil).
requirements.what: The player must be ASKED which school. The legal list is CLOSED and exactly these seven — abjuration, conjuration, enchantment, evocation, illusion, necromancy, transmutation. It is not a free choice of cantrip, not the wider school list, and not the character's own tradition; the seven Thassilonian schools are fixed by the text and each is welded to one named cantrip. One pick, taken once, no repeats and no later re-scaling. Because the answer's only consequence is which cantrip you get (Q20 test 1: the app models the consequence, so a label is not enough), each option must SHOW the cantrip it grants at the moment of choosing — a bare school name gives the player nothing to choose on. The pick is re-editable in the builder and needs no separate sheet surface of its own (principle K).

requirements.clause: You can cast the associated cantrip (listed in parentheses) as an innate arcane spell at will.
requirements.what: The cantrip paired with the chosen school (Shield / Tangle Vine / Daze / Electric Arc / Ghost Sound / Void Warp / Sigil, one only) must appear on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the ARCANE tradition, granted by this feat and named as such, with the spell's own details reachable from the entry. Its tradition must be legible where the player reads the spell — the entry must not be filed under a tradition it does not have (Q12: whichever spelling leaves the player least confused; the sheet must not state something false about the spell). "At will" means NO use resource: no per-day pip, no counter, nothing consumed on casting and nothing to restore at daily preparations — the entry must read as unlimited, since a use pip here would state a limit the feat does not impose (cf. principle O2, a counter is for a resource that runs out).

requirements.clause: You can attempt an Athletics or Warfare Lore check with a DC determined by the GM (but usually 15 for common armor, DC 20 for uncommon armor, and DC 25 for rare armor) to halve the time you take to don armor.
requirements.what: A `*` on BOTH skills the text names as able to perform this check — Athletics and Warfare Lore — because that is where the player looks the number up (principle D / ruling C: star every skill that could perform the named action, not just one). The Warfare Lore star lands on that specific Lore subskill where the character has it, not on every Lore. The note carries what the check achieves (halve your own donning time) and the GM's DC guidance (usually 15 common / 20 uncommon / 25 rare), with click-through to the full text (ruling H: notes cap at about a line). No number moves: donning time is not a sheet stat, and the DC is one you roll AGAINST, so it gets no row of its own (ruling D: a skill DC gets no surface at all).

requirements.clause: You can halve an ally's time to don armor by working with them to don the armor and succeeding at an Athletics or Warfare Lore check against the same DC.
requirements.what: NOTHING OF ITS OWN on your sheet — the effect lands on a teammate (ruling F). But it is not silent either: per principle A the ally half must still be READABLE on the record it modifies, which here is the same Athletics / Warfare Lore star and the feat's own description. No second star, no second number, no ally-side model.

requirements.clause: You can attempt an Athletics or Warfare Lore check…
requirements.what: NO QUESTION IS ASKED. The feat offers no build-time choice at all: "Athletics or Warfare Lore" is chosen per attempt at the table, not once in the builder, so no picker should exist for it. Both skills are starred instead (see above).

requirements.clause: [one action] impulse (earth, impulse, kineticist, primal) … you can Dismiss this impulse.
requirements.what: The impulse itself must appear as a usable 1-action activity in the character's action list, carrying its traits (earth, impulse, kineticist, primal) and its full text in the popup, plus the ability to Dismiss it. Owning the feat and having no way to invoke it on the sheet is the failure mode.

requirements.clause: The stone armor lasts for 10 minutes, and you can Dismiss this impulse. If you use this impulse again, any existing one ends.
requirements.what: A TOGGLEABLE MODE, not a passive: it can be shut down (Dismiss) and it outlasts a round — 10 minutes — so Q11 and Q1 both put it in the mode lane, with real numbers rather than text (its effects all land on YOUR own sheet). While it is on, the sheet must make plain that a mode is running and WHAT CHANGED (Q3's shape — the armour statistics it overrides are the character's own defence numbers). It is self-exclusive: turning it on again ends any existing instance, so two copies can never be running. The 10-minute duration is displayed text, not a tracked clock.

requirements.clause: The stone armor's statistics are: AC Bonus +4; Dex Cap +1; Check Penalty –2; Speed Penalty –10 feet; Strength +3; Bulk 1; Group plate.
requirements.what: While the mode runs, these statistics REPLACE the character's worn armour rather than adding to it (the SET shape, not the ADD shape): AC item bonus +4, Dex cap +1, check penalty −2, Speed penalty −10 ft, Strength threshold 3, Bulk 1, armour group plate, category MEDIUM armour. They must behave as an armour's real stats and feed the ordinary armour rules the app already applies — the Dex cap capping the Dex contribution to AC, and the Strength threshold reducing the check and Speed penalties when the character meets it — not sit on the sheet as inert printed numbers. AC, the Speed row and skill check penalties must all move when the mode is switched on and revert exactly when it ends.

requirements.clause: The stone armor is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency.
requirements.what: The AC computed from the stone armour must use the character's HIGHEST armour proficiency rank from any source, not the rank they hold in medium armour. This is the load-bearing half of the clause for a kineticist who is untrained in medium armour: resolving it against the medium rank would silently produce a far worse AC than the impulse promises. The breakdown must name which proficiency it used.

requirements.clause: You gain its armor specialization effect.
requirements.what: The plate group's armour specialization effect must be live while the mode runs and gone when it ends — an effect, not a label. It is computed off the STONE armour: its group (plate) and its category (medium, heavy from 3rd level), and off whatever potency the replication clause below gives it, never off the suppressed worn armour.

requirements.clause: Any bonuses, runes, and magical abilities of your actual armor are suppressed, but any runes that could apply to the stone armor are replicated onto it.
requirements.what: Two movements of the same numbers while the mode runs. (a) SUPPRESS: the worn armour's item bonus, its runes and its magical abilities stop counting — its potency, resilient and property runes must drop out of AC, saves and anywhere else they feed. (b) REPLICATE: every rune of that armour that could legally apply to the stone armour is copied onto it, so potency still raises AC and resilient still raises saves. The net result is the stone armour's own +4 (later +5) carrying the character's runes, and the player must be able to see that this is what happened rather than watching their AC change for no stated reason.

requirements.clause: **Level (3rd)** The armor becomes heavy armor. Its AC Bonus becomes +5, and it gains the bulwark armor trait.
requirements.what: An automatic level-scaling rewrite of the SAME mode at character level 3 and above: category becomes HEAVY armour (which also changes which armour specialization tier applies), the AC item bonus becomes +5 replacing the +4, and the armour gains the BULWARK trait — a real armour trait that must do what bulwark does, not a decorative word on the stat block. Below 3rd level the mode must state the medium/+4 version and nothing else.

requirements.clause: **Level (3rd)** The armor becomes heavy armor…
requirements.what: NO QUESTION IS ASKED — this feat offers the player no choice anywhere in its text. In particular the 3rd-level upgrade must NOT be rendered as a second pick or an option list; it is an automatic consequence of the character's level.

requirements.clause: You become trained in light armor. … you gain training in medium armor. … you become trained in heavy armor.
requirements.what: The character's proficiency rank in the resulting armour category becomes TRAINED, and everything that reads that rank must follow — above all the AC of armour in that category, which for an untrained wearer is not merely lower but flat. Exactly one category is granted per instance of the feat.

requirements.clause: If you already were trained in light armor, you gain training in medium armor. If you were trained in both, you become trained in heavy armor.
requirements.what: WHICH category is granted is COMPUTED, never asked: a three-step cascade — light, else medium, else heavy — resolved against the training the character already holds from every source (class, ancestry, background, other feats, and any earlier instance of this same feat). Because the answer differs per character and per instance, the sheet must SAY which category this feat gave: a grant the player cannot identify reads as a feat that did nothing (Q27's principle — a control that is inert without looking inert reads as a broken app).

requirements.clause: If you already were trained in light armor, you gain training in medium armor…
requirements.what: The builder asks NO question here — there is no picker to draw. What it must do instead is show, before the player commits, WHICH armour category taking this feat will grant them, since the text's answer depends entirely on their existing training and the player cannot read it off the feat's name.

requirements.clause: If you are at least 13th level, you become an expert in this armor type.
requirements.what: An automatic upgrade to EXPERT in that same granted armour category, keyed to the character's CURRENT level being 13 or higher — not to the level at which the feat was taken. A character who takes this at 1st level must see the rank change from trained to expert on reaching 13th, and each separate instance of the feat upgrades its own category. No second choice is involved.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you become trained in the next type of armor, as detailed above.
requirements.what: The feat must remain SELECTABLE after it has already been taken — it is explicitly repeatable, so the ordinary once-only filter must not remove it, and each instance runs the cascade afresh against the training the previous instance granted (light, then medium, then heavy). Once the character is trained in all three categories there is no "next type" left and a further pick is genuinely wasted across their whole career, so per Q21 it should be filtered — and if it is shown at all it must be greyed and say why it cannot be taken (Q27), never rendered live and silently inert.

requirements.clause: You treat heavy armor as being 1 Bulk lighter than it actually is.
requirements.what: Every HEAVY armour item's Bulk counts as 1 less for this character — the Bulk total on the inventory must actually drop, and the encumbered / maximum-Bulk thresholds must be judged against the reduced total. It applies to heavy armour only, not to other armour categories and not to gear generally, and it follows the ordinary Bulk floor rather than going negative. Ideally the item's own Bulk line shows the reduced figure, so the total is explicable.

requirements.clause: you can rest normally while wearing armor of any type.
requirements.what: The armoured-rest penalty must not be applied to this character when they rest, in any armour category. The marker belongs on the thing it modifies — the Rest / daily-preparations flow (ruling D) — so the player sees it at the moment it matters rather than only in the feat's own text. No stat row changes.

requirements.clause: In exploration mode, you and your allies use your normal Speeds without including your armors' Speed penalties to determine your travel Speed.
requirements.what: A `*` on the Speed row carrying this clause. Crucially it must NOT remove the armour's Speed penalty from the character's ordinary (encounter) Speed — the printed Speed keeps the penalty, and the star explains that travel Speed in exploration mode is figured without it. If the sheet prints a travel or exploration Speed of its own, that figure must be computed without the armour Speed penalty.

requirements.clause: you and YOUR ALLIES use your normal Speeds … to determine your travel Speed.
requirements.what: The allies' half produces NOTHING on your sheet (ruling F) — no ally model, no second number. It survives only as text inside the Speed star's note and in the feat's own description (principle A: an ally-facing effect must still be readable on the record it modifies).

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: NO QUESTION IS ASKED. The feat contains no choice of any kind — nothing to pick, nothing to name, nothing that scales at a later level — so the builder owes it no picker.

requirements.clause: You treat heavy armor as being 1 Bulk lighter than it actually is
requirements.what: Every HEAVY armour the character has reads 1 Bulk lower than the item's printed Bulk, and that reduced figure is what feeds the carried-Bulk total and the encumbered/maximum thresholds — otherwise the clause changes nothing the player reads. Scope is narrow and must stay narrow: heavy armour only (not medium, not light, not shields, not other gear), and it is a flat -1, not a proportional or a category change. It applies to the armour whether worn or stowed, because the text conditions on the armour being heavy, not on wearing it.

requirements.clause: you can rest normally while wearing armor of any type
requirements.what: A marker on the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D) — the Rest / daily-preparations surface — stating that this character rests normally in armour of any type. This overrides a general rule that otherwise costs the player something at rest, so with no marker the player has no way to know the general rule stopped applying to them. No number on any stat row.

requirements.clause: In exploration mode, you and your allies use your normal Speeds without including your armors' Speed penalties to determine your travel Speed.
requirements.what: A `*` on the Speed row carrying this clause. The Speed row is exactly where the armour's Speed penalty has already been subtracted, so the player reads the penalised number and must be told that travel Speed in exploration mode uses the unpenalised one. The star's note must name the restriction (exploration-mode travel Speed only — combat Speed is unchanged), because a star reading 'ignore your armour's Speed penalty' would be false.

requirements.clause: you and your allies use your normal Speeds
requirements.what: The ally half needs no surface of its own. A bonus that lands on a teammate puts no number and no star on your sheet (Ruling F); the feat's own description, already reachable from the feat entry, is where the player reads what the allies get. Do NOT report the allies' travel Speed as unreached.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing. No choice, no free text, no scaling pick at a later level — every clause is unconditional on acquisition. A picker here would be invented.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Crafting (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Crafting)
requirements.what: A conditional question, asked ONLY when the character is already trained in Crafting: 'choose another skill'. Legal options are any skill the character is not already trained in — the text puts no category restriction on the substitute (it is 'another skill of your choice', not another Crafting-like skill), so the list is the full skill list minus what is already trained. Options that cannot be taken must look untakeable — greyed with the reason, not rendered live and silently inert (Q27). When the character is NOT already trained in Crafting there is no question at all: the grant is fixed and offering a picker would be a phantom question.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Crafting (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Crafting)
requirements.what: Crafting — or, where the fallback fired, the skill the player chose — reads TRAINED on the skills list, with the rank feeding that skill's modifier, and the feat named as the source in the skill's breakdown. Exactly one skill becomes trained either way; the fallback replaces the Crafting grant, it does not add a second one.

requirements.clause: gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat
requirements.what: The named feat Specialty Crafting is actually OWNED — listed among the character's feats, attributed to Artisanal Crafter, with its own description surfaced — and its own mechanics are live, not merely its name printed. A grant that shows a label and delivers none of the granted record's effects delivers nothing (Principle G). It is granted free: it must not be charged against a skill-feat slot the player selects.

requirements.clause: in your choice of blacksmithing, leatherworking, or stonemasonry
requirements.what: Choose one specialty, and the list must be exactly those three — blacksmithing, leatherworking, stonemasonry — NOT Specialty Crafting's own full specialty list, which is considerably longer. This is the Q9 case in its plainest form: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, and offering the whole list here would let the character take a specialty this feat does not grant. One pick, no repeats, no later-level second pick.

requirements.clause: gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat in your choice of blacksmithing, leatherworking, or stonemasonry
requirements.what: The chosen specialty must be recorded ON the granted Specialty Crafting entry and reach that feat's own effect — the specialty is what decides which Crafting checks Specialty Crafting improves, so an unrecorded or unreadable answer makes the grant inert (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). The player must be able to read which specialty they hold from the Specialty Crafting entry itself, not only from this feat.

requirements.clause: You gain the Adopted Ancestry feat.
requirements.what: The named feat Adopted Ancestry is owned and listed among the character's feats, attributed to As in Life, So in Death, with its own description surfaced and its own effects live (Principle G). Granted free — not charged against an ancestry-feat slot.

requirements.clause: You gain the Adopted Ancestry feat. You can choose any ancestry
requirements.what: Adopted Ancestry's ancestry pick must be OFFERED here — a granted record's choice is part of the grant (Principle G) — and the legal list is widened to ANY ancestry. This feat overrides the granted feat's normal restriction, so the picker must not be filtered to common ancestries or to ancestries the character has some association with. One pick. The remainder of the sentence ('likely to be one that matches both your skeleton heritage and who you were in life') is advice, not a filter, and must not narrow the list.

requirements.clause: You can choose any ancestry
requirements.what: The widening must be reflected in Adopted Ancestry itself, not held only on this feat (Principle C) — the picker the player actually uses is Adopted Ancestry's, so that is the picker whose option list must be the unrestricted one. Downstream, the picked ancestry is what Adopted Ancestry keys its own grant off, so the answer must reach the ancestry-feat list the builder offers.

requirements.clause: As long as your body is completely covered by armor or clothing, you do not have to attempt Deception checks against a creature's Perception DC to successfully Impersonate yourself as a member of that ancestry.
requirements.what: A `*` on Deception AND a marker on the Impersonate action (Q2/Q8 — both, because the player may look up either), carrying the auto-success clause. The note must state all three conditions the text sets, since each one is what makes the claim true rather than an overstatement: body completely covered by armour or clothing; only when impersonating a member of the adopted ancestry (naming the ancestry the player picked, which the app knows); and that it removes the need for the check, rather than granting a bonus to it. No number moves on the Deception row.

requirements.clause: This is a non-magical disguise that doesn't protect against divination. This disguise doesn't provide any benefit against a creature actively attempting a Perception check against you.
requirements.what: The two carve-outs must appear in the same note as the clause above. They are the limits of the ability, and a sheet that shows the auto-success without them tells the player something false in exactly the two situations where it matters — a divination effect, and a creature actively attempting Perception against them. Not a separate surface; the same note, and it must not be truncated away from them.

requirements.clause: As long as your body is completely covered by armor or clothing
requirements.what: No question here. Whether the body is covered is a fact about the moment of play, not a build-time pick; it belongs in the note's wording as a condition, not as a toggle or a picker.

requirements.clause: You automatically succeed at the flat check to target a concealed creature if that creature is concealed only by smoke or mist.
requirements.what: A marker on the thing this modifies — the Concealed condition entry — carrying the clause, in the shape Ruling D specifies for a bonus with no stat row of its own (as The Survivor marks Dying). The note must carry the restriction verbatim in substance: it applies ONLY when the concealment comes from smoke or mist and from nothing else, so a note reading 'you ignore the flat check to target a concealed creature' would be false in every other concealment case. No number moves anywhere on the sheet: the flat check to target a concealed creature has no row, and this clause removes the roll rather than modifying a modifier.

requirements.clause: You automatically succeed at the flat check to target a concealed creature
requirements.what: Explicitly NOT three things it superficially resembles. It is not a sense grant — the character does not see through smoke or mist and the creature stays concealed; it is not a degree-of-success shift — a flat check has no degrees to shift; and it does not remove or alter the Concealed condition itself, only the check to target through it. Modelling any of those would make the sheet claim more than the feat gives.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — no choice, no free text, no later-level scaling. It is a single unconditional clause.

requirements.clause: You keep the bone of an ancestor or a friend to call upon for advice. Attempt to Recall Knowledge.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a named activity, so it must appear in the character's actions list as its own entry rather than living only inside the feat's text. Its popup carries what the activity does — attempt a Recall Knowledge check — and its frequency. The player performs the Recall Knowledge check themselves; only the activity's EXISTENCE is owed, not an internal roll.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use displayed with the activity, consumed when the player uses it and restored at daily preparations. Per-day frequencies are a resource that runs out across a scene and get a use pip — unlike a per-round frequency, which gets none (Principle O2).

requirements.clause: If the bones belonged to a person particularly knowledgeable on the subject, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check.
requirements.what: The conditional +1 circumstance bonus is stated in the activity's own popup, with its trigger — whether the bones' owner was knowledgeable on the subject, which is a GM adjudication the app cannot evaluate. It gets NO star on the Recall Knowledge skills: the bonus exists only inside an activity the player has deliberately chosen to use, and a benefit gated behind a deliberate action needs no star because the player already knows they did the thing (Principle P). This is the opposite shape to Mastermind's Eye, which modifies every ordinary Recall Knowledge and therefore stars every skill that can perform one.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No question is asked at build time. The bone of an ancestor or friend is flavour framing the activity, not an inventory item the player must select or supply, and no skill is chosen in the builder — which skill answers a given Recall Knowledge is decided at the table.

requirements.clause: Choose a skill you're trained in.
requirements.what: Ask the player which skill this Assurance applies to. LEGAL OPTIONS ARE RESTRICTED: only skills in which the character is ALREADY trained or better — an untrained skill is not a legal answer. Lores count, since a Lore is a skill you can be trained in. Per Q9 the list shows only what may legally be picked; per Q27 anything shown-but-unpickable must be greyed with the reason. No level scaling: the answer never changes rank or expands, so Q21's career test does not reopen the untrained skills.

requirements.clause: You can forgo rolling a skill check for that skill to instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (do not apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers).
requirements.what: A `*` on the CHOSEN SKILL's row, carrying this feat. This is the owner's own worked example in Q20: nothing on the sheet moves — you get a flat result instead of a d20 roll — and the skill is still starred, because the skill row is where the player looks the number up. The star's note must carry the substitute result: 10 + proficiency bonus only (level + rank), explicitly WITHOUT the attribute modifier, item, status, circumstance bonuses or any penalty, so the player can see it is a different number from the printed skill total sitting next to it. One star per taken instance, each on its own skill.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different skill and gain the benefits for that skill.
requirements.what: The feat must be selectable MORE THAN ONCE — a single-take gate would be wrong here. Each instance opens its own skill question, and the options must exclude (or grey per Q27) every skill already chosen by an earlier Assurance, because the text requires a different skill each time. Each instance's answer is independent and produces its own star; taking it twice must not overwrite the first pick.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Athletics and Nature.
requirements.what: Athletics and Nature both read TRAINED on the skills list, with this feat named as the source in each one's breakdown. Two separate named skills, not a choice — the player is asked nothing here.

requirements.clause: If you automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: When another source (background, class, ancestry) already makes the character trained in Athletics or in Nature, the builder must ASK for a replacement skill. LEGAL OPTIONS: any skill of the player's choice — the text puts no restriction on the replacement list, so it is not confined to Athletics/Nature or to any category; per Q27 a skill the character is already trained in should be shown greyed rather than offered as a live but wasted pick. ⚠ The trigger is per-skill and can fire TWICE: a character trained in both Athletics and Nature from elsewhere owes TWO replacement questions, not one. The question must also re-open if the redundancy appears later (a class or background change makes a previously-needed grant redundant).

requirements.clause: …you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: Each replacement skill the player names reads TRAINED on the skills list with this feat as the source. The redundant grant must not be silently swallowed — a character trained in Nature from their class must end up with one MORE trained skill than a character who was not, and the sheet has to show which.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Athamaru Lore.
requirements.what: The Additional Lore general feat appears among the character's feats, attributed to this feat and costing no feat slot the player chose, with its own details readable from the entry. Its benefit resolves against the named subject, so a Lore skill called ATHAMARU LORE must appear on the skills list at whatever rank Additional Lore confers (including any level-scaled rank increases Additional Lore itself states).

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Athamaru Lore.
requirements.what: NO Lore-subject question is asked. Additional Lore normally lets the player name the Lore; here this feat has already answered it — 'for Athamaru Lore'. Any picker that feat would open must arrive pre-filled and closed, not offered as an open choice, and the player must not be able to point it at a different Lore.

requirements.clause: You have familiarity with weapons with the athamaru trait and with crossbows, heavy crossbows, longspears, spears, and tridents—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons.
requirements.what: A proficiency remap over a NAMED, CLOSED set: every weapon with the ATHAMARU trait, plus crossbow, heavy crossbow, longspear, spear and trident. Any member of that set whose category is MARTIAL is rolled at the character's SIMPLE-weapon proficiency rank; members that are already simple or advanced are untouched by the clause. The attack rows for those weapons must show the resulting (better) modifier, and the breakdown must name this feat as the reason — a remap that silently changes a number is unreadable. Per Q10 the remap applies only where it makes the player BETTER; a character whose martial rank already exceeds their simple rank must not be pushed down to the simple rank.

requirements.clause: At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.
requirements.what: From 5th level on, the same weapon set gains its critical specialization effect, surfaced on the weapon's own strike entry (that is where the player is looking when a crit lands) — the group's crit spec text reachable from the strike, not a general note elsewhere. LEVEL-GATED: absent below 5th, present from 5th, so it cannot be authored as an unconditional grant. The set is exactly the set from the first clause ('one of these weapons') — athamaru-trait weapons, crossbows, heavy crossbows, longspears, spears, tridents — and here it is NOT restricted to the martial ones, since this sentence carries no 'that are martial' qualifier.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NOTHING. Both benefits are fixed by the printed weapon list; there is no pick, no subject, no scaling choice. Stated explicitly so the absence of a builder question is not read as a missing picker.

requirements.clause: You gain either a claw or pincer unarmed attack.
requirements.what: Ask which unarmed attack the body part is. EXACTLY TWO legal options — claw or pincer — both always legal, neither filtered (no prerequisite, no redundancy, and taking the feat twice is not offered by the text). Not repeatable and not both: 'either…or'.

requirements.clause: The claw deals 1d4 slashing damage, is in the brawling group, and has the agile, finesse, and unarmed traits.
requirements.what: If claw was picked: a CLAW unarmed strike on the Strikes tab, present without any inventory item — 1d4 SLASHING, weapon group BRAWLING, traits AGILE, FINESSE, UNARMED. Each of those does work and must actually reach the row: finesse means the attack roll may use Dexterity, agile means its multiple-attack penalty step is the agile one, brawling decides which critical specialization applies, and unarmed governs what runes/handwraps it inherits. A row carrying the die but not the traits is only half the clause.

requirements.clause: The pincer deals 1d6 piercing damage, is in the brawling group, and has the grapple and unarmed traits.
requirements.what: If pincer was picked: a PINCER unarmed strike on the Strikes tab — 1d6 PIERCING, weapon group BRAWLING, traits GRAPPLE and UNARMED. Note the differences from the claw that must not be copied across: bigger die, different damage type, NO agile and NO finesse (so it is Strength-based and takes the normal MAP step), and it carries GRAPPLE, which the claw does not.

requirements.clause: Your body can be reconfigured; you can select this feat at any level, and you can retrain into or out of this feat or change the type of attack you gain.
requirements.what: Two builder obligations. (1) The feat must be offerable in ANY qualifying ancestry-feat slot regardless of the level printed on the record — its own text overrides the usual level gate. (2) The claw/pincer answer must be CHANGEABLE afterwards in the builder, and changing it must swap the strike cleanly (old row gone, new row with the new die/type/traits). ⚠ No lane in the manual covers a feat that rewrites its own level availability — flagging it as a candidate no-lane rather than forcing it into an existing key. Per principle K, re-choosing in the builder needs no sheet surface of its own.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** Your attacking part is reinforced. Increase the damage die of the unarmed attack you gain from this feat by one step (from 1d4 to 1d6, or from 1d6 to 1d8).
requirements.what: When this feat is enhanced, the strike THIS feat granted shows the stepped die — claw 1d4→1d6 (still slashing), pincer 1d6→1d8 (still piercing). The change must appear on the strike row itself and name the Enhancement as the source (Principle C: a clause that modifies a granted thing is reflected in that thing). Only the die changes: damage type, group and traits are untouched, and the step applies once, only to the attack from THIS feat and to no other unarmed attack the character has.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** Your attacking part is reinforced.
requirements.what: The Enhancement is printed under its own heading as a separate benefit, not part of what taking the feat grants — so the player must be able to record whether THIS feat is enhanced, and the die step must follow that answer rather than applying automatically on taking the feat. An unenhanced automaton keeps 1d4/1d6.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Arcana and Crafting.
requirements.what: Arcana and Crafting both read TRAINED on the skills list, with this feat named as the source in each breakdown. Two fixed named skills; the player is asked nothing for this clause.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: When another source already trains the character in Arcana or in Crafting, the builder must ASK for a replacement skill. LEGAL OPTIONS: any skill of the player's choice — the text restricts the list in no way; per Q27 a skill they are already trained in should appear greyed with the reason rather than as a live pick. ⚠ Can fire TWICE (a wizard trained in both Arcana and Crafting from elsewhere owes two questions), and must re-open if a later class/background change creates the redundancy.

requirements.clause: …you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: Each replacement skill reads TRAINED with this feat as the source. The character must end up with the same NUMBER of new trained skills either way — the redundant grant is converted, never dropped.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore feat for Automaton Lore.
requirements.what: Additional Lore appears among the character's feats, attributed to this feat, with its details readable. Its benefit resolves against the named subject, so a Lore skill called AUTOMATON LORE appears on the skills list at whatever rank Additional Lore confers, including that feat's own later-level rank increases.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore feat for Automaton Lore.
requirements.what: NO Lore-subject question. The subject is fixed by this feat's text ('for Automaton Lore'); any picker Additional Lore would normally open arrives pre-filled and closed, and the player cannot retarget it at another Lore.

requirements.clause: **Enhancement** … Increase your proficiency rank in your choice of either Arcana or Crafting to expert.
requirements.what: Ask which of TWO options — Arcana or Crafting, and nothing else — the enhancement raises. ⚠ Q21 CASE: an option the character is ALREADY EXPERT in must NOT be filtered out, because the next sentence turns that pick into master. Filtering the redundant-looking option would deny the feat its better outcome. Both options stay live at all times. Like Automaton Armament's, this benefit sits under its own **Enhancement** heading, so the player must also be able to record whether this feat is enhanced at all; the rank change follows that answer rather than arriving with the feat.

requirements.clause: Increase your proficiency rank in your choice of either Arcana or Crafting to expert. If you were already an expert in the chosen skill, increase your rank to master instead.
requirements.what: The chosen skill's rank on the skills list reads EXPERT — or MASTER if the character was already expert in it from any other source — with this feat named in that skill's breakdown, and the modifier recomputed from the new rank. Two-step escalation in one clause: the result depends on the rank the character already has at the moment it applies, so it cannot be authored as a flat 'set to expert'. It is a SET/upgrade, not an addition — a character already master or legendary is not lowered.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Access** mountain dwarf ethnicity **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet gains the dying condition.
requirements.what: The feat is a REACTION and must appear in the reactions list, with its trigger ("an ally within 30 feet gains the dying condition") and its frequency printed in its popup — Principle E, the shape agreed for Minor Omen. The Access line is an access clause and is print-only (NOT-lanes: prerequisites and access clauses are not mechanical lanes).

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: A once-per-DAY resource: one spendable use displayed beside the reaction, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations. Round 4 #4's "no use pip" ruling is explicitly about a once-per-ROUND frequency; a per-day frequency is the `limitedUses` lane ("N times per day/hour, a per-day resource").

requirements.clause: gaining temporary Hit Points equal to your level for 1 minute
requirements.what: The effect runs 1 minute, so per Q1 it earns a MODE the player turns on when the reaction fires (Q11 — it can be shut down, i.e. when the temporary Hit Points are gone). Entering the mode grants temporary Hit Points equal to the character's LEVEL (a computed value, not a fixed number) and leaving it takes them back — the shape Round 10 built for BattleForm.tempHp, where temporary HP granted on entry and removed on exit was ruled a real reader rather than prose. The mode must also make plain it is running.

requirements.clause: As long as you have these temporary Hit Points, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack and damage rolls.
requirements.what: While that mode is active, a +1 circumstance bonus that really moves numbers on every Strike's attack roll AND its damage — both halves, on the strike rows where the player reads them. The condition ("as long as you have these temporary Hit Points") is exactly the mode's own on/off state, so inside the mode the numbers are real rather than display-only; Ruling E case 2. Note that Ruling E's "HP and damage never move sheet stats" concerns healing and damage taken, not a printed +1 damage bonus on a Strike.

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: NOTHING is asked of the player at build time. The feat names no choice; the only variables are the trigger (a play-time event, never the app's to fire — Principle M2's timing rule) and the ethnicity access clause, which is an eligibility line, not a question.

requirements.clause: You become trained in the Lore skill corresponding to one creature type mentioned by your vow (for example, Fey Lore if your heritage is deny the firstborn pursuit).
requirements.what: The player must be ASKED which creature type's Lore. The legal options are NOT the whole Lore list and not the whole creature-type list: only the creature type(s) NAMED BY THAT CHARACTER'S OWN VOW, which comes from their yaksha heritage — Q9, the builder shows only what the player may legally pick (Domain Fluency filtering to the mystery's domains is the same shape). The parenthetical is illustrative of the mapping, not an option list. If the character's vow names exactly one creature type the answer is forced and no phantom question should be posed (the Exemplar Dedication rule); if the vow names more than one, the pick is between those.

requirements.clause: You become trained in the Lore skill corresponding to one creature type mentioned by your vow
requirements.what: The chosen Lore (e.g. Fey Lore) appears on the skills list at trained rank, with its modifier computed — the answer to the pick must reach a skill row, not merely relabel the feat (Q20's "a label is not enough").

requirements.clause: you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against that creature's attacks and abilities for 1 round
requirements.what: A `*` on AC carrying this text. The duration is 1 round, so per Q1 NO NUMBER MOVES — the requirement is the indication, on the stat the clause names (Principle J: situational stars go on the specific stat affected, and AC is a stat row the player reads).

requirements.clause: a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against that creature's attacks and abilities
requirements.what: A `*` on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will. Q2: when a clause applies to saves generally rather than naming one, star all three. Again indication only (1 round, Q1).

requirements.clause: Whenever you successfully Recall Knowledge about this type of creature
requirements.what: A `*` on the ACTION/skill that triggers the reward, so the player sees what a success buys at the moment they roll it: the granted Lore skill, and per Ruling C (a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it) and Ruling H (where the rules are open, stay open) every skill that could Recall Knowledge about that creature type. Q2 requires both halves — the skill and the action — not one.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Arcana and Nature.
requirements.what: BOTH Arcana and Nature appear at trained rank on the skills list with their modifiers computed. Two skills, not one — this is the clause a reader most easily half-delivers.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: When (and only when) the character would already be trained in Arcana or Nature from another source, the player must be ASKED for a substitute skill. Legal options: any skill — the text places no restriction beyond the substitution being worth something, so skills the character is already trained in must not be silently inert; per Q27 they are shown greyed with the reason, or filtered per Q9. The trigger is per-skill: the text says "one of those skills", so the redundancy test runs against each of Arcana and Nature and the question appears only for the one(s) that are redundant.

requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: The substituted skill appears at trained rank on the skills list. The redundant grant must not silently vanish — the player must be able to read on the sheet that the replacement landed.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Awakened Animal Lore.
requirements.what: The Additional Lore general feat is granted and appears on the feats list with its own details reachable — a named feat grant (Principle G: a granted feature needs its details surfaced), and it must actually DELIVER what that feat delivers rather than be a name on a list: the Awakened Animal Lore Lore skill appears as a trained Lore on the skills list and follows Additional Lore's own level-scaled rank ladder as the character levels.

requirements.clause: the Additional Lore general feat for Awakened Animal Lore
requirements.what: The granted feat's usual "choose a Lore" question must NOT be asked — this feat pre-answers it ("for Awakened Animal Lore"). Posing it anyway is the phantom-question defect the owner named on Exemplar Dedication: a picker rendering a decision the text already made.

requirements.clause: You gain one cantrip from the occult spell list.
requirements.what: The player must be ASKED to pick one cantrip. Legal options: cantrips ON THE OCCULT SPELL LIST — not the character's own tradition, not the full spell list, and cantrips only (not 1st-rank spells). One pick, made at build time and permanent (not re-chosen at daily preparations — Q23 governs daily picks, and this is not one).

requirements.clause: you can cast this spell as an innate spell at will
requirements.what: The chosen cantrip appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the OCCULT tradition, with the granting feat named and the spell's own details reachable from the entry. Per exemplar 10's one real defect, the tradition must be legible AT THE ENTRY — an occult innate cantrip must not be filed under a pooled header asserting some other tradition.

requirements.clause: at will
requirements.what: The entry must read as AT WILL — unlimited, with no spendable use pip and nothing consumed on casting. This is the one shape where the absence of a per-day resource has to be stated positively on the entry.

requirements.clause: As long as you possess your head gem, you can cast this spell as an innate spell at will.
requirements.what: The possession condition is written into that spell's entry, attributed to this feat and visually separated from the spell's own printed rules — Principle N2 (a feat that modifies a spell it grants writes its text into that spell's description under the feat's name). The grant is conditional on holding the head gem, which the app cannot verify, so the player must be able to read the condition where they read the spell (Q7's shape for a conditional grant).

requirements.clause: A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: The entry displays the cantrip at its CURRENT heightened rank, ceil(level/2), with the heightened values that rank produces — not the base rank. This sentence restates the general cantrip rule the app applies everywhere (NOT-lanes: "restating a general rule"), so it demands nothing new; it demands only that the innate copy resolve through the same rule rather than sitting frozen at rank 1.

requirements.clause: Choose one cantrip from the primal spell list.
requirements.what: The player must be ASKED to pick one cantrip. Legal options: cantrips ON THE PRIMAL SPELL LIST — cantrips only, and filtered to primal rather than to the character's own tradition or the full spell list. One pick, permanent, made in the builder.

requirements.clause: You can cast this spell as an primal innate spell at will.
requirements.what: The chosen cantrip appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the PRIMAL tradition, with this feat named as its source and the spell's details reachable. Per exemplar 10, the primal tradition must be legible at the entry itself — an awakened animal who also holds innate spells of another tradition must not see this one mislabelled by a pooled section header.

requirements.clause: at will
requirements.what: The entry reads AT WILL — unlimited casting, no use pip, nothing consumed and nothing to restore at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: The entry shows the cantrip at rank ceil(level/2) with that rank's heightened values. This restates the general cantrip rule (NOT-lanes), so the requirement is only that the innate grant resolve through it rather than display a frozen base rank.

requirements.clause: When you awakened, primal magic was released within you.
requirements.what: Nothing else is asked. The feat poses exactly one question — the cantrip — and no second picker (tradition, rank, uses) should be rendered, since the text fixes all three.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Diplomacy and Society.
requirements.what: Diplomacy and Society each read TRAINED on the skills list, with the modifier recomputed from that rank and Axiomatic Lore named as the source in the breakdown. Two named skills, unconditionally, no pick. It must never LOWER an existing rank — a character already expert in Diplomacy from another source keeps expert (the better-rank rule; same shape the owner endorsed in Q10).

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A conditional question, asked ONCE PER NAMED SKILL that another source already trains — so it fires zero, one or two times depending on background/class. Legal options: ANY skill; the text places no restriction at all, so the list must not be narrowed to the named pair, to a class list, or to non-Lores.
