Two constraints on the offer: (i) a skill the character is already trained in is a wasted pick — per Q27 it is shown GREYED with the reason, not filtered silently and not rendered live-but-inert; (ii) if the question fires twice the second pick must not repeat the first. It must re-evaluate when the character's background or class changes, appearing and disappearing accordingly, and must NOT be asked when neither Diplomacy nor Society is redundant.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The skill(s) chosen by that fallback read TRAINED on the skills list with the modifier recomputed and Axiomatic Lore named as the source — the answer to the question must actually move the rank, not merely label the feat (Q20 refinement: a label-only picker is a defect wherever the app models the consequence, and a trained rank is modelled).

requirements.clause: You also become trained in Axis Lore.
requirements.what: Axis Lore appears in the skills list as a trained Lore skill with its own computed modifier, sourced to this feat. The subject is NAMED by the feat, so there is no builder requirement here — the generic 'name your Lore' prompt must not fire for this grant.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Athletics and Nature.
requirements.what: Athletics and Nature each read TRAINED on the skills list, modifier recomputed from that rank, Azarketi Lore named as the source. Unconditional, no pick; must never lower a rank the character already has from elsewhere.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A conditional question asked ONCE PER NAMED SKILL (Athletics, Nature) that another source already trains — so zero, one or two prompts. Legal options: ANY skill, unrestricted by the text. Already-trained skills must appear greyed with the reason rather than filtered away or shown live-but-inert (Q27); a second prompt must not allow repeating the first pick. The prompt must re-evaluate as background/class change and must not appear when neither named skill is redundant.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: Each skill chosen by the fallback reads TRAINED on the skills list with its modifier recomputed and this feat named as the source — the pick must produce the rank, not only a label on the feat.

requirements.clause: You also become trained in Azarketi Lore.
requirements.what: Azarketi Lore appears in the skills list as a trained Lore skill with its own computed modifier, sourced to this feat. Subject is named by the feat — no builder prompt, and the generic Lore-subject picker must not fire.

requirements.clause: You are trained with Crossbows, Hand Crossbows, Longspears, Spears, and Tridents.
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in five SPECIFICALLY NAMED weapons — crossbow, hand crossbow, longspear, spear, trident — not in a weapon group and not in a whole category. Each named weapon's Strike row computes its attack modifier at trained when the character's own rank in it would be lower, with this feat named in the breakdown, and the grant is visible wherever weapon proficiencies are listed. It must not lower a higher existing rank (a fighter expert in martial weapons keeps expert).

requirements.clause: In addition, you gain access to all uncommon azarketi weapons.
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Owner ruling Q5: an 'access to uncommon X' clause needs nothing — the inventory/shop stays open, item rarity does not gate it, and Q9's 'only what you may legally pick' governs the BUILDER's choices, not the item list. Neither a builder question nor a sheet surface is owed.

requirements.clause: For the purpose of determining your proficiency, martial azarketi weapons are simple weapons and advanced azarketi weapons are martial weapons
requirements.what: A proficiency REMAP, not a grant: for any weapon carrying the azarketi trait, proficiency is resolved one category down — a martial azarketi weapon uses the character's simple-weapon rank, an advanced azarketi weapon uses their martial rank. This requires the app to know which weapons have the azarketi trait and each one's own category. Per owner ruling Q10 the remap is applied ONLY WHEN IT MAKES THE PLAYER BETTER — RAW's strict replacement is rejected because it could lower a rank (an advanced azarketi weapon in the hands of a character with advanced-weapon training must not drop to martial). The Strike row must show the resulting proficiency and name this feat as the reason, otherwise the number looks wrong.

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: NO BUILDER REQUIREMENT. The feat names its five weapons, its trait and its remap outright — the player is asked nothing at any level, and no picker should appear.

requirements.clause: You ignore non-magical difficult terrain due to light undergrowth and shallow bogs, mud, and water
requirements.what: A `*` on the Speed row (the stat the player reads to work out how far they move) carrying this clause verbatim, moving no number — the app cannot know what terrain the character is standing in, so the value is uncomputable and the marker is the whole surface (Ruling D: a benefit with no stat row of its own attaches to the thing it modifies; Ruling H: keep the printed trigger in the note). The note must preserve BOTH qualifiers the text makes load-bearing — non-magical only, and only terrain arising from light undergrowth / shallow bogs, mud and water — since a marker reading 'ignores difficult terrain' would state something the feat does not grant.

requirements.clause: and you treat non-magical greater difficult terrain due to these features as difficult terrain instead.
requirements.what: A SECOND, distinct promise on the same surface: greater difficult terrain from those same features is downgraded to ordinary difficult terrain (it is not ignored). It must be carried alongside the first clause on the Speed row's `*`. Carrying only the 'ignore' half is the documented failure mode — the same shape as Dragon's Presence shipping one half of a two-direction sentence — because a player reading only 'you ignore this terrain' would move through greater difficult terrain for free.

requirements.clause: whole feat
requirements.what: NO BUILDER REQUIREMENT. The feat names its own terrain types and offers no option, scaling or later-level choice — the player is asked nothing.

requirements.clause: You are trained in Bardic Lore, a special Lore skill that can be used only to Recall Knowledge, but on any topic.
requirements.what: Bardic Lore appears in the skills list as a trained Lore skill with its own computed modifier, sourced to this feat. The subject is fixed by the feat, so no Lore-subject prompt is owed and the generic 'name your Lore' picker must not fire.

requirements.clause: a special Lore skill that can be used only to Recall Knowledge, but on any topic
requirements.what: The Bardic Lore entry must state both halves of what makes it unlike every other Lore: it can be used ONLY to Recall Knowledge, and it can do so on ANY topic. This is where the player looks the number up, and a Lore row that behaves differently from all its neighbours without saying so reads as a mistake. It also means Bardic Lore belongs among the skills surfaced wherever Recall Knowledge is looked up (Ruling C / owner answer #6: every skill that could perform the named action is marked, so the player sees it where they check that action's number).

requirements.clause: If you have legendary proficiency in Occultism, you gain expert proficiency in Bardic Lore
requirements.what: A conditional, AUTOMATIC rank upgrade — not a choice and not a fixed level. While the character's Occultism rank is legendary, Bardic Lore reads EXPERT and its modifier recomputes from that rank; if Occultism is anything less it stays trained. It must re-evaluate whenever Occultism's rank changes, and the reason for the upgrade should be legible in the skill's breakdown.

requirements.clause: but you can't increase your proficiency rank in Bardic Lore by any other means.
requirements.what: A hard exclusion the builder must enforce: Bardic Lore may not be selected in any skill-increase picker at any level, nor raised by any other rank-granting feat or source. Per Q27 the option must LOOK unpickable — shown greyed with the reason ('Bardic Lore's rank can only be raised by legendary Occultism') rather than filtered away silently or rendered identically to a live option and quietly inert.

requirements.clause: but you can't increase your proficiency rank in Bardic Lore by any other means.
requirements.what: The Bardic Lore entry must say why its rank does not move. A Lore skill sitting at trained while the character spends skill increases elsewhere, with no explanation on the row, reads as a broken app rather than as the rule the feat prints.

requirements.clause: You can Earn Income using Diplomacy, spending your days hunting for bargains and reselling at a profit.
requirements.what: Diplomacy joins the set of skills that can perform Earn Income. The marker belongs on the Diplomacy row itself (Ruling D / Principle C — the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters, and an action's performing skills must be visible where the number is read), and Earn Income must be readable as a Diplomacy activity attributed to this feat. No number moves: the roll is an ordinary Diplomacy check at the task's level DC.

requirements.clause: you can also spend time specifically sniffing out a great bargain on an item; this works as if you were using Earn Income with Diplomacy, except instead of gaining money, you purchase the item at a discount equal to the money you would have gained, gaining the item for free if your earned income equals or exceeds its cost.
requirements.what: A SECOND, distinct use of the same activity, and it must be readable on the Earn Income (Diplomacy) surface the previous clause creates rather than only inside the feat's own blurb (Principle A — the indication lives on the record it modifies). Its text: run as Earn Income with Diplomacy, but the proceeds become a discount on one named item, and the item is free when the income earned equals or exceeds its price. Nothing is computed — the item, the task level and the roll are table facts, and the result lands on a purchase, not on a stat.

requirements.clause: if you select Bargain Hunter during character creation at 1st level, you start play with an additional 2 gp.
requirements.what: A real number the player reads off the inventory: +2 gp of starting money. ⚠ NO LANE IN THE MANUAL covers starting funds — this is the 'clearly mechanical, no lane at all' bucket, not a promised-but-empty field. Two conditions are part of the requirement: (a) granted ONLY when the feat occupies a 1st-level character-creation slot, so a character who picks it up later as a level-up general feat or by retraining gets nothing; (b) it is a ONE-TIME write into the character's money, never a derived value — once the player spends it, re-deriving the sheet must not restore it or add it twice.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NOTHING and no picker is owed. The Diplomacy use is fixed, the bargain-hunted item is chosen in play rather than at build time, and the 2 gp is decided by which slot the feat sits in, not by a question.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're holding or wearing a healer's toolkit. --- You can patch up wounds, even in combat. Attempt a Medicine check with the same DC as for Treat Wounds and restore the corresponding amount of HP
requirements.what: Battle Medicine appears in the actions list as a 1-action activity carrying its healing and manipulate traits, with its REQUIREMENT (holding or wearing a healer's toolkit) stated in its popup — Principle E's shape, which the owner set for reactions, applied to an action: trigger/requirement in the popup is often the whole surface. The popup must also say which check it rolls (Medicine) and that the DC is Treat Wounds' DC.

requirements.clause: restore the corresponding amount of HP; this doesn't remove the wounded condition.
requirements.what: The healing amounts (Treat Wounds' DC-to-healing table) must be readable in the popup, because the app computes no heal — Ruling E: HP and damage never move a sheet stat, so the player applies the result through the HP control. The 'doesn't remove the wounded condition' clause prints alongside it; no wounded interaction is calculated.

requirements.clause: As with Treat Wounds, you can attempt checks against higher DCs if you have the minimum proficiency rank.
requirements.what: The higher-DC tiers are gated by THIS character's Medicine proficiency, so the popup must state which tiers this character may attempt rather than listing them all flat. A tier the character's rank forbids must not read as available (Q27 — what cannot be taken must look untakeable, and ideally say why).

requirements.clause: The target is then [immune] to your Battle Medicine for 1 day. This does not make them immune to, or otherwise count as, Treat Wounds.
requirements.what: A fact about the TARGET, not a resource of yours — Ruling F. Explicitly NOT a use pip, a per-day counter or a limitedUses resource on your sheet: nothing of yours is spent, and the immunity is per-target, which the app cannot track. The clause lives as text in the action's popup so the player can hold it at the table, together with the sentence that it does not block Treat Wounds.

requirements.clause: Attempt a Medicine check with the same DC as for Treat Wounds
requirements.what: NO star on Medicine is owed. The feat modifies no number on that check — it creates an action that uses it. Principle C stars every skill that could perform an action only when a BONUS is named after the action, and this feat names none.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — no choice of skill, target, DC tier or option. Which DC to attempt is decided in play, not at build time.

requirements.clause: You are trained in Intimidation.
requirements.what: Intimidation shows trained on the skills tab, with the rank attributed to Battleblooded so the player can see where it came from.

requirements.clause: If you were already trained in Intimidation (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A CONDITIONAL question: the picker appears only when the character is already trained in Intimidation from another source, and disappears if that source goes away — so it must be evaluated against the rest of the build rather than frozen at the moment the feat was clicked, and must not depend on the order the player made their picks. Legal options: any skill (the ordinary skill list) EXCEPT skills the character is already trained in, Intimidation itself included since by definition it is one of them. Per Q9/Q27 those are either not offered or shown greyed with the reason — never rendered live and silently inert. One pick, no repeats, no later-level scaling.

requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: Whichever skill the fallback picker returns shows trained on the skills tab, attributed to Battleblooded — occupying the same surface as the Intimidation grant it replaces, never sitting beside it, because the text says 'instead'.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Intimidating Glare skill feat.
requirements.what: Intimidating Glare must be OWNED, not named in prose: it appears in the character's feat list attributed to Battleblooded, its details are readable from there, it costs no feat slot of any kind, and its own mechanics reach the sheet through its own record. A granted feat that exists only as a sentence delivers nothing.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Intimidating Glare skill feat.
requirements.what: The granted feat is named outright, so no picker is owed for it — this is a fixed grant, not a choose-a-skill-feat.

requirements.clause: You become trained in the Nature skill
requirements.what: Nature shows trained on the skills tab, attributed to Beast Trainer.

requirements.clause: You become trained in the Nature skill
requirements.what: ⚠ NO redundancy fallback is printed here, unlike the sibling lineage feats in this same batch. If the character is already trained in Nature the grant is simply wasted, and the builder must NOT invent a 'choose another skill instead' question. Nothing is asked for this half of the feat.

requirements.clause: gain your choice of the Pet general feat or the Train Animal skill feat.
requirements.what: A two-option picker, and the legality of the list is the requirement: EXACTLY Pet and Train Animal — not the general feat list, not the skill feat list, not 'a feat of 1st level or lower'. One pick, no repeats, no second pick at a later level. Both options are live at 1st level; neither is filtered by prerequisites the feat does not state.

requirements.clause: gain your choice of the Pet general feat or the Train Animal skill feat.
requirements.what: Whichever option is picked must be OWNED outright — in the feat list, attributed to Beast Trainer, costing no feat slot, details readable — and its own grants must land through its own record: Pet's creature has to exist as a Companions-tab entry, Train Animal's activity has to appear as an action rolled with Nature. A picker whose answer only changes a label is a defect (Round 5, Q20).

requirements.clause: You're trained in Society.
requirements.what: Society shows trained on the skills tab, attributed to Beastbrood.

requirements.clause: If you're already trained in Society (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A CONDITIONAL question: offered only when the character is already trained in Society from another source, and withdrawn if that source changes — evaluated against the whole build rather than frozen at pick time, and independent of the order the player made their picks. Legal options: any skill (the ordinary skill list) EXCEPT ones the character is already trained in, Society included. Per Q9/Q27 those are either filtered or shown greyed with the reason, never live-looking and inert. One pick, no repeats, no later-level scaling.

requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: The chosen fallback skill shows trained on the skills tab, attributed to Beastbrood, REPLACING the Society grant rather than sitting beside it — the text says 'instead', so the character must never end with both.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Courtly Graces skill feat.
requirements.what: Courtly Graces must be OWNED, not merely mentioned: listed among the character's feats attributed to Beastbrood, details readable, costing no feat slot, and its own mechanics delivered by its own record.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Courtly Graces skill feat.
requirements.what: The granted feat is named outright, so no picker is owed for it.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance equal to half your level to the damage type dealt by the breath of your draconic benefactor.
requirements.what: A resistance entry in the character's defences, attributed to this feat. Its VALUE is a formula — half the character's level — so it must be recomputed at every level-up and never stored as a fixed number; the player reads a live figure (1 at 2nd, 5 at 10th, 10 at 20th). Its TYPE is not asked for and not authored on this record: it is resolved from the draconic benefactor the character already chose on another record, i.e. the damage type of that benefactor's breath weapon. If the character has no draconic benefactor recorded, the feat can produce no resistance and must say so rather than emitting an untyped one.

requirements.clause: If your draconic benefactor's breath deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, instead of gaining resistance to that type, you must choose acid, cold, fire, electricity, or sonic.
requirements.what: A conditional damage-type question. It is asked ONLY when the already-chosen benefactor's breath is bludgeoning, piercing or slashing; when the breath is already an energy type the player must not be asked anything (asking would be a phantom question — the type is derived). The legal options are exactly five and no more: acid, cold, fire, electricity, sonic. The breath's own physical type is not among them, and no other damage type (force, vitality, void, poison, mental, spirit, bleed) is legal. One pick, no repeats, no rescaling or second pick at a later level.

requirements.clause: instead of gaining resistance to that type, you must choose acid, cold, fire, electricity, or sonic
requirements.what: In that branch the resistance the sheet shows is to the CHOSEN energy type INSTEAD of the breath's physical type. 'Instead of' replaces: this feat must contribute exactly one resistance line, never both the physical type and the chosen one, and never a bludgeoning/piercing/slashing resistance at all. The value is still half your level, on the same live formula.

requirements.clause: You gain your choice of one of the following unarmed attacks. ... **Claw** 1d4 slashing (agile, finesse, unarmed, versatile piercing) **Hoof** 1d6 bludgeoning (finesse, unarmed) **Jaws** 1d6 piercing (finesse, unarmed) **Tail** 1d4 bludgeoning (agile, finesse, unarmed)
requirements.what: Exactly one pick from a closed list of four named options — Claw, Hoof, Jaws, Tail. No repeats, no second pick, no scaling at a later level, and no other unarmed attack (from any other source or list) is a legal answer. Each option must display its damage die, damage type and trait line at the point of choosing, because those stats are the only thing that distinguishes the four and the pick is permanent.

requirements.clause: The attack is in the brawling group and has the listed damage die and traits.
requirements.what: The chosen attack appears on the Strikes tab as a real, rollable unarmed Strike attributed to this feat — with an attack modifier, a damage line, weapon group brawling, and exactly the picked row's die, damage type and traits: Claw 1d4 slashing (agile, finesse, unarmed, versatile piercing); Hoof 1d6 bludgeoning (finesse, unarmed); Jaws 1d6 piercing (finesse, unarmed); Tail 1d4 bludgeoning (agile, finesse, unarmed). The traits must be live rather than printed decoration: finesse must let the attack roll off Dexterity when that is higher, agile must change the multiple attack penalty step for that Strike, brawling must be the group the character's unarmed proficiency and critical specialization read, and Claw's versatile piercing must offer piercing as a selectable alternative damage type on the strike row.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into or out of this feat, nor can you change the type of attack you gained.
requirements.what: A selection restriction the builder must enforce from this record's own text: the feat is offerable only in a 1st-level feat slot and must not appear as a live option in any later slot; once taken, neither the feat itself nor the attack it chose may be changed or retrained away. This is the explicit exception to the app's usual 'the player just re-chooses in the builder' freedom, so the attack picker must become locked after the first answer — and, being inert, it has to LOOK locked and say why rather than silently refusing the click.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're wielding a loaded firearm. --- ... You shoot your firearm at a lock within 10 feet. Make an attack roll against the DC required to Pick the Lock
requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list at its printed action cost, with its Requirement ('You're wielding a loaded firearm') and its full effect text — the 10-foot range and the attack roll against the lock's Pick a Lock DC — shown in its popup. Its existence, cost, requirement and text are the whole surface: the attack roll it calls for is the firearm Strike modifier the Strikes tab already prints, so the action creates no new statistic and owes no row of its own, and the target DC belongs to the lock (the GM's number).

requirements.clause: **Failure** ... Future attempts to Pick the Lock or Blast the Lock take a -2 circumstance penalty. **Critical Failure** ... take a -4 circumstance penalty.
requirements.what: The four degrees of success are prose that belongs in the action's popup, complete and including the two penalty lines. They owe no computed number and no star: the −2/−4 attaches to the particular lock the character shot, not to the character, and nothing on the sheet can know which lock is in front of them — so Thievery / Pick a Lock must NOT carry a standing penalty or a `*` from this feat. It is also not a degree-of-success shift: no degree is converted into another degree here, the four entries merely describe outcomes.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No requirement. The feat asks the player nothing at build time — there is no option, no list, no free text, no later-level pick. Everything it decides is decided at the table when the action is used.

requirements.clause: Add up to three of your deity's spells (spells your deity grants to clerics) to your spell list.
requirements.what: A picker for up to three spells whose legal options are exactly the cleric spells granted by THE CHARACTER'S OWN DEITY — the parenthesis defines the list, so it is not the divine spell list, not every deity's spells, and not the whole spell corpus; it must be filtered to the deity actually recorded on this character. 'Up to three' means one or two is a legal, complete answer, and the builder must not force three. Three distinct spells, no repeats. If the character has no deity the question has no legal options and must say that rather than presenting an empty or unfiltered list.

requirements.clause: ...to your spell list. ... but you can select them just as you would spells normally on the divine spell list.
requirements.what: The picked spells must actually become legal repertoire options: wherever the character chooses spells for their repertoire, these appear alongside the spells already on their list, at their own ranks, selectable on exactly the same terms — and identifiable as having come from this feat. A pick that only relabels the feat and reaches no spell-selection list is a dead answer; the mechanical consequence here is one the app models, so the answer must produce it.

requirements.clause: They are not automatically added to your repertoire
requirements.what: A negative requirement, stated because the obvious wrong build is the failure: nothing from this feat may appear on the Spells page as a known, prepared, innate or otherwise castable spell. The feat changes the OPTIONS available when building the repertoire and nothing else; the player still has to spend a repertoire slot. The three chosen names should be readable off the feat's own entry so the player can see which ones they added, but no spell entry is created.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day --- **Effect** You call out to The Godclaw to heal your allies.
requirements.what: The ability appears in the actions list with its Frequency line and its complete effect text in the popup, at the cost the text states (it casts the 3-action version of Heal). Both of its uses — the mass heal and the alternative revival below — must be readable from that one entry, because they are one ability sharing one use.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: A single spendable use displayed on the ability: one pip, consumed when the ability is used, restored at daily preparations. Per-DAY, so it does earn a counter — this is the shape that runs out across a scene, unlike a per-round frequency, which gets none.

requirements.clause: You cast the 3‐action version of Heal, heightened to a rank one lower than half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: Heal must be reachable and castable from this ability, specifically the 3-action version and not the 1- or 2-action ones, at a COMPUTED rank — (your level ÷ 2, rounded up) − 1 — shown to the player as an actual rank number and recomputed at every level, never authored as a fixed rank. Where it also surfaces on the Spells page it must be marked as this feat's once-per-day use rather than reading as a free extra Heal. Note the formula yields rank 0 at 1st–2nd level, so whatever renders it has to handle a rank the character cannot actually cast.

requirements.clause: You can select up to five creatures in the area to remain unaffected by the spell.
requirements.what: This sentence changes the Heal it grants, so it must be written into that Heal's description, attributed to this feat by name and visually separated from Heal's own printed rules, so the player cannot mistake it for how Heal normally works. Which five creatures are excluded is a table-time targeting decision, not a builder question and not a number.

requirements.clause: You can instead use this ability to bring a creature within 30 feet that has died within the last round back from the dead. If you do, the creature is restored to 1 Hit Point and is Doomed 1.
requirements.what: The alternative use is part of the same ability's popup text, and the player must be able to see that 'instead' means it spends the same single daily use rather than being a second resource. The 1 Hit Point and the Doomed 1 land on ANOTHER creature — they touch no number on this character's sheet and must not be modelled as one; text only, and the healing itself never moves a sheet stat in any case.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: No requirement. The feat asks the player nothing at build time: the choice between the heal and the revival, the five excluded creatures, and Heal's targets are all decided when the ability is used.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** A creature targets you with a spell of the same tradition as your bloodline.
requirements.what: The feat is a TRIGGERED ability and must appear in the list for its printed cost — the reactions/triggered-actions list — with the Trigger printed in its popup (Principle E; the whole surface for Minor Omen). The trigger is not a fixed sentence: 'the same tradition as your bloodline' must resolve against the character's own bloodline, so the player reads which tradition actually triggers it.

requirements.clause: You generate a blood magic effect you know, even if you are already under the effects of blood magic. The target must be either you or the creature that triggered Blood Rising.
requirements.what: The popup carries the full effect text: that it fires a blood magic effect off its normal schedule, that it works even while another blood magic effect is already running, and the two legal targets (you, or the triggering creature). 'a blood magic effect you know' is character-specific, so the blood magic effect(s) the character's own bloodline gives must be reachable from this entry rather than described generically. Which one is generated is picked in play — an internal step of the activity, not a builder question.

requirements.clause: If the effect has a duration, it instead lasts until the beginning of your next turn.
requirements.what: A marker on the bloodline's blood magic feature/effect saying this feat overrides its duration when generated this way (Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing). No timer and no number: the replaced duration is measured in rounds, which are not tracked (Q1), so the requirement is the text on the modified record, attributed to this feat.

requirements.clause: If the blood magic effect grants you a bonus to AC or the appropriate saving throw, that bonus applies against the triggering spell.
requirements.what: This half is self-facing but single-instance — one bonus against one triggering spell — so it moves NO number on the AC row or any save row. The requirement is the clause being readable where it matters: in the reaction's popup and on the blood magic effect it modifies (Ruling D, the mark lives on the thing you are looking at). If a blood magic effect is modelled with an AC or save bonus of its own, this clause must be reflected on that record too (Principle C).

requirements.clause: **Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of your bloodline.
requirements.what: The feat's own displayed trait list must include a COMPUTED tradition trait (arcane/divine/occult/primal) taken from the character's bloodline — a static trait list on the record cannot say this, and the trait is what decides whether other effects keying off tradition traits reach it. ⚠ No lane in the manual covers a record's own trait line being derived per character; the closest lane, `creatureTrait`, is about traits on YOU, not on the record.

requirements.clause: whole feat — no clause states a choice made while building
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NOTHING at build time — no picker is owed. The only choice it contains ('a blood magic effect you know') is made in play at the moment the reaction fires, from effects the character already owns, and the tradition trait is derived from the bloodline rather than chosen. A builder picker here would be a phantom question of the Exemplar Dedication kind.

requirements.clause: Your blowgun Strikes can apply injury poisons even if they deal no damage due to a creature's resistance.
requirements.what: A `*` on every blowgun Strike row the character has, carrying this rule (Ruling D/G — the marker lives on the action you are looking at when it matters; Q8 confirms marking the action the feat modifies). It moves no number: it changes whether a poison lands, not the attack or the damage. It must sit on the Strike row itself, not on a general stat and not only inside the feat's own text.

requirements.clause: If you critically succeed at a blowgun Strike using a poisoned dart, the target's initial save against the poison is one degree of success worse than the creature rolls; this is a misfortune effect.
requirements.what: The shifted degree belongs to the TARGET's save, not to any statistic of yours, so this earns NO degree-shift entry on your own saves or skills — enemy-facing effects get no surface of their own (decided scope; Q2's 'star the skill and the action' governs shifts on YOUR rolls). What is owed is that the clause reads on the blowgun Strike marker above, including the 'poisoned dart' condition, the crit-success trigger and the misfortune tag, so the player meets the rule where the Strike is rolled.

requirements.clause: if you make a blowgun Strike while hidden or undetected, you don't automatically become observed. Instead, immediately attempt a Stealth check against the Perception DC of the target. If you succeed, you don't become observed, and are hidden (if you were undetected, you still become hidden rather than remaining undetected).
requirements.what: Two marks for one clause, per Q2 (star the skill AND the action): a `*` on STEALTH — that is where the player looks up the number this clause makes them roll — and a mark on the blowgun Strike row, because the clause fires off making that Strike. Both carry the full text: the hidden/undetected precondition, the check against the target's Perception DC, and both outcomes (stay unobserved but hidden; drop from undetected to hidden). No number moves.

requirements.clause: whole feat — no clause states a choice
requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing — no choice, no option list, no level-scaling pick. Every clause is a standing rule about blowgun Strikes, so a builder picker here would be invented.

requirements.clause: During your daily preparations, choose one of your allies as your charge.
requirements.what: The player is asked WHO their charge is, and per Q23 the question must NOT render in the builder — it belongs to Daily preparations and defaults to the last charge chosen. Legal answers: exactly one ally, and the feat restricts the list no further, so the character's own records cannot supply it — free text is a legitimate answer type here (Principle I). If a party/campaign roster exists it may back the field, but the feat itself imposes no filter and allows no repeats: one charge at a time, and a new answer replaces the old.

requirements.clause: You can take 10 minutes to change who your charge is before your next daily preparations.
requirements.what: The same question must be re-openable BETWEEN daily preparations — the control cannot be locked until the next rest, which is the natural way a daily choice gets built. The 10-minute cost is prose the player observes at the table; per Principle P a benefit gated behind a deliberate out-of-combat action needs no star, so nothing is owed on a stat row for this clause — only that the answer stays editable mid-day.

requirements.clause: When you Taunt, the penalty your taunted enemy takes increases to –2 against your charge.
requirements.what: The –2 is a penalty on the ENEMY, so no number lands on any row of your sheet (Ruling F / enemy scope). What is owed is a marker on the TAUNT action recording that this feat raises the penalty to –2 against your charge (Ruling D and Q8 — mark the action the feat modifies), and per Ruling C, if Taunt is performed by a skill check, that skill carries the same `*` so the player meets it where the roll is looked up.

requirements.clause: choose one of your allies as your charge … the penalty your taunted enemy takes increases to –2 against your charge
requirements.what: The daily answer must have a CONSUMER, not merely a stored label: the current charge's name has to be readable on the sheet — on the Taunt marker above ("–2 against <charge>") and/or on the feat's own entry — because the clause cannot be read without knowing who was named. Principle K ('what is re-chosen in the builder needs no sheet surface') does not cover this: it is re-chosen at daily preparations, and the Taunt rule depends on the answer.

requirements.clause: You launch an insightful quip at a foe, distracting them. Choose a foe within 30 feet and roll a Diplomacy check against the target's Will DC.
requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list at its printed cost, whose popup states the 30-foot range and the check it calls for — a Diplomacy check against the target's Will DC. Choosing the foe is an in-play step of the activity, never a builder question.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The target is distracted and takes a –3 status penalty to Perception and Will saves for 1 minute … **Success** As critical success, but the penalty is –2.
requirements.what: The whole degree-of-success table must be readable in the action's popup (every printed degree, including the retort escape clause and the GM-adjudicated skill actions that qualify). The –3/–2 status penalties land on the ENEMY, so they touch no row of your sheet and no enemy condition is modelled (decided scope; the Q4 shape — the entry is the whole surface). Nothing here is a degree-shift on your own statistics.

requirements.clause: **Critical Failure** Your quip is atrocious. You take the same penalty an enemy would take had you succeeded. This ends after 1 minute or if you issue another Bon Mot and succeed.
requirements.what: The clause that lands on YOU, and the easy one to miss. It is a –2 status penalty to your own Perception and your own Will saves — the app must resolve the back-reference 'the same penalty an enemy would take had you succeeded' to the Success row's –2 rather than printing the sentence — lasting 1 minute. Self-facing, longer than a round, and able to be shut off → a MODE the player turns on when they critically fail (Q1 + Q11) that moves the real numbers on Perception and Will, carrying its end condition in its text (ends after 1 minute, or when you issue another Bon Mot and succeed). Q15 does not excuse it — that ruling governs effects firing on a critical SUCCESS.

requirements.clause: roll a Diplomacy check against the target's Will DC
requirements.what: No `*` and no bonus is owed on the Diplomacy row: the feat USES Diplomacy, it does not change the number, and no choice names that stat (the Q20/Assurance refinement applies to a chosen stat, which this is not). Naming the check inside the action's popup is the entire surface.

requirements.clause: whole feat — no clause states a choice made while building
requirements.what: The feat asks the player nothing at build time — no options, no list, no scaling pick. The only 'choose' in the text ('Choose a foe within 30 feet') is targeting at the table.

requirements.clause: Choose one cantrip from either the occult spell list or the primal spell list.
requirements.what: A picker for exactly ONE cantrip. The legal options are the union of two lists — every cantrip on the occult spell list plus every cantrip on the primal spell list — filtered to cantrips only, and NOT filtered to the character's repertoire or class list, and NOT filtered by the tradition picked in the Special clause (the text allows either list whichever tradition is chosen). One pick, taken once when the feat is gained; no repeats and no later-level second pick. Per Q9 the picker offers only what may legally be chosen, and per Q27 anything shown but unpickable must look unpickable.

requirements.clause: You can cast this cantrip as an innate spell at will
requirements.what: The chosen cantrip appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell marked at will — no use pips, no per-day counter, no limited-uses resource — with its details reachable and this feat named as its source. Its tradition is whichever the Special clause's answer named, not a hardcoded one.

requirements.clause: and it's heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: The entry displays a rank of exactly ceil(level/2), and the cantrip's heightened values are shown at that rank rather than at rank 1 — re-derived as the character levels, so the number on the sheet changes at every odd level. The text states its own formula, so this is a computed rank, never a fixed one.

requirements.clause: **Special** Choose when you gain this feat whether your innate spells are primal or occult;
requirements.what: A second, separate question asked once at the moment the feat is gained: primal OR occult. Exactly two legal options — no other tradition is available — and the answer is independent of which list the cantrip above came from. A build-time pick, not a daily one, and not re-asked later.

requirements.clause: this choice applies to all innate spells you gain from lizardfolk ancestry feats that have Bone Magic as a prerequisite.
requirements.what: The tradition answer must have a consumer beyond this feat's own label: it tags this cantrip's innate entry AND every innate spell granted by any later lizardfolk ancestry feat that names Bone Magic as a prerequisite. Those downstream feats must not ask the question again, and must display the tradition this answer set rather than one hardcoded on their own record — otherwise the sheet states a false tradition for spells the player reads elsewhere (Q12: the sheet must not say something false about the spell).

requirements.clause: Trigger An adjacent ally attempts to High Jump or Long Jump.
requirements.what: The feat is a REACTION and must appear in the reactions list as its own entry, with its trigger printed in its popup: "An adjacent ally attempts to High Jump or Long Jump" (and the adjacency condition, which the app can never evaluate, stated rather than modelled). Per principle E this reaction entry is the surface the player reads; without it the feat is invisible, because every number it produces lands on someone else.

requirements.clause: The triggering ally gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their Athletics check to High Jump or Long Jump. This bonus increases to +2 if you're an expert in Athletics, +3 if you're a master, and +4 if you're legendary.
requirements.what: The reaction's popup must carry this scaling text in full (principle B). ⚠ The tier is keyed to YOUR OWN Athletics proficiency rank, which is a fact the sheet already holds, so the entry must not present a bare "+1" — it must show the value that currently applies to this character (+1 trained / +2 expert / +3 master / +4 legendary) alongside the ladder, or the player reads the wrong number off their own reaction.

requirements.clause: The triggering ally gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their Athletics check ... the triggering ally's Leap distance on a successful check increases by 2 feet for a High Jump or 5 feet for a Long Jump, even if it would allow the ally to Leap further than their land Speed.
requirements.what: NOTHING FURTHER IS OWED. Both numbers land on the triggering ALLY: no bonus to your Athletics, no `*` on your Athletics row, and no change to your own Leap or land Speed (Ruling F — an effect that lands on a teammate produces no star and no modifier on your sheet). The 2 ft / 5 ft Leap increase and the "even if it would allow the ally to Leap further than their land Speed" override belong in the same reaction popup as text, and nowhere else.

requirements.clause: Prerequisites Trained in Athletics
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NO question — there is no choice of skill, target, bonus or shape anywhere in its text. "Trained in Athletics" is an eligibility prerequisite, not a choice (prerequisites are explicitly not a mechanical lane); it governs whether the feat may be offered at all, per Q9.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Acrobatics
requirements.what: Acrobatics is set to trained, and the Acrobatics modifier the player reads on the skills page must actually include that proficiency (level + trained). This is the default path — no question is asked of a character who is not already trained in Acrobatics.

requirements.clause: (or another skill of your choice, if you were already trained in Acrobatics)
requirements.what: A CONDITIONAL choice: the app must ask "which skill?" ONLY when the character is already trained in Acrobatics at the moment the feat is taken; otherwise it must ask nothing and silently train Acrobatics. The question is not asked twice and does not repeat at later levels.

requirements.clause: or another skill of your choice
requirements.what: LEGAL OPTIONS when that fallback fires: any OTHER skill (i.e. the whole skill list minus Acrobatics itself). A skill the character is already trained in is a wasted pick and there is no later-level upgrade to redeem it (contrast Canny Acumen, Q21), so those options must not be live — and per Q27 they must LOOK unpickable: greyed with the reason ("already trained"), never rendered identical to a live option and silently inert. The text does not restrict the list by category, does not allow repeats, and does not scale at any later level.

requirements.clause: or another skill of your choice, if you were already trained in Acrobatics
requirements.what: Whichever skill the fallback answer names becomes trained, and that skill's printed modifier must move accordingly. The answer must reach a proficiency rank — an answer that only relabels the feat is a defect (Q20).

requirements.clause: You also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Acrobatics checks to Tumble Through a foe's space.
requirements.what: A restricted bonus, so it must NOT be added into the flat Acrobatics total (Ruling B). It appears as a `*` on the Acrobatics row carrying "+2 circumstance to Tumble Through a foe's space" and linking back to this feat — that is where the player looks the number up. Per Q2/Q8 the Tumble Through action entry ALSO carries the marker, since the bonus is named after an action; Tumble Through is performed only with Acrobatics, so no second skill is starred (Ruling C is satisfied by the one skill).

requirements.clause: You can hold your breath for 25 times as long as usual before suffocating.
requirements.what: A printed statement the player can read off the sheet: breath-holding duration is ×25. There is no stat row for suffocation, so per Ruling D it attaches to the thing it modifies — the drowning/suffocation rule or, failing that, a note carried by the character rather than left only inside the feat's flavour paragraph. If the sheet prints a breath-holding duration anywhere, that printed value must be the multiplied one, not the base.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against inhaled threats, such as inhaled poisons
requirements.what: A `*` on the saves, carrying "+1 circumstance vs inhaled threats (e.g. inhaled poisons)" and linking to this feat; it must NOT be folded into any flat save total, because the bonus is restricted (Ruling B). ⚠ The text says "saving throws" without naming one, so per Q2 ALL THREE saves are starred — narrowing it to Fortitude because inhaled poisons usually call for Fortitude would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's (Ruling H: where the rules are open, stay open).

requirements.clause: if you roll a success on such a saving throw, you get a critical success instead
requirements.what: A success→critical success upgrade on saves against inhaled threats — a SECOND requirement on the same rolls as the +1, not a restatement of it. Per Q2 it is registered as a degree shift so that all three saves are marked and the marker states its condition ("against inhaled threats"); it must live in one registry with the star above rather than being hand-copied as prose, and it must not be omitted just because the +1 bonus is already shown.

requirements.clause: (whole feat)
requirements.what: The feat asks the player NOTHING. There is no choice of save, threat type, or skill anywhere in its text, and nothing here is a daily or repeatable pick.

requirements.clause: you can exhale a torrent of energy in a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line, dealing 1d4 damage
requirements.what: A named action, Breath of the Dragon, must appear in the actions list with a popup carrying its area, damage, save and recharge. ⚠ Two things the popup must NOT do: print "a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line" as if the player picks one at use time (the later sentence fixes the shape from the draconic exemplar), and state an action cost — the text as given states none, so the cost must come from the record's own action-cost data and cannot be read out of this prose.

requirements.clause: The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar (see above).
requirements.what: The action entry must show the RESOLVED values for this character — the one shape (cone or line, with its printed distance), the one damage type, and the one save named by that character's draconic exemplar — not the generic sentence. Three separate facts about the action are decided by an answer given elsewhere on the character, and an entry that repeats "match those of your draconic exemplar" leaves the player unable to use it. The "(see above)" points at a table this text does not contain, so the values must be looked up from the exemplar record.

requirements.clause: The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar (see above).
requirements.what: This feat asks NO NEW QUESTION — it reads an answer the character already gave. But that answer must be a recorded, readable pick: the app must be able to resolve the character's draconic exemplar (the dragon type chosen by the granting draconic feature), because shape, damage type and save all hang off it. If the character has no recorded exemplar, the choice must be offered by whatever grants it — legal options being that feature's own dragon list — or this action can state none of its three defining values.

requirements.clause: Each creature in the area must attempt a basic saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC.
requirements.what: The popup must print the actual DC as a NUMBER, computed as the higher of this character's class DC and spell DC. ⚠ Resolved by comparing the VALUES, not the ranks — an expert spell DC on a high attribute can beat a master class DC on a lower one. This is a third number printed nowhere else on the sheet, so restating the sentence is not delivery; and "basic saving throw" must be stated so the player knows the four-degree scaling applies.

requirements.clause: At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4.
requirements.what: The damage shown must be the character's CURRENT damage, not the printed base: 1d4, plus 1d4 at 3rd level and at every odd level thereafter (2d4 at 3rd, 3d4 at 5th … 10d4 at 19th). A level-scaled action that keeps displaying 1d4 is wrong for every character above 2nd level.

requirements.clause: You can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.
requirements.what: NO counter, pip, or spendable resource. The recharge is measured in rounds, and rounds are not tracked (owner: rounds are not tracked; per O2 a per-round frequency gets no use pip) — and the duration is itself a die roll the app cannot resolve. The requirement is only that the sentence appears in the action's popup so the player knows to track it themselves.

requirements.clause: This ability has the trait associated with the type of damage it deals.
requirements.what: The action's trait list must contain the resolved damage-type trait for this character's exemplar (fire, cold, acid, electricity, etc.), derived from the damage type above. A blank or generic trait line means the player cannot tell whether an enemy's resistance or immunity applies.

requirements.clause: Breath of the Dragon Source Player Core 2 pg. 45 ... Breath of the Dragon leads to... Debilitating Breath, Energize Bite, Formidable Breath, Lingering Breath
requirements.what: Catalogue chrome, not rules: the repeated title, the "Source … pg. 45" line and the "leads to…" trailer are website navigation embedded in the text. They must not be rendered to the player as part of the ability's rules text. Nothing mechanical is owed by them.

requirements.clause: you can exhale a torrent of energy in a or a , dealing 1d4 damage
requirements.what: A named action, Breath of the Dragon, in the actions list, with a popup carrying area, damage, save and recharge. ⚠ THE AREA IS MISSING FROM THIS RECORD'S TEXT — "in a or a ," has lost both values (the sibling record prints "a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line"). The action must state an area, so the numbers have to be recovered from the source; they cannot be read out of this text, and rendering the sentence as-is shows the player an ability with no area at all. The text also states no action cost, so the cost must come from the record's own action-cost data.

requirements.clause: The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar.
requirements.what: The entry must show the RESOLVED shape, damage type and save for this character's draconic exemplar — three separate facts, each decided by an answer given elsewhere on the character. Repeating the sentence leaves the action unusable. Note this also fixes WHICH of the two areas applies, which is the second reason the missing area values above matter.

requirements.clause: The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar.
requirements.what: No new question is asked by this feat; it consumes an existing answer. The requirement is that the character's draconic exemplar is a recorded, readable pick — offered by whatever grants it, with that feature's dragon list as the legal options — because without it none of the three derived values can be printed. The feat itself must not present a shape/damage-type picker of its own; that would be asking the prerequisite as a question (the Exemplar Dedication phantom-picker failure).

requirements.clause: Each creature in the area must attempt a basic saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC.
requirements.what: Print the DC as an actual number: the higher of this character's class DC and spell DC, compared by VALUE and not by rank. It is a number that appears nowhere else on the sheet, so the sentence alone is not delivery. "Basic" must be stated, since it defines the four degrees of success.

requirements.clause: At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4.
requirements.what: The displayed damage scales with the character's level: 1d4, +1d4 at 3rd and every 2 levels thereafter (2d4 at 3rd, 3d4 at 5th … 10d4 at 19th). The number shown must be the character's current one, not the printed base.

requirements.clause: You can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.
requirements.what: No counter and no use pip — the recharge is in rounds (untracked, per O2) and its length is a die roll. Only the sentence itself is owed, inside the action's popup.

requirements.clause: This ability has the trait associated with the type of damage it deals.
requirements.what: The action's traits must include the resolved damage-type trait for this character's exemplar, so the player can tell whether a target's resistance or immunity bites.
